docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The backend is a FastAPI app (backend/app/main.py). Every endpoint is under /api except /health and /health/agents. A running instance serves Swagger UI at /docs, ReDoc at /redoc and the schema at /openapi.json; locally that is http://localhost:8001/docs.

Authentication. Send the token from POST /api/auth/login as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Tokens are HS256 JWTs valid for 24 hours. In the tables below:

  • user: a valid token for an active user is required (401 otherwise).
  • admin: the user must also be an admin (403 otherwise).
  • optional: anonymous calls are allowed. With a valid token for an active user, the Taste Graph is applied and rate limits count per user; otherwise (including a deactivated user's token) the caller is anonymous and counted per IP.
  • none: no token needed.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
Endpoints that call the AI agents are rate-limited per caller (the signed-in user, or the client IP for anonymous requests) over a sliding 10-minute window (backend/app/core/rate_limit.py). Every accepted request counts, including cached responses and requests later rejected as invalid (422) or unauthenticated (401); only requests answered with 429 do not.

Bucket Endpoints Default limit search POST /api/search, POST /api/search/sync 10 chat POST /api/chat 30 compare POST /api/compare/destination 30 discover POST /api/discover 10 import POST /api/import/extract, POST /api/import/resolve-place 20 light_ai POST /api/flights, /hotels, /activities and their /filtered variants, /flights/fare-calendar, /visa, /sim, /tips, /getting-around, /forex, /itinerary, /events, /walking-tours, /layover, /stress-test, /nearby, /live-check, /fare-watches (create), /fare-watches/{id}/check, /price-watches (create), /price-watches/{id}/check, PUT /auth/email 60

Each bucket is counted separately, with one exception: a chat turn that starts a full trip plan (including a refinement that rebuilds the itinerary) also takes one token from the caller's search bucket, so searches and chat-planned trips share one budget; over it, the already-open chat stream answers with a friendly delta saying roughly how many minutes to wait, then done (no 429, no error). Over the limit the API answers 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds) and:

{"detail": "Too many requests — please wait 42 seconds and try again."}

Limits are configurable (see Configuration). The counter is in-process, so each backend process counts on its own.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: Accounts, sessions, OAuth sign-in, the account area, avatars, export and deletion, the daily AI quota, the game and admin invites are specified in Accounts API, the frozen contract the web, iOS and Android clients build against. This page covers the original auth endpoints; the legacy request and response keys are unchanged.

docs.title: POST /api/auth/login
docs.text:
{ "username": "admin", "password": "your-password" }

Response (401 for wrong credentials or an inactive account):

{
  "access_token": "eyJ...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "user": { "username": "admin", "is_admin": true, "requires_password_change": false, "email": null }
}

If requires_password_change is true, the frontend sends the user to /change-password first.

docs.title: POST /api/auth/change-password
docs.text:
{ "current_password": "old", "new_password": "at-least-8-chars" }

Returns {"access_token": "...", "token_type": "bearer"} with a fresh token. 400 if the current password is wrong or the new one is shorter than 8 characters.

docs.title: GET /api/auth/me
docs.text: Returns { "username", "is_admin", "requires_password_change", "email" }.

docs.title: PUT /api/auth/email
docs.text:
{"email": "me@example.com"} sets the account email (trimmed, lower-cased; not verified, so the route is rate-limited in the light_ai bucket); "" clears it and turns email off on all the user's fare watches. Returns {"email": ...}. 422 for an address that isn't local@domain.tld; 409 when another account uses it. Set from the Preferences page.

Self-registration is POST /api/auth/signup (see Accounts API). Admins can also create users:

docs.title: POST /api/admin/users
docs.text:
{ "username": "newuser", "password": "TemporaryPassword123", "email": null, "is_admin": false }

201 with the user (no password hash). The new user must change the password on first login. 409 for a duplicate username or email, 400 for a password under 8 characters. POST /api/admin/users/{username}/reset-password takes {"new_password": "..."}.

docs.title: POST /api/search
docs.text:
The main endpoint. It streams results as Server-Sent Events. Auth: optional. Responses for a complete, error-free run are cached for 30 minutes and replayed instantly.

Request body (TravelSearchRequest, backend/app/schemas/request.py):

{
  "origin": "London",
  "destination": "Tokyo",
  "departure_date": "2026-06-01",
  "return_date": "2026-06-14",
  "nationality": "British",
  "interests": ["food", "history", "nature"],
  "budget_usd": 4000,
  "num_travelers": 2,
  "adults": 2, "children": 0, "seniors": 0, "infants": 0,
  "accessibility_needs": [],
  "residence_permits": [],
  "existing_visas": [],
  "destinations": null,
  "destination_nights": null,
  "pace": "balanced",
  "serendipity": 0.5,
  "locale": "de"
}

locale is optional: one of en, es, de, fr, hi, zh, bn (anything else is a 422). When it is not English, every model call for the request is told to write its human-readable text in that language (JSON keys, enum values, codes, URLs, prices, currency codes, dates and place names stay as in English), and the response cache keeps a separate entry per language. Absent or en behaves exactly as before. The static Phase 0 data (visa, SIM, tips, getting around, forex, emergency card) stays English until the AI result replaces it. The same field is accepted by POST /api/chat, /api/discover, /api/compare/destination and the single-agent and /filtered routes. The web app sends the UI language.

Two optional fields carry a trip imported with POST /api/import/extract:

  • must_include (at most 25): places the plan must contain, each {name, kind, city, town?, lat?, lng?, note?, quote?, verified}. city is the trip stop the place belongs to, and town is its own town when that differs (a day trip). They lead the activities results as source: "your_link", from_link: true items, folding in the agent's own copy of the same place, and they stay even when the activities agent fails. Each item's verification_note is "Located on Google Maps" or "From your link — not independently checked". After the itinerary (AI or template) is built, a deterministic check marks the slots that name each place (from_link, link_place, link_places, link_quote, link_note). A slot counts only if the place's name appears in its activity or location text as one contiguous, ordered phrase. The match ignores accents and filler words ("the", "de"), treats hyphens, spaces and apostrophes alike, and drops a possessive "'s". Run-together spellings count only on whole tokens ("Senso-ji" ~ "Sensoji", "Time Out" ~ "TimeOut"). So "Tokyo Tower" is not "Tokyo Skytree … tallest tower", and "Ark Hills" is not "Park Hills". On multi-city trips, the slot must also be on a day in the place's own city. Travel slots may name a place through their activity text ("Train to Sintra for Pena Palace", "Hop on Tram 28"), but are never replaced. Arrival, departure and hotel slots never stand for a place. Missing places go into the most replaceable slot on a day in the right city: free time first, food at lunch or dinner, and never a logistics slot on any day. Logistics means arrivals, departures, check-in/out, flights, trains, Shinkansen, buses, ferries, drives, transfers, "→", "to ", two of the trip's stops joined by "–", "⇒" or "to", or a transport category. Each stop's travel-in day is skipped when that city has another day. A place of kind transport is never put into a slot: unmatched, it becomes a note on one of its city's days. A replaced slot drops the old activity's cost, booking link and times, and that cost is taken off the day's and the trip's totals. When every such slot already holds a link place, the place goes into the day's link_extras. The itinerary also carries link_coverage: {total, scheduled, extras, missing}.
  • import_source: {url?, title}, where the trip came from. url must be http(s). Saved plans keep it in search_data, and the share page, print view and calendar export show "Inspired by …".

    • destinations and destination_nights describe a multi-city trip (see Multi-City Trips). taste_context is set by the server from the user's Taste Graph; a client value is ignored. origin and destination may be city names, typeahead labels or airport codes; the validator resolves them to airport codes for live flight search (see Place and Airport Data).

    Response: Content-Type: text/event-stream. Each event is data: {JSON}\n\n, and : keepalive comments are sent while agents run.

    Event Phase source Notes visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex 0, then 1 static, then ai Static-backed; an AI error is not sent, so the static data stays confidence 0 static Travel Ease grade: total out of 100 and green/amber/red, from visa ease, safety, English friendliness, cost vs budget and tourist infrastructure emergency_card 0, then 1 static, then ai Static-backed agent_status — — {agent, status: "searching" \| "done"} for the 15 agents at start, and for stress_test flights, weather, hotels, activities, places_to_see, walking_tours, events 1 ai hotels, activities and places_to_see are sent twice: before and after link enrichment packing_list deferred ai (static for the template fallback) Starts when activities and weather are in pricing_advisor deferred ai Starts when flights have at least 3 results; skipped on error or after 120 s itinerary 2 none Starts when activities and hotels are in; template fallback after 60 s stress_test after the itinerary ai 90 s timeout; on error an error section is sent done — — Always last

    Every non-error section carries data.verification (see Agent System). An agent that fails sends {"error": "..."} as its data (except the static-backed ones), so the UI can show "not available" instead of waiting. When the monthly AI spend cap has tripped, the data is {"error": "AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st.", "error_code": "ai_limit"}; single-agent routes return the same object.

docs.title: POST /api/search/sync
docs.text: Same request and agents, run sequentially; returns a single JSON object. For testing only.

docs.title: POST /api/discover
docs.text:
Surprise me. Auth: optional. Returns 5 destination suggestions.

{
  "origin": "JFK",
  "nationality": "American",
  "departure_date": "2026-08-01",
  "return_date": "2026-08-08",
  "budget_usd": 3000,
  "interests": ["food", "history"],
  "adults": 1, "children": 0, "seniors": 0, "infants": 0
}

return_date and budget_usd are optional. Response:

{
  "destinations": [
    {
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "country": "Portugal",
      "estimated_cost_usd_low": 1400,
      "estimated_cost_usd_high": 2200,
      "visa_type": "visa-free",
      "visa_verified": true,
      "weather_emoji": "☀️",
      "weather_description": "Warm and sunny, 22–26°C in August",
      "flight_duration_hours": 7.5,
      "flight_duration_label": "~7h 30m from New York",
      "match_reasons": ["Exceptional food scene", "Rich Age of Discovery history"],
      "highlights": ["Alfama district", "Sintra", "Belém Tower"]
    }
  ]
}

visa_verified: true means the visa type came from the static visa table; otherwise it is the model's guess and the UI shows a warning badge. Errors: 422 invalid request, 504 after 30 s, 500 agent failure, 503 with detail "AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st." when the monthly AI spend cap has tripped (not cached). Results are cached for 30 minutes.

docs.title: POST /api/import/extract
docs.text:
Plan from a link: reads a web page, pasted text or screenshots and returns the places in it, resolved and grouped into a trip for the traveller to review. Auth: user. Bucket: import.

Request body: exactly one of:

{"url": "https://blog.example/48-hours-in-lisbon"}
{"text": "48 hours in Lisbon: Time Out Market, Belém Tower, LX Factory…"}
{"images": [{"media_type": "image/png", "data_base64": "iVBORw0…"}]}

text is at most 20,000 characters. images holds 1–4 PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF images of up to 5 MB each, decoded. On Gemini (Vertex AI reads no GIF) a GIF is converted to PNG when Pillow is installed, otherwise refused with gif_unsupported. The type is sniffed from the bytes, and HEIC is refused with a friendly message. Images are sent as JSON base64, not multipart.

Link fetching (backend/app/services/link_fetch.py): - Only http and https on the default ports, with no credentials in the URL. - The host is resolved, and every address must be public. Private, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved and CGNAT ranges are refused, as are their IPv6, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, 6to4 and Teredo forms. The connection goes to that vetted IP, with the original Host header and TLS SNI, so DNS rebinding cannot redirect it. - Redirects are followed by hand, at most 3, and each hop is checked again. - There is a 10-second ceiling, and only HTML, XHTML and plain text are accepted. - Only gzip and deflate compression is requested and accepted. The body is read as raw bytes, at most 2 MB, and inflated with a bounded zlib decompressor that stops at 2 MB of output, so a compression bomb cannot grow. Brotli, zstd, stacked and unknown encodings get unsupported_encoding. - Every hop sends Connection: close, so no pooled connection is reused across hosts. - HTML is parsed with BeautifulSoup in a worker thread, off the event loop. - From the page come the title, the OpenGraph and Twitter description, JSON-LD (articleBody, ItemList, places and attractions) and the readable main text, capped at 30k characters. The main text comes from the biggest article or content block, keeps headings and list items, and drops nav, footer, script and style. - YouTube and TikTok links are read through their public oEmbed endpoints, plus the YouTube watch page's description. - Instagram, Facebook, X and Threads get a specific blocked_source error, including when a shortener redirects to them. - Scripts are never run, and links in the content are never followed.

Extraction: the link_import agent (.agents/link_import.md, the agent model; screenshots go as vision image blocks). Everything taken from the source (site name, title, author, description, text) is wrapped as untrusted data between <<<SOURCE_<nonce>>>> and <<<END_SOURCE_<nonce>>>> markers. The nonce is random for each request, and anything in the source that looks like a marker is stripped. Only fixed labels ("a web page", "pasted text", "screenshots") sit outside the fence. The system prompt says to ignore any instructions inside the source. The output is validated with Pydantic: places without a name are dropped, at most 40 are kept, fields are clamped, and a quote is kept only when it appears in the source text word for word: case-sensitive, whole words only, with curly and straight quote marks treated as the same. A day_hint is kept only when the source text itself names that day ("Day 2", "Day 2–3", "days 4 to 5").

Resolution (backend/app/services/link_import.py): - Each place's city is resolved with resolve_place to a canonical town, country, coordinates and airports. A town within 45 km of a bigger stop in the same country joins that stop as a day trip. - Stops are ordered by the source's day hints, then by source order. With more than 3 stops, the 3 with the most places are kept and the rest are listed in also_mentioned. - Nights are split by place count, with at least 1 per stop. The trip length is suggested_days, or else about 4 sightseeing places a day, between 3 and 14 days. - With SERPER_KEY, up to 25 places are looked up on Google Maps (5 at a time, cached). A hit within 60 km of the town that shares a word with the name gives exact coordinates (verified); otherwise the place sits at its town centre (approximate).

Response (200) — ImportPreview:

{
  "source": {"kind": "url", "url": "https://…", "title": "…", "site_name": "Wander Blog", "favicon_url": "https://…", "author": null},
  "title": "48 hours in Lisbon",
  "summary": "Viewpoints, pastries and a day trip to Sintra.",
  "destinations": [{"name": "Lisbon, Portugal", "city": "Lisbon", "country": "Portugal", "airports": ["LIS", "CAT"], "lat": 38.73, "lng": -9.15, "place_count": 5, "nights": 3}],
  "places": [{"id": "p1", "name": "Time Out Market", "kind": "food", "city": "Lisbon", "country": "Portugal", "destination": "Lisbon, Portugal", "lat": 38.707, "lng": -9.146, "approximate": false, "verified": true, "address": "…", "rating": 4.4, "note": "Lunch under one roof", "quote": "start at Time Out Market", "day_hint": 1, "confidence": 0.95}],
  "unresolved": [],
  "also_mentioned": [],
  "suggested_days": 3,
  "season_hint": null,
  "interests": ["food", "viewpoints"],
  "warnings": []
}

kind is one of sight, food, drink, stay, activity, nature, shopping, nightlife, event, transport or area. Places whose town could not be resolved are returned in unresolved, so the traveller can assign them to a stop.

Errors: 422 with detail: {code, message}, where message is written for the traveller:

code When invalid_url, blocked_address, unreachable, timeout, too_many_redirects, not_found, paywall (401/402), blocked_by_site (403, usually bot blocking), http_error, unsupported_content, unsupported_encoding Fetching the link failed blocked_source Instagram, Facebook, X or Threads ("…doesn't let apps read posts. Paste the caption or drop a screenshot instead.") empty_page The page had almost no readable text no_places Nothing was found ("We couldn't spot any places — try pasting the part of the article with the list.") heic_unsupported, gif_unsupported, unsupported_image, image_too_large, too_many_images A screenshot problem

413 (string detail) means the request body is over 30 MB. It is refused before it is parsed, whether the size is declared or streamed (chunked). Each image's base64 must be at most 5 MB (image_too_large). The browser shrinks screenshots before uploading them: long edge ≤ 1568 px, WebP or JPEG at quality 0.85.

502 with code: extract_failed means the extraction agent failed; 503 with code: ai_limit means the monthly AI spend cap has tripped (ai_billing: billing is disabled for the AI service). Plain FastAPI 422 validation errors mean the body did not carry exactly one source. Successful previews are cached for 30 minutes, keyed by a hash of the request.

docs.title: POST /api/import/resolve-place
docs.text:
Places one of the preview's "Couldn't place" spots in a town the traveller types. Auth: user. Bucket: import.

Request: {id?, name, kind?, city, country?, note?, quote?}.

Response (200): {place, destination}. place has the same shape as a preview place. destination is a preview destination (place_count 1, nights 1), so the client can add it as a new stop when the route has fewer than 3.

Errors: 422 with code: city_not_found when the town cannot be resolved, for example an unknown name or a country typed alone.

docs.title: POST /api/compare/destination
docs.text:
Lightweight summary of one destination, used by the Search page's Compare mode (one call per destination, in parallel). Runs flights, hotels (no URL enrichment), weather and visa concurrently with per-piece timeouts (flights and hotels 45 s, weather and visa 30 s). The visa piece uses the static visa table when it has an entry.

Auth: user. Bucket: compare.

Request body: a TravelSearchRequest for a single destination. destinations must be null or have at most one entry; multi-city requests return 422 ("Compare works with single destinations").

Response (200) — example for 2 adults, 7 nights, budget_usd: 3000:

{
  "destination": "Lisbon, Portugal",
  "label": "Lisbon",
  "flight": {"price_usd": 620, "stops": 0, "duration_minutes": 895, "airline": "TAP Air Portugal", "source": "google_flights"},
  "hotel": {"typical_nightly_usd": 110, "cheapest_good_nightly_usd": 70, "count": 5},
  "weather": {"avg_high_c": 24.4, "avg_low_c": 15.7, "poor_days": 1, "total_days": 7, "source": "open-meteo"},
  "visa": {"visa_type": "visa-free", "max_stay_days": 90, "fee_usd": 0, "processing_time": "Not required", "verified": true},
  "ease": {"total": 80, "grade": "green", "safety": 18, "english": 15, "infrastructure": 17, "visa_ease": 10},
  "daily_cost_usd": 100,
  "estimate": {
    "total_usd": 1320,
    "flight_usd": 620,
    "stay_usd": 385,
    "daily_usd": 700,
    "included_in_daily": true,
    "nights": 7,
    "partial": false,
    "budget_status": "under"
  },
  "missing": []
}

Any piece that failed or timed out is null and its name is listed in missing; ease/daily_cost_usd are null for destinations outside the static tables. flight.source of estimate marks a non-live fare; visa.verified is true only for static-table data. ease.grade is green (≥ 71), amber (41–70) or red (≤ 40).

Estimate (per traveller): flight_usd is the cheapest fare (flight.price_usd, round trip, per person). daily_usd = daily_cost_usd × days (days = nights, min 1; nights default to 7 without a return_date). daily_cost_usd is an all-in daily budget that already includes lodging, so when it is known total_usd = flight_usd + daily_usd and stay_usd is shown for reference only (included_in_daily: true) — above, 620 + 700 = 1320. When the daily figure is unknown, total_usd = flight_usd + stay_usd and included_in_daily is false. stay_usd = typical nightly × nights × rooms ÷ travellers, with rooms = ⌈(adults + seniors) ÷ 2⌉ (falling back to ⌈num_travelers ÷ 2⌉) — above, 110 × 7 × 1 ÷ 2 = 385. partial is true when the flight or the daily figure is unknown; the total then sums only the known parts. budget_status compares total_usd × num_travelers with budget_usd (the party's budget): over, under (only for a complete estimate), or null with no budget or when a partial total is still within it.

Errors: 422 for multi-city or invalid requests; 502 when every piece failed; 503 whose detail is the friendly AI-paused text ("AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st.", or the billing-disabled message) when any piece hit the AI spend cap or disabled billing.

Caching: only complete results (empty missing) are cached in the shared TTL cache, keyed on the full request; partial results and 502s are never cached.

docs.title: POST /api/chat
docs.text:
Auth: user. Streams SSE.

{
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Plan a 5-day trip to Bangkok for two people" }],
  "selections": {},
  "search_results": {},
  "session_context": {},
  "locale": "de"
}

locale is optional (see POST /api/search): replies, narrative, suggestion chips and the itinerary text come back in that language.

Event types: delta (text), done, error, suggestions, session_context_update, plan_action, planning_start, trip_map, itinerary_generating, comprehensive_itinerary, planning_done, agent_status and section_result. A planning request streams planning_start → trip_map → itinerary_generating → comprehensive_itinerary → planning_done; section_result appears only in the specialist fallback and refinement paths. An exception still ends the stream with a fallback delta, error and done. When the monthly AI spend cap has tripped, the reply is a delta "AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st." and done (no error). See Chat Assistant.

docs.title: GET /api/plans, POST /api/plans
docs.text:
List the caller's plans, or save one. Saving records Taste Graph signals.

{
  "name": "The Rainy Tokyo Adventure",
  "search_data": { "origin": "London", "destination": "Tokyo", "departure_date": "2026-04-01" },
  "selections": {
    "flight": {},
    "hotel": {},
    "activities": [],
    "itinerary_slots": [],
    "itinerary": {},
    "itinerary_layout": {},
    "itinerary_edits": {},
    "itinerary_notes": {}
  }
}

docs.title: GET, PUT, DELETE /api/plans/{id}
docs.text: Get, update (name and/or selections) or delete one of the caller's plans; 404 for another user's plan.

docs.title: POST /api/plans/{id}/share and GET /api/share/{token}
docs.text: POST returns {"share_token": "..."} (the existing token if there is one). GET /api/share/{token} needs no auth and returns the plan's name, timestamps, selections and only these search fields: origin, destination, destinations, dates, interests, traveller counts and pace. DELETE /api/plans/{id}/share revokes the token. See Sharing and Plans. Share links 2.0 (options for dates, origin and name; card PNG; Open Graph page; list and revoke) is specified in the frozen Sharing API; these legacy routes are unchanged.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text: Trips are plans with dates and a phase (Dreaming, Planning, Ready, On the road, Memories). Every /api/trips* route needs sign-in and acts only on the caller's own trips. The full contract (frozen, additive changes only) is Trips API: GET/POST /trips, GET/PATCH/DELETE /trips/{id}, GET /trips/stats, prep (/trips/{id}/prep), PUT /trips/{id}/snapshot, GET /trips/{id}/offline-pack, expenses, journal, places, check-ins and recap.

docs.title: GET, PUT /api/preferences
docs.text: The caller's preferences: budget_category, nationality, current_residence, residence_permits, existing_visas, interests, num_travelers, adults, children, seniors, infants, accessibility_needs. They pre-fill the Search form, and the Search form writes back to them.

docs.title: GET, POST /api/recent-searches; DELETE /api/recent-searches/{id}
docs.text: GET returns the caller's last 8 searches, newest first, each { "id", "search", "last_used_at" }, where search is the Search form as submitted (route with multi-city stops and optional nights, dates, nationality, permits, visas, interests, budget, traveller mix, accessibility needs, serendipity). POST records one: an identical search (interests in any order) is moved back to the top instead of duplicated, and only the newest 8 are kept. DELETE returns 204, or 404 if the entry does not exist or belongs to someone else.

docs.title: GET, DELETE /api/taste-profile
docs.text: GET returns the learned signals (flight style, hotel tier, activity categories, budget band) and the summary injected into agent prompts. DELETE resets them.

docs.title: POST /api/feedback
docs.text:
{ "page": "results", "rating": 4, "category": "praise", "message": "Great activity suggestions!" }

rating is 1–5; category is bug, feature_request, general or praise; message (optional) is at most 500 characters; metadata is an optional object. Returns 201. Admins read feedback with GET /api/admin/feedback?page=&category=&min_rating=.

docs.title: POST /api/analytics/events
docs.text: Up to 50 batched UI events per call, written to the log as JSON. Returns 204.

docs.title: POST /api/telemetry
docs.text: Body {"client": {anon_id, session_id, platform, app_version, locale}, "events": [{event, ts, screen, props}]}. Auth is optional (a signed-in caller's user id is stored). Each event and prop is checked against a closed registry; unknown events, unknown props and values that are not short tokens, numbers, booleans or listed enums are dropped silently, so a well-formed batch always returns 204. 422 for a malformed envelope or more than 100 events; 413 when the body exceeds 64 KB (or 256 KB once gunzipped; Content-Encoding: gzip is accepted); 404 when TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false. Own rate bucket telemetry (600 per 10 minutes); never behind ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_AI.

docs.title: GET /api/config
docs.text: Public, Cache-Control: max-age=300. Returns {"public_base_url", "telemetry": {"enabled", "flush_interval_s", "max_batch"}, "features": {"telemetry"}}. Clients treat a 404 as "telemetry off".

docs.title: GET /api/admin/telemetry/summary?days=30
docs.text: Admin only. Returns {"days": [{day, users, sessions, events}], "top_events": [{event, events}], "top_screens": [{route, views}], "users_7d"} from the daily rollups plus today's live numbers. users (signed-in user, else anonymous id) and sessions are exact distinct counts across all events and platforms, read from telemetry_daily_totals. users_7d is the distinct users over the trailing 7 UTC days, today included, counted from raw events. Rolled-up days are re-rolled for the trailing 7 days, so late events from offline clients are included.

docs.title: Single-agent and helper endpoints
docs.text:
Each takes the TravelSearchRequest body of /api/search unless noted. Auth: optional (except the fare calendar). Bucket: light_ai.

Endpoint Returns POST /api/flights Flight options; multi-city returns ordered legs. Live single-city results may carry price_insights POST /api/flights/filtered Flights with max_stops, max_price_usd, departure_time_earliest/latest, arrival_time_earliest/latest; enriched and verification-labelled POST /api/hotels Hotels across budget tiers POST /api/hotels/filtered Hotels with num_beds, max_price_per_night_usd, wifi_quality, max_distance_from_center_km, private_washroom POST /api/activities Interest-ranked activities POST /api/activities/filtered Activities with filter_interests, max_price_usd, available_from/to, min_rating POST /api/visa, /api/sim, /api/tips, /api/getting-around, /api/forex The corresponding specialist result POST /api/itinerary Day-by-day itinerary POST /api/events What's On during the trip POST /api/walking-tours Crawled free walking tours (see below) POST /api/layover Layover plan. Own body: city, duration_hours (> 0, ≤ 48), nationality, optional airport, arrival_time (HH:MM) and interests POST /api/stress-test Audit of an itinerary. Body: the search request plus itinerary (required) and optional flights, visa and weather

docs.title: Flight price_insights
docs.text:
When flights come from Google Flights (SerpAPI) on a single-city trip, the result may include Google's own price verdict, taken from the outbound search response (no extra calls). Fields are kept only when well-formed; the object is omitted when there is no usable price_level or lowest_price. Model-generated flight results never carry it (stripped like live_fare), and it does not change the section's verification label.

"price_insights": {
  "lowest_price": 512,
  "price_level": "low",
  "typical_price_range": [600, 820],
  "price_history": [[1727740800, 650], [1727827200, 512]]
}

price_level is low, typical or high.

docs.title: POST /api/flights/fare-calendar
docs.text:
Auth required (401 without a valid token); light_ai rate-limit bucket. Body: the same TravelSearchRequest as /api/search.

For each departure date from 3 days before to 3 days after the requested one, it makes one Google Flights outbound search (SerpAPI) with the return date shifted by the same amount, so the trip length stays the same, and takes the cheapest price (for a round trip that is already the round-trip total). There are no return-leg calls, so this is at most 7 calls, run 4 at a time. Overlapping requests for the same dates (a second tab, a double-mounted component) share the lookups already in flight, so each date costs one call. Dates before tomorrow are skipped. An unfiltered main flight search stores its own cheapest outbound-stage price as the calendar entry for its dates. The requested date shows the lower of that price and the cheapest flight card of the cached main search, so it matches the cards (the main round-trip search always return-prices the lowest-priced outbound, wherever Google lists it, plus the earliest and latest departures); Google's price_insights.lowest_price is used only when neither is available. Each date's price is cached for 30 minutes (serp-cal:{origin}:{dest}:{dep}:{ret}:{travelers}). A date that fails for any reason (HTTP error, timeout, unreadable response) or has no flights comes back as null; the calendar as a whole never fails, and failures are not cached.

{
  "dates": [
    {"departure_date": "2026-10-31", "return_date": "2026-11-07", "cheapest_usd": 610.0, "is_selected": false},
    {"departure_date": "2026-11-03", "return_date": "2026-11-10", "cheapest_usd": 565.0, "is_selected": true},
    {"departure_date": "2026-11-04", "return_date": "2026-11-11", "cheapest_usd": null, "is_selected": false}
  ],
  "currency": "USD",
  "source": "google_flights"
}

Errors (string detail):

Status When 401 Not signed in 422 Multi-city request ("Fare calendar is only available for single-destination trips.") or invalid body 429 Rate limit (see above) 503 {"detail": "Fare calendar needs live flight data, which isn't configured."} — SERPAPI_KEY is not set

docs.title: POST /api/walking-tours
docs.text:
Free and pay-what-you-wish walking tours at the destination (every stop on multi-city trips). Tours are crawled from the providers' public city pages; the LLM only chooses and explains them by id, so every url is a real provider tour page. Same request body as /api/search.

{
  "origin": "NYC",
  "destination": "Lisbon, Portugal",
  "departure_date": "2026-04-01",
  "return_date": "2026-04-08",
  "interests": ["history", "food"],
  "num_travelers": 2
}

Response:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "t3",
      "name": "Lisbon Old Town Free Walking Tour",
      "provider": "GuruWalk",
      "provider_key": "guruwalk",
      "url": "https://www.guruwalk.com/walks/...",
      "image_url": "https://...",
      "description": "Alfama, the cathedral and the viewpoints, with a local guide.",
      "rating": 4.9,
      "review_count": 1280,
      "duration": "2h 30m",
      "price_note": "Free (tip your guide)",
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "reason": "Covers the old-town history you asked for.",
      "top_pick": true
    }
  ],
  "sources": [
    {
      "provider": "GuruWalk",
      "provider_key": "guruwalk",
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "url": "https://www.guruwalk.com/lisbon",
      "count": 6,
      "status": "ok"
    }
  ]
}

sources has one entry per provider and city; status is ok, none (page found, no free tours) or error. Each city is topped up to at least min(4, available) tours. The endpoint returns {"error": ...} only when every provider fails.

docs.title: Fare watches and notifications
docs.text: A fare watch re-checks one single-destination trip's live Google Flights fare (SerpAPI) about twice a day and creates a notification when it is worth telling the traveller. All prices are the total for the trip's travellers, like the Flights section. Every route needs a signed-in user and only sees that user's watches and notifications (404 otherwise), except the unsubscribe link. See Trip Planning Features for the alert rules.

docs.title: POST /api/fare-watches
docs.text:
{
  "origin": "Berlin", "destination": "Lisbon",
  "departure_date": "2026-12-10", "return_date": "2026-12-17", "num_travelers": 2,
  "alert_mode": "any_drop", "target_price": null, "flexible_days": 0, "email_enabled": false
}

Or {"plan_id": 12, ...options} to watch a saved plan's trip. Codes are resolved like a search (typed cities work). alert_mode is any_drop (default) or below_target (needs target_price); flexible_days is 0 or 3 (also watch departures ±3 days, same trip length); email_enabled needs an account email and SMTP (422 otherwise).

Today's price is taken straight away as the baseline (never an alert) when the daily SerpAPI budget allows; otherwise the scheduler takes it. Returns the watch (below) with already_watching: false, or the existing watch for the same trip with already_watching: true. Errors: 503 without SerpAPI; 422 for multi-city ("Fare watch works for single-destination trips for now"), an unknown city, a departure today or earlier, or a return before departure; 409 at FARE_WATCH_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER active watches. Rate-limited (light_ai).

A watch:

{
  "id": 1, "plan_id": null, "origin_code": "BER", "destination_code": "LIS,CAT",
  "origin_label": "Berlin", "destination_label": "Lisbon",
  "departure_date": "2026-12-10", "return_date": "2026-12-17", "num_travelers": 1, "cabin": "economy",
  "flexible_days": 0, "alert_mode": "any_drop", "target_price": null, "email_enabled": true,
  "status": "active",
  "baseline_price": 220.0, "last_price": 150.0, "lowest_price": 150.0, "lowest_price_date": "2026-12-10",
  "last_notified_price": 150.0, "last_notified_at": "2026-11-04T08:50:51+00:00",
  "google_price_level": "low", "google_typical_low": 140, "google_typical_high": 210,
  "check_count": 3, "failure_count": 0, "problem": null,
  "last_checked_at": "...", "next_check_at": "...", "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "...",
  "history": [{"checked_at": "...", "price": 150.0, "cheapest_price": null,
               "cheapest_departure_date": null, "cheapest_return_date": null, "price_level": "low"}],
  "booking_url": "https://www.google.com/flights#flt=BER.LIS.2026-12-10*LIS.BER.2026-12-17;c:USD;e:1;sd:1;t:f"
}

status is active, paused, expired (departure day reached) or error (three failed checks in a row). already_below_target / already_low say the baseline already met the target / was rated "low" by Google (that signal's first alert then needs a full max($15, 5 %) drop below the baseline); problem is a plain-language reason for the latest failed check (null when healthy); the raw error stays server-side. history holds up to 120 checks, oldest first. The alert state per signal (last_notified_*, own_peak_price, own_lowest_price, cheaper_notified_*, cheaper_peak_price) is also returned.

docs.title: GET /api/fare-watches, GET /api/fare-watches/{id}
docs.text: The caller's watches (ordered by departure date) or one watch, each with its history.

docs.title: POST /api/fare-watches/match
docs.text: Body: the trip fields of POST /api/fare-watches. Returns {"watch": {...}} or {"watch": null}; makes no live lookup. The "Watch fare" buttons use it to show "Watching · $412".

docs.title: PATCH /api/fare-watches/{id}
docs.text: Any of status ("paused" or "active"), alert_mode, target_price, flexible_days, email_enabled. Resuming an error watch clears the failures and checks it on the next scheduler tick (the "Retry" action). 409 to resume an expired watch or past the active limit; 422 for below_target without a target or email without an address/SMTP. Scheduler fields can't be set.

docs.title: DELETE /api/fare-watches/{id}
docs.text: Deletes the watch and its history. Returns {"deleted": true}.

docs.title: POST /api/fare-watches/{id}/check
docs.text: "Check now": one live check (also on a paused watch), with the same alert rules as scheduled checks. It never answers from the 30-minute result cache (fares a search or an earlier check left there are looked up again, and the fresh answer replaces them); its SerpAPI calls are reserved from the daily budget and the caller's share like any other check, so it is never free. A new watch's baseline and scheduled checks still reuse cached fares. Returns the watch plus check_status (checked, failed, errored, postponed, expired, skipped, deleted) and notification (the alert this check created, or null). 429 with Retry-After (seconds to the next UTC day) when today's fare-watch budget, or the caller's share of it (FARE_WATCH_USER_DAILY_SHARE), is spent — the detail says which; 409 while the watch is being checked or after it expired; 503 without SerpAPI. Rate-limited (light_ai).

docs.title: GET /api/fare-watches/unsubscribe?token=
docs.text: The signed link at the bottom of alert emails. Returns a confirmation page with a "Stop emails for this fare" button and changes nothing (mail scanners and prefetchers follow GET links). 400 for an invalid token.

docs.title: POST /api/fare-watches/unsubscribe?token=
docs.text: Turns email off for that one watch, without login, and returns a small HTML page; in-app alerts continue. It is the confirmation page's form and the RFC 8058 one-click target: alert emails carry List-Unsubscribe: <…/api/fare-watches/unsubscribe?token=…> and List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click, and the body is ignored. Idempotent; 400 for an invalid token.

docs.title: Price watches
docs.text: A price watch re-checks a hotel's, an activity's or a whole saved trip's live price about twice a day, with the same alert rules as fare watches (whole trips use a step of max($25, 4 %)). Prices are totals (all nights and rooms, all travellers, or the whole trip) in the watch's currency: USD, except an activity watch, which keeps its listing's currency and only ever compares like with like. Ownership, rate limits and the daily SerpAPI budget work as for fare watches, and FARE_WATCH_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER counts fare and price watches together. Which kinds are available depends on the price sources the server registers; an unknown kind is a 422.

docs.title: POST /api/price-watches
docs.text:
{"kind": "hotel", "hotel": {...kind-specific spec...},
 "plan_id": null, "alert_mode": "any_drop", "target_price": null, "email_enabled": false}

The spec rides under the kind's own key (a top-level plan_id is passed into it). The server matches it to a live price and stores that look as the baseline (never an alert). Returns the watch (below) with already_watching: false, or the caller's existing non-expired watch for the same subject with already_watching: true (no live lookup). When nothing live matches:

{"detail": "We couldn't find live prices for this hotel on Google Hotels.",
 "code": "no_live_price", "message": "We couldn't find live prices for this hotel on Google Hotels.",
 "suggestions": [{"title": "Lumen Hotel & The Lisbon Light Show", "subtitle": "Baixa", "price": 398.0,
                  "link": "https://…", "spec": {...}}],
 "estimate": {"price": 420.0, "source": "ai_estimate"}}

with status 422; sending a suggestion's spec back watches it instead. A below_target request may carry target_currency (the currency the target was typed in): when the live price is in another currency nothing is created and the answer is 422 {code: "target_currency_mismatch", message, currency, price, unit_price}, so the client can ask again in that currency (the retry reuses the cached look). Other errors: 422 for an invalid or oversized spec (the detail says why), below_target without a target, email without an address/SMTP, or a subject ending today; 409 at the active limit; 429 with Retry-After when today's budget or the caller's share is spent; 502 when live prices fail; 503 without SerpAPI. Rate-limited (light_ai).

Hotel spec: {name, city, check_in, check_out, adults, rooms?, property_token?, estimate_total?}. city may be "Lisbon, Portugal" or an airport code ("LIS"); it is watched as the city ("Lisbon"). rooms defaults to one room for up to 4 guests, then one per 4 — the rule a trip's hotel uses too. A spec with property_token (a picked suggestion) is priced directly; otherwise the name is matched on Google Hotels. The baseline is always the property's own look by token, as every check. A plan_id is stored only when it is the caller's own plan (otherwise null). The same Google property for the same stay, guests and rooms already watched under another name returns that watch with already_watching: true (after the matching lookup).

Creating a watch holds its kind's worst case from the daily SerpAPI budget and the caller's share (hotel 2 calls, activity 2, trip 10) and gives back what it didn't spend.

A price watch:

{
  "id": 4, "kind": "hotel", "plan_id": null, "title": "Lumen Hotel", "subtitle": "Lisbon · 10–14 Dec",
  "subject": {...as matched...}, "currency": "USD",
  "alert_mode": "any_drop", "target_price": null, "email_enabled": false, "status": "active",
  "baseline_price": 398.0, "last_price": 352.0, "lowest_price": 352.0,
  "last_notified_price": 352.0, "last_notified_at": "...", "own_peak_price": 352.0,
  "last_observation": {"price": 352.0, "unit_price": 88.0, "status": "ok", "source": "google_hotels",
                       "link": "https://…", "breakdown": null, "observed": {...}, "observed_at": "..."},
  "link": "https://…", "expires_on": "2026-12-10",
  "check_count": 3, "failure_count": 0, "unavailable_count": 0, "problem": null, "already_below_target": false,
  "last_checked_at": "...", "next_check_at": "...", "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "...",
  "history": [{"checked_at": "...", "price": 352.0, "breakdown": null, "observed": {"status": "ok"}}]
}

status is active, paused, expired (the expires_on day — check-in, activity date or departure — has come) or error (three failed checks, or three "unavailable" looks, in a row). An unavailable look (sold out for the dates, listing gone) has price: null in history and last_observation.status: "unavailable"; it never alerts.

docs.title: Activity watches
docs.text:
{"kind": "activity", "activity": {"name": "Belém walking tour", "city": "Lisbon",
 "date": "2026-12-10", "travellers": 2, "listing_url": null, "estimate_price": 30}}

name and city are required; date (optional, must be in the future) ends the watch, which otherwise runs 180 days; travellers is 1–20 (default 1); estimate_price is the AI's per-person estimate, shown labelled in a no_live_price answer and never watched. The server searches Google (SerpAPI) for " getyourguide" (then Viator) and watches the best-matching specific listing; category or attraction pages are never watched. The price is the listing's per-person "from" price × travellers (last_observation.unit_price is per person), as Google results show it — getyourguide.com and viator.com are never fetched. A no_live_price answer suggests up to 3 priced specific listings; their spec carries listing_url, and a watch of a picked listing is its own subject (the original activity stays unwatched). A check that can't find the listing, finds it without a price, or finds it in another currency is unavailable (observed.reason: not_found, no_price, currency_changed). A listing matches only when it names every place / proper-noun word of the activity; generic tour words ("small group walking tour") never carry a match alone. Activity alerts use a step of max(1, 5 %) in the listing's currency. "Already watching" is by name, city and travellers (the date only ends the watch), and also by the same listing and travellers however it was found.

docs.title: GET /api/price-watches, GET /api/price-watches/{id}
docs.text: The caller's price watches (?kind=hotel|activity|trip to filter; ordered by expires_on) or one, each with its history.

docs.title: POST /api/price-watches/match
docs.text: Body: {"kind": ..., "<kind>": spec, "plan_id": ...} as for create. Returns {"watch": {...}} or {"watch": null} (also for an unknown kind or an unusable spec); makes no live lookup.

docs.title: PATCH /api/price-watches/{id}
docs.text: Any of status ("paused" / "active"), alert_mode, target_price, email_enabled. Resuming an error watch clears both streaks and checks it on the next tick ("Retry"). 409 to resume an expired watch or past the active limit; 422 as for fare watches.

docs.title: DELETE /api/price-watches/{id}
docs.text: Deletes the watch and its history. Returns {"deleted": true}.

docs.title: POST /api/price-watches/{id}/check
docs.text: "Check now" (also on a paused watch). Like the fare-watch check, it never answers from the 30-minute cache: the look is live, refreshes the cache, and its calls count against the daily budget and the caller's share. Returns the watch plus check_status (checked, unavailable, failed, errored, postponed, expired, skipped, deleted) and notification. 429 / 409 / 503 as for fare watches. Rate-limited (light_ai).

docs.title: GET, POST /api/price-watches/unsubscribe?token=
docs.text: As the fare-watch unsubscribe link, for one price watch (its own signed token; a fare-watch token is refused with 400).

docs.title: /api/alerts/*
docs.text: Price alerts 2.0. The full contract (objects, advice codes, error codes, delivery rules) is the frozen Alerts API. In short: every route needs a signed-in user and acts only on the caller's watches (404 watch_not_found). GET /api/config reports features.alerts_api: 2, features.price_alerts_v2 (PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED) and features.live_prices (a SerpAPI key is set). The read routes always exist; the pipeline behind them (drop facts, savings rows, Deal-hunter XP, delivery rules, digest) runs only when PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED=true. Every watch object also carries pending_first_check, and drop notifications may carry extra data.drop / data.game keys, and a price_digest kind with data.digest exists; clients that don't know them ignore them.

docs.title: GET /api/notifications
docs.text:
?unread_only=false&limit=20&offset=0 → {"items": [...], "total": n, "unread": n}, newest first. An item:

{
  "id": 3, "kind": "fare_drop",
  "title": "Berlin → Lisbon dropped to $150 (−$70)",
  "body": "For 10–17 Dec · total for 1 traveller. The lowest we've seen since you started watching.",
  "data": {"watch_id": 1, "price": 150.0, "previous_price": 220.0, "delta": -70.0, "is_lowest": true,
           "departure_date": "2026-12-10", "return_date": "2026-12-17", "num_travelers": 1,
           "links": {"alerts": "/alerts?watch=1", "replan": "/alerts?watch=1&replan=1", "book": "https://www.google.com/flights#..."}},
  "created_at": "...", "read_at": null, "emailed_at": "..."
}

kind is fare_drop, fare_target, fare_low_level, fare_cheaper_date (data adds selected_price, saving, cheapest_departure_date, cheapest_return_date), watch_expired or watch_error (data action: "retry"). Price watches add hotel_drop, hotel_target, activity_drop, activity_target, trip_drop and trip_target; every price-watch notification (including its watch_expired / watch_error, whose data adds reason: failed or unavailable) has data.watch_kind and data.links.alerts = /alerts?kind=<kind>&watch=<id>, plus price, previous_price, delta, baseline_price, target_price, is_lowest, title, subtitle and links.book (the listing) for alerts. Fare-watch notifications have no watch_kind.

docs.title: GET /api/notifications/unread-count
docs.text: {"count": 2}. The header bell polls it every 60 s while the tab is visible.

docs.title: POST /api/notifications/read
docs.text: {"ids": [3, 4]} or {"all": true} → {"updated": n, "unread": n}. Only the caller's notifications change. 422 without either.

docs.title: Mobile app: push devices and Near me
docs.text: Added for the Android app. Every route needs a signed-in user and only touches that user's data. An FCM token only ever travels in a request body, never in a URL, so request and access logs never carry one; logs show at most its last 6 characters.

docs.title: POST /api/devices
docs.text:
Registers the app's FCM registration token for push alerts.

{"token": "eXaMpLe...:APA91b...", "platform": "android", "locale": "de-DE"}

token 1–4096 characters; platform only "android" (the default); locale optional (≤ 35). → 200 with the device, token masked to its last 6 characters:

{"id": 12, "token": "…Xy12Ab", "platform": "android", "locale": "de-DE",
 "created_at": "2026-11-05T09:00:00.123456+00:00", "last_seen_at": "2026-11-05T09:00:00.123456+00:00"}

Registering again refreshes locale and last_seen_at (call it on every app start and token refresh). A token registered by another user moves to the caller (a shared phone). A user keeps at most 20 devices; the least recently seen is dropped.

docs.title: GET /api/devices
docs.text: {"items": [device, ...]}, most recently seen first, tokens masked as above.

docs.title: DELETE /api/devices/{id}
docs.text: Removes one of the caller's devices by its id (for example a lost phone, from a "Your devices" list). 204; 404 {"detail": "Device not found"} when the caller has no device with that id (another user's device is never touched); 422 for a non-numeric id.

docs.title: POST /api/devices/unregister
docs.text: Sign-out: {"token": "<the full FCM token>"} → 204, always (idempotent; a token the caller doesn't own is left alone and gets the same answer). Call it before dropping the JWT.

docs.title: Push messages
docs.text:
When FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE is set (/health push_configured), every new fare- or price-watch notification is also pushed to each of the owner's devices over FCM HTTP v1, in the background as a data-only message (no notification block, so the app always builds the notification itself): Android priority high (normal for watch_expired / watch_error), and string data (the notification's title and body ride in data too):

{"kind": "fare_drop", "notification_id": "42", "link": "/alerts?watch=7", "watch_id": "7"}

link is the web deep link (data.links.alerts of the notification: /alerts?watch=<id> for fare watches, /alerts?kind=<kind>&watch=<id> for price watches); price watches add watch_kind. The notification itself is unchanged in /api/notifications. A deactivated user gets no pushes. A token is deleted only when FCM says it is dead (error code UNREGISTERED, or INVALID_ARGUMENT naming message.token); every other failure, including a bare 404 from a wrong Firebase project, keeps the token, is logged, and the notification stays in-app only.

docs.title: POST /api/nearby
docs.text:
Bucket: light_ai.

{"lat": 35.0116, "lng": 135.7681, "interests": ["temples", "food"], "limit": 8}

lat −90…90, lng −180…180, interests optional (≤ 20, each trimmed and 1–60 characters; default: the saved preferences' interests), limit 1–20 (default 8). The nearest place in the local GeoNames table (towns of 1,000+ people) within 75 km is chosen; a ward or suburb yields to a place at least 10× bigger within 15 km ("Kamigyō-ku" → Kyoto). The existing activities agent then runs for "Place, Region, Country" ("Portland, Maine, United States"; the region is left out when it repeats the name, "Kyoto, Japan") with those interests and the caller's Taste Graph. → 200:

{
  "place": {"name": "Kyoto", "region": "Kyoto", "country": "Japan", "country_code": "JP",
            "lat": 35.02107, "lng": 135.75385, "distance_km": 1.4},
  "items": [{"name": "Fushimi Inari Taisha Early Morning Hike", "category": "culture",
             "similarity_score": 0.95, "rating": 4.8, "review_count": 12000,
             "source": "getyourguide", "booking_url": "https://www.getyourguide.com/s/?q=...", "...": "..."}]
}

items are the activities agent's results, unchanged (the shape of POST /api/activities), first limit. region is the state / province (GeoNames first-level division) name, or null. distance_km is from the point to the place's centre. Results are cached for an hour per 0.05° cell (about 5 km), place, interests and taste profile. Errors: 404 {"detail": {"code": "no_place", "message": "..."}} when no known place is within 75 km; 502 {"detail": {"code": "agent_error", "message": "..."}} when the agent fails (not cached); 503 with code: ai_limit when the monthly AI spend cap has tripped.

docs.title: Near me v2: sections: true
docs.text:
{"lat": 38.72, "lng": -9.14, "limit": 6, "sections": true, "language": "en"}

Same place lookup as above, then one Gemini call grounded with Google Maps around lat/lng (language: optional BCP-47-style code such as en or pt-PT, default en; limit: per section, 1–10, default 6; interests as above, used as a hint). Without sections (or with false) the route is exactly v1, so installed apps keep working. → 200:

{
  "place": {"name": "Lisbon", "region": null, "country": "Portugal", "country_code": "PT",
            "lat": 38.72, "lng": -9.14, "distance_km": 0.4},
  "sections": [
    {"id": "see",  "title": "Places to see",  "items": []},
    {"id": "eat",  "title": "Places to eat",  "items": [
      {"name": "Time Out Market Lisboa", "summary": "One-line why, from the grounded answer",
       "maps_uri": "https://maps.google.com/?cid=…", "place_id": "ChIJ…", "category": "eat"}]},
    {"id": "shop", "title": "Places to shop", "items": []},
    {"id": "stay", "title": "Places to stay", "items": []}
  ],
  "attribution": "Google Maps",
  "sources": [{"title": "Time Out Market Lisboa", "uri": "https://maps.google.com/?cid=…"}]
}

The four sections always come in this order and may be empty. The model answers under one heading per group (## See, ## Eat, ## Shop, ## Stay) with one place per line (Name - why; split on the first dash, or on : only when there is none). A heading is a # line, a fully bold line or a bare section word; its section comes from a keyword anywhere in it (see/sight, eat/food/restaurant/drink, shop/market, stay/hotel/sleep — so ## Where to eat, ### 🍽️ Eat, ## 1. See work), and a heading naming no section, or several, stops the current one so its items are dropped rather than misfiled. Each line is matched to a Maps grounding chunk whose title matches the place's name (folded exact, or one containing the other for names of 6+ characters; chunks the line's grounding supports cite are tried first, but never taken on a support alone), and the item takes the chunk's title (without Google's " - Google Maps" suffix), uri (maps_uri) and placeId (place_id, without the places/ prefix; may be null). A place without a Maps chunk with a link is dropped, so no item is invented. sources lists every Maps chunk with a link. Each model call has a 45 s request timeout and a 50 s ceiling including the wait for the shared AI concurrency gate, with no SDK-level retries; an answer with text but no Maps chunks is retried once, then returned with empty sections. A Review of … chunk (a link to a review of the place) loses that prefix, the place's own chunk is preferred over it, and a place appears at most once. Location privacy: v2 passes the request's lat/lng to Google Maps grounding through Vertex AI (Google's retrieval config) so results are near the user; clients round them to about 100 m first. The backend never stores or logs the coordinates (request logs hold the path only, and the llm_usage line holds counts). Not cached (Google's Maps grounding terms; see Live web check and Near me). Errors: 404 no_place and 502 agent_error (the model call failed) as in v1; 422 for limit > 10 with sections: true; 503 {"detail": {"code": "ai_limit" | "ai_billing" | "grounding_unavailable", "message": "…"}} — grounding_unavailable ("Live web and map results need the Gemini provider.") when the backend runs on the Anthropic provider (v1 is unaffected).

docs.title: POST /api/live-check
docs.text:
Bucket: light_ai. Signed-in users only. "Search the web now" for one of the caller's watches: a Gemini call grounded with Google Search, built server-side from the stored watch (route, dates and travellers; hotel, dates and guests; activity, city and date; a trip's flight, hotel and activities). There is no free-text prompt: unknown fields are 422.

{"kind": "hotel", "watch_id": 123}

kind is flight (a fare watch, /api/fare-watches/{id}) or hotel / activity / trip (a price watch of that kind, /api/price-watches/{id}). → 200:

{
  "kind": "hotel",
  "watch_id": 123,
  "checked_at": "2026-11-06T18:00:00Z",
  "summary": "Plain-text answer from Gemini (grounded), unmodified.",
  "quotes": [{"label": "Booking.com, 3 nights", "amount": 412.0, "currency": "EUR", "source_index": 0}],
  "sources": [{"title": "booking.com", "uri": "https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/…"}],
  "searched_for": ["memmo alfama lisbon price 1-4 dec 2026"],
  "disclaimer": "From a live web search just now. Prices change quickly — check the provider before booking. Not used for your price alerts."
}

summary is the model's grounded text (whitespace-trimmed only). sources are the web grounding chunks with a link, once per link, as Google returns them. quotes are parsed from the answer's bullet lines (- Seller, what: EUR 412; also - **Seller:** EUR 412 and Seller:EUR 412 — the label is everything before the last colon ahead of the price). Each keeps only an amount and ISO 4217 currency copied from the text, and an unclear price gives no quote rather than a wrong one. The text is tokenised into whole numeric runs: a run counts only if it is one number in comma-thousands / dot-decimal form (1 234, 1'234, 1.234,56, 412,50 are rejected whole, never read as part of the run); no letter may touch it (5k) and no magnitude word may follow (1.5 million, 2 lakh); the currency must touch it, with at most one space, on one side only — a known ISO code (EUR 412, 412.50 EUR; TAP, NYC aren't currencies) or an unambiguous symbol (€, £, ₹, US$, C$, A$, NZ$, S$, HK$; never a bare $ or ¥); a code touching two numbers (99 EUR 2 nights) voids the line. The price must be covered by a grounding support whose chunk is one of sources (source_index): by the support's byte range when Vertex gives one (a missing start means 0), else by its text (at least 12 characters, containing the price). Anything else is left out, so quotes may be empty. searched_for are the web searches the model ran (show them as "Searched for", linking to Google Search). Nothing is written to the database, cached or used for alerts; only an llm_usage line (tokens, search-query and chunk counts, latency; never content) is logged.

Each model call has a 45 s request timeout and a 50 s ceiling including the wait for the shared AI concurrency gate, with no SDK-level retries; an answer without web sources is retried once. Errors: 404 {"detail": "Watch not found"} (not the caller's watch, or not of that kind); 409 {"detail": {"code": "watch_expired", "message": "This trip's date has passed, so there's nothing left to check."}} when the watch is expired or its date (departure; check-in / activity date / trip departure via expires_on) is more than a day in the past in UTC (before yesterday, so a date that is still today somewhere on Earth can be checked), without a model call; 429 rate limit; 502 {"detail": {"code": "live_check_failed", "message": "…"}} when the model fails or the answer still has no grounding sources; 503 {"detail": {"code": "ai_limit" | "ai_billing" | "grounding_unavailable", "message": "…"}}.

docs.title: GET /api/airports/search?q=&limit=
docs.text: Airport and place typeahead (limit 1–50, default 10). Matches airport codes, cities, names and countries, plus GeoNames places and curated hints by folded name prefix ("kyoto" → ITM, KIX; "milan" → MXP, LIN, BGY). Rows: iata_code, name, city, country, country_code. Ordering and rules: Place and Airport Data.

docs.title: GET /api/nationalities/search?q=&limit=
docs.text: Nationality typeahead over 202 seeded rows.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text: {"status": "ok", "service": "travel-planner-backend", "serpapi_configured": true|false, "fare_watch_available": true|false, "email_alerts_available": true|false, "push_configured": true|false}. No auth. The frontend reads it once per page load: serpapi_configured offers the fare calendar, fare_watch_available (SerpAPI set and FARE_WATCH_ENABLED) offers "Watch fare", email_alerts_available (SMTP_HOST set) offers "Also email me". push_configured (FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE names an existing file) tells the Android app that alerts are pushed, so it can poll less. Docker Compose uses this endpoint as the backend healthcheck.

docs.title: GET /health/agents
docs.text: A deep check: one tiny call (15 s timeout, no retries) to the configured provider, cached for 5 minutes. Reports llm (ok, empty-response, spend-cap, billing-disabled or error: <ExceptionType>), llm_provider (gemini or anthropic), llm_provider_reason (how LLM_PROVIDER resolved, e.g. auto: GCP_PROJECT set), serpapi_configured and backup_configured.

docs.title: Accounts API
docs.text: Frozen 2026-11-11. Changes are additive only; each change is listed in a Changelog section at the bottom.

docs.title: API contract (frozen at the end of wave 0)
docs.text: All paths are under /api. JSON in and out. Unless noted, auth means Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Error envelope for every new error: {"detail": "<English sentence>", "error_code": "<code>"}, plus extra keys where listed. Clients render text from error_code (web: the errors namespace) and fall back to detail. Malformed bodies keep FastAPI's default 422 {"detail": [...]}. Every 429 carries Retry-After (seconds).
  • client is optional on every endpoint that issues a session: "web" (default), "ios" or "android". Mobile clients receive a refresh_token. Optional device_name is a string of at most 64 characters.
  • locale is optional: one of en es de fr hi zh bn. It selects the email language and is stored as users.locale.
  • Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with Z. Days are YYYY-MM-DD (UTC unless stated).

docs.title: Shared objects
docs.text:
User, returned by login, /auth/me, sessions and /account. Every legacy key is kept:

{"id": "6f1c…uuid", "username": "jane_doe", "display_name": "Jane", "email": "jane@example.com",
 "email_verified": true, "is_admin": false, "requires_password_change": false,
 "account_verified": true, "has_password": true, "signup_method": "password",
 "avatar_url": "https://<base>/api/avatars/6f1c….webp?v=3"}

display_name falls back to username. avatar_url is null when there is no avatar (clients draw initials). account_verified is signup_method == "admin" or verified_at is not null. signup_method is one of admin|password|oauth.

Session:

{"access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 86400,
 "refresh_token": "rt_…", "user": User}

refresh_token is present only for client ios/android. expires_in is 86400 for web and 3600 for mobile. The JWT claims are sub (username), uid, tv, is_admin, is_first_login, iat, exp.

GameDelta. It is empty when nothing was awarded, and it is always present where listed:

{"xp": 150, "awards": [{"rule": "email_verified", "points": 50}],
 "badges": [{"id": "verified", "earned_at": "2026-11-11T10:00:00Z"}],
 "level_up": {"from": 1, "to": 2}}

When nothing was awarded: {"xp": <total>, "awards": [], "badges": [], "level_up": null}. When the game is disabled: null.

Settings. Every key is always present, and PATCH accepts any subset; unknown keys return 422:

{"language": null, "theme": "system", "currency": "USD", "units": "metric", "timezone": null,
 "hide_game": false, "hide_community": false, "profile_visibility": "public", "telemetry_opt_out": false,
 "bucket_list_goal": null}

language is one of the 7 codes or null. theme is system|light|dark. currency matches ^[A-Z]{3}$. units is metric|imperial. timezone is an IANA name that zoneinfo accepts, or null. profile_visibility is public|followers|private.

Additive (Phase 2). Settings gains bucket_list_goal: int 1..250 | null (default null; see Trips-API.md). The Phase 2 journey rules, badges and the trip_checkin streak appear in GET /game/catalog; PUT /account/onboarding with traveller_type awards traveller_type once and merges that into game.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Request 200 response Errors GET /config (additive) — — existing keys plus "auth": {"signup_mode": "open"\|"invite", "signup_available": bool, "password_reset_available": bool, "min_password_length": 10, "verify_ttl_s": 1800}, and features.accounts: true, features.game: bool — GET /auth/providers (filled in) — — {"providers": [{"id": "apple"\|"google"\|"facebook"\|"github", "configured": bool, "start_url": "/api/auth/oauth/<id>/start" \| null, "id_token": bool}]}, always in the order apple, google, facebook, github —

signup_available = email delivery available (SMTP set, or dev link logging on). password_reset_available uses the same rule. id_token is true when native ID-token sign-in is configured (Apple and Google only).

docs.title: Native accounts
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Request Success Errors POST /auth/signup — {"username", "email", "password", "display_name"?, "invite_code"?, "locale"?, "client"?} 202 {"status": "verification_sent", "email": "<as given, lower-cased>", "expires_in": 1800}. The same response when the email already belongs to an active account: that owner gets an "already registered" email instead, and nothing is created 409 username_taken, 422 username_invalid, 422 username_reserved, 422 email_invalid, 422 password_too_short, 422 password_too_long, 422 password_common, 422 password_matches_identity, 422 display_name_invalid, 403 invite_required, 403 invite_invalid, 503 email_unavailable, 429 rate_limited POST /auth/verify-email/resend — {"email", "locale"?} 202 {"status": "verification_sent"}, always (no enumeration) 429 rate_limited, 503 email_unavailable POST /auth/verify-email — {"token", "client"?, "device_name"?} 200 {"status": "verified", "session": Session \| null, "game": GameDelta}. session is set when the token activated a pending account and null when it confirmed an email on an already active account 400 token_invalid, 410 token_expired, 409 token_used, 409 email_changed (the account's email is no longer the one the token was issued for) POST /auth/password-reset/request — {"email", "locale"?} 202 {"status": "reset_sent"}, always 429 rate_limited, 503 email_unavailable POST /auth/password-reset/confirm — {"token", "new_password", "client"?, "device_name"?} 200 {"status": "password_reset", "session": Session}. It bumps token_version and revokes every refresh token. A pending account becomes active and verified (the email is proven) 400 token_invalid, 410 token_expired, 409 token_used, the password errors above POST /account/email/verify yes {"locale"?} 202 {"status": "verification_sent", "email": "…", "expires_in": 1800} 409 already_verified, 422 no_email, 503 email_unavailable, 429 rate_limited

Username rule: lower-cased, then ^[a-z0-9_]{3,20}$, not in RESERVED_USERNAMES (Task 2), and unique case-insensitively against every existing username. Email: the existing _EMAIL_RE, lower-cased, ≤ 254. display_name: NFC, stripped, 1–50 characters, no control characters. Tokens expire 30 minutes after issue and are single use. Issuing a new token of the same purpose invalidates the previous ones. Emails go to <base>/verify?token=… and <base>/reset-password?token=….

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Request Success Errors POST /auth/login (additive) — {"username", "password", "client"?, "device_name"?}. username may also be the account's email 200 Session, with the legacy keys kept: user.username, user.is_admin, user.requires_password_change, user.email 401 (unchanged text) for bad credentials, 403 {"error_code": "account_pending", "email_hint": "j•••@example.com"} only when the password was right, 429 POST /auth/refresh — {"refresh_token"} 200 {"access_token", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "rt_…"}, rotated 401 refresh_stale (an already-rotated token reused ≤ 30 s after rotation; the family is kept), 401 refresh_invalid (unknown, expired, revoked, user inactive, or reused after the grace window, which revokes the family), 429 POST /auth/logout optional {"refresh_token"?} 204, and revokes that refresh token's family — POST /auth/logout-all yes — 204; bumps token_version and revokes every refresh token — GET /auth/sessions (additive, 2026-11-12) yes optional header X-Refresh-Token: rt_… (never logged) 200 {"sessions": [{"id", "client", "device_name", "created_at", "last_used_at", "current"}]}: the caller's live refresh-token families (one per mobile sign-in; web logins have none), most recently used first. id is the family id and stays the same across refreshes. current is true for the family the X-Refresh-Token belongs to. Revoked and expired families are not listed. Bucket account 401, 429 DELETE /auth/sessions/{id} (additive, 2026-11-12) yes — 204, revokes that whole family (its next refresh answers 401 refresh_invalid) 404 session_not_found (unknown, already revoked, or another user's), 429 POST /auth/change-password (additive) yes {"current_password", "new_password", "client"?}. current_password may be "" when has_password is false 200 {"access_token", "token_type", "expires_in"}, plus refresh_token for mobile. Bumps token_version, revokes every refresh token, and the new token keeps this session alive 400 "Current password is incorrect" (unchanged), the password errors above as 400 with error_code GET /auth/me (additive) yes — User 401 session_revoked when tv is stale PUT /auth/email (additive) yes unchanged {"email", "email_verified": false, "verification_sent": bool}. A changed email starts unverified, and a link is sent when email is available unchanged

Any authenticated route answers 401 {"error_code": "session_revoked"} when the JWT's tv ≠ users.token_version.

docs.title: OAuth
docs.text:
<p> is one of apple, google, facebook, github.

Method, path Auth Request Success Errors GET /auth/oauth/<p>/start — (browser navigation) query client=web\|ios\|android, return_to=/path (web; same-origin path, default /), challenge=<b64url S256> (required for ios/android), redirect_uri=<allow-listed> (ios/android; default <base>/auth/callback), link=<ticket> (optional) 302 to the provider. Sets the cookie tp_oauth=<binding> (HttpOnly, Path /api/auth/oauth, Max-Age 600, SameSite=None; Secure on https, else Lax) Unknown <p>: 404. Not configured, bad return_to, missing challenge or bad redirect_uri: 302 to <final>?error=<code> GET/POST /auth/oauth/<p>/callback — (provider redirect; Apple uses POST form_post) the provider's code, state, error, Apple's user 302 to <final>?code=<handoff> 302 to <final>?error=<code> POST /auth/oauth/exchange — (web also sends the tp_oauth cookie) {"code", "verifier"?, "device_name"?} (the client type is the one given at start) one of the three results below 400 code_invalid (unknown, expired, used, or the cookie/verifier doesn't match) POST /auth/oauth/complete — {"signup_token", "username", "display_name"?, "invite_code"?, "client"?, "device_name"?, "locale"?} 201 {"status": "signed_in", "session": Session, "game": GameDelta} 400 signup_token_invalid, 409 username_taken, 422 username_invalid, 422 username_reserved, 403 invite_required, 403 invite_invalid POST /auth/oauth/link-ticket yes {"provider", "client"?} 200 {"start_url": "/api/auth/oauth/<p>/start?link=<ticket>&client=web"} (the ticket lasts 5 min and is single use) 404 provider_unknown, 409 provider_unavailable POST /auth/oauth/<p>/id-token (apple, google) — {"id_token", "nonce"?, "authorization_code"? (apple), "display_name"?, "client": "ios"\|"android", "device_name"?} the same results as exchange 404 when native is not configured for <p>, 400 id_token_invalid DELETE /account/identities/<p> yes — 204 404 identity_not_found, 409 last_sign_in_method

<final> is <base>/auth/callback for web, or the client's redirect_uri for mobile. redirect_uri must exactly match one entry of OAUTH_MOBILE_REDIRECTS (default ["voyager://auth/callback", "<base>/auth/callback"]). Callback error codes: cancelled, state_invalid, provider_error, provider_unavailable, email_in_use_unverified, identity_in_use, account_inactive, bad_request. The handoff code lasts 120 s and is single use. Web exchange needs the tp_oauth cookie whose hash was stored at start. Mobile exchange needs verifier, with b64url(sha256(verifier)) == challenge.

Exchange / id-token results:

{"status": "signed_in", "session": Session, "game": GameDelta, "return_to": "/"}
{"status": "needs_username", "signup_token": "…", "suggested_username": "jane", "display_name": "Jane Doe",
 "email": "jane@example.com", "invite_required": false, "return_to": "/"}
{"status": "linked", "provider": "github", "return_to": "/account"}

signup_token lasts 30 min. email is null when the provider gave none.
