docs.title: Mobile flow
docs.text: All examples use client: "ios"; Android is identical with "android". Mobile sessions carry a refresh_token and a 3600 s access token. Store the refresh token in the Keychain / Android Keystore-backed storage, never in plain preferences.

docs.title: 1. Native sign-up and email verification
docs.text:
POST /api/auth/signup
{"username": "jane_doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "password": "correct horse battery", "locale": "en", "client": "ios"}

202 {"status": "verification_sent", "email": "jane@example.com", "expires_in": 1800}

The account stays pending until the email is confirmed. The email links to the universal link / app link <base>/verify?token=…. Register /verify (and /reset-password) as associated domains so the app opens instead of the browser. The app reads token from the URL and calls:

POST /api/auth/verify-email
{"token": "<token from the link>", "client": "ios", "device_name": "Jane's iPhone"}

200 {"status": "verified", "session": {"access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600,
     "refresh_token": "rt_…", "user": {…}}, "game": {"xp": 50, "awards": […], "badges": […], "level_up": null}}

session is null when the token only confirmed an email on an already active account; show a confirmation and keep the current session. On 410 token_expired offer POST /auth/verify-email/resend. Until verified, login answers 403 account_pending (with email_hint) and the AI routes answer 403 email_unverified.

docs.title: 2. Login
docs.text:
POST /api/auth/login
{"username": "jane_doe", "password": "correct horse battery", "client": "ios", "device_name": "Jane's iPhone"}

200 {"access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "rt_…", "user": {…}}

docs.title: 3. OAuth with the system browser
docs.text:
Use ASWebAuthenticationSession on iOS and Custom Tabs on Android.

  1. Generate a random verifier (43 to 128 URL-safe characters, per RFC 7636) and keep it in memory. Compute challenge = base64url(sha256(verifier)) without padding.
  2. Open the system browser at: <base>/api/auth/oauth/github/start?client=ios&challenge=<challenge>&redirect_uri=voyager%3A%2F%2Fauth%2Fcallback redirect_uri must exactly match an allow-listed entry (default voyager://auth/callback or <base>/auth/callback).
  3. The provider flow ends with a redirect to voyager://auth/callback?code=<handoff> (or ?error=<code>, for example cancelled). The handoff code lasts 120 s and is single use.
  4. Exchange it:
POST /api/auth/oauth/exchange
{"code": "<handoff>", "verifier": "<verifier>", "device_name": "Jane's iPhone"}

Handle the three results:

  • {"status": "signed_in", "session": {…}, "game": {…}, "return_to": "/"}: store the session.
  • {"status": "needs_username", "signup_token": "…", "suggested_username": "jane", …}: ask for a username, then POST /auth/oauth/complete with {"signup_token", "username", "client": "ios", "device_name"} which returns 201 {"status": "signed_in", "session": {…}, "game": {…}}.
  • {"status": "linked", …}: returned only for linking, which is started from a signed-in session with a link ticket (the contract example uses client=web).

400 code_invalid means the code expired, was used, or the verifier does not match; restart from step 1.

For Apple and Google, native ID-token sign-in skips the browser when GET /auth/providers reports "id_token": true:

POST /api/auth/oauth/apple/id-token
{"id_token": "<jwt>", "nonce": "<raw nonce>", "authorization_code": "<apple code>", "client": "ios", "device_name": "Jane's iPhone"}

The result is one of the same three shapes as the exchange.

docs.title: 4. Calling the API and refreshing (single flight)
docs.text:
Send Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. When a call answers 401 (expired access token) or 401 session_revoked, refresh. Run at most one refresh at a time: the first request that needs a refresh starts it, and every other request that gets a 401 meanwhile waits for that same refresh to finish, then retries with the new access token.

POST /api/auth/refresh
{"refresh_token": "rt_old"}

200 {"access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "rt_new"}

Refresh tokens rotate: persist rt_new immediately and discard rt_old. Failure handling:

  • 401 refresh_stale: the old token was already rotated at most 30 s ago (for example a second process, or a response lost in transit). The family is still valid. Re-read the newest stored refresh token and retry the refresh once with it. If that also fails, treat it as refresh_invalid.
  • 401 refresh_invalid: the token is unknown, expired, revoked, the user is inactive, or it was reused after the grace window (which revokes the family). Clear stored tokens and sign the user out.
  • 429: wait Retry-After seconds, then retry. Do not sign out.

On 401 session_revoked, try one refresh; if the refresh fails, sign out.

docs.title: 5. Sign out
docs.text:
POST /api/auth/logout
{"refresh_token": "rt_new"}

204

This revokes that refresh token's family. Clear local tokens regardless of the response. POST /auth/logout-all (authenticated) revokes every device.

docs.title: Contract notes
docs.text:
Clarifications of behaviour the frozen contract left implicit. None changes a request or response shape.

  • Off-site return_to. On GET /auth/oauth/<p>/start, a return_to that is not a same-origin path (an absolute URL, a //host form, or anything not starting with a single /) is refused like any other bad start parameter: 302 to <final>?error=bad_request. It is never followed.
  • Apple native secret. For Apple the server stores the refresh token it needs to revoke on account deletion as "<client_id>|<refresh_token>", Fernet-encrypted (see Global constraints). This is internal storage: no request or response field changes.
  • Unverified or untrusted provider email. A provider email that is unverified, or verified but not trusted (Facebook, unless FACEBOOK_EMAIL_TRUSTED=true), never deletes and never links to an existing account. If it matches an existing account that has no verified email (for example an admin-created one), the callback answers email_in_use_unverified. Only a pending native account is replaced, and only by a trusted, verified provider email.
  • Password reset goes only to a proven address. POST /auth/password-reset/request sends a link only when the address is the account's verified email, or the account is pending (a reset then activates and verifies it, as above). For an active account's unverified email it sends nothing and answers the same 202, so POST /auth/password-reset/confirm never marks an active account's unverified email verified.
  • Sign-up needs the operator's opt-in. signup_available is true only when email delivery is available and the server sets SIGNUP_ENABLED=true; otherwise POST /auth/signup answers 503 email_unavailable. OAuth sign-up is not gated by it.
  • An untrusted provider email is not the account's email until confirmed. After an OAuth sign-up whose provider email is unverified or untrusted, User.email is null and email_verified false; the verify link goes to the provider address, and redeeming it sets email (and email_verified: true) unless another account holds that address by then (409 email_changed). needs_username.email still shows the provider address. While email is null, POST /account/email/verify re-sends the link to that pending address (email in the 202 is that address); it answers 422 no_email only when there is no pending address.

docs.title: Agent System
docs.text: How agents are defined and executed, what each one does, and how static data and verification wrap around them.

docs.title: Agent definitions
docs.text:
Each agent's system prompt lives in .agents/<name>.md at the repo root: YAML frontmatter with name and description, followed by the prompt body.

---
name: flights
description: Expert flight search specialist — finds available round-trip flights ...
---

You are a flight search specialist...

backend/app/agents/loader.py reads the file into an AgentDefinition(name, description, system_prompt). The directory comes from AGENTS_DIR (default <repo>/.agents). Changing an agent's behaviour usually means editing its prompt; the Python class builds the user prompt and post-processes the JSON.

There are 22 definition files:

.agents file Python class (backend/app/agents/) Used by flights.md flights_agent.py search, /flights, compare, chat fallback weather.md weather_agent.py search, compare hotels.md hotels_agent.py search, /hotels, compare, chat activities.md activities_agent.py search, /activities, chat places.md places_agent.py search (places_to_see) walking_tours.md walking_tours_agent.py search, /walking-tours events.md events_agent.py search, /events, chat warnings visa.md visa_agent.py search, /visa, compare, chat sim.md sim_agent.py search, /sim, chat tips.md tips_agent.py search, /tips, chat emergency_card.md emergency_card_agent.py search getting-around.md getting_around_agent.py search, /getting-around, chat forex.md forex_agent.py search, /forex packing_list.md packing_list_agent.py search (deferred) pricing_advisor.md pricing_advisor_agent.py search (deferred) itinerary.md itinerary_agent.py search Phase 2, /itinerary stress_test.md stress_test_agent.py search (after the itinerary), /stress-test discovery.md discovery_agent.py /discover layover.md layover_agent.py /layover chat.md chat_agent.py /chat chat-itinerary.md chat_itinerary_agent.py chat comprehensive planning orchestrator.md none Descriptive only; the orchestrator is the Python TravelOrchestrator

docs.title: Execution: BaseAgent
docs.text:
backend/app/agents/base_agent.py:

  • One API call per attempt. execute(prompt) calls core.llm.generate with role agent (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite on Gemini, Claude Haiku 4.5 on Anthropic; see Architecture), max_tokens 16384, JSON output, the definition's prompt as the system prompt (plus "Return ONLY valid JSON") and the agent's prompt as the single user message (text, or text and image blocks for vision). No tools are passed to the model.
  • Concurrency. A global semaphore limits concurrent calls to AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 6), so a burst of agents does not trip the organisation's rate limits. The SDK client also retries 429/5xx 3 times on its own.
  • Retries. Up to 4 attempts. Rate-limit, overload and connection errors back off min(2^n, 10) seconds; other errors back off 2n seconds.
  • Token cap. If a response stops at max_tokens, the next attempt adds a "be compact" instruction instead of repeating the same request.
  • JSON parsing (_parse_json), three strategies: parse the whole text, extract a fenced code block, then take the outermost {...}.
  • Failure. After the last attempt the agent returns {"error": "..."} rather than raising. When the monthly AI spend cap has tripped it returns {"error": "AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st.", "error_code": "ai_limit"} at once, without retrying.

ToolAgent (a BaseAgent subclass) adds enrich(data), which the orchestrator runs in the background after the first result has streamed; a changed result is streamed again. Flights (LLM results only), hotels, activities, places, visa, sim, tips, getting around and forex override it to look up real links (DuckDuckGo through web_tools.py, at most 4 concurrent searches; Serper as a second tier for activities and places when SERPER_KEY is set). Only hotels, activities and places_to_see mark their first yield as verification-pending.

Every specialist subclass overrides run(request) to build its user prompt and post-process the result. No agent has its own API plumbing.

docs.title: The specialists
docs.text:
Flights. With SERPAPI_KEY, live Google Flights results via SerpAPI (services/serp_flights.py), marked live_fare; single-city results may carry Google's price_insights. Multi-city trips search one leg at a time (see Multi-City Trips). Without a key, or for legs SerpAPI cannot serve, the LLM produces estimates.

Weather. Open-Meteo forecast when the trip starts within 16 days and the city has coordinates (utils/geo.py), otherwise an LLM seasonal estimate. Multi-city trips get a forecast per stay.

Hotels. Options across budget tiers (luxury, premium, mid-range, budget); links are searched and checked during enrichment.

Activities. Activities matched to the traveller's interests. The model itself assigns each activity a relevance similarity_score; there is no embedding model in the code base.

Places to See. Landmarks and sights. With SERPER_KEY, Google Places data from Serper is passed to the model; otherwise the model works alone.

Free Walking Tours. services/walking_tours.py crawls the public city pages of GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, FreeWalkingTour.com and SANDEMANs NewEurope (free and pay-what-you-wish tours only; cached per provider and city). The LLM only picks and explains tours by candidate id, so every URL comes from the crawl. Each city is topped up to at least min(4, available) tours; if the LLM fails, a rating-and-reviews ranking is used.

Events (What's On). Festivals, concerts and markets during the dates. A ~ on a date marks a typical-season estimate.

Visa, SIM, Tips, Getting Around, Forex. Static-backed (see below). Forex runs several DuckDuckGo searches for current rates in parallel and has the model extract them.

Emergency Card. Per-city police, ambulance and fire numbers, the traveller's embassy (skipped for home-country cities), hospitals, survival phrases and local laws. The frontend can print it.

Packing List (deferred). Starts when activities and weather are both in; a template list is used after 120 s or on error.

Pricing Advisor (deferred). Starts once flights have at least 3 results; gives booking-timing advice and the data for the sparkline in the Flights section. Skipped after 120 s or on error.

Itinerary. Day-by-day plan with morning, afternoon and evening slots, each with duration_hours and lat/lng, which the frontend uses to derive estimated times. Template fallback after 60 s.

Stress Test. Audits the final itinerary against flights, visa and weather: pacing, timings, visa deadlines, weather clashes. Also callable with an edited itinerary through POST /api/stress-test (the "Re-check" button).

Discovery. Powers Surprise me (POST /api/discover): five destinations with cost range, weather, visa type, flight time and match reasons. The visa type is replaced by the static visa table when it has an entry; otherwise it is shown as unverified. 30 s timeout (504), cached.

Layover. A mini-plan for a long connection (POST /api/layover, up to 48 h).

Chat and Chat-Itinerary. See Chat Assistant.

docs.title: Static data and fallbacks
docs.text:
backend/app/agents/static_results.py holds curated tables:

Table Entries Feeds _VISA_TABLE 34 (nationality, destination) pairs Phase 0 visa, visa verification, discovery and compare visa _DESTINATION_SCORES 49 Travel Ease grade (get_confidence_score), daily cost _EMERGENCY_NUMBERS 40 Phase 0 emergency card, emergency verification _CITY_TO_COUNTRY 204 Matching a destination to a table country _GLOBAL_ESIMS / _LOCAL_SIMS 4 / 10 countries Phase 0 SIM _UNIVERSAL_TIPS / _DESTINATION_TIPS universal + 6 countries Phase 0 tips _GETTING_AROUND_TABLE 13 Phase 0 getting around _FOREX_TABLE, _DEST_CURRENCY, _NATIONALITY_TO_CURRENCY 6, 52, 37 Phase 0 forex

Six agents are static-backed: visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex and emergency_card. Phase 0 sends their static result; Phase 1 replaces it with the AI result; if the AI fails, the error is suppressed and the static data stays. Phase 0 also sends a confidence event with the Travel Ease grade.

Matching a destination to a table country (_place_country) uses whole names only, never substrings. A stated country wins. Otherwise the city map is used, including St/Saint variants and city aliases, and checked against a stated region or ISO code ("Miami, FL", "Perth, WA", "Berlin, DE", "Cartagena, ES" → Spain). A city not in the map falls back to the GeoNames place resolver ("Zermatt" → Switzerland), then to unique region names or codes, then to "City Country" written without a comma.

docs.title: Source verification
docs.text:
The orchestrator attaches data.verification to every non-error section just before yielding it (attach_verification in backend/app/services/verification.py); the filtered endpoints attach the same final label. The function is pure: it uses only evidence already in the data and never calls the network or an LLM. The object never contains an error key, so it cannot trip the cache's error guard.

Section Evidence Rule flights live_fare on options mapped from SerpAPI (never trusted from LLM output) all live → verified; some → partial; none → unverified hotels link_verified from enrichment: a search result whose title or path contains the hotel's distinctive name words counted over the hotels actually searched activities, places_to_see link_checked on every item the resolvers searched; link_verified when a trusted result's title contains the item's distinctive name words "1 of the 5 checked were found online by name" walking_tours crawl provenance verified weather source: "open-meteo" verified; LLM estimates unverified visa compared with the static visa table match → verified; different visa type → conflict; no entry → unverified emergency_card compared with the static emergency numbers verified only when at least 2 of police/ambulance/fire were compared and all matched; any mismatch → conflict sim, tips, getting_around, forex (Phase 0 yields) curated reference data verified everything else (AI yields of the above, itinerary, stress test, packing list, pricing advisor) none unverified

Name matching (services/name_match.py) drops destination words and generic words ("hotel", "tour", "museum", …) first, so "Berlin City Tour" is not evidence for a "Top Berlin Tours" page. The first, pre-enrichment yield of hotels, activities and places is pending: true; the frontend clears a still-pending label when the stream ends. Model-supplied link_verified and link_checked flags are stripped, and saved plans drop them.

docs.title: Adding an agent
docs.text:
1. Create .agents/<name>.md with name and description frontmatter and the system prompt.
  2. Create backend/app/agents/<name>_agent.py: subclass BaseAgent (or ToolAgent if it needs link enrichment), load the definition, and implement run(request).
  3. Wire it into TravelOrchestrator (backend/app/agents/orchestrator.py) in the right phase, and add a route under backend/app/api/routes/ if it should be callable alone (add the light_ai rate-limit dependency in main.py).
  4. If the section should be labelled, add a rule to verify_section in services/verification.py; otherwise it is "AI-generated".
  5. Frontend: add the event type to AGENT_ORDER / the agent config in frontend/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx and write the section component.
  6. Add tests under backend/tests/ (the agent classes are excluded from coverage, so test the parsing and orchestration paths directly).

docs.title: Alerts API
docs.text:
Frozen with Phase 3 wave 0. Changes: later changes are additive only (new fields, endpoints or error codes; nothing renamed, removed or re-typed). Every change needs a contract-change note in its PR and an update to this page in the same PR.

Price alerts 2.0 adds a price story for each watch, a drop moment on real drops, a savings tally, one-tap watches, suggestions, a weekly digest and delivery controls (quiet hours, caps, grouping). It is additive to /api/fare-watches*, /api/price-watches* and /api/notifications*, which keep their request fields, response keys and semantics.

docs.title: API contract
docs.text: All paths are under /api, with JSON in and out. Every route needs Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and acts only on the caller's watches: another user's watch answers 404 watch_not_found. Errors use the Phase 1 envelope {"detail", "error_code"}, and timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with Z. kind is one of flight | hotel | activity | trip. flight means a fare_watches row, and the other kinds are price_watches rows.

docs.title: Discovery (additive)
docs.text: GET /config gains features.alerts_api: 2 (the routes below exist), features.price_alerts_v2: bool (PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED) and features.live_prices: bool (a SerpAPI key is configured).

docs.title: Shared objects
docs.text:
Money: {"amount": 412.0, "currency": "USD"}.

PriceStory:

{"kind": "flight", "watch_id": 7, "currency": "USD", "mode": "below_target", "target": 380.0,
 "points": [{"at": "…Z", "price": 455.0}], "baseline": 455.0,
 "latest": {"at": "…Z", "price": 412.0}, "lowest": {"at": "…Z", "price": 398.0},
 "typical": {"low": 390.0, "high": 520.0, "source": "google"},
 "verdict": "good", "advice": {"code": "near_target", "params": {"gap": 32.0}},
 "checked_at": "…Z", "checked_days_ago": 0, "next_check_at": "…Z", "pending_first_check": false,
 "estimate": null, "caught": 57.0, "live_prices": true}
  • points: observed prices only, oldest first, at most 90 (the newest).
  • typical: for flights, Google's google_typical_low/high (source: "google"), and null when Google gave none. For other kinds, when there are at least 6 points, the nearest-rank p25 and p75 of the points (source: "history"), otherwise null. Nearest rank: sort the n prices, then p25 = sorted[ceil(0.25 n) - 1] and p75 = sorted[ceil(0.75 n) - 1].
  • verdict, for the latest price p and typical [lo, hi]: p < lo is great; p <= lo + 0.25 (hi - lo) is good; p <= hi is typical; otherwise high. It is null without typical or latest, and null when checked_days_ago > 3 and live_prices is false. A stale no-key story still shows typical.
  • estimate: {"price", "source"} for a frozen estimate (labelled "estimate"), else null. An estimate is never a point, never latest, and never changes the verdict.
  • caught: the watch's saving as defined under Savings, or null.
  • advice.code: the first rule that matches, in this order:
# Code (params) Matches when 1 pending there is no observed point yet (including a watch that holds only an estimate) 2 checks_paused {days} live_prices is false and checked_days_ago > 3; days is checked_days_ago 3 below_target {by} a target is set and latest <= target; by = target - latest 4 near_target {gap} a target is set and latest - target <= the kind's step evaluated at the target (price_rules: flight and hotel max($15, 5 %), activity max(1, 5 %), trip max($25, 4 %)); gap = latest - target 5 at_lowest latest == lowest and there are at least 3 points 6 below_typical, within_typical, above_typical the verdict is great or good, typical, or high 7 steady {days} at least 5 points and the last 5 are within 1 % of each other (max - min <= 0.01 min); days is the whole days from the 5th-newest point to the newest 8 few_checks {n} otherwise; n is the number of points

Golden cases: backend/tests/fixtures/alerts/story_cases.json, shared by every client (see Golden cases).

Savings:

{"total_usd": 245.0, "by_currency": {"EUR": 12.0}, "drops_caught": 4, "targets_hit": 1,
 "watches_active": 6, "best": {"kind": "hotel", "watch_id": 3, "title": "…", "caught": 120.0, "currency": "USD"},
 "milestones": [50, 200, 1000], "next_milestone": 1000, "progress_pct": 24, "since": "…Z"}
  • A watch's caught amount = max(0, baseline - the lowest alerted observed price), taken from alert_savings rows. Repeat alerts on one watch count once, through their lowest price. Estimate rows (observed: false) are ignored everywhere. A watch is identified by (kind, watch_id), so a flight 1 and a hotel 1 are two watches.
  • Watches are summed: USD watches into total_usd, other currencies into by_currency (only amounts above 0, rounded to 2 decimals). Nothing is ever converted.
  • drops_caught = the number of watches with caught > 0. targets_hit = the number of those with at least one target_hit alert.
  • best = the watch with the largest caught, USD watches first (a non-USD watch is best only when no USD watch has a saving), ties to the lower watch_id; null when no watch has a saving.
  • next_milestone = the smallest milestone strictly above total_usd (so a total of exactly 50 has passed 50), and null once $1,000 is reached. progress_pct = floor(100 * total_usd / next_milestone), and 100 when next_milestone is null.
  • Deleted watches still count. since is the time of the first counted row (the earliest observed row, estimate rows excluded), null with none. watches_active is the count of the caller's active watches, from the watch stores, not from the rows.
  • Wording: always "caught a drop of $X", never "you saved" (the app cannot know whether the user booked).

Golden cases: savings_cases.json.

AlertPrefs:

{"digest_weekly": false, "digest_push": false, "digest_day": 1, "instant": "all",
 "quiet_hours": {"enabled": true, "start": "22:00", "end": "07:00"},
 "daily_cap": {"flight": 3, "hotel": 3, "activity": 3, "trip": 3}, "group_window_min": 15,
 "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata", "quiet_hours_active": true}
  • digest_weekly is the opt-in for the weekly digest (in-app and email). digest_push (bool, default false) additionally sends the digest as a push; it has no effect while digest_weekly is false.
  • digest_day is an ISO weekday (1 = Monday).
  • instant is all or targets_only. With targets_only, only target hits push or email, and everything else waits for the digest.
  • Caps run from 1 to 10 and group_window_min from 0 to 120. start and end are HH:MM.
  • timezone is read-only here, a mirror of the account setting (null when unset). Without a usable timezone, quiet hours are not applied, and quiet_hours_active is false. It is also false when quiet hours are disabled (enabled: false, or start == end).

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /alerts/summary none Savings none GET /alerts/watches/{kind}/{id}/story none PriceStory 404 watch_not_found, 422 kind_invalid POST /alerts/watches/{kind}/{id}/advice none {"tip": "…", "source": "ai", "generated_at": "…Z", "cached": bool}. Uses the pricing-advisor agent with the stored history (no SerpAPI) and is cached 24 h per watch. The light_ai bucket and the AI gate apply 422 advice_unsupported (not flight), 503 ai_limit, 404 POST /alerts/quick-watch {"kind", "title": 1..120, "subtitle"?: <=160, "spec": {…}, "plan_id"?: int, "surface": "results"\|"chat"\|"trip"\|"suggest"}. A flight spec holds the POST /fare-watches trip fields. The other kinds hold their POST /price-watches spec 201 {"kind", "watch": Watch, "existing": false}. The watch is pending: alert_mode: any_drop, email off, no live look, first check queued. A match of an existing active watch answers 200 with "existing": true 503 live_prices_off, 409 watch_limit (the shared active limit, with the existing message), 422 spec_invalid GET /alerts/suggestions?plan_id= none {"suggestions": [{"kind", "title", "subtitle", "spec", "reason": "selected_in_plan"\|"trip_total"\|"departure_soon", "already_watching": bool}], "live_prices": bool}, at most 5, built locally; in the order flight, hotels (≤ 2), activities (≤ 2), trip, so a full plan fills the cap and the trip total is dropped 404 trip_not_found GET /alerts/preferences none AlertPrefs none PUT /alerts/preferences any subset of the writable AlertPrefs keys (everything except timezone and quiet_hours_active) AlertPrefs 422 alert_prefs_invalid GET /alerts/digest/unsubscribe?token= and POST none HTML page (the same pattern as the watch unsubscribe pages); sets digest_weekly=false none

Additive clarifications (Task 4).

  • POST /alerts/watches/{kind}/{id}/advice can also answer 502 advice_failed (the advisor returned nothing usable; retry later), 503 ai_billing (AI billing is off, like ai_limit) and 422 advice_no_data (the flight watch has no observed price yet, so no model call is made). Clients translate all three codes.
  • A story's target and the below_target / near_target advice use the watch's target only when mode is below_target; in any_drop mode target is null even if a stale target price is stored.

Watch objects (additive). Every watch from /fare-watches* and /price-watches* gains pending_first_check: bool. A pending watch has last_price: null.

Notifications (additive).

  • A drop notification's data gains drop: {"from", "to", "amount", "pct", "currency", "target_hit": bool, "observed": true} and game: GameDelta | null.
  • A price-drop, watch_expired or watch_error notification's data may carry i18n: {"title", "body"}, a structured spec the server renders in the user's language for push, email and the digest. title and body stay English; clients can ignore i18n.
  • The new kind price_digest has the usual title and body plus data.digest: {"week": "2026-W46", "watches": [{"kind", "watch_id", "title", "latest", "change_7d", "lowest", "checked_at"}], "savings": Savings}.
  • A grouped push carries data.group_count (a string).

GameDelta is exactly as in Accounts API.

docs.title: Delivery rules (push and email only)
docs.text:
The in-app notification row is always written. For each new notification, in order:

  1. expired and error notes are delivered as today.
  2. instant = targets_only and not target_hit: no push or email.
  3. The category's sent count today (the user's local day) >= daily_cap[kind]: no push or email.
  4. Local time in quiet hours ([start, end), wrapping midnight; start == end means disabled; skipped without a timezone): due at the next local end.
  5. Otherwise due now. If a push for this user went out less than group_window_min ago, the item is held until that window ends and is sent then as one push covering every item held for that user ("3 prices dropped").

Email keeps the per-watch email_enabled opt-in and follows rules 1 to 4, never grouping.

Quiet-hours details (rule 4). The local time of day is HH:MM in the user's timezone. A window with start < end holds when start <= t < end. A window with start > end wraps midnight and holds when t >= start or t < end. The end is exclusive: at exactly end the item is due now. The due time is the next wall-clock end in the local zone, converted to UTC, so a DST change between now and then is honoured (7:00 after a spring-forward night is one hour earlier in UTC than the night before). An unknown timezone name is treated like no timezone.

Golden cases: quiet_hours_cases.json.

docs.title: Golden cases
docs.text:
backend/tests/fixtures/alerts/{story_cases,savings_cases,quiet_hours_cases}.json. Each file is a list of {"name", "input", "expected"} with unique names. Every backend implementation and every client must pass them.

  • story_cases.json: input is {"kind", "currency", "target", "points": [{"days_ago", "price"}] (oldest first), "google_typical": [lo, hi] | null, "live_prices", "checked_days_ago": int | null, "pending_first_check", "estimate"}. expected is {"typical", "verdict", "advice": {"code", "params"}, "lowest", "latest"} (lowest and latest are prices, or null without points). Numbers compare by value (2 equals 2.0).
  • savings_cases.json: input is {"rows": [{"kind", "watch_id", "title", "currency", "baseline", "alerted_price", "notification_id", "at", "target_hit", "observed", "watch_deleted"}], "watches_active"}. expected is the full Savings object.
  • quiet_hours_cases.json: input is {"now_utc", "timezone": string | null, "quiet_hours": {"enabled", "start", "end"}}. expected is {"deliver": "now" | "held", "due_utc"}; due_utc equals now_utc when deliver is now.

docs.title: Client notes
docs.text:
• Feature detection. Read features.alerts_api from GET /config. Without it (an older backend) render today's Alerts page and no v2 control. v2 controls show when features.price_alerts_v2 is true, or features.alerts_api === 2 and the browser has localStorage.tp_alerts2 = "1". Never assume a route exists without the flag.
  • No live prices. When features.live_prices is false there is no one-tap watch button and no suggestions sheet (quick-watch answers 503 live_prices_off). Stories, savings and the digest still work from stored data.
  • "Checked N days ago". Every price is shown with its age from checked_days_ago (and checked_at). Never present a stale price as current. With advice.code = checks_paused, say live checks are paused. Never say "great price now".
  • Codes to translate. advice.code (with params), verdict, suggestions[].reason, and the error codes watch_not_found, kind_invalid, advice_unsupported, ai_limit, live_prices_off, watch_limit, spec_invalid, trip_not_found and alert_prefs_invalid. The server sends codes and numbers, never English advice text. Format amounts, dates and "N days ago" with the locale.
  • No live calls from clients. Clients never call SerpAPI or any price source. Every number comes from these routes.
  • Estimates and currencies. An estimate is labelled "estimate" and never counts as a price, a saving or XP. Never convert currencies: show total_usd and list by_currency separately.
  • Old data. Pending watches (last_price: null), price_digest notifications and drop data with extra keys must not break a client that does not know them.

docs.title: Fake SerpAPI (tests, dev, E2E)
docs.text:
The real SerpAPI is never used in tests, dev or E2E (the Free Plan has 250 searches a month). backend/scripts/fake_serpapi.py serves /search.json from backend/tests/fixtures/serpapi/, routed by engine:

engine Fixture google_flights flights/outbound.json, or flights/return_leg.json when departure_token is given google_hotels hotels/city_search_lisbon.json, or hotels/property_details_browns.json when property_token is given google activities/gyg_belem_tower_recheck.json 
cd backend
python -m scripts.fake_serpapi --port 8765 [--drop-after N]
curl http://127.0.0.1:8765/__calls        # {"total": 3, "by_engine": {"google_flights": 3}}

With --drop-after N, every search after the first N serves prices 12 % lower (so an end-to-end run sees a real drop). To run the backend against it, use the launcher, which patches serp_flights.SERP_URL, serp_flights._SERP_URL, hotel_prices.SERP_URL, activity_prices.SERP_URL and activity_url_resolver._SERPAPI_URL before importing app.main:

SERPAPI_KEY=fake FAKE_SERPAPI_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/search.json \
  python -m scripts.run_with_fake_serpapi --port 8001

The key is a dummy. The fake never reads, stores or logs the query.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: How Travel Planner fits together, from a submitted search to the last section on screen.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Browser (React 18 SPA, Vite)
  ├── sseWorker.js  ── POST /api/search  (SSE)
  ├── chatWorker.js ── POST /api/chat    (SSE)
  └── axios         ── everything else  (JSON)
Android app (separate repo) ── the same JSON / SSE API with a Bearer token,
                               plus /api/devices (push) and /api/nearby (Near me)
            │
            ▼
FastAPI backend (uvicorn, one process)
  ├── middleware: CORS, request logging, X-Request-ID
  ├── routers: one per domain, rate-limit dependency on AI routes
  ├── TravelOrchestrator ── Phase 0 static tables
  │                       ├── Phase 1: 13 specialist agents in parallel (+2 deferred)
  │                       └── Phase 2: itinerary → stress test
  ├── ChatAgent ── routing, knowledge answers, comprehensive planning
  ├── services: SerpAPI flights, Serper places, link resolvers,
  │             walking-tour crawler, verification, compare
  ├── watch scheduler (background task) ── fare + price watch re-checks (SerpAPI), alert emails (SMTP),
  │                                         alert pushes to registered phones (FCM, optional)
  ├── TTLCache (in memory, 30 min)
  └── SQLite: $DATA_DIR/airports.db (25 tables) + telemetry.db ── optional GCS backup every 60 s
            │
            ▼
External: Gemini on Vertex AI (3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.8 Flash; or Anthropic as a fallback),
          SerpAPI, Serper, DuckDuckGo,
          Open-Meteo, walking-tour provider sites, optional SMTP server,
          optional Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM HTTP v1)

In the container setup, nginx serves the built frontend and proxies /api/ and /health to the backend.

docs.title: The search pipeline
docs.text: POST /api/search (backend/app/api/routes/search.py) checks the cache, then streams TravelOrchestrator.stream_run() (backend/app/agents/orchestrator.py).

docs.title: Phase 0: static data (instant)
docs.text: Lookup tables in backend/app/agents/static_results.py produce, in this order: visa, sim, tips, getting_around and forex; then a confidence event (the Travel Ease grade); then emergency_card. All carry source: "static", and the UI marks those sections "Enhancing…" until the AI version arrives.

docs.title: Phase 1: thirteen agents in parallel
docs.text:
flights, weather, hotels, activities, places_to_see, walking_tours, events, visa, sim, tips, emergency_card, getting_around and forex start together. Each has a 240 s ceiling. A section is yielded as soon as its agent finishes, with source: "ai".

  • Static-backed agents (visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex, emergency_card): if the AI result is an error, it is not yielded, so the Phase 0 data stays. The frontend also refuses to replace valid data with an error.
  • URL enrichment: hotels, activities and places_to_see are yielded first with verification.pending = true, then again after their links have been searched and checked.
  • Deferred agents: packing_list starts once activities and weather are both in (template fallback after 120 s or on error). pricing_advisor starts once flights have at least 3 results (skipped after 120 s or on error).

docs.title: Phase 2: itinerary and stress test
docs.text:
The itinerary agent starts as soon as activities and hotels are both in, not after all of Phase 1. After 60 s, or on an empty or malformed result, a template itinerary built from the available activities is used instead. Once the itinerary is final, the stress-test agent audits it (pacing, timings, visa deadlines, weather clashes) with a 90 s timeout.

The stream always ends with {"type": "done"}. While agents run, the server sends : keepalive comments.

POST /api/search/sync runs the same agents sequentially and returns one JSON object; it is meant for testing.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: A complete, error-free run is stored as its list of SSE events in the TTL cache for 30 minutes, keyed by the md5 of the request JSON (which includes the user's Taste Graph context), and replayed instantly on a repeat. Runs with any error are never cached.

docs.title: Plan from a link
docs.text:
POST /api/import/extract (backend/app/api/routes/link_import.py) turns a link, pasted text or screenshots into a preview the traveller reviews before anything is planned:

url ──► link_fetch.read_link ──► text ─┐
text ──────────────────────────────────┼─► LinkImportAgent (agent model; vision for images)
images (sniffed, ≤4 × 5 MB) ───────────┘        │  untrusted-data fencing, Pydantic validation
                                                ▼
                     link_import.build_preview: resolve_place per city → stops
                     (day trips merged, ≤3 stops, nights split) → Serper POI lookups
                                                ▼
                     ImportPreview ──► review in the browser ──► POST /api/search
                                                   with must_include + import_source

link_fetch is the only place the backend fetches a user-supplied URL. It vets every DNS answer and every redirect hop, and connects to the vetted IP with the original Host and SNI (see API Reference). In the search, ActivitiesAgent merges the places into its results (services/must_include.merge_into_activities). ItineraryAgent lists them as must-schedule in its prompt and runs ensure_must_include on its result, and the orchestrator's template fallback runs the same check, so every itinerary reports link_coverage.

docs.title: SSE envelope
docs.text:
data: {"type": "visa", "data": {...}, "source": "static"}

data: {"type": "agent_status", "agent": "flights", "status": "searching"}

data: {"type": "flights", "data": {..., "verification": {...}}, "source": "ai"}

data: {"type": "itinerary", "data": {...}}

data: {"type": "done"}

The full list of event types is in API Reference. The frontend parses the stream in a Web Worker (frontend/src/workers/sseWorker.js) so that large JSON payloads do not block rendering. If the stream ends without done, the worker reports an interruption and the page says so.

Both /api/search and /api/chat go through core/sse.guarded_stream:

  • Keepalives. It sends a : keepalive comment after 15 s of silence (SSE_KEEPALIVE_SECONDS). Proxies and phone networks keep the connection, and a vanished client is noticed at the next write.
  • Cancel on disconnect. When the client goes away before done, it cancels every task the stream started, nested ones included, so abandoned agents stop spending tokens and release the LLM semaphore.
  • Tasks are attributed through a context variable that a small task factory reads, so agent code knows nothing about it.
  • Alert pushes start in a fresh context, so they survive.

docs.title: Source verification
docs.text: Every non-error section streamed by /api/search, and the responses of /api/{flights,hotels,activities}/filtered, carry data.verification: {level, label, summary, checks[], items_verified, items_total, pending}. backend/app/services/verification.py computes it from evidence the pipeline already holds: live SerpAPI fares, link checks from enrichment, crawl provenance, Open-Meteo provenance, and comparisons with the static visa and emergency tables. It makes no network or LLM calls. The levels are verified ("Verified"), partial ("Partly verified"), unverified ("AI-generated") and conflict ("Check details"). See Agent System for the per-section rules. Chat does not use verification.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Every model call goes through one module, backend/app/core/llm.py (generate, stream, and generate_sync for the IATA lookup fallback). LLM_PROVIDER picks the provider; callers only name a role. The default, auto, resolves to gemini when GCP_PROJECT is set (production), to anthropic when only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set (a typical local .env), and otherwise to gemini if Application Default Credentials resolve a project, else anthropic. The choice is logged once at startup and reported by /health/agents.

Role Used by gemini (production) anthropic (local dev / rollback) agent Every specialist agent (BaseAgent), packing list, pricing advisor, itinerary, stress test, link import, discovery, layover, the chat-itinerary agent, chat routing, parameter extraction, plan actions and suggestion chips, /health/agents gemini-3.5-flash-lite (GEMINI_MODEL_AGENT), thinking minimal claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 chat Chat conversational answers (streamed token by token) and the planning narrative gemini-3.8-flash (GEMINI_MODEL_CHAT), thinking low claude-sonnet-4-6

Gemini on Vertex AI uses the google-genai SDK with vertexai=True and Application Default Credentials (the VM's service account in production, gcloud auth application-default login locally); there is no API key. The project and location come from GCP_PROJECT (empty: the ADC / GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT project) and GCP_LOCATION (default global). Agent prompts (.agents/*.md) are sent unchanged as the system instruction; JSON callers also set response_mime_type: application/json. Because Gemini counts thinking tokens against max_output_tokens, each call adds headroom for the thinking level on top of the caller's budget (512 for minimal, 2048 for low); only generated tokens are billed. The SDK retries 429/5xx up to 3 times, like the Anthropic client's max_retries, and every request has a 120 s timeout (the SDK default is none); network errors from either transport (httpx, or aiohttp when installed) count as capacity errors. The one blocking call, the IATA lookup fallback (generate_sync, run during request validation), has an 8 s timeout and no retries. A chat stream the client abandons is closed at once, and its usage is still logged with aborted=True. The shared clients are closed on shutdown. At startup llm.log_provider() rejects a thinking level the configured Gemini model refuses (minimal on Gemini 3.7 or 3.8 Flash, or an unknown level) with a clear error. Vertex reads PNG, JPEG and WebP screenshots but not GIF: on Gemini, /api/import/extract converts a GIF to PNG when Pillow is installed and otherwise refuses it (422 gif_unsupported). Safety filters are left at the Vertex default, which is off for Gemini 3.5 Flash and later; a blocked reply would arrive as empty text and be retried as unparseable.

BaseAgent.execute() makes one llm.generate call per attempt with max_tokens 16384, behind a global semaphore (AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENCY, default 6). See Agent System.

Usage accounting. Every call logs one llm_usage line: label (the agent or chat step), provider, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, cached_tokens, latency_ms, truncated. Prompts and replies are never logged. llm.record_usage() collects the same records for a block of code (the eval harness uses it to price a whole search).

Spend cap. Production AI spend is hard-capped by a Cloud Billing spend-cap budget on Vertex AI: when it trips, new calls are refused until the 1st of the next month. Google documents no specific API error for this (only that usage is "paused"), so a 403 or 429 whose error message (not the help links or metadata in its details) names billing, a budget, a spend cap/limit, a usage limit or the credit balance is treated as the cap, as is an Anthropic 400 about the credit balance or reached usage limits; a plain 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED stays an ordinary retryable quota error. A 403/400 with reason BILLING_DISABLED (or "requires billing to be enabled") is not the cap: it gets its own message, "AI features are unavailable right now: billing is disabled for the AI service. Please try again later." (error_code: "ai_billing"). Either way llm raises a user-facing LLMError (user_code), logs the HTTP status, status name and ErrorInfo reasons, and refuses further calls for 5 minutes without contacting the provider. Users see "AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st.": as a section's {"error": ..., "error_code": "ai_limit"} in searches (static-backed sections keep their static data; the Results page shows the text once as a banner), as a chat delta, and as 503 from /api/discover, /api/compare/destination, /api/import/extract and /api/nearby. /health/agents reports llm: "spend-cap" (or "billing-disabled").

Evaluation. backend/scripts/llm_eval.py is a manual tool (never run in CI) that sends the six saved searches in backend/tests/fixtures/llm_eval/requests.json (single city, multi-city, family, budget, accessibility, long trip) through the real search pipeline on a chosen provider and model, stores the final sections, per-call usage, latency and estimated cost, and in compare mode writes a Markdown report per section (validity, item counts, fields the baseline always had, verification levels, cost per search).

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
There is one main SQLite file, $DATA_DIR/airports.db (backend/app/db/database.py), opened in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL and a 5 s busy timeout. Despite its name it holds every application table (25). The one exception is raw telemetry, telemetry_events in a separate $DATA_DIR/telemetry.db so event ingestion never contends with user data (see Telemetry); it is pruned after 90 days and not backed up.

Table Holds airports Airports from OurAirports plus the curated list (IATA, ICAO, name, served city, country, coordinates, region, rank, scheduled) places GeoNames places with their linked airports place_names Folded own and alternate names for place lookup admin1 First-level divisions (states, provinces) meta Key/value, including place_data_version nationalities 202 nationality → country rows for the nationality typeahead users Accounts: bcrypt hash, is_admin, is_first_login, is_active plans Saved plans: search data, selections (JSON), share token preferences Saved preferences per user recent_searches Up to 8 per user feedback Feedback widget submissions taste_signals Taste Graph signals mined from saved plans fare_watches Watched fares: trip, alert settings, baseline / last / lowest prices, per-signal alert state (last alerted price and time, peak since), Google's verdict, status, schedule and lease fare_watch_history Each check's prices (up to 120 rows per watch) fare_watch_quota SerpAPI calls spent by fare watches per UTC day fare_watch_user_quota The same per user, for the per-user daily share price_watches Watched hotel / activity / trip prices: kind, the matched subject (JSON, kind-specific), match_key, title and subtitle, alert settings, baseline / last / lowest prices, alert state (last alerted price and time, peak since), last_observation (JSON: status, unit price, source, link, trip breakdown), failure and unavailable streaks, expires_on, status, schedule and lease price_watch_history Each look: total price (null when unavailable), trip breakdown and raw observed details as JSON (up to 120 rows per watch) telemetry_daily Telemetry rollups: events, users and sessions per day, event and platform telemetry_daily_totals Exact distinct users, sessions and events per day and platform (* = all) telemetry_rollups UTC days already rolled up notifications In-app notifications (fare and price alerts, watch ended / on hold), read and emailed times devices Push devices: id, username, FCM token (unique: one owner at a time), platform (android), locale, created and last-seen times; at most 20 per user

The first six are reference data seeded from files committed to the repo; see Place and Airport Data.

docs.title: Backups (optional)
docs.text:
Backups are active only when BACKUP_BUCKET is set, in one of two modes (BACKUP_MODE):

  • vm (production, backend/app/db/vm_backup.py). The persistent disk is the source of truth.
  • Restore only if missing. At start the DB is downloaded from sqlite-backups/airports.db only when airports.db doesn't exist. Stray -wal/-shm files are deleted first, and the download is checked with quick_check and renamed into place atomically.
  • Mount guard. That happens only when DATA_DIR holds the provisioning marker .voyager-data-disk. A missing marker, or a missing DB that GCS can't supply, stops the start rather than run on the wrong directory or empty.
  • No merge, ever. A merge would bring back deleted watches, devices, plans and taste resets.
  • Change-only uploads. Every 5 min the non-place tables are exported from one read snapshot into a tmpfs. The export is uploaded only when its SHA-256 differs from the last upload, kept in the object's metadata so a restart doesn't re-upload. One more cycle runs at a clean shutdown.
  • Visible. /health reports backup_ok, which the uptime check content-matches.
  • cloudrun (legacy, backend/app/db/backup.py, the default). Built for an ephemeral disk. It restores every *.db at startup, uploads a snapshot every 60 s with GCS generation checks and an INSERT OR IGNORE merge of newer remote data (skipped during a 150 s startup window), and forces one final upload on shutdown.

In both modes the regenerable place tables and the place-data version are left out, so a restored database reseeds them on start. Locally backups are off.

docs.title: Fare-watch scheduler
docs.text:
backend/app/services/fare_watch.py, started in the lifespan (start_scheduler) only when SERPAPI_KEY is set and FARE_WATCH_ENABLED is true, and cancelled on shutdown.

  • Every FARE_WATCH_TICK_SECONDS (300) it sweeps notifications older than 180 days (once per UTC day), ends paused / on-hold watches whose departure day has come, and lists up to 50 due active watches. Each one is leased only when its turn comes (claim_watch(..., due_only=True): one UPDATE that also checks it is still active, due and unleased; lease_until = now + 10 min), so a watch taken meanwhile by "Check now" or another scheduler is skipped, and a slow batch never outlives its leases; a crashed worker's lease simply expires. Creating a watch and "Check now" take the same lease for their inline check.
  • Leased watches are checked three at a time (check_watch): departure reached → expired + one notice; otherwise the check's SerpAPI cost is estimated (cached fares are free) and reserved all-or-nothing from the day's FARE_WATCH_DAILY_CALL_BUDGET and from the owner's share of it (FARE_WATCH_USER_DAILY_SHARE) (over either → moved to early next UTC day; the pool running out is logged once); the fare comes from serp_flights.watch_fares (the fare calendar's outbound-stage price plus Google's insights, and the calendar's ±3 days for flexible watches, reusing a cached search). A failure retries in 1 h, three in a row put the watch on hold (error + one notice); SerpAPI's own quota error postpones without a strike. A watch deleted while its fares were fetched ends as deleted with nothing recorded. A success appends history, applies evaluate (the pure trigger and anti-spam rules, with separate references for the trip's own dates and the nearby dates, re-armed after rebounds; see Trip Planning Features), stores at most one notification, emails it when enabled (alert_email.py, smtplib in a thread, failures only logged), and schedules the next check in FARE_WATCH_INTERVAL_HOURS ±10 %.
  • The tests never start the loop (FARE_WATCH_ENABLED=false); they drive run_due and check_watch with an injected clock and fetch.
  • The same loop then runs the price-watch pass (price_watch.run_due, below); a failing pass of either kind is logged and never stops the other.

docs.title: Shared alert rules
docs.text: backend/app/services/price_rules.py holds the kind-agnostic own-price rules both kinds of watch use: the reference (baseline, last alerted price, or the peak once re-armed), the step (FARE_STEP max($15, 5 %), also used by hotels; ACTIVITY_STEP max(1 unit of the listing currency, 5 %); TRIP_STEP max($25, 4 %) for whole-trip totals), target re-arming, the baseline-already-good rule, the 24 h cooldown cap and the state a check leaves behind. Fare watches add their Google-"low" and nearby-dates signals on top. test_price_rules_equivalence.py checks the extraction against a frozen copy of the original fare rules.

docs.title: Price watches
docs.text:
Hotel, activity and whole-trip prices are watched by backend/app/services/price_watch.py, with tables in db/price_watch_db.py and routes in api/routes/price_watches.py. The pipeline is generic; each kind plugs in a price source:

  • PriceSource (protocol): kind; match_key(spec) (dedupe key from the client's spec, no live calls); async create(spec, user, api_key) → CreatedWatch (matched subject, baseline PriceObservation, title, subtitle, expires_on, plan_id) or NoLivePrice (message, up to 3 live suggestions, the AI estimate); async check(watch, api_key) → PriceObservation; estimate_calls(watch); compose(kind, watch, obs, ref) → the alert's title, body and extra data; optional step, max_create_calls (the most calls create may spend, default 1: hotel 2, activity 2, trip 10) and existing_watch(user_id, created) (the same subject found another way: hotel by property, stay, guests and rooms; activity by listing and travellers).
  • PriceObservation: price (the total, in the watch's currency: USD, except an activity watch, which keeps its listing's currency), unit_price, status (ok / unavailable), source, link, breakdown (trips), observed (raw details), calls.
  • Hotels everywhere (a hotel watch, and a trip's hotel) are priced for hotel_prices.rooms_for(guests) rooms: one room for up to 4 guests, then one per 4 (the UI's hotelGuests mirrors it). A trip's hotel baseline is the property look by property_token — the look every check makes — never the search list's price, so an unchanged trip never shows a hotel drop.
  • A spec's city may be the airport code the search form stores ("LIS"), or "City, Country" (cut at the comma): the hotel and activity sources and the trip component builder name it from the local airport data (database.airport_city, no web lookup), so subjects, alert copy and Google queries say "Lisbon". A multi-city trip's activities use their own leg's city.
  • Sources register with register_source; built-in ones are listed in price_watch.SOURCE_MODULES (each module exposes SOURCE) and registered in the lifespan. Tests use a fake test source only.

Creating a watch holds the kind's worst case (max_create_calls: hotel 2, activity 2, trip 10) from the shared daily budget and the owner's share, all or nothing (refused with 429 when either can't cover it), lets the source match and take the baseline, then gives back what it didn't spend (fare_watch_db.adjust_calls; settlement never charges more than the hold, so price spending can't postpone fare checks). A failure whose spend is unknown keeps the whole hold. Calls are counted as made: a lookup answered from the 30-minute cache is free. A failed check's text is stored and logged redacted (price_watch.redact_error: the HTTP status without the response body, never the key). The baseline is stored as the first check (never an alert). Each later check (check_watch, leased exactly like fare checks, three at a time) reserves its worst case, estimate_calls, all or nothing from the same budget as fare watches and settles it to obs.calls afterwards (in practice only giving calls back) (a failing create may report its spend as exc.calls); expires on expires_on; postpones on a spent budget or SerpAPI quota; retries a failure in 1 h and puts the watch on hold after three (a crash in the source's own code after the live look, e.g. in compose, counts as a failure too, so a broken watch is never retried every tick); records an unavailable look (sold out, listing gone) without alert or strike, holding the watch only after three in a row; and otherwise applies the shared rules to the total, storing at most one <kind>_drop / <kind>_target notification (data carries watch_kind, watch_id and links.alerts = /alerts?kind=<kind>&watch=<id>) and emailing it when enabled (alert_email.deliver_price, its own unsubscribe token). FARE_WATCH_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER counts fare and price watches together. Estimates are frozen at creation and never alert on their own; a source never presents an estimate as a live price.

The fare scheduler (fare_watch.run_scheduler) runs the fare pass on every tick and starts the price pass (price_watch.run_due) as its own task, so a slow price pass never delays fare checks; at most one price pass is in flight (a tick that finds one running starts none), and stopping the scheduler cancels and awaits it.

docs.title: Mobile client and push
docs.text:
The Android app (its own repository) is a second client of the same API: it signs in with the same JWT, streams /api/search and /api/chat, and reads /api/notifications. Two additions exist for it:

  • Push. The app registers its FCM token with POST /api/devices (devices table; a token belongs to one user at a time) and forgets it on sign-out with POST /api/devices/unregister; tokens travel only in request bodies and are logged masked. When FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE is set, or FCM_USE_ADC=true (production: the VM's service account, with no key file), services/push.py sends every new fare- or price-watch notification to the owner's devices. The hook is the _notify helper of each watch service, right after the notification row is stored: push.notify (guarded by its own try) starts a background task, so alert creation keeps its latency and outcome, and with push off it does nothing; shutdown gives pending pushes 5 s, then cancels them (push.drain). The task looks up the user (inactive users are skipped), signs a JWT with the service-account key (google-auth's RS256 signer) and exchanges it for an OAuth access token, or in ADC mode refreshes the metadata-server token in an executor (one exchange at a time, cached until a minute before it expires, dropped on an FCM 401), and sends one data-only FCM HTTP v1 message per device concurrently over httpx (no notification block, so the app builds and dedupes the notification itself): string data title, body, kind, notification_id, link (the web deep link, data.links.alerts), watch_id and, for price watches, watch_kind. Expired / on-hold notices go at normal Android priority, alerts at high. Only FCM's own verdict that a token is dead deletes it (error code UNREGISTERED, or INVALID_ARGUMENT with a violation on message.token); a bare 404 (a wrong Firebase project) and every other failure is logged and dropped, keeping the token (the alert stays in-app and in email). The app polls /api/notifications as a safety net either way.
  • Near me. POST /api/nearby finds the nearest known place to a coordinate (places_db.nearest_place: a lat/lng bounding box on the places table's idx_places_lat_lng index, wrapping the antimeridian, then great-circle distances, up to 75 km; a ward or suburb yields to a place at least 10× bigger within 15 km), then runs the existing activities agent for "Place, Region, Country" (the GeoNames admin1 name tells Portland, Maine from Portland, Oregon; left out when it repeats the name) with the body's interests (else the saved preferences') and the caller's Taste Graph. Results are cached for an hour in their own TTLCache, per 0.05° cell, place, interests and taste. With sections: true (v2) the same place lookup is followed by one Gemini call grounded with Google Maps (llm.generate_grounded, services/nearby_grounded.py) for places to see / eat / shop / stay; items come only from Maps grounding chunks and nothing is cached.
  • Live web check. POST /api/live-check (api/routes/live_check.py, services/live_check.py) checks the caller's own fare or price watch: the question is built from the stored watch and answered by one Gemini call grounded with Google Search; quotes are kept only when a grounding support cites them. Nothing is stored, cached or used by the watch scheduler (Google's grounding terms; see Trip Planning Features).

docs.title: Cache
docs.text: One process-wide cachetools.TTLCache (backend/app/core/cache.py, size CACHE_MAXSIZE 500, TTL CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 1800) holds full search runs, discover and compare results (complete ones only), the /health/agents result, SerpAPI flight results and per-date calendar fares, activity and place link resolutions, Serper places data and walking-tour crawls. It does not survive a restart. Inside fresh_reads() (a watch's "Check now") get_cache() returns a view in which older entries are misses, so the look is live, and what it fetches is written back for everyone. Near me results have their own one-hour cache (api/routes/nearby.py).

docs.title: Authentication and access
docs.text:
• POST /api/auth/login returns an HS256 JWT valid for 24 h (backend/app/core/auth.py). Passwords are bcrypt-hashed. Users sign up with email verification (/api/auth/signup, see Accounts API) or are created by an admin.
  • Most routes require a valid token (get_current_user). Admin routes also require is_admin.
  • /api/search, /api/search/sync, /api/discover and every single-agent ("light_ai") route accept anonymous calls, unless ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_AI=false (production): then every AI router answers 401 to anonymous callers (require_ai_access). They use get_optional_user: with a valid token for an active user, the Taste Graph is applied and the rate-limit key is the user; otherwise, including for a deactivated user's token, the caller is anonymous and keyed by client IP. The SPA itself requires login for every page except /share/:token.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text: backend/app/core/rate_limit.py is an in-process sliding-window limiter attached to routers as a FastAPI dependency (backend/app/main.py). Defaults per 10 minutes: search 10, chat 30, compare 30, discover 10, import 20, light_ai 60, and login 10 per client IP. Failed logins lock a username for the failing IP only (10), with a far higher ceiling per username across all IPs (200), both checked before bcrypt, so attackers elsewhere can't lock a user out. Behind Caddy the client IP comes from X-Forwarded-For, trusted only from the compose network (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS), so it can't be spoofed. A chat turn that starts a full trip plan also takes a search token (try_consume), answering with a friendly in-stream message when over. Over the limit the API returns 429 with Retry-After and a string detail that the frontend shows as-is. Being in-process, it only works for a single backend process. See Configuration. Fare and price watches share their own daily SerpAPI budget, stored in SQLite (see Fare-watch scheduler).

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
• CORS from CORS_ORIGINS.
  • AnalyticsMiddleware logs every request as JSON, except /health, /docs, /openapi.json and /redoc.
  • RequestIdMiddleware propagates or creates X-Request-ID.

UI analytics events are batched by the frontend (utils/analytics.js, every 5 s or 10 events) and posted to POST /api/analytics/events, which logs them to stdout.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Changes since the project started on 2026-05-17. From 2026-08-30 on, every change went through a pull request; dates are merge dates (UTC). A "(#N)" inside a PR title refers to a backlog item, not a PR.

docs.title: Unreleased: price alerts 2.0
docs.text:
Contract: Alerts API. Settings: Configuration. Everything is additive and gated by PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED (default true since the switch-on merge; set false in app.env to revert).

  • Backend. New /api/alerts/* routes (summary, story, flight advice, quick-watch, suggestions, preferences, digest unsubscribe), five tables (alert_prefs, alert_savings, alert_outbox, alert_digests, alert_advice), pending_first_check on every watch, and data.drop, data.game and the price_digest kind on notifications. With the flag on, one seam in each watch service's _notify records savings (observed drops only, USD and other currencies kept apart, estimates never count), awards Deal-hunter XP, and applies the delivery rules to push and email: instant mode, per-kind daily caps, quiet hours in the account timezone, grouped pushes. An opt-in weekly digest goes in-app and by email (push only with digest_push). The scheduler orders first looks of one-tap watches and adapts intervals.
  • Honest without a key. Without SERPAPI_KEY stories, savings, digest and suggestions work from stored data, prices say "checked N days ago", and one-tap watch answers 503 live_prices_off.
  • Web. Price story and chart, drop moment, savings tally and share card, Deal-hunter track, one-tap watch on Results, Chat and Trip, suggestions on saving a plan, and alert preferences, in all seven languages.
  • Settings. PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED, ALERT_DIGEST_HOUR_LOCAL, ALERT_FLUSH_INTERVAL_S, ALERT_ADVICE_TTL_HOURS.

docs.title: Unreleased: the trip journey, trips API and offline pack
docs.text:
Contract: Trips API. Runbook: Deployment on GCP.

  • Trips. A plan with dates is a trip with a phase (Dreaming, Planning, Ready, On the road, Memories) derived from its dates, with an override. New /api/trips* routers (trips, trip_prep, trip_money, trip_journal, trip_offline, trip_today, trip_recap) and seven tables (trip_expenses, trip_journal, trip_ratings, trip_prep, trip_snapshots, trip_checkins, user_countries), all additive.
  • Web journey (on by default; JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED=false turns it off). Trips hub, trip screen (overview, prep checklist, offline pack, Today with check-in, expenses with a currency converter, journal and place ratings, recap with passport stamps), plus Explore, Play and You tabs. Teal-700 is the primary colour.
  • Journey UI on by default. JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED now defaults to true, so the Trips hub, trip screen and Explore, Play and You tabs are visible to everyone. Setting JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED=false in app.env and restarting the app turns it off, with no rebuild.
  • Offline pack. Saving a pack registers /sw.js (app shell), keeps the trip snapshot in IndexedDB and queues expenses and journal writes while offline. OFFLINE_PACK_ENABLED=false removes it from every client on its next load. Packs are cleared on sign-out.
  • Settings. JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED, OFFLINE_PACK_ENABLED, READY_WINDOW_DAYS, TRIP_MAX_EXPENSES, TRIP_MAX_JOURNAL, TRIP_MAX_PLACES, TRIP_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES.
  • Languages. New namespaces in all seven languages; English is bundled per route.

docs.title: Unreleased: faster deploys (per-image build alongside CI, skip unchanged images)
docs.text:
Runbook: Deployment on GCP; workflows: Testing and CI.

  • Build in parallel with CI; sign and promote only after it passes, per image. deploy.yml's single publish job is now build-app / build-caddy (alongside ci, no id-token: build, push sha-<commit>, Trivy-scan) and promote-app / promote-caddy (plain needs: [ci, build-<image>]; deploy/ci/promote-image.sh: HEAD check, cosign sign, verify as the VM will, move prod). Every signed image has passed CI and was main's HEAD when signed, and one image's failure never blocks the other.
  • Unchanged images aren't rebuilt. deploy/ci/image-inputs-id.sh hashes everything a build can read: the Dockerfile, .dockerignore, the files its COPYs take (derived from the Dockerfile) and the base images pinned by digest (PYTHON_BASE; CADDY_BASE and the SPA builder's NODE_BASE). Images carry it as io.voyager.app-inputs / io.voyager.caddy-inputs. When prod already has the id, nothing is built and prod stays, so a frontend-only merge no longer restarts the app (open chats survive) and a backend-only merge leaves the SPA alone. Anything it can't account for exactly builds: foreign --from, context mounts (any case of type=bind), a FROM that is neither an earlier stage, a pinned build arg nor a digest-pinned image, and unusual .dockerignore re-includes. !**/NAME re-includes files and whole directories named NAME.
  • Weekly refresh and daily prod scan. pip's version ranges resolve at build time and aren't in the id, so the Deploy workflow also runs every Monday (and by hand, force) and rebuilds both images without cache. The new digests also end holds on the VM. Images record their last refresh (io.voyager.fresh-at), and any run refreshes an image whose prod copy is over 8 days old, so a scheduled run dropped from the queue or disabled by GitHub (after 60 days without repository activity; gh workflow enable) doesn't stop refreshes. prod-scan.yml scans both prod images daily and fails visibly.
  • Compatibility in both directions. The images ship independently, so backend changes must keep serving the previous SPA (no removed or renamed endpoints, fields or semantics without a deprecation step), just as frontend changes already had to tolerate the previous backend.
  • The images that ship are scanned. One Trivy policy (deploy/ci/trivy-scan.sh: 0.70.0, checksum-pinned, fixed CRITICAL fails, .trivyignore) replaces CI's build-and-scan, which scanned the undeployed nginx image. It runs in the deploy build jobs before signing, in PR CI's image-builds (app and Caddy, path-filtered) and daily on prod.
  • Caddy 2.11 (caddy:2.11-alpine, was 2.10). The 2.10 base carries fixed CRITICAL CVEs (CVE-2025-44005, CVE-2025-68121, CVE-2026-30836, CVE-2026-31789, CVE-2026-33186) that would fail the new gate. The runtime id changes, so the rollout recreates Caddy once, after draining open streams.
  • CI. image-builds builds and scans only the images a change touches (plus the nginx image docker compose up uses, build only), and is skipped when deploy.yml calls CI. The deploy-kit tests run in their own parallel job, test-deploy-kit.
  • Timing (estimated from recent job times). Workflow ≈ 3.5–4.5 min (was 6–8). Merge → live ≈ 4.5–6 min for frontend-only merges, ≈ 5.5–8.5 min with backend changes (was 7–9, measured 8 min 53 s).

docs.title: Unreleased: everything auto-deploys within minutes (no Caddy window)
docs.text:
Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-auto-deploy-edge.md. Runbook: Deployment on GCP.

  • SPA and Caddyfile without a Caddy restart. deploy.sh copies /srv and the Caddyfile out of each signed Caddy image into /var/lib/voyager/edge/releases/<digest>. It refuses symlinks, missing assets and oversize releases, then switches current/prev1/prev2 symlinks. Caddy mounts the directory read-only and serves /assets/* from the last three releases. A changed Caddyfile is validated in a throwaway container and hot-reloaded through the admin API, so open SSE streams survive. Failures switch back, hold the digest and send an email.
  • Caddy runtime changes are automatic. New image label io.voyager.caddy-runtime (deploy/gcp/caddy-runtime-id.sh: pinned base digest plus the Dockerfile's runtime lines). Only a change there recreates Caddy: it drains open streams (new app endpoint GET /internal/streams, up to 90 s), then checks health and rolls back on failure. A changed compose.yaml for Caddy is drained the same way.
  • Faster pickup. voyager-deploy.timer runs every 60 s. A no-change run is one cached GHCR token plus two HEADs, with back-off on 429, failed signature checks retried after 10 min, and refused downgrades remembered. Merge to live is about 7–9 min.
  • --rollback-edge and --rollback-caddy join --rollback. --window is a no-op alias, and the weekly window now only reboots when an upgrade requires it.
  • App restarts drain open streams too, for up to 90 s (not when rolling back an unhealthy app).
  • Failure handling (after review):
  • Every deploy step runs with set -e really active, and every pull, compose, copy and write is checked.
  • Health only counts once the container runs the intended image ID, and an unreadable build label is refused.
  • Only content/validation failures, unhealthy apps and unhealthy Caddy runtimes (by runtime id, held-runtimes) are held; infrastructure failures retry after 5 min. A held runtime never gets recreated onto; its images ship content only.
  • Emails and repeated errors are rate-limited (1 an hour), and a broken edge directory never blocks app deploys or rollbacks.
  • A no-change run is one docker ps; converge runs only on config changes or stopped services.
  • Old images are removed by digest (current + previous kept). Caddy health needs no certificate on a fresh VM, but a wrong HTTPS answer always fails, and so does no answer when HTTPS worked before the change. An SPA served wrongly after its switch is held, and a compose failure that repeats twice holds the digest.
  • caddy.Dockerfile: runtime layers come before the SPA layer (the VM pulls only the SPA on frontend changes), and /edge/current falls back to the image's own content. Missing assets are now an uncached 404 instead of being cached for a year.

docs.title: Unreleased: live web check and Near me v2 (Google grounding)
docs.text:
Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-live-check-and-near-me-v2.md.

  • llm.generate_grounded(): one Gemini call with Google Search or Google Maps grounding (text output, agent model), returning the text, grounding chunks, supports and the searches run. Same timeout, spend-cap/billing handling and llm_usage log (plus search_queries and grounding_chunks counts). On the Anthropic provider it raises grounding_unavailable.
  • POST /api/live-check ("Search the web now"): a Search-grounded look at one of the caller's watches. Returns the answer, its sources, "Searched for" queries and quotes backed by a source. Never stored or cached, and never used for alerts. Sign-in, light_ai bucket.
  • Near me v2: POST /api/nearby with sections: true returns places to see / eat / shop / stay from one Maps-grounded call. Each item has its Google Maps link and place id, and nothing is cached. v1 is unchanged.
  • Both answer within 45 s per call and retry once when Google returns an answer with no grounding sources. Live check answers 409 watch_expired for an expired watch or one whose date is before yesterday (UTC). Quotes need a source covering the price and an unambiguous ISO amount; prices are tokenised so an unclear number is dropped, never misread. Grounded calls share the agents' concurrency gate.
  • Web: Near me page (/nearby, new header tab): asks for the browser's location after a short explainer, then shows places to see, eat, shop and stay from Google Maps grounding (POST /api/nearby with sections: true), each with an "Open in Google Maps" link, plus Google Maps attribution and sources. Clear copy for denied / unavailable / timed-out location and for 404 / 429 / 502 / 503 errors. Results are kept in component state only.
  • Web: Search the web now on every active fare, hotel, activity and trip watch card (POST /api/live-check): one live, Google Search–grounded answer shown under the card with its quotes, sources, "Searched for" links and disclaimer. Dismissible, never stored, and never used for the watch's price, history or alerts.
  • Docs: the Google terms these features follow (only for the requesting user, no storage, Search Suggestions) in Trip Planning Features.

docs.title: Unreleased: production on one e2-micro VM (GCP)
docs.text:
Deployment kit for the approved lean GCP design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-gcp-lean-deploy-design.md): one always-free e2-micro VM in us-east1, Caddy + the app, SQLite on the persistent disk, about $4/month for hosting. Runbook: Deployment on GCP.

  • Operator password tool: python -m app.set_password USERNAME (reset, reactivate) or --create --admin; reads the password twice with getpass, never from arguments (runbook §5a).
  • Backend production mode:
  • BACKUP_MODE=vm: disk authoritative, restore only if the DB is missing (stray WAL/SHM removed), mount-guard marker, no merge, user-table export to tmpfs uploaded on hash change every 5 min plus a clean-shutdown flush, backup_ok in /health.
  • python -m app.entrypoint: Secret Manager secrets into memory, refuses an empty JWT_SECRET_KEY, uvicorn with --timeout-graceful-shutdown 5 and proxy headers only from the compose network.
  • login rate-limit bucket plus a per-username failure lock, and ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_AI=false for production.
  • FCM push through the VM's service account (FCM_USE_ADC).
  • 15 s SSE keepalives, and agent tasks cancelled when a search or chat client disconnects.
  • Image: runs through the entrypoint; the unused claude-agent-sdk and python-dotenv are gone.
  • deploy/gcp/:
  • compose (memory limits, log rotation, health checks), Caddyfile and a Caddy image with the SPA baked in;
  • a tiered egress governor in DOCKER-USER: per IP ≈ 4 Mbit/s and 3 GiB/day, a warning at 150 GiB, ports closed at 200 GiB, the billing month in Pacific time;
  • a signed-digest pull deployer with automatic rollback;
  • first-boot provisioning for Debian 13 (Docker, zram, unattended-upgrades, a weekly Berlin-night window) and systemd units.
  • infrastructure/gcp/:
  • an idempotent bootstrap.sh with --dry-run; it detects the existing INR budgets and Gemini spend cap by name;
  • migrate_old_prod.py: strips the 886 MB 2026-08-30 export to its 17 users and their plans, preferences, taste signals and feedback.
  • CI/CD: deploy.yml runs on every push to main. After all of CI it builds, pushes to GHCR, signs with cosign keyless and moves prod; the VM verifies and pulls. The Cloud Run Terraform, its scripts and the old workflow were removed.

docs.title: Unreleased: Gemini on Vertex AI
docs.text:
• Gemini replaces Claude in production. Every model call now goes through one provider seam, backend/app/core/llm.py. LLM_PROVIDER=auto (default) picks Gemini when GCP_PROJECT is set (or, with no Anthropic key, when ADC resolves a project) and Claude otherwise, so an existing local .env with only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY keeps working; the choice is logged at startup and shown by /health/agents (llm_provider, llm_provider_reason).
