Gemini Gemini on Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials (no API key; GCP_PROJECT, GCP_LOCATION default global): Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite (gemini-3.5-flash-lite, thinking minimal, JSON mode) for every specialist agent, packing, pricing advisor, itinerary, stress test, link import, discovery, layover, chat itinerary and chat routing/extraction; Gemini 3.8 Flash (gemini-3.8-flash, thinking low) for chat answers, streamed token by token, and the planning narrative. LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic forces Claude (Haiku 4.5 / Sonnet 4.6) for local development and rollback. Agent prompts are unchanged. New settings: LLM_PROVIDER, GCP_PROJECT, GCP_LOCATION, GEMINI_MODEL_AGENT, GEMINI_MODEL_CHAT, GEMINI_THINKING_AGENT, GEMINI_THINKING_CHAT (see Configuration).
  • Monthly AI spend cap. When the Vertex AI spend-cap budget trips, users see "AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st." in search sections (error_code: "ai_limit", one banner on the Results page), as a chat reply, and as 503 from /api/discover, /api/import/extract and /api/nearby, instead of failures; further calls are skipped for 5 minutes. /health/agents reports llm_provider and llm: "spend-cap".
  • Hardening. Gemini requests time out after 120 s; the blocking IATA lookup fallback after 8 s, without retries. Abandoned chat streams are closed (usage still logged, aborted=True), clients are closed on shutdown, aiohttp network errors back off like other capacity errors, and a thinking level the Gemini model rejects stops startup with a clear error. Disabled billing (BILLING_DISABLED) gets its own message (error_code: "ai_billing") instead of the spend-cap text; the cap is recognised from the error message and reasons, not help links. Compare mode shows the AI-paused text (503). On Gemini, GIF screenshots in Plan from a link are converted to PNG when Pillow is installed, otherwise refused with 422 gif_unsupported; the copy now suggests PNG, JPEG or WebP.
  • Token usage per call. Every model call logs an llm_usage line (label, model, input/output/thinking tokens, latency; never content).
  • LLM eval harness. backend/scripts/llm_eval.py runs six saved searches on a chosen provider/model and compares two runs per section (validity, item counts, required fields, verification levels, cost) in a Markdown report. Manual only, never in CI.
  • Dependencies: google-genai 2.34.0 added; the unused claude-agent-sdk and python-dotenv removed (pydantic-settings still brings python-dotenv for .env). Docker Compose passes LLM_PROVIDER, GCP_PROJECT and GCP_LOCATION.

docs.title: Unreleased: fixes from the Android end-to-end run
docs.text:
• Check now is live. POST /api/fare-watches/{id}/check and POST /api/price-watches/{id}/check no longer answer from the 30-minute result cache, so pressing Check now can show a new price; the fresh answer refreshes the cache. Their SerpAPI calls are reserved from the daily budget and the owner's share as before (a Check now right after a search is no longer free). Scheduled checks and a new watch's baseline still reuse cached prices (core/cache.fresh_reads).
  • Fare alerts name cities. A fare watch whose labels are bare airport codes (as the Android app saves them, "JFK" → "LIS") now reads "New York → Lisbon" in alert titles, emails and pushes, using the local airport data; an unknown code stays as it is.
  • Chat plan commands know the items. The plan-command model now sees a compact, bounded line per flight, hotel and activity (name, price, rating…, with a ref) instead of only counts, so "add the cheapest hotel" works; the server fills the full result item in from the ref.
  • Hotel alert numbers agree. A Google nightly rate on another taxes basis than the stay's total (e.g. $73.60 a night before taxes next to $294 for 3 nights with taxes) is replaced by the total's per-night share, and hotel drop/target alerts (in-app, email and push) now read "That's the total for 3 nights, 2 guests ($98 a night) on Google Hotels, taxes and fees included.", as on the Alerts page.

docs.title: Unreleased: backend for the Android app
docs.text:
• Push alerts: POST /api/devices, GET /api/devices, DELETE /api/devices/{id} and POST /api/devices/unregister (sign-out) manage the app's FCM tokens (table devices, at most 20 per user, tokens shown masked and never in URLs). With FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE set, every new fare- or price-watch notification is also pushed to the owner's devices over FCM HTTP v1 in the background as data-only messages (data title, body, kind, notification_id, link; the app builds the notification itself), only tokens FCM reports as dead are pruned, and failures never affect the alert. /health reports push_configured. google-auth is now a direct dependency.
  • Near me: POST /api/nearby {lat, lng, interests?, limit?} returns the nearest known place with its region (local GeoNames data, up to 75 km) and the activities agent's things to do there, cached an hour per ~5 km cell; 404 no_place when nothing is near. light_ai bucket.

docs.title: 2026-11-05: price watch for hotels, activities and whole trips
docs.text:
• Watch a hotel's stay price, an activity's per-person price or a whole saved trip's total, next to the flight fare watch. Watch price on hotel and activity cards, in My Plan and in chat; Watch whole trip on saved plans. The Alerts page gets tabs per kind and a card per kind (trip cards show a per-part breakdown).
  • Honest prices: every part is observed (a live Google Hotels, Google Flights or Google result) or a labelled estimate. Estimates are frozen and never alert, a watch with no live part can't be created, activity prices come from Google results for GetYourGuide / Viator listings (those sites are never scraped) in the listing's currency, and a trip's flight is the cheapest fare on your dates.
  • Alert steps: fares and hotels max($15, 5 %), activities max(1 unit, 5 %), trips max($25, 4 %) on the total, with the same anti-spam rules as fares. One scheduler loop, one daily SerpAPI budget and one active-watch limit for all kinds.
  • /api/price-watches (CRUD, match, check, unsubscribe; 422 no_live_price with suggestions, 422 target_currency_mismatch), tables price_watches and price_watch_history, a PriceSource registry, notification kinds hotel_*, activity_*, trip_*, and kind-aware alert emails. See Trip Planning Features.

docs.title: Unreleased: plan a trip from a link or screenshot
docs.text:
• New Search mode, From a link ✨. Paste a travel blog, YouTube or TikTok link, a caption or a message, or drop up to 4 screenshots. The places come back on a map for review (tick, rename, move between stops, place the unplaced, set nights), then a normal search plans the trip around them.
  • POST /api/import/extract, with SSRF-safe link fetching (public addresses only on every redirect hop, pinned IP, 10 s and 2 MB limits), YouTube and TikTok oEmbed, friendly errors for Instagram, Facebook, X and Threads, and a hardened link_import extraction agent. Rate bucket import, default 20 (RATE_LIMIT_IMPORT).
  • TravelSearchRequest.must_include and import_source. Imported places lead Activities and are always scheduled in the itinerary by a deterministic post-check (from_link slots, link_extras, link_coverage). Results show a coverage banner and "From your link" tags; the share page, print and calendar export credit the source.
  • Chat replies to a pasted trip link with a "Plan a trip from this link" button that opens the import flow.
  • Hardening:
  • bounded gzip/deflate decompression (other encodings refused), with parsing off the event loop;
  • nonce-fenced prompts;
  • a strict, city-aware scheduling match and a logistics guard on every day;
  • screenshots shrunk in the browser, with 32 MB nginx and 30 MB backend body limits;
  • POST /api/import/resolve-place to place spots by town;
  • deep links that survive the login redirect.

docs.title: Unreleased: documentation and housekeeping
docs.text:
• Fare watch and price alerts (branch feat/price-alerts): watch a single-destination trip's live fare from the Flights header, the fare calendar, My Plan or a saved plan; a background scheduler re-checks it about twice a day within a daily SerpAPI budget and notifies on a meaningful drop, a target price, a new Google-rated low or a cheaper date ±3 days, never on the baseline, never for a rise, never for small drifts (repeats need a further max($15, 5 %) drop unless the price rebounded) and at most once a day; each user gets at most 30 % of the daily SerpAPI budget. New /alerts page, header bell with toasts and optional browser notifications, optional SMTP email with a one-click stop link, and an email field on Preferences. New tables fare_watches, fare_watch_history, fare_watch_quota, notifications; new settings FARE_WATCH_*, SMTP_*, APP_BASE_URL. See Trip Planning Features.
  • Developer docs consolidated into one set of pages (this site and the GitHub wiki share them), with new pages for trip-planning features, place and airport data, testing and CI, and this changelog.
  • Added an MIT LICENSE file.
  • App footer credits the place data: "Place data © GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) · Airport data: OurAirports".
  • docker-compose.yml now builds the backend from the repo root, so docker compose up --build works.
  • get_optional_user treats a deactivated user's token as anonymous.
  • Removed the unused knowledge_planner.py and the unused tools / max_turns agent frontmatter fields.
  • Place resolution (GeoNames allCountries, CC BY 4.0): countries resolve by their native and other-language names ("Deutschland", "Brasil", "Nippon", "Suomi"; KSA, PRC, ROK and ROC, and names that are also a town's, as qualifiers only); a suburb no longer beats a namesake with its own named airport ("Peoria" → PIA, "Pontevedra" → Spain); 31,995 notable islands, parks, glaciers, caves, mountains, regions, sites and famous districts resolve to their airports ("Kakadu" → DRW, "Grand Teton" → JAC, "Ealing" → LHR); district names many cities share give no answer ("Centar", "Chinatown"). See Place and Airport Data.

PR Merged Title #1 2026-08-30 chore: decommission GCP deploy pipeline

Production on Cloud Run was shut down and the GCP project deleted; deploy.yml became manual-only. See Deployment.

docs.title: Before pull requests (2026-05-17 to 2026-07-05)
docs.text:
About 100 commits went straight to main. Highlights, from the git history:

  • 2026-05-17 to 05-21: first version and production. The initial commit brought the multi-agent planner: FastAPI backend, three-phase orchestrator with static-first visa, SIM, tips and transport, SSE streaming through a Web Worker, React frontend, JWT login with admin-created accounts, saved plans and preferences. The same days set up GCP Cloud Run deployment with Terraform and GitHub Actions, CI with ruff, bandit, pip-audit and Trivy, the docs site with its custom homepage, deterministic activity-link resolution (Serper as a second tier) in place of model-invented URLs, and a chat agent with session memory and routing.
  • 2026-05-21 to 05-31: more agents and views. Places to See (Serper data plus Claude). The weather section with traveller profiles and accessibility needs. Chat itinerary overhaul (multi-city route ordering, specialist routing). Destination discovery (Surprise me), the Travel Ease confidence score, the emergency card, the packing list, the flight price advisor and the Timeline view. A large batch of extra agents added on 05-30 was reverted the next day.
  • 2026-07-04 to 07-05: multi-city, personalization and resilience. Trip Remix presets; the itinerary stress test (health check); the Taste Graph; the layover optimizer; multi-city routing (up to 4 cities); the What's On events layer; public share links with a full-page PNG trip card; a more natural chat that answers from knowledge, with specialists only as a fallback. Fixes for API bursts and oversized multi-city outputs (global concurrency cap, compact retry), retries for severed SSE streams, responsive database operations under load, and backups that no longer lose WAL-only rows.

docs.title: Chat Assistant
docs.text: The chat (POST /api/chat, frontend/src/pages/ChatPage.jsx, backend/app/agents/chat_agent.py) is a travel advisor. It answers questions from the model's own knowledge, and it can plan a whole trip inside the conversation.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Task Model on Gemini (production) On Anthropic Conversational answers (streamed token by token) and the planning narrative gemini-3.8-flash, thinking low claude-sonnet-4-6 Intent routing, trip-parameter extraction, plan commands, suggestion chips gemini-3.5-flash-lite, thinking minimal claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 The chat itinerary (.agents/chat-itinerary.md, ChatItineraryAgent) gemini-3.5-flash-lite claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 Specialist fallbacks and refinements the specialist agents (agent model, via BaseAgent) same

All calls go through backend/app/core/llm.py (see Architecture). When the monthly AI spend cap has tripped, chat answers with one delta, "AI limit reached for this month — try again on the 1st.", then done.

docs.title: Knowledge first, specialists last
docs.text:
Topic questions ("do I need a visa for Japan?", "which area of Barcelona is best for nightlife?") are answered from the model's own knowledge and stream straight away. No agents run, and no background verification happens.

The specialist agents (visa, sim, tips, getting_around, hotels, activities, flights) run only if the model fails to answer: the stream errors, the answer is empty, or the model says it doesn't know. Only then does the chat extract trip parameters and run the matching specialists as a fallback.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
Each message goes through an ordered router in ChatAgent.stream():

Step Trigger Behaviour 0 Jailbreak or off-topic patterns Polite refusal; chat only discusses travel 1 Plan commands ("add … to my plan", "remove …", "show my plan", "clear my plan") plan_action events that the frontend applies to My Plan. The model sees one compact line per flight, hotel and activity in the current results (up to 20 each: name or airline, price, rating, tier…, with a ref such as H2), so "add the cheapest hotel" works; it answers with the ref and the server puts the full result item into the action 1.5 A reply to a pending clarifying question (for example the origin) Resumes planning with that slot filled 2 Planning patterns ("plan a week in Lisbon…") Comprehensive planning, or a clarifying question if something essential is missing 3 A specific topic (flights, hotels, visa, SIM, tips, transport, forex…) Knowledge-only answer; specialists only on failure 3.5 A change to the trip being discussed ("make it cheaper", "add 2 days") Refinement: re-runs only the affected specialists 3.6 Knowledge patterns (culture, packing, weather, neighbourhoods…) Knowledge answer 3.7 Anything of 4 or more words not caught yet One intent-classification call (agent model), which catches soft phrasings such as "we're thinking Lisbon in October, maybe with the kids?" 4 Everything else Plan-aware conversation

docs.title: Comprehensive planning
docs.text:
A planning request streams this sequence (_run_comprehensive_planning):

  1. planning_start with the destination.
  2. trip_map: city coordinates computed in Python, so the map appears at once.
  3. itinerary_generating.
  4. comprehensive_itinerary: the day-by-day plan from the chat-itinerary agent (60 s timeout, 120 s for multi-city).
  5. Proactive warnings, checked in parallel while the itinerary builds: rainy or rough-weather days (weather agent) and major events or disruptions on the trip dates (events agent).
  6. session_context_update, suggestions (tappable follow-up chips) and planning_done.

Each full plan also takes one token from the caller's search rate-limit bucket (shared with /api/search); over that limit the chat streams a friendly "try again in about N minutes" delta and done instead of planning. Questions answered from knowledge cost only the chat bucket.

The frontend renders this as a TripPlanView: a Leaflet map, day cards, a budget tracker, suggestion and follow-up chips, and retry actions. Items can be added to the chat's My Plan drawer, which has the same features as on the Results page.

Clarifying questions with slot memory. If only the origin is missing, the chat asks exactly that ("Which city will you be flying from?"), remembers everything else and resumes when the user answers.

section_result events (with per-section agent_status) are used only in the specialist fallback and the refinement path (_run_specialist_agents), where individual specialists run with a 45 s timeout each.

docs.title: Refinement
docs.text:
"Make it cheaper" does not re-run everything. The chat compares the changed request with the previous one and re-runs only the specialists whose inputs changed (_FIELD_AGENTS):

Changed field Re-run departure or return date flights, hotels, activities budget flights, hotels travellers flights, hotels interests activities origin flights, visa destination flights, hotels, activities, visa, sim, tips, getting_around

docs.title: Session context and history
docs.text:
The chat endpoint is stateless. The frontend sends the messages, current selections, any search results and a session_context (destination, dates, budget, travellers, a pending question) with each request, and the server returns session_context_update events. Follow-ups like "what about hotels there?" resolve against the trip being discussed, and naming a different city in the question always wins over the remembered trip.

Chat history is stored in the browser under localStorage['chat_history_<username>'], trimmed to the last 20 messages if storage is full. utils/chatHistory.js builds text stand-ins for structured turns before they are sent back to the model.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: delta (text), done, error, suggestions, session_context_update, plan_action, planning_start, trip_map, itinerary_generating, comprehensive_itinerary, planning_done, agent_status and section_result. If the server hits an exception, it still closes the stream with a fallback delta, then error and done. The frontend parses the stream in workers/chatWorker.js.

docs.title: Personalization and safety
docs.text:
For signed-in users, the saved preferences and a short Taste Graph summary (see Personalization) are added to the system prompt and to any specialist runs, so suggestions lean towards the user's demonstrated style.

The chat does not reveal its prompts, agent names or tooling, rejects jailbreak attempts and only discusses travel. It does not show verification badges.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The backend is configured through environment variables, read by pydantic-settings in backend/app/core/config.py. Variable names are the upper-case field names. Every setting has a default, so the app always starts; the ones marked needed below must be set for it to be useful.

Settings are read from the process environment and from a .env file in the working directory (env_file=".env", unknown keys ignored). For start.sh and a manual uvicorn run that is backend/.env. For Docker Compose, put the values in your shell or a root .env, which Compose uses for variable substitution (see Setup and Installation).

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning JWT_SECRET_KEY "" Needed. HS256 signing key for login tokens (24 h lifetime). Changing it logs everyone out. Generate one with python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))". CORS_ORIGINS ["http://localhost:5174","http://localhost:5173"] Allowed browser origins, as a JSON list. AGENTS_DIR <repo>/.agents Directory of the agent definition files. A relative path that does not exist falls back to <repo>/.agents. AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENCY 6 Global cap on concurrent model calls across all agents. CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 1800 TTL of the in-memory result cache. CACHE_MAXSIZE 500 Maximum entries in that cache.

docs.title: LLM
docs.text:
Every model call goes through backend/app/core/llm.py; see Architecture.

Variable Default Meaning LLM_PROVIDER auto gemini: Gemini on Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials (no API key). anthropic: Claude via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, for local development or a rollback. auto: gemini when GCP_PROJECT is set; otherwise anthropic when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set; otherwise gemini if Application Default Credentials resolve a project, else anthropic. The choice is resolved once, logged at startup (LLM provider: gemini (auto: GCP_PROJECT set) …) and shown by /health/agents as llm_provider / llm_provider_reason. GCP_PROJECT "" Needed for Gemini. Google Cloud project that runs Vertex AI, e.g. voyager-prod-ohzkl; setting it also makes auto choose Gemini. Empty falls back to GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or the ADC project. GCP_LOCATION global Vertex AI location. global routes to any region with capacity; us and eu keep processing in that multi-region. GEMINI_MODEL_AGENT gemini-3.5-flash-lite Model for every specialist agent, itinerary, stress test, packing, pricing advisor, link import, discovery, layover, chat itinerary and chat routing/extraction. GEMINI_MODEL_CHAT gemini-3.8-flash Model for chat conversational answers and the planning narrative. GEMINI_THINKING_AGENT minimal Thinking level of the agent model: minimal, low, medium or high. GEMINI_THINKING_CHAT low Thinking level of the chat model: low, medium or high (Gemini 3.8 Flash rejects minimal). On Gemini, a level the model refuses stops the app at startup with a clear error. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "" Needed for Claude (LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic, or auto without GCP_PROJECT). Unused on Gemini.

With Gemini, the credentials need the Vertex AI User role (roles/aiplatform.user) on the project. Locally, run gcloud auth application-default login once. If no credentials are found, every AI section fails and /health/agents reports the error.

docs.title: Storage and backup
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning DATA_DIR backend/data Directory of the single SQLite file airports.db, which holds every table (users, plans, preferences, place data and so on). Created automatically. TELEMETRY_ENABLED true Product telemetry. false makes POST /api/telemetry answer 404 (clients then switch themselves off) and GET /api/config report it disabled. Raw events live in $DATA_DIR/telemetry.db (not backed up); daily aggregates in the telemetry_daily table of airports.db. TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS 90 Raw telemetry events older than this are pruned by the hourly maintenance loop, which also rolls up each finished UTC day. TELEMETRY_MAX_DB_MB 1024 Global disk guard: while telemetry.db plus its WAL is larger than this, POST /api/telemetry still answers 204 but drops the batch (one warning per hour in the log). The size is re-read about once a minute. TELEMETRY_MAX_EVENTS_PER_DAY 200000 Global daily cap: once this many events have been stored in the current UTC day (all callers together), further batches are dropped the same way until midnight UTC. PUBLIC_BASE_URL "" Absolute origin returned by GET /api/config (for share links). Empty: the request's own base URL. BACKUP_BUCKET "" Google Cloud Storage bucket for SQLite backups. Empty disables backup and restore. Uses Application Default Credentials. BACKUP_MODE cloudrun cloudrun (legacy, for ephemeral disks): restore at every start, upload every 60 s with a generation-safe merge, force an upload on shutdown. vm (production): the disk is authoritative. The app restores only when airports.db is missing (stray -wal/-shm removed first), never merges, and uploads the user tables (everything except the regenerable place data) only when their SHA-256 changed, plus once at a clean shutdown. In vm mode, DATA_DIR must contain the marker file .voyager-data-disk written when the disk was provisioned, or the app refuses to start. A missing DB that can't be fetched from GCS also refuses to start. GET /health then reports backup_ok and backup. BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS 300 vm mode: how often the user tables are exported and compared. backup_ok turns false after 3 missed intervals or on any failed cycle. BACKUP_EXPORT_DIR system temp vm mode: scratch directory for the export (a tmpfs in production, so the slow disk is never touched).

docs.title: Live data (optional)
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning SERPAPI_KEY "" SerpAPI key for live Google Flights fares, the fare calendar and Google's price insights. Empty means flights are LLM estimates and POST /api/flights/fare-calendar returns 503. GET /health reports serpapi_configured. SERPER_KEY "" Serper.dev key for Places-to-See data (Google Places) and the second tier of activity and place link resolution. Empty means Places to See is LLM-only.

Other web lookups (link enrichment for hotels and activities, the forex agent's rate searches, walking-tour city-page discovery, and identifying an unknown airport code) go through DuckDuckGo via the ddgs package and need no key.

docs.title: Fare watch and email alerts (optional)
docs.text:
Fare watch re-checks watched fares in the background and needs SERPAPI_KEY. Price watches for hotels, activities and whole trips use the same settings, scheduler and SerpAPI budget: there is no separate price-watch configuration, and the daily budget, the per-user share and the active limit count all kinds of watch together. Email alerts need an SMTP server; without one, alerts still appear in the app.

Variable Default Meaning FARE_WATCH_ENABLED true Starts the fare-watch scheduler at startup (only when SERPAPI_KEY is set). false stops background checks and hides "Watch fare" (GET /health reports fare_watch_available). The test suite sets it to false. FARE_WATCH_TICK_SECONDS 300 How often the scheduler looks for watches that are due. FARE_WATCH_INTERVAL_HOURS 12 Time between two checks of one watch, ±10 % jitter. FARE_WATCH_DAILY_CALL_BUDGET 200 SerpAPI calls per UTC day that all watches (fare, hotel, activity and trip) may spend together (scheduled checks, baselines and "Check now"). A fare check costs 1 call for exact dates or up to 7 with nearby dates; a hotel or activity check 1, a trip check up to 8; creating a price watch holds its worst case (hotel 2, activity 2, trip 10) and gives back what it didn't spend. Answers cached in the last 30 min cost nothing. When spent, remaining checks move to the next day and "Check now" answers 429. Searches and the fare calendar are not counted. FARE_WATCH_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER 10 Active watches per user, of every kind together (paused and ended ones don't count). FARE_WATCH_USER_DAILY_SHARE 0.3 Largest share of FARE_WATCH_DAILY_CALL_BUDGET one user's watches may spend per UTC day (at least 1 call), so one account can't use up everyone's checks. Over it, that user's checks wait for the next day and their "Check now" answers 429. SMTP_HOST "" SMTP server for alert emails. Empty disables email (GET /health reports email_alerts_available). SMTP_PORT 587 SMTP port. SMTP_USERNAME "" Login user; empty skips AUTH. SMTP_PASSWORD "" Login password. Never logged. SMTP_FROM "" From header, e.g. Voyager <alerts@example.com>. Falls back to SMTP_USERNAME, then alerts@localhost. SMTP_STARTTLS true Upgrade the connection with STARTTLS before logging in. APP_BASE_URL http://localhost:5174 Public URL of the frontend, used for the links in alert emails ("See flights", "Re-plan", and the stop-emails link, which goes to APP_BASE_URL/api/..., so the frontend's host must proxy /api). That link opens a confirmation page (GET) and the change is a POST, which is also the RFC 8058 one-click target named in the List-Unsubscribe / List-Unsubscribe-Post headers. Account emails are not verified: setting one is signed-in only and rate-limited.

docs.title: Price alerts 2.0
docs.text:
See Alerts API. With the flag off, fare and price watches, email and push behave exactly as before; the /api/alerts/* read routes are always served.

Variable Default Meaning SHARING_V2_ENABLED true Share links 2.0 (Phase 4): /api/shares* and the new-style GET /api/share/{token} fallback. Off, they answer 404 (sharing_disabled for the authenticated routes) and features.sharing is 0; legacy plan share tokens keep working either way. Contract: Sharing API. Set PUBLIC_BASE_URL in production: share links, og:url and the absolute og:image of the crawler page are built from it (else the request's base URL, which behind a proxy may not be the public host). SOCIAL_ENABLED true Phase 5: profiles, follows, blocks, the ideas feed, comments, reports and the admin moderation queue under /api/social/*. Off, every route answers 404 social_disabled and features.social is 0. Handles, privacy and limits: Social API. No AI call is ever made. PLAY_ENABLED true Phase 5: quizzes, head-to-head, leaderboards and weekly challenges under /api/play/*. Off, they answer 404 play_disabled and features.play is 0; it also needs GAME_ENABLED. PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED true Turns on the v2 pipeline: drop facts, savings rows, Deal-hunter XP, delivery rules (quiet hours, caps, grouping), the outbox flush loop, the weekly digest and adaptive scheduling. Reported as features.price_alerts_v2; the web UI shows it only when this is true (or for one browser with localStorage.tp_alerts2 = "1"). Runbook: turning it off discards pushes and emails held at that moment (quiet hours, group window); in-app alerts stay. Held items more than 12 h past due are dropped as stale instead of sent. ALERT_DIGEST_HOUR_LOCAL 9 Local hour (user's account timezone) from which a user's weekly digest is due on their chosen weekday. ALERT_FLUSH_INTERVAL_S 60 How often the delivery loop sends held (quiet-hours, grouped) pushes and emails. ALERT_ADVICE_TTL_HOURS 24 How long an AI price tip for a flight watch is cached.

Without SERPAPI_KEY, features.live_prices is false: stories, savings, the digest and suggestions work from stored data, every price shows "checked N days ago", and one-tap watch answers 503 live_prices_off.

docs.title: Push alerts (optional)
docs.text:
Fare- and price-watch alerts can also be pushed to the Android app's registered devices (/api/devices) through Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM HTTP v1). Without it, alerts still appear in the app and by email, and the Android app polls /api/notifications.

Variable Default Meaning FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE "" Path to a Firebase service-account JSON key (Firebase console → Project settings → Service accounts → Generate new private key) for the project the Android app is registered in. Its project_id picks the FCM project. Empty, or a path that does not exist, disables push (GET /health reports push_configured). Keep the file out of the repo (*service-account*.json and *-key.json are git-ignored) and readable only by the backend. The key is read once: restart the backend after rotating it. FCM_USE_ADC false With no key file: send with Application Default Credentials (on the VM, its service account through the metadata server; it needs FCM send rights, e.g. roles/firebasecloudmessaging.admin). The key file wins when both are set. FCM_PROJECT_ID "" FCM project for ADC mode; empty uses GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, which the entrypoint sets from the metadata server. NOTIFICATIONS_V2_ENABLED true Notifications 2.0: category checks on price pushes, trip pushes (T-30, T-7, T-1, morning brief) and iOS/Android push routing. Trip pushes run inside the alert loop, so they also need PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED=true (the loop does not start without it). With no FCM/APNs credentials only in-app rows are written. false restores the Phase 3 behaviour. APNS_TEAM_ID "" Apple developer Team ID for iOS pushes (APNs token auth). Inert until APNS_TEAM_ID, APNS_KEY_ID and a key (APNS_KEY_P8 or APNS_KEY_FILE) are all set; only used when NOTIFICATIONS_V2_ENABLED=true, which routes iOS devices to APNs and Android devices to FCM. APNS_KEY_ID "" Key ID of the APNs auth key (.p8). APNS_KEY_P8 "" The .p8 key contents (PEM; \n escapes accepted). Wins over APNS_KEY_FILE. APNS_KEY_FILE "" Path to the .p8 key file. APNS_BUNDLE_ID io.github.rupakc.travelplanner The iOS app's bundle id (apns-topic). APNS_SANDBOX false Use Apple's sandbox host (development builds).

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning ADMIN_USERNAME admin Username of the seeded admin. ADMIN_PASSWORD "" Password for the seeded admin. Empty means no admin is created. Used only when that user does not exist yet; the seeded admin is not forced to change it. ADMIN_EMAIL "" Optional email for the seeded admin.

With SIGNUP_ENABLED=true and email delivery available, anyone can create an account with POST /api/auth/signup (a verification email is sent first) unless SIGNUP_MODE=invite; admins can still create users from the Admin page, and those accounts count as verified for AI. Contract: Accounts API.

docs.title: Sign-up, sessions and email links
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning SIGNUP_ENABLED false Operator opt-in for native (password) sign-up. While false, POST /api/auth/signup answers 503 email_unavailable and GET /api/config reports signup_available: false, even when SMTP is set for fare alerts. OAuth sign-up and password reset are not affected. SIGNUP_MODE open open, or invite (sign-up and OAuth sign-up need an invite code from POST /api/admin/invites). EMAIL_LOG_LINKS false Dev only: with SMTP_HOST unset, log verification and reset links instead of sending them (also on when the base URL host is localhost). ACCOUNT_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES 30 Lifetime of verify-email and password-reset tokens (single use). PENDING_PURGE_DAYS 7 An unverified (pending) account is deleted after this many days; the hourly maintenance task also purges expired tokens. REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS 60 Mobile refresh-token lifetime (rotated on use). REFRESH_FAMILY_MAX_DAYS 365 Absolute lifetime of a refresh-token family from sign-in. MOBILE_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES 60 Access-token lifetime for client ios/android (web stays 24 h). PUBLIC_BASE_URL / APP_BASE_URL see above Every absolute URL (email links, OAuth redirect_uri, avatar URLs) is PUBLIC_BASE_URL, else APP_BASE_URL, without a trailing /.

docs.title: Sign-in providers (all optional)
docs.text:
A provider is on only when all its credentials are non-empty; otherwise its button shows "coming soon". Secrets go in Secret Manager in production. Setup per provider: Deployment on GCP.

Variable Default Meaning GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET "" Google web OAuth client. GOOGLE_NATIVE_CLIENT_IDS [] JSON list of the iOS/Android client IDs accepted by POST /api/auth/oauth/google/id-token. GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET "" GitHub OAuth app. FACEBOOK_APP_ID, FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET "" Meta app with Facebook Login. FACEBOOK_GRAPH_VERSION v24.0 Graph API version used for the profile call. FACEBOOK_EMAIL_TRUSTED false Treat Facebook's email as verified. Off by default, so a Facebook email never auto-links to an existing account. APPLE_SERVICES_ID, APPLE_TEAM_ID, APPLE_KEY_ID, APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY "" Sign in with Apple: Services ID, team, key ID and the .p8 key contents. APPLE_NATIVE_CLIENT_IDS [] JSON list of iOS bundle IDs accepted by POST /api/auth/oauth/apple/id-token. OAUTH_MOBILE_REDIRECTS ["voyager://auth/callback"] Exact-match allow-list of mobile redirect_uri values (<base>/auth/callback is always allowed).

docs.title: Daily AI quota and game
docs.text:
A signed-in user who has not verified their email cannot use AI routes (403 email_unverified). Verified users also have a per-UTC-day allowance per bucket on top of the 10-minute windows; 0 means unlimited, and admins are exempt.

Variable Default Meaning AI_DAILY_QUOTA_ENABLED true Master switch for the daily quota. AI_DAILY_QUOTA_SEARCH 20 Per day: /api/search, /api/search/sync and chat full plans. AI_DAILY_QUOTA_CHAT 100 Per day: /api/chat. AI_DAILY_QUOTA_COMPARE 40 Per day: /api/compare/destination. AI_DAILY_QUOTA_DISCOVER 20 Per day: /api/discover. AI_DAILY_QUOTA_LIGHT_AI 200 Per day: the light-AI routes. AI_DAILY_QUOTA_IMPORT 20 Per day: /api/import/extract. GAME_ENABLED true XP, badges, levels and streaks (GET /api/game/* answer 404 when off). GAME_RULES_PATH "" Alternative rules file; empty uses backend/app/game/rules.json.

docs.title: Trips and the journey
docs.text:
See Trips API. GET /api/config reports the two flags as features.journey and features.offline_pack.

Variable Default Meaning JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED true Turns on the journey UI in the web app: Trips hub, trip screen with phases, Explore, Play and You tabs. The trips API is always served. The owner can set JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED=false in app.env and restart the app to turn it off, with no rebuild. OFFLINE_PACK_ENABLED true Kill switch for the offline pack. false makes every client unregister /sw.js, clear its caches and delete saved packs on its next load (see Deployment on GCP). READY_WINDOW_DAYS 14 Days before the start date at which a dated trip becomes Ready. TRIP_MAX_EXPENSES 2000 Expenses per trip (409 expense_limit beyond). TRIP_MAX_JOURNAL 500 Journal entries per trip (409 journal_limit). TRIP_MAX_PLACES 1000 Rated or visited places per trip (409 places_limit). TRIP_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES 262144 Largest offline snapshot per trip (413 snapshot_too_large).

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
AI-calling endpoints are rate-limited per signed-in user, or per client IP for anonymous callers, in an in-process sliding window (backend/app/core/rate_limit.py). See API Reference for the endpoints in each bucket.

Variable Default Applies to RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED true Master switch. The test suite sets it to false. RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS 600 Window length. RATE_LIMIT_SEARCH 10 /api/search, /api/search/sync, and full trip plans started from chat (/api/chat also charges its own bucket) RATE_LIMIT_CHAT 30 /api/chat RATE_LIMIT_COMPARE 30 /api/compare/destination RATE_LIMIT_DISCOVER 10 /api/discover RATE_LIMIT_IMPORT 20 /api/import/extract (plan from a link, text or screenshots) RATE_LIMIT_TELEMETRY 120 POST /api/telemetry (batches per caller; a real web client sends about 40 per 10 minutes; not an AI route, so never behind ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_AI). The total across callers is bounded by TELEMETRY_MAX_DB_MB and TELEMETRY_MAX_EVENTS_PER_DAY. RATE_LIMIT_LIGHT_AI 60 Single-agent routes, /*/filtered, /api/flights/fare-calendar, /api/stress-test, /api/layover, /api/events, /api/walking-tours, creating a fare watch, its "Check now", /api/nearby, /api/live-check and changing the account email RATE_LIMIT_SOCIAL_WRITE 30 Phase 5: social writes per user (profile, follow, block, ideas, comments, reports); not an AI route. RATE_LIMIT_SOCIAL_READ 120 Phase 5: social reads per user (profiles, lists, feed). RATE_LIMIT_PLAY 60 Phase 5: every /api/play/* route per user. RATE_LIMIT_ADMIN 120 Phase 5: the admin moderation queue and decisions per user. RATE_LIMIT_SHARE_PUBLIC 120 Public share routes (GET /api/share/{token}, /page and /card.png), per client IP. RATE_LIMIT_SHARE_MANAGE 30 /api/shares create, list and revoke, per signed-in user. RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN 10 /api/auth/login attempts per client IP RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_FAILURES 10 Failed logins per username from one client IP per window; over it that IP waits for that username (checked before bcrypt, even for a correct password). Failures from other IPs never lock the real user out. RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_FAILURES_GLOBAL 200 Failed logins per username from all IPs together: a backstop against distributed guessing RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_EMAIL 10 Verify-email and password-reset requests per client IP RATE_LIMIT_EMAIL_ADDRESS 3 Emails sent to one address per window (verify, reset, resend), so nobody can be mail-bombed RATE_LIMIT_SIGNUP 5 /api/auth/signup per client IP RATE_LIMIT_OAUTH 30 /api/auth/oauth/* per client IP RATE_LIMIT_REFRESH 60 /api/auth/refresh per client IP RATE_LIMIT_ACCOUNT 30 Account writes: profile, settings, onboarding, avatar, delete

Counters live in process memory: they reset on restart and are not shared between processes or instances, so a multi-instance deployment would need a shared store. Anonymous callers are keyed by the connecting address; behind a reverse proxy all anonymous traffic shares one key unless the proxy address is replaced (for example with uvicorn --proxy-headers).

docs.title: Production (container entrypoint)
docs.text:
The image starts with python -m app.entrypoint, which execs uvicorn (one worker, --timeout-graceful-shutdown 5).

Variable Default Meaning SECRET_MANAGER_SECRETS "" Comma-separated env vars to read from Secret Manager at start (Application Default Credentials), into the process environment only, never a file. The secret id is the lower-cased, dashed name (JWT_SECRET_KEY → jwt-secret-key), or give it as ENV=secret-id. A secret with no version is skipped; a variable already set wins. Any other error stops the start. GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT from ADC Project for Secret Manager (and FCM ADC). The entrypoint sets it from the metadata server when missing. FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS "" Addresses or networks of the reverse proxy whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted (production: the compose network 172.30.0.0/24). Empty turns proxy headers off. * and 0.0.0.0/0 are refused. ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_AI true false (production) makes every AI route answer 401 unless signed in. SSE_KEEPALIVE_SECONDS 15 /api/search and /api/chat send a : keepalive comment after this much silence. When the client disconnects, every task the stream started is cancelled. PORT, GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_SECONDS 8001, 5 uvicorn port and graceful-shutdown timeout.

The entrypoint refuses to start when JWT_SECRET_KEY is empty after the secrets are read.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: LOG_FORMAT is read directly with os.getenv in backend/app/main.py, not through Settings. The default, json, gives one JSON object per line (stdlib logging with a custom formatter in backend/app/core/logging_config.py). Any other value gives plain-text logs.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
The frontend reads no environment variables at build or run time.

  • Dev: Vite proxies /api and /health to http://localhost:8001 (frontend/vite.config.js).
  • Container: nginx renders frontend/nginx.conf.template with BACKEND_URL (envsubst) and proxies /api/ and /health to it. Proxy buffering is off so SSE streams, with a 120 s read timeout. /api/ allows request bodies up to 32 MB (client_max_body_size 32m) for screenshot imports; the backend itself refuses import bodies over 30 MB.

Browser storage used by the app: tp_token (login token), tp_recent_searches_open, tp_tour_done:<username>, chat_history_<username>, and the packing-list checkbox state.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
backend/.env for local development:

# Claude: an Anthropic key and no GCP_PROJECT (LLM_PROVIDER=auto picks anthropic)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
# …or Gemini on Vertex AI (after `gcloud auth application-default login`):
# GCP_PROJECT=voyager-prod-ohzkl
JWT_SECRET_KEY=3f0c...   # 64 hex characters
ADMIN_PASSWORD=LocalDevPassword123
# Optional
SERPAPI_KEY=
SERPER_KEY=
FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE=   # e.g. /path/to/firebase-service-account.json (git-ignored name)
RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false
LOG_FORMAT=text

Values set by docker-compose.yml: LLM_PROVIDER (default auto), GCP_PROJECT, GCP_LOCATION (default global), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY (default change-me-in-compose), ADMIN_PASSWORD (default admin-dev-password), DATA_DIR=/data, BACKUP_BUCKET= (empty) and CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8080 for the backend, and BACKEND_URL=http://backend:8001 for the frontend.

Production on the VM (see Deployment on GCP): deploy/gcp/compose.yaml sets DATA_DIR=/data (the disk), BACKUP_MODE=vm, BACKUP_EXPORT_DIR=/tmp (tmpfs), AGENTS_DIR, FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=172.30.0.0/24 and LOG_FORMAT=json. Everything else is in /opt/voyager/app.env (deploy/gcp/app.env.example): SECRET_MANAGER_SECRETS, BACKUP_BUCKET, ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_AI=false, FCM_USE_ADC=true, LLM_PROVIDER=gemini, GCP_PROJECT, GCP_LOCATION, the SMTP settings and FARE_WATCH_DAILY_CALL_BUDGET=6.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
# Backend
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
# create backend/.env with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (Claude) or GCP_PROJECT (Gemini via ADC),
# plus JWT_SECRET_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD

# Frontend
cd frontend
npm install

# Optional: pre-commit hooks
make install-hooks

Run both servers with ./start.sh (backend 8001, frontend 5174) and stop them with ./stop.sh. Details: Setup and Installation.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Branch off main.
  2. Make the change with tests: backend/tests/ for Python, *.test.js(x) next to the code for the frontend.
  3. Run the checks locally with make ci from the repo root: lint (ruff and ESLint), the security scans and both test suites, mirroring CI. See Testing and CI.
  4. Push and open a pull request to main. CI (ci.yml) runs lint, security audits, both test suites with the 70% backend coverage gate, and build-only checks of the Docker images your change touches (the images that ship are Trivy-scanned by the deploy workflow on main).
  5. Merging to main publishes the docs site (docs.yml) and deploys the app: deploy.yml reruns CI, then publishes signed images that the production VM picks up within about 5 minutes, rolling back on its own if the new app is unhealthy (see Deployment on GCP). Keep schema changes additive so a rollback can always read the database.

Merged PRs are listed in the Changelog.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Backend: ruff for lint and format (ruff check, ruff format), Python 3.12, Pydantic v2 models for request and response shapes.
  • Frontend: ESLint with the project config; import lucide icons that shadow globals (Map, Image, History…) under an alias. Tailwind utility classes; keep pure logic in src/utils/ where it can be unit-tested.
  • Comment only where the reason is not obvious from the code.
  • No error handling for cases that cannot happen, and no abstractions beyond what the task needs.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Agent prompts are config. Change agent behaviour in .agents/<name>.md (name and description frontmatter plus the prompt). The Python class builds the user prompt and parses the JSON. See Agent System for adding an agent.
  • Agents return JSON, parsed by BaseAgent._parse_json.
  • Parallel first. Independent agents run concurrently; only the itinerary and stress test depend on other results.
  • Static first. Visa, SIM, tips, getting around, forex and the emergency card have static tables; an AI failure must never replace valid static data with an error.
  • Verification from evidence only. services/verification.py must stay pure (no network or LLM calls) and must never put an error key in the verification object.
  • Place data is generated. Do not hand-edit airports.csv, places.csv.gz, admin1.csv or countries.csv; regenerate them (see Place and Airport Data). hints.json is hand-curated; add a golden-set case for every hint you add.
  • Prompts pair a city with its country ("Lisbon, Portugal"), so agents do not guess the wrong namesake.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: The project is released under the MIT License (LICENSE). Place data contains data from GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0, and must keep that attribution; OurAirports data is public domain.

docs.title: Deployment on GCP (e2-micro VM)
docs.text:
The production setup for Voyager: one always-free e2-micro VM in us-east1 running the app container and Caddy, with SQLite on the VM's persistent disk. The design and its reviews are in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-gcp-lean-deploy-design.md.

Monthly cost: hosting ≈ $4 (the static IPv4 address is $3.65; the VM, the 30 GB disk and egress up to 200 GiB are free; snapshots cost cents). Gemini is extra, capped at ₹1,800 a month by a spend cap. The egress governor on the VM keeps hosting from growing under abuse.

Piece Where Project voyager-prod-ohzkl (billing account 010A0B-F39593-14A899, in INR) VM voyager-vm, e2-micro, us-east1-b, Debian 13, 30 GB pd-standard, Shielded VM, OS Login, IPv4 only (Standard tier) Site https://<a-b-c-d>.sslip.io (from the static IP). Your own domain later Images ghcr.io/rupakc/travel-planner-app and -caddy, signed by deploy.yml Data /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db on the VM's disk (authoritative) Backups user tables → gs://voyager-prod-ohzkl-voyager-backup/sqlite-backups/airports.db (when changed, every 5 min) + daily disk snapshots (keep 7) Secrets Secret Manager, read into memory at container start Files on the VM /opt/voyager (compose, app.env, site.env, images.env, governor.py, deploy.sh), /etc/voyager/governor.env 
Browser / Android ──HTTPS──► voyager-vm (e2-micro)
                              ├─ caddy  : TLS, SPA, /api + /health → app (SSE flushed)
                              ├─ app    : FastAPI + SQLite on the disk, Gemini via the VM's service account
                              └─ host   : egress governor (every minute), deployer (every minute),
                                          weekly reboot window (Sun 04:00 Berlin), unattended-upgrades (03:30 Berlin)
GitHub: merge to main → CI ∥ build + scan → sign (cosign) → GHCR `prod` tag ──(pulled by the VM)

docs.title: 1. Before you start
docs.text:
• gcloud CLI installed and signed in as the account that owns the project (gcloud auth login), with the beta component: notification channels have no GA command yet (alerting policies and uptime checks use GA commands, so alpha isn't needed). The script checks this first and stops before changing anything; install it with gcloud components install beta --quiet. A gcloud installed with apt/dnf has no component manager; see Managing gcloud CLI components.
  • You don't need to change gcloud's default project. As soon as the project exists, the script sets CLOUDSDK_BILLING_QUOTA_PROJECT=voyager-prod-ohzkl (unless you already set it), so billing, budget and monitoring calls bill their quota to this project. Without it they used the account's default quota project and failed with does not have permission to access billingAccounts (first run, 2026-11-06).
  • Check that nothing else on the billing account uses the free tier: one free e2-micro, 30 GB of standard disk and 200 GiB of Standard-tier egress are free per billing account, not per project.
  • The project voyager-prod-ohzkl exists with billing linked and aiplatform.googleapis.com enabled. The two budgets also exist already: "Voyager total (alerts)" (₹2,300, email alerts) and "Voyager Gemini spend cap" (₹1,800, a hard cap on Agent Platform). The bootstrap script finds them by name and doesn't duplicate them.

docs.title: 2. Bootstrap (together, once)
docs.text:
Preview every command first. The dry run prints the commands and calls nothing:

infrastructure/gcp/bootstrap.sh --dry-run voyager-prod-ohzkl 010A0B-F39593-14A899 you@example.com

Then run it for real (it is idempotent: re-running skips whatever exists):

infrastructure/gcp/bootstrap.sh voyager-prod-ohzkl 010A0B-F39593-14A899 you@example.com

It enables the APIs and creates:

  • the vm-runtime service account, with two custom roles and per-resource grants: voyagerGeminiInvoker (only aiplatform.endpoints.predict, which authorises Gemini prompt requests), voyagerFcmSender (only cloudmessaging.messages.create), objectUser on the backup bucket only, and secretAccessor on each secret;
  • the static IP and the firewall: 80/443 open, 22 only from IAP; the default network's SSH/RDP-from-anywhere rules are deleted;
  • the bucket and the empty secrets;
  • the snapshot schedule, attached to the VM's boot disk;
  • the VM, and the uptime check with its alert.

CI has no identity in GCP: it pushes to GHCR and signs with Sigstore.

During rollout, check the narrow Gemini role with one real search. If Vertex answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, the call needs another permission: add it to GEMINI_PERMS and re-run the script. Don't fall back to roles/aiplatform.user. The VM starts provisioning itself straight away (section 4); the app waits for its secrets.

Optional overrides via environment: ZONE, BUCKET, SITE_HOST (your own domain), ACME_EMAIL, BUDGET_CURRENCY/TOTAL_BUDGET/AI_SPEND_CAP (used only when a budget is missing), CLOUDSDK_BILLING_QUOTA_PROJECT.

The host bundle (deploy/gcp without its tests, sent as instance metadata) is built with COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 and without extended attributes or AppleDouble files (--no-mac-metadata --no-xattrs on macOS, --no-xattrs with GNU tar), from a sorted file list. Built on a Mac it used to carry com.apple.provenance as LIBARCHIVE.xattr headers, which Debian's tar warned about on every boot.

Spend cap fallback. If the script can't create the spend cap through the Budget API (it has no gcloud flag yet), create it in the console: Billing → Budgets & alerts → Create budget → Spend cap enforcement, name "Voyager Gemini spend cap", project voyager-prod-ohzkl, service Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (C7E2-9256-1C43), amount ₹1,800. When the cap trips, Gemini calls fail until the 1st (or until you lift it on the budget's page), and the rest of the app keeps working.

docs.title: 3. Secrets
docs.text:
The secrets are created empty, and you add the values. They go from your terminal to Secret Manager and never touch the VM's disk, the repo or a log. Use printf (no trailing newline) and read -s (no shell history):

P=voyager-prod-ohzkl
openssl rand -base64 48 | tr -d '\n' | gcloud secrets versions add jwt-secret-key --data-file=- --project=$P
read -rs V; printf '%s' "$V" | gcloud secrets versions add admin-password --data-file=- --project=$P; unset V
read -rs V; printf '%s' "$V" | gcloud secrets versions add serpapi-key    --data-file=- --project=$P; unset V   # optional
read -rs V; printf '%s' "$V" | gcloud secrets versions add serper-key     --data-file=- --project=$P; unset V   # optional
read -rs V; printf '%s' "$V" | gcloud secrets versions add smtp-password  --data-file=- --project=$P; unset V   # optional

There is no Anthropic key in production: Gemini on Vertex AI uses the VM's service account (LLM_PROVIDER=gemini, GCP_PROJECT, GCP_LOCATION=global in app.env).

  • jwt-secret-key is required: the app refuses to start without it.
  • The app runs as uid 10001 and Caddy as uid 10002. Both drop all capabilities, and only the app container can reach the metadata server: the governor's VOYAGER-GUARD chain blocks Caddy.
  • A secret with no version is simply skipped.
  • After changing a secret, restart the app: sudo docker compose -f /opt/voyager/compose.yaml --project-directory /opt/voyager restart app (or wait for the next deploy).

Email (optional). For the governor, deploy and alert emails, set the non-secret SMTP settings as instance metadata (voyager-smtp-host, voyager-smtp-port, voyager-smtp-username, voyager-smtp-from). Also set SMTP_HOST etc. in /opt/voyager/app.env for the app's alert emails. Port 25 is blocked on GCE; use 587.

Firebase (push). Add Firebase to voyager-prod-ohzkl in the Firebase console and register the Android app there. Download its new google-services.json for the Android build, whose PROD_BASE_URL must be the site URL. The VM sends pushes with its own service account (FCM_USE_ADC=true), so there is no key file.

docs.title: 4. First boot and first deploy
docs.text:
Images. Merge to main (or re-run the Deploy workflow) so that deploy.yml publishes the first signed images. Then, once, make both GHCR packages public (GitHub → Packages → travel-planner-app / travel-planner-caddy → Package settings → Change visibility → Public), so the VM can pull them without credentials.

Watch the VM provision itself:

gcloud compute ssh voyager-vm --zone=us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap -- \
  sudo journalctl -u google-startup-scripts -f

first-boot.sh installs Docker Engine and the compose plugin, configures zram swap and unattended-upgrades, unpacks the host bundle from instance metadata into /opt/voyager, and writes the data-disk marker /var/lib/voyager/data/.voyager-data-disk. It also installs the systemd units, runs the first deploy, and then starts voyager.service with --no-block (the script runs inside google-startup-scripts.service, so it never waits on another unit). The unit must be active even though the first deploy, not the unit, started the containers: only an active unit runs its ExecStop (graceful stop and backup flush) at shutdown. If the first deploy fails, the unit's start is skipped (no images.env yet) and deploy.sh starts it once a later deploy lands. The unit's compose up, deploy.sh and first-boot.sh's own compose up all hold /run/voyager-deploy.lock, so they never run at the same time. Each later boot re-runs it, which is harmless, and applies any changed compose.yaml/app.env with compose up -d. It fails closed: when required metadata (voyager-bucket, voyager-site-host, voyager-acme-email, voyager-alert-email, the bundle) is missing or the metadata server errors, it stops rather than write empty settings such as BACKUP_BUCKET=. /opt/voyager/app.env is required by compose.

Disk benchmark (rollout step 3). pd-standard is slow (about 3.6 MiB/s). Benchmark it; if image pulls and the first reseed are painful, switch to a 10 GB pd-balanced boot disk (about +$1/month).

sudo apt-get install -y fio && sudo fio --name=t --filename=/var/lib/voyager/fio.tmp --size=256M \
  --rw=randrw --bs=4k --direct=1 --runtime=30 --time_based && sudo rm /var/lib/voyager/fio.tmp

Check the unit. After the first boot has finished (and after every reboot):

gcloud compute ssh voyager-vm --zone=us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap -- systemctl is-active voyager

It must print active. On the first boot of 2026-11-06 it printed inactive although the containers were up, so a shutdown would have skipped the graceful stop and the backup flush. If you see inactive and /opt/voyager/images.env exists, run sudo systemctl start voyager (a no-op compose up -d); if it is failed, see journalctl -u voyager. CI checks this with deploy/gcp/tests/first_boot_sim.sh (job host-checks).

Smoke test. Then check:

  • https://<host>/health shows "backup_ok":true.
  • Log in, run a search (the results stream) and send a chat message.
  • Run a watch check (Alerts → Check now) and send a push to a real phone.
  • Reboot: sudo systemctl reboot. Afterwards systemctl is-active voyager prints active again.
  • Run both restore drills (section 7) and the governor test (section 8).
  • Deploy during an active search: Caddy holds new requests while the app restarts, but open streams end.

docs.title: 5. Migrating the old-prod users (decision §13.4)
docs.text:
The 2026-08-30 export is 886 MB, almost all of it a broken sqlite_sequence table. Strip it to the user tables on your laptop. The export is opened read-only, and the tool checks its hash before and after:

python3 infrastructure/gcp/migrate_old_prod.py --out /tmp/voyager-migration/airports.db
cat /tmp/voyager-migration/migration-report.md     # per-table counts must match

The dry run on 2026-11-06 migrated users 17, plans 11, preferences 8, taste signals 73 and feedback 2 (about 270 KB). preferences.visited_destinations is no longer in the schema and is dropped. Price watches, notifications and devices didn't exist then.

Put the file where restore-if-missing finds it. Restore happens only when the disk has no DB, so the order matters:

  1. Before the first boot (the right time, right after bootstrap and before the first images are published): upload it, as below. The first start restores it.
  2. If the app already started (it created an empty DB): run sudo systemctl stop voyager on the VM, upload the file, run sudo rm -f /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db* (keep the marker), then sudo systemctl start voyager.

Upload:

gcloud storage cp /tmp/voyager-migration/airports.db \
  gs://voyager-prod-ohzkl-voyager-backup/sqlite-backups/airports.db

At start, the app sees no DB on the disk, restores this file and reseeds the place data. The old passwords keep working.

docs.title: 5a. Forgotten password or a new admin
docs.text:
There is no self-service reset; the operator sets a password on the VM. The tool asks for it twice with no echo, so it never appears in shell history, ps or a log, and nobody else (including an assistant) has to see it:

gcloud compute ssh voyager-vm --zone=us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --project=voyager-prod-ohzkl -- -t \
  sudo docker exec -it voyager-app-1 python -m app.set_password admin
  • A reset also reactivates the account and skips the forced change on next login (you chose the password).
  • New admin: python -m app.set_password NEWNAME --create --admin.
  • Minimum length is the app's (8 characters). The change reaches the GCS backup within 5 minutes.

docs.title: 6. Day-to-day: deploys and rollback
docs.text:
• Auto-deploy. Every merge to main that passes all of CI moves the prod tags to images signed by deploy.yml. Each image is built and Trivy-scanned while CI runs (jobs build-app, build-caddy); only after CI and its own build passed is it signed and its prod tag moved (promote-app, promote-caddy), so every signed image has passed CI, and a failure of one image never holds back the other. An image whose inputs didn't change isn't rebuilt and its prod tag isn't moved (labels io.voyager.app-inputs / io.voyager.caddy-inputs, deploy/ci/image-inputs-id.sh), so a frontend-only merge never restarts the app (open chats survive) and a backend-only merge leaves the SPA alone. Pip's version ranges in backend/requirements.txt resolve at build time and are not part of that id: a weekly refresh (Mondays 04:17 UTC, the Deploy workflow on a schedule) rebuilds both images without cache, so dependency and base-image fixes flow; it restarts the app once a week after draining open streams. Each image records its last refresh in the label io.voyager.fresh-at, and any Deploy run, a push included, refreshes an image whose prod copy is over 8 days old or lacks the label. So a scheduled run that a queued push replaced (the concurrency group keeps only the newest pending run) still gets its refresh with the next push. GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days without repository activity (it emails the owner): re-enable them with gh workflow enable deploy.yml and gh workflow enable prod-scan.yml, or in the Actions tab (select the workflow, "Enable workflow"). Until then, the next push still refreshes stale images, but nothing scans prod daily. A daily scan (prod-scan.yml) checks the two prod images with the same Trivy policy and fails visibly, without touching anything. Within a minute voyager-deploy.timer on the VM resolves prod to a digest and checks the cosign signature: it must come from rupakc/travel-planner's deploy.yml on refs/heads/main. It then pulls by digest, waits up to 90 s for open SSE streams to end (the same drain as for Caddy, logged as drain: …; an automatic rollback doesn't wait), pins the digest in /opt/voyager/images.env (keeping the previous one), runs docker compose up -d, and waits up to 240 s for the app to report healthy (longer than the container's 180 s start period, so a slow reseed isn't mistaken for a failure). Each run also converges: compose up -d brings back anything that was stopped, e.g. by a Docker upgrade.
  • Automatic rollback. If the new app isn't healthy, the previous digest goes back in. The bad digest is held in /opt/voyager/failed-digests and never retried. You get an email if SMTP is set. Before health counts, deploy.sh checks that the container really runs the new image's ID; if compose up failed or left the old container, the new digest is rolled back too.
  • Held vs retried. Only deterministic failures hold something:
  • Held: content that fails its checks (SPA, Caddyfile validation, a Caddyfile Caddy refuses), and an app that never gets healthy (by digest, in failed-digests).
  • Held by runtime id: a Caddy runtime that fails its checks after a recreate, in /opt/voyager/held-runtimes.
  • Held as well: an SPA release that Caddy serves wrongly right after the switch (it is switched back).
  • Retried after 5 min, nothing held: infrastructure failures (pull, docker create/cp, compose up, a full disk, Caddy or its admin API not answering). A compose up that fails, or leaves the old container, twice in a row for the same digest holds it.
  • While the app only waits to retry, the edge still deploys. So a frontend release can go live before its app (the app waiting to retry, or held after a failed health check). Frontend changes must therefore work against the previous backend: feature-detect new endpoints or fields, and never assume an API change is live just because the SPA is.
  • The reverse holds too: the two images are built, scanned and promoted independently (a failed Caddy build or scan never holds back the app, and vice versa), so a new app can run behind the previous SPA for as long as the Caddy side is held or failing. Backend changes must keep serving the previous SPA: never remove or rename an endpoint, a field or its meaning in one step. Add the new one, ship the SPA that uses it, and remove the old one in a later merge.
  • Refused images (downgrades, no build label) are removed from the disk.
  • Releasing a hold: publish a new digest (merge a fix, or run Deploy by hand: gh workflow run deploy.yml --ref main rebuilds both images, -f force=false only what changed), or delete the digest's line in /opt/voyager/failed-digests (runtime ids: /opt/voyager/held-runtimes).
  • A build label that can't be read is refused (fail closed), never treated as "not a downgrade".
  • Emails and repeated error logs go out at most once an hour per kind.
  • Manual rollback to the previous app digest: sudo /opt/voyager/deploy.sh --rollback. The digest you rolled back from is held: it goes into /opt/voyager/failed-digests, so the timer doesn't redeploy it while prod still points there. Publishing a newer digest ends the hold, because only the listed digests are skipped. To release a held digest by hand, delete its line.
  • No silent downgrades. An image built by an older deploy run than the running one (label io.voyager.build) is refused, even if prod points at it. That covers a moved tag and a re-run of an old workflow. To deploy it on purpose: sudo /opt/voyager/deploy.sh --allow-downgrade.
  • Caddy image (SPA + Caddyfile + Caddy runtime): also automatic, within a minute. There is no weekly window for it anymore (--window is accepted and ignored). For each new signed Caddy digest deploy.sh:
  • copies /srv and the Caddyfile out of the image (docker create + docker cp; the image never runs) into /var/lib/voyager/edge/releases/<full digest>/. It refuses symlinks, devices and anything else that isn't a regular file or directory, an index.html that loads a missing /assets/… file, and more than 200 MB. Files become root-owned 0644/0755.
  • switches the relative symlinks current → new, prev1 → old current, prev2 → old prev1 (atomic rename). Caddy mounts /var/lib/voyager/edge read-only at /edge, serves the SPA from /edge/current/srv and looks /assets/* up in current, prev1 and prev2, so a browser still holding an older index.html gets its lazy chunks. A missing asset is an uncached 404. Three releases are kept; older ones are deleted.
  • SPA only changed: nothing restarts. It checks through Caddy that / is the new index.html and one of its assets loads; otherwise it switches back.
  • Caddyfile changed: it adapts and validates the new Caddyfile in a throwaway container (no network, read-only, real SITE_HOST/ACME_EMAIL), then loads it through Caddy's admin API (127.0.0.1:2019 inside the container). That's graceful: open connections, SSE included, keep running. If Caddy refuses it, Caddy keeps its old config, the symlinks go back, the digest is held and you get an email.
  • Caddy runtime changed (the label io.voyager.caddy-runtime, a hash of the pinned base image digest and the runtime lines of caddy.Dockerfile; see deploy/gcp/caddy-runtime-id.sh): it waits up to 90 s for open SSE streams to end (the app's GET /internal/streams, reachable only on the compose network), recreates the container, and checks Caddy without needing a valid certificate: the container runs the new image, the admin API answers, /edge/current/srv/index.html is readable, and plain HTTP gets the site's redirect to HTTPS. HTTPS must serve the release's / and an asset: a wrong answer always fails. No HTTPS answer at all is accepted only if HTTPS gave no answer before the change either (probed first; e.g. no certificate yet) or on a first deploy. The same rule applies to a converge recreate and to --rollback-caddy. The previous image is deleted only after the new runtime passes. If the checks fail, it rolls back to the previous image and release, holds that runtime id in /opt/voyager/held-runtimes and emails you. Later images with a held runtime still ship their SPA and Caddyfile, on the current runtime; only a new runtime id is recreated onto. Expect this when the upstream caddy:2.11-alpine image is rebuilt (roughly monthly) or caddy.Dockerfile's runtime part changes.
  • A changed compose.yaml for Caddy (after --update-host) is also applied with the drain first: the converge step compares compose's config hash with the running container's.
  • images.env: CADDY_IMAGE/PREV_CADDY_IMAGE is the runtime compose runs and changes only on runtime changes; CADDY_CONTENT_IMAGE/PREV_CADDY_CONTENT_IMAGE is where the live SPA and Caddyfile came from. Every digest, content-only ones included, is cosign-verified, and downgrades are refused as for the app (io.voyager.build; for content, compared with the live release's BUILD file).
  • Timing. The deploy workflow takes about 3.5–4.5 min: CI's slowest jobs (test-backend, test-deploy-kit, host-checks) take ≈ 2–3.2 min each, the build jobs (≈ 1–2 min each) run alongside them, and each promote job (cosign sign + verify, then the tag moves) adds ≈ 40–60 s. The VM then notices within ≈ 60 s (voyager-deploy.timer: every 60 s, ±5 s). An SPA/Caddyfile change is live ≈ 30–60 s later (cosign ≈ 10–20 s plus pulling only the small SPA layer, since the runtime layers are shared). An app change takes ≈ 1–4 min more (pull, drain of open streams up to 90 s, health check). Merge to live, estimated from the job times of the 2026-11-06/07 runs (before this change: 7–9 min, measured 8 min 53 s):
  • Frontend-only (frontend/, the Caddyfile): only the Caddy image is rebuilt; the app isn't touched (no restart). ≈ 4.5–6 min.
  • Backend-only (backend/, .agents/): only the app; the SPA isn't touched. ≈ 5.5–8.5 min, ≈ 6 typical (no open streams, healthy at the first 30 s health check).
  • Both: ≈ 6–9 min.
  • Neither (docs, tests, workflows): nothing is built and prod doesn't move; CI only.
  • A new base image digest (python:3.12-slim; caddy:2.11-alpine, node:20-alpine) counts as a change of that image.
  • On the VM, a run with nothing new costs one cached anonymous GHCR token (refreshed every 4 min), two HEAD requests and one docker ps: no pull, no cosign, no compose. Converge (compose up -d) runs only when compose.yaml, site.env, app.env or images.env changed, or a service isn't running. A GHCR 429 backs off (Retry-After, else 1, 2, 4 … up to 30 min). A failed signature check is retried after 10 min, not every minute.
  • Rollbacks, by part:
  • App: sudo /opt/voyager/deploy.sh --rollback (as before).
  • SPA + Caddyfile: sudo /opt/voyager/deploy.sh --rollback-edge. It swaps current and prev1 (no restart; the Caddyfile is reloaded if it differs), holds the digest you left and releases the one you return to. It's a toggle: running it again undoes it.
  • Caddy runtime: sudo /opt/voyager/deploy.sh --rollback-caddy. It checks the live Caddyfile against the previous image, drains, recreates and holds. If the Caddyfile doesn't fit the old runtime, run --rollback-edge first.
  • --rollback-caddy holds the runtime id you left (/opt/voyager/held-runtimes), so a frontend-only merge afterwards ships its SPA on the old runtime instead of recreating Caddy onto the one you rolled back from.
  • Held digests are in /opt/voyager/failed-digests, held runtimes in /opt/voyager/held-runtimes, refused downgrades in /opt/voyager/refused-digests. Delete a line to release one.
  • If /var/lib/voyager/edge is lost and can't be rebuilt, app deploys and --rollback keep working; Caddy is left alone and you get one email an hour. The live content image is kept until it is replaced, so the rebuild needs no registry.
  • Logs. Docker keeps 10 MB × 5 per container on the VM; there is no Cloud Logging agent and so no ingestion bill.
  • sudo docker compose -f /opt/voyager/compose.yaml --project-directory /opt/voyager logs -f app
  • journalctl -u voyager-deploy -u voyager-governor (deploys log SPA live: release …, Caddyfile reloaded (graceful), drain: …, Caddy healthy on the new runtime …)
  • ls -l /var/lib/voyager/edge/ shows which release current, prev1 and prev2 point at; cat /var/lib/voyager/edge/current/SOURCE shows its image.
  • Host scripts changed (deploy/gcp/**): re-run infrastructure/gcp/bootstrap.sh --update-host …, then on the VM run sudo google_metadata_script_runner startup. It returns as soon as the bundle is unpacked and compose up -d has applied the changes; units are started with --no-block, so it never waits on itself. Afterwards check IPv4 forwarding: cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward must print 1, and curl -m 10 https://<host>/health must answer. If it prints 0, see Troubleshooting.
  • Schema changes stay additive. A rollback must never meet a DB it can't read.

docs.title: Offline pack and the journey flag
docs.text:
• Service worker. The offline pack's service worker is /sw.js, served by Caddy with Cache-Control: no-cache so a new deploy is picked up on the next load. It is registered only when a user saves an offline pack, caches the app shell and the hashed /assets/* files listed in /sw-assets.json, and never intercepts /api/*. Trip data lives in the browser's IndexedDB, not on the VM.
  • Kill switch. Set OFFLINE_PACK_ENABLED=false in app.env and restart the app. GET /api/config then reports features.offline_pack: false, and each client unregisters the worker, deletes the voyager-* caches and removes saved packs on its next load. Set it back to true to allow packs again.
  • JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED. On by default. To turn the journey UI off, set JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED=false in app.env and restart the app: the SPA then shows the classic search-first app and the new paths (/trips, /explore, /play, /you) fall back to /. The trips API is served either way, so flipping the flag needs only an app restart, never a rebuild.

docs.title: 7. Backups and restore drills
docs.text:
The disk is authoritative (BACKUP_MODE=vm):

  • The app restores from GCS only when airports.db is missing and the data-disk marker is present. It never merges.
  • Every 5 minutes it exports the user tables to tmpfs and uploads them only when their SHA-256 changed. It flushes once more on a clean shutdown.
  • /health reports backup_ok. The uptime check alerts you when that is false, or when the site is down, for 10 minutes.
  • Daily disk snapshots (kept 7 days, stored in us-east1) are crash-consistent copies of the whole disk.

Which copy to restore from. GCS holds the user tables at most about 5 minutes old; a disk snapshot can be up to 24 hours old.

  • When the disk is lost, prefer GCS: start from a fresh disk with the marker and no DB, and the app restores from GCS.
  • When you do restore a snapshot (the OS or Docker state is broken), the snapshot's DB is older than GCS, and the next changed export would overwrite the newer GCS copy. GCS keeps up to 100 noncurrent versions for 30 days, so nothing is lost, but restore in this order:
  • Stop the app on the restored VM: sudo systemctl stop voyager.
  • Download the current object: gcloud storage cp gs://voyager-prod-ohzkl-voyager-backup/sqlite-backups/airports.db /tmp/gcs.db.
  • Replace the snapshot's DB with it as uid 10001: sudo rm -f /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db*, sudo install -o 10001 -g 10001 -m 0644 /tmp/gcs.db /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db. Or simply delete the snapshot's DB and let restore-if-missing fetch it.
  • Start the app: sudo systemctl start voyager. It reseeds the place data.

Drill A, fresh disk from GCS (about 5 min of data at risk). Then log in and check the plan counts:

sudo systemctl stop voyager
sudo mv /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db.drill   # keep the marker!
sudo rm -f /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db-wal /var/lib/voyager/data/airports.db-shm
sudo systemctl start voyager            # restores from GCS, reseeds place data

Drill B, new VM from a snapshot. Create a disk from the newest snapshot of voyager-vm and boot a temporary VM from it, with no static IP, an ephemeral address and the same service account. Check /health over IAP port forwarding, then delete the temporary VM and disk.

After a real snapshot restore, the governor's counter is up to 24 hours old. Raise it to Monitoring's month-to-date sent_bytes_count for the VM (Metrics Explorer), or to a safe 150 GiB:

sudo /opt/voyager/governor.py seed --gib 150

Refusals you may see: - has no .voyager-data-disk means the data directory isn't the provisioned disk (a wrong mount). Fix the mount; never just create the marker on an empty directory. - restore … failed means the DB is missing and GCS couldn't be read. The app won't start empty over a good backup; fix access and restart.

docs.title: 8. Egress governor
docs.text:
Egress on the Standard tier is free up to 200 GiB a month per billing account, then $0.085/GiB. The governor enforces this on the VM itself (/opt/voyager/governor.py, every minute, rules in Docker's DOCKER-USER chain).

How the rules are applied:

  • The governor owns DOCKER-USER; don't add rules of your own there.
  • Its rules are replaced in one iptables-restore transaction, validated first. A rejected ruleset leaves the previous rules in force and sends one email ("egress governor rules FAILED to apply", and another when they apply again). The voyager-governor unit then fails, so it shows in systemctl --failed.
  • CI runs the real rules against iptables-nft on Debian 13 for every tier (job host-checks).
  • Every tick first checks /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward, before it reads the egress state, so a corrupt state.json can't stop the check. The check keeps its own small state in /var/lib/voyager/governor/ip_forward.json. If forwarding is 0, the governor sets it back to 1 and logs an error, so a reset costs at most about a minute of downtime. Emails:
  • after a successful restore: "net.ipv4.ip_forward was reset to 0; restored to 1", at most one a day;
  • when the restore fails: "could NOT be restored", sent at once on the first failure even if a restore email went out shortly before, then repeated at most once a day, plus one email when forwarding is back to 1.

See Troubleshooting. - Applying the rules also sets the FORWARD policy to DROP when it isn't already. Docker sets DROP only when it turns forwarding on itself, and with 99-voyager-docker.conf forwarding is already on at boot. Only the built-in policy is changed; Docker's own chains are left alone. Check with sudo iptables -S FORWARD | head -1, which must print -P FORWARD DROP.

Month-to-date egress (billing month, 00:00 America/Los_Angeles) Action always each client IP: ≈ 4 Mbit/s and ≈ 3 GiB per 24 h; whole NIC shaped to 50 Mbit/s 150 GiB email warning; NIC shaped to 20 Mbit/s 200 GiB ports 80/443 closed until the month resets; email

One IP needs over 60 days to use the whole allowance, so a single abuser can't close the site. The counter counts every byte the VM sends, including free Google traffic, so it errs towards closing early. It survives reboots.

sudo /opt/voyager/governor.py status            # month, tier, GiB used
sudo ipset save voyager_perip | sort -k8 -n | tail   # top talkers (bytes in the last 24 h)
sudo /opt/voyager/governor.py reopen --extra-gib 20   # reopen; closes again 20 GiB later (≈ $1.70 overage)
