Either an Anthropic API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), or Gemini on Vertex AI: a Google Cloud project with the Vertex AI API enabled, Application Default Credentials (gcloud auth application-default login) and GCP_PROJECT set. With the default LLM_PROVIDER=auto, GCP_PROJECT selects Gemini; an Anthropic key without it selects Claude. Without either the app starts, but every AI section fails.
  • Docker with Compose, only for the container setup.
  • Optional: a SerpAPI key (SERPAPI_KEY) for live Google Flights fares, the fare calendar and price insights, and a Serper key (SERPER_KEY) for Places-to-See data and link resolution. Without them, flights come from the LLM and the fare calendar is hidden.

docs.title: Option A: start.sh (recommended for development)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rupakc/travel-planner.git
cd travel-planner

# Backend dependencies (a virtualenv is recommended)
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt          # add -r requirements-dev.txt for tests and linters
cd ..

Create backend/.env. The backend reads .env from its working directory, which is backend/ when started by start.sh:

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...        # Claude (LLM_PROVIDER=auto picks it without GCP_PROJECT)
# GCP_PROJECT=voyager-prod-ohzkl    # …or Gemini on Vertex AI, via ADC
JWT_SECRET_KEY=<output of: python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))">
ADMIN_PASSWORD=<a password for the seeded admin account>
# Optional
SERPAPI_KEY=
SERPER_KEY=

Then, from the repo root:

./start.sh              # backend on :8001, frontend on :5174
./start.sh --backend    # just one side
./start.sh --frontend
./stop.sh               # stop both (--backend, --frontend, --force)

start.sh runs uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8001 from backend/ and npm run dev (Vite on port 5174) from frontend/. It runs npm install when node_modules is missing, warns when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or backend/.env is missing, waits up to 30 s for each port, writes PIDs to .pids/ and logs to .logs/backend.log and .logs/frontend.log. stop.sh gives each process a 10 s grace period; --force sends SIGKILL.

Open http://localhost:5174. The API's Swagger UI is at http://localhost:8001/docs.

docs.title: Option B: by hand
docs.text:
# Terminal 1
cd backend && pip install -r requirements.txt && uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001 --reload

# Terminal 2
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev

The Vite dev server proxies /api and /health to http://localhost:8001 (frontend/vite.config.js). The frontend has no .env and reads no VITE_* variables.

docs.title: Option C: Docker Compose
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rupakc/travel-planner.git
cd travel-planner
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...   # or put it in a .env file at the repo root
docker compose up --build
  • Frontend (nginx): http://localhost:8080
  • Backend: http://localhost:8001 (Swagger UI at /docs)

docker-compose.yml builds the backend from the repo root (context: ., dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile), because the image copies both backend/ and .agents/. Compose reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY and ADMIN_PASSWORD from your shell or a root .env. If unset, JWT_SECRET_KEY falls back to change-me-in-compose and ADMIN_PASSWORD to admin-dev-password; change both for anything other than a local trial. The backend stores its database in the backend_data volume (DATA_DIR=/data), GCS backup is off, and the frontend waits for the backend's /health check. docker compose down -v also deletes the volume and therefore all users and plans.

docs.title: What happens on first start
docs.text:
The backend's startup (backend/app/main.py, lifespan) runs in this order:

  1. Restore from GCS (only when BACKUP_BUCKET is set).
  2. Seed the place and airport data into $DATA_DIR/airports.db. This takes about 2 s on the first start and about 5 ms afterwards, because the seed is versioned (see Place and Airport Data).
  3. Build the in-memory airport-name index (about 0.06 s).
  4. Seed the nationalities and create the remaining tables.
  5. Seed the admin account, if ADMIN_PASSWORD is set.
  6. Start the 60 s backup loop (a no-op without BACKUP_BUCKET).

All data lives in one SQLite file, $DATA_DIR/airports.db. DATA_DIR defaults to backend/data, which is gitignored.

docs.title: First login
docs.text:
Others can create an account from the sign-in page (email verification needs SMTP_*), or an admin can create them.

  1. Open the app and sign in as admin (or your ADMIN_USERNAME) with the ADMIN_PASSWORD you set. The seeded admin is not asked to change the password.
  2. Open the Admin tab and create users with a temporary password (at least 8 characters). Those users must change it on first login.

ADMIN_PASSWORD is only used to create the admin account when it does not exist yet. Changing it later does not change an existing admin's password.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q
cd frontend && npm test

See Testing and CI for coverage, lint and the Node 20.18 workaround.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Every AI section shows an error. On Gemini: no Application Default Credentials, GCP_PROJECT unset, the Vertex AI API not enabled, or the credentials lack roles/aiplatform.user. On Anthropic: the key is missing or invalid, or the account is out of quota. Check .logs/backend.log. GET /health/agents makes one tiny call to the configured provider and reports whether the LLM is reachable.

"AI limit reached for this month". The project's Vertex AI spend cap has tripped; AI features resume on the 1st (or when the cap is lifted in Cloud Billing).

"Network Error" in the browser. The backend is not running on port 8001, which the Vite proxy expects.

No fare calendar and only estimated fares. SERPAPI_KEY is not set. GET /health reports serpapi_configured. The same key enables fare watch ("Watch fare" and the Alerts page); alert emails also need SMTP_HOST (see Configuration).

429 "Too many requests". You hit a rate limit (for example 10 searches per 10 minutes). Raise the RATE_LIMIT_* values or set RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false for local work (see Configuration).

Port already in use. Run ./stop.sh --force, or change the host port mappings in docker-compose.yml.

Log lines are JSON. That is the default. Set LOG_FORMAT to any value other than json for plain-text logs.

docs.title: Sharing API
docs.text:
Frozen with Phase 4. Changes: later changes are additive only (new fields, endpoints, kinds, options or error codes; nothing renamed, removed or re-typed). Every change needs a contract-change note in its PR and an update to this page in the same PR.

Share links 2.0 turns a plan, a trip recap or the price-alert savings tally into a share link, a share card (a PNG drawn by the server) and a public page whose Open Graph tags give a proper preview on X, Facebook, WhatsApp, LinkedIn and chat apps. The sharer chooses what is revealed, and can list and revoke links. The old POST /api/plans/{id}/share and its tokens are unchanged and keep working (see Legacy links).

docs.title: API contract
docs.text: All paths are under /api. JSON in and out, except the page (HTML) and the card (PNG). Management routes need Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and act only on the caller's shares. Errors use the Phase 1 envelope {"detail", "error_code"}; timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC. Routes that depend on the flag answer 404 when SHARING_V2_ENABLED is off.

docs.title: Discovery (additive)
docs.text: GET /config gains features.sharing: 0 | 1 (1 when SHARING_V2_ENABLED is on). Clients show the new share flow only when it is >= 1, and otherwise keep the legacy plan share (a backend without the field is the same as 0).

docs.title: POST /shares
docs.text:
Auth, bucket share_manage.

{"kind": "plan", "plan_id": 12,
 "options": {"dates": "hidden", "show_origin": false, "show_name": false},
 "locale": "en"}
  • kind: plan (a plan, covers its itinerary), recap (a trip's memories recap) or savings (the price-alert savings tally). plan_id is required for plan and recap and ignored for savings. Added in Phase 5 (additive): quiz (extra request field session_id: the caller's finished quiz session, 404 session_not_found otherwise; 404 play_disabled while Play is off; idempotent per session; the card is the pack and correct answers out of the total, e.g. Flags quiz: 4/5, never time, points or answers) and status (optional plan_id: an active, on-the-road trip of the caller, else the caller's first active trip; 422 no_active_trip when there is none; the card is Day N in Place from server data and the link answers 404 once the trip is over). Neither carries search_data/selections; both return a card like recap, and the name is shown only with show_name. More kinds may be added later; clients treat an unknown kind as a plain link.
  • options (all optional, private defaults shown): dates is hidden | month | exact; show_origin and show_name are booleans. Any other value falls back to the private default.
  • locale (optional, at most 8 characters): the language of the server-rendered page (en es de fr hi zh bn; anything else is English).
  • Idempotent per (user, kind, plan_id): a second call returns the same token and replaces its options.

Answer 200:

{"token": "…", "kind": "plan", "url": "https://host/share/<token>",
 "card_url": {"link": "https://host/api/share/<token>/card.png?size=link",
              "story": "https://host/api/share/<token>/card.png?size=story"},
 "options": {"dates": "hidden", "show_origin": false, "show_name": false},
 "created_at": "…Z"}

URLs are absolute: PUBLIC_BASE_URL, else the request's own base URL; the page's Open Graph URLs use the same rule.

Errors: 404 sharing_disabled, 404 plan_not_found (missing or not the caller's plan), 422 invalid_kind, 429 (rate limit).

docs.title: GET /shares
docs.text:
Auth, share_manage. The caller's own shares, newest first, at most 100:

{"shares": [{"token": "…", "kind": "plan", "title": "Lisbon in May", "url": "…",
             "options": {"dates": "hidden", "show_origin": false, "show_name": false},
             "created_at": "…Z"}]}

title is the plan's name (Price alerts for savings). Each row (and the POST /shares answer) also carries an additive plan_id (int, or null for savings). Additive field legacy_plan_shares: [{"plan_id", "name", "url"}] lists the caller's plans that still have a legacy share token (url is <base>/share/<token>; the token is exposed nowhere else). Errors: 404 sharing_disabled.

docs.title: DELETE /shares/{token}
docs.text: Auth, share_manage. Revokes the share: 204 with no body. The public routes answer 404 at once and the rendered card is dropped from the server cache. 404 share_not_found when the token is not the caller's, and 404 sharing_disabled. Revoking a legacy plan token is still DELETE /plans/{id}/share.

docs.title: GET /share/{token}
docs.text:
Public (no auth), bucket share_public, per client IP. Answers for both token kinds:

  • A legacy plan token answers exactly as before: name, created_at, updated_at, search_data (whitelisted fields), selections.
  • A Phase 4 token answers the same keys with the sharer's options applied, plus:
  • kind, options (the three options; no locale);
  • owner_name, only with show_name;
  • for recap and savings, card: {"headline", "stats": [{"key", "count"}], "destination"?, "period"?}. For savings, search_data and selections are empty objects and name is Price alerts.

404 ({"detail": "Shared plan not found"}) for an unknown or revoked token, or while the flag is off for a Phase 4 token.

docs.title: GET /share/{token}/page
docs.text:
Public, share_public. Server-rendered HTML for link-preview crawlers: <title>, description, og:type/site_name/title/description/image/image:width/image:height/url, twitter:card=summary_large_image (+ title, description, image), <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">, a heading, and a link to the SPA page /share/<token>. og:image is the absolute card.png?size=link. There is no inline script and no tracking. Headers: X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, Cache-Control: public, max-age=300. 404 share_not_found (a JSON error, no tags) for an unknown, revoked or disabled share; only Phase 4 tokens have a page (a legacy token answers 404, and the SPA serves it as before).

Native clients do not need this route: it exists for crawlers (see Crawlers and Open Graph).

docs.title: GET /share/{token}/card.png?size=link|story
docs.text: Public, share_public. A PNG: size=link is 1200x630 (the default, used by og:image), size=story is 1080x1920. Headers: Content-Type: image/png, X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, Cache-Control: public, max-age=300. 404 share_not_found for an unknown or revoked token; 422 for another size. 503 card_busy when too many cards are rendering at once (retry). One renderer serves every client, so web, iOS and Android show identical cards. Clients show or save the image as is and add their own caption and link.

docs.title: Card and snapshot fields
docs.text:
The page and the card are drawn from one snapshot built from a whitelist (services/share_public.py); it never holds exact dates.

Field Meaning headline 7 days in Lisbon, Trip to Lisbon, My trip to Japan: recap, Caught drops worth $412, or the plan name when there is no destination. A headline with glyphs the card font lacks (CJK, Devanagari, Bengali) falls back to a plain English one on the PNG. destination / destinations Up to 5 destination names (joined with /). days Trip length from the dates, else from the itinerary; null when unknown. stats At most three chips of counts only: plan activities, hotels, places; recap places, activities; savings drops_caught, targets_hit. Zero counts are omitted; labels are singular for 1 (1 hotel). period YYYY-MM, only when options.dates is month or exact. origin Only with show_origin. owner_name Only with show_name (the display name, else the username; never an email: a name containing @ is dropped).

docs.title: Privacy defaults and the date scrub
docs.text:
A new share reveals only the title, destination(s), number of days and the plan's selections. Everything else is opt-in:

  • dates: hidden (default) removes departure_date and return_date from search_data and scrubs the selections; month cuts every date to YYYY-MM; exact leaves the dates and selections as saved.
  • show_origin: without it origin is removed from search_data.
  • show_name: without it there is no owner_name anywhere.
  • search_data is a whitelist (origin, destination(s), dates, interests, traveller counts, pace). Email, nationality, visas, permits, accessibility needs and the raw search request are never exposed.
  • Selections scrub (hidden and month): any key whose name looks like a date or time (date, time, departure, arrival, check_in, check_out, …) is removed, and so is any string value that is an ISO date or datetime. With month, ISO date values become YYYY-MM and date-named keys keep that month. Prices and counts are untouched.
  • Always removed from new shares (every date mode): owner-private free text (itinerary_notes, itinerary_edits and any notes field). Without show_origin, origin keys (origin, leg_from, ...), a return leg's destination and flight booking links are removed from selections in every date mode, including exact.
  • Dates in strings (hidden, month): URL values that carry a date (flt=...2026-05-01, checkin=, ...) are dropped; an ISO date inside any other string drops the value (hidden) or becomes YYYY-MM (month). time_of_day and duration* keys are kept.
  • Timestamps: created_at / updated_at of a new share are null with dates=hidden, YYYY-MM with month, as saved with exact. New plan shares may carry the whitelisted search_data.import_source ({url, title}) like legacy ones. A recap answers with empty search_data and selections (only card).
  • Plan names are truncated to 200 characters on save; card headlines to 120.
  • Open Graph tags and the card show at most the month and year, even with dates=exact.
  • No XP, badge or other reward is given for sharing, and views are not counted (no tracking of visitors; the web app sends a share_view telemetry event, enum props only).

docs.title: Crawlers and Open Graph
docs.text: Production Caddy serves the SPA at /share/<token>. A request whose User-Agent matches the fixed crawler list (facebookexternalhit, Twitterbot, WhatsApp, LinkedInBot, Slackbot, Discordbot, TelegramBot, Pinterest, Skype, Embedly, Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot, iMessage, Redditbot, Mastodon) and whose path is /share/<8 to 64 URL-safe characters> is rewritten to /api/share/<token>/page. People get the SPA as before. If the app answers 4xx or 5xx (revoked share, flag off, an older build without the route) Caddy serves the SPA index.html instead, so a link never breaks. Both images ship independently, so either order of deploy is safe. The absolute URLs in the tags come from PUBLIC_BASE_URL, else the request's base URL (behind Caddy that is the public host). Search engines are told not to index: the page, the card and every public share answer carry noindex.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: Buckets per 10 minutes, in-process sliding window: share_public (default 120, per client IP, IPv6 clients keyed by /64: GET /share/{token}, /page, /card.png) and share_manage (default 30, per signed-in user: /shares create, list, revoke). Over the limit: 429 with Retry-After and a string detail. Settings RATE_LIMIT_SHARE_PUBLIC, RATE_LIMIT_SHARE_MANAGE.

docs.title: Caching and revocation
docs.text: Rendered cards sit in a small in-process TTL cache (64 entries, 10 minutes) keyed by token, size and content; revoking clears the token's entries and every public route answers 404 immediately. The one residual exposure is the HTTP cache: Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 means a browser, proxy or link-preview service that already fetched a page or card may keep showing it for up to five minutes (and previews that chat apps stored on their side can last longer; a revoked link cannot be recalled from them). Treat a revoked share as "stops working within minutes".

docs.title: Legacy links
docs.text: POST /plans/{id}/share (no body, {"share_token"}), DELETE /plans/{id}/share and the legacy tokens keep their request and response shapes, and GET /share/{token} answers them byte for byte as before; they ignore the options above (dates and origin are as the legacy whitelist). New clients should use POST /shares when features.sharing >= 1.

docs.title: Quiz and status shares (Phase 5)
docs.text: Nothing is deferred for Phase 5: kind: "quiz" (session_id, the caller's finished quiz session; the card shows the pack and score out of 5, never time or answers) and kind: "status" (plan_id, an active trip of the caller; 422 no_active_trip otherwise; the card reads "Day N in Place") are served additively, see Social and Play API.

docs.title: Sharing and Plans
docs.text: The My Plan drawer, saved plans, export and public share links.

docs.title: My Plan drawer
docs.text:
Both the Results page and Chat page carry a plan drawer. Anything in the results can be selected into it:

  • Flights: one per leg on multi-city trips (selections.flights is an array keyed by leg_index); a single round-trip selection otherwise
  • Hotel, activities, places to see, free walking tours (selections.walking_tours, keyed by url), events, SIM plan, tips, transport options and packing-list items
  • Itinerary slots: individual morning, afternoon or evening activities. A picked slot keeps its estimated start and end times, so My Plan, saved and shared plans show, for example, "Day 2 · Afternoon · 13:30–16:00".

Alongside the picks, a plan stores an itinerary snapshot and the itinerary overlays: itinerary_layout (drag-and-drop moves and removals), itinerary_edits (edited activity, location or cost) and itinerary_notes. See Trip Planning Features.

The drawer shows a live cost total (computePlanCost sums flight legs, hotel nights, and per-person activity prices) and supports drag-and-drop from result cards.

Under the plan name, Where the money goes (components/CostBreakdown.jsx) breaks that total down by category — flights, hotel, activities, SIM — as a stacked bar plus one row per category with its amount and share, biggest first. The rows come from computePlanCostBreakdown() and computePlanCost() is defined as their sum, so the parts always add up to the total. Local transport only carries free-text fares, so it's left out and the drawer says so when transport options are selected.

docs.title: Export: calendar and print/PDF
docs.text:
The My Plan drawer (Results and Chat) and the saved-plan viewer have two export buttons (components/PlanExport.jsx):

  • Add to calendar downloads an .ics file (buildPlanIcs in frontend/src/utils/planExport.js) that Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook can import. It holds one event per itinerary activity at its estimated start and end time (the same derived schedule the Results page shows, scheduleDays in utils/schedule.js, applied to the arranged itinerary), with your slot edits and notes. Picks from plans saved before timed itineraries fall back to fixed slot hours (morning 09:00–12:00, afternoon 13:00–17:00, evening 18:00–21:00). Flights are timed events from their departure time and duration (all-day when the time is unknown), the hotel is an all-day span from check-in to check-out, and selected local events cover their dates. Times are floating — they read as local time at the destination; a flight's description also gives its local arrival time and booking link. Event IDs come from the saved plan's id (or, for an unsaved plan, its route, dates and name), so two plans never overwrite each other's events and renaming a saved plan keeps its IDs. How a calendar app treats a re-import of the same file varies — some skip events they already have, some update them. Selected walking tours are not exported to the calendar, because tours carry no dates.
  • Print / PDF opens a clean, printable page of the whole plan (buildPlanPrintHtml in frontend/src/utils/planPrint.js): cost breakdown, flights, hotel, day-by-day itinerary, activities, places, free walking tours, events, SIM, transport and tips. Print it or choose Save as PDF in the print dialog. All plan text is HTML-escaped, only http(s) booking links are kept, and the page carries a Content-Security-Policy that lets nothing run except its own print button.

When a saved plan is loaded into a drawer, export (and the cost breakdown, budget status and saving) use that plan's trip details and itinerary snapshot — never the itinerary of the search currently on screen, which may be a different trip.

docs.title: Saved plans
docs.text:
Plans are stored in the plans table through /api/plans (list, create, get, rename/update, delete; each user sees only their own). The drawer can save, rename, load and delete plans, and the current plan can be dragged onto the saved-plans drop zone. Saving records Taste Graph signals (see Personalization).

A saved plan embeds a snapshot of the generated itinerary (days and estimated cost) alongside the selections, so reopening a plan months later shows the schedule as it was, including moves, edits and notes. Live verification evidence (link_verified, link_checked) is stripped from saved items, because it belongs to the live search. While a saved plan is loaded, itinerary editing is off until the user starts a new plan.

PlanViewModal shows a saved plan in full (flights per leg, hotel, the day-by-day itinerary and every selected item), each removable individually.

docs.title: Share links
docs.text:
Share calls POST /api/plans/{id}/share, which creates a random token (or returns the existing one), and copies ${origin}/share/<token> to the clipboard. Anyone with the link can open it without logging in.

GET /api/share/{token} returns a sanitised plan: the name, timestamps, the selections and only these search fields: origin, destination(s), dates, interests, traveller counts and pace. Nationality, visas, residence permits, accessibility needs and budget are dropped.

frontend/src/pages/SharePage.jsx renders a read-only trip card:

  • Route header (origin → stops in journey order) and dates
  • Flights (each leg with airline, times and price), hotel and cost summary
  • The arranged day-by-day itinerary, including edits and notes
  • Activities, free walking tours, events, SIM plan, transport picks and tips

Download as PNG draws the whole share page onto a canvas sized to fit (one pass measures and wraps every line, a second pass paints it) and downloads a single image, with no external libraries or server round-trip.

DELETE /api/plans/{id}/share revokes a link, but no UI calls it yet; it is available through the API only.

docs.title: Social and Play API
docs.text:
Status: frozen 2026-11-12 (Phase 5). Changes: later changes are additive only (new fields, endpoints, enum values, error codes; nothing renamed, removed or re-typed). Every change needs a contract-change note in its PR and an update to this page in the same PR. Clients ignore fields, enum values and notification kinds they do not know.

Phase 5 adds profiles, an ideas feed, moderation (/api/social/*) and Play (quizzes, head-to-head, leaderboards, weekly challenges; /api/play/*). Two independent flags, both default on (set either to false to turn it off): SOCIAL_ENABLED and PLAY_ENABLED (Play also needs GAME_ENABLED).

All paths are under /api, JSON in and out, Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. Nothing here is available anonymously. Errors use the Phase 1 envelope {"detail", "error_code"}.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text: GET /config gains features.social: 0|1 and features.play: 0|1 (1 = the routes exist). Off, every route below answers 404 social_disabled / 404 play_disabled. Clients feature-detect and hide the entry points otherwise.

docs.title: Privacy model (binding for every client)
docs.text:
• A handle (3-20 chars [a-z0-9_], unique, case-insensitive, reserved words refused) is the only public identity. It is chosen by the user and is never derived from the username or email. The username, email, real name, plan details and dates are never returned by any route here.
  • A user has no profile until they create one (PUT /social/profile). Profile visibility is private (default: invisible to everyone, no feed posting, not searchable, not on boards), followers or public. Every extra field is a separate opt-in, all default off: show_avatar, show_home_country, show_countries, show_level, show_badges.
  • Leaderboards are opt-in (leaderboard_opt_in, default false) and show handles only.
  • Hide Play and points (hide_game account setting): all /play/* routes answer 403 game_hidden, the user is excluded from every board and never gets quiz or challenge notifications, and the game fields (level, badges, XP) are omitted from their own profile and are never shown on it to others. The feed and profiles themselves are social, not game, and stay.
  • Text is plain. Titles, captions, comments and reasons are stored as plain text (control characters removed, whitespace collapsed, length capped). No markdown, no HTML, no auto-links; clients render them as text only.
  • Blocking is two-way and silent: a blocked pair cannot see each other's profile, ideas, comments or board rows, follow, comment, challenge or notify each other.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
GET /social/profile (own): {"handle": null|str, "visibility", "bio", "show_avatar", "show_home_country", "show_countries", "show_level", "show_badges", "leaderboard_opt_in", "home_country": str|null, "created_at"}. handle: null means no profile yet (defaults shown).

PUT /social/profile (rate bucket social_write): any subset of handle (required the first time; changeable once per 30 days, 409 handle_taken, 422 handle_invalid|handle_reserved|handle_rate_limited), visibility, bio (<= 160), the show_* flags, leaderboard_opt_in, home_country (ISO alpha-2). Answers the own-profile object. Bio goes through the keyword filter (422 content_rejected).

GET /social/profile/{handle}: {"handle", "bio", "avatar_url"?, "home_country"?, "countries"?: [alpha2], "level"?, "badges"?: [{id,tier}], "ideas_count", "followers_count", "following_count", "you": {"following": bool, "pending": bool, "follows_you": bool, "blocked": bool}}. Optional fields appear only when the owner opted in (and, for level/badges, the owner is not hidden-game). 404 profile_not_found when private, unknown, blocked either way or the owner is the caller's blocker. A followers profile shows only handle and counts to non-followers.

GET /social/handles/check?handle=: {"available": bool, "reason"?: "invalid"|"reserved"|"taken"}.

docs.title: Follow and block
docs.text:
• PUT /social/follow/{handle} -> {"state": "following"|"pending"}. Public profile: immediate. followers profile: pending until the owner accepts. private or blocked: 404 profile_not_found. Self: 422 cannot_follow_self. Daily cap 200 (429-like 422 limit_reached).
  • DELETE /social/follow/{handle} -> 204 (unfollow or cancel request).
  • GET /social/follow-requests -> {"requests":[{"handle","created_at"}]}; POST /social/follow-requests/{handle}/accept and /decline -> 204.
  • GET /social/following and GET /social/followers -> {"users":[{"handle"}], "next": cursor|null}.
  • PUT /social/block/{handle} -> 204 (also removes follows both ways); DELETE /social/block/{handle} -> 204; GET /social/blocks -> {"users":[{"handle"}]}.

Clarifications (T1). The first handle is free; the 30-day clock starts at the first change (422 handle_rate_limited carries retry_after seconds). Handles are stored lower-case. home_country that is not a known ISO code: 422 country_invalid. Following needs a handle (403 profile_required). A request to accept or decline that does not exist: 404 request_not_found. Blocking yourself: 422 cannot_block_self; a bad list cursor: 422 invalid_cursor. Because a blocked pair gets 404 profile_not_found both ways, you.blocked is always false in practice (use GET /social/blocks to unblock). followers_count, following_count and the follower/following lists leave out users whose profile is private. GET /social/profile/{own handle} works for the owner whatever the visibility. The own-profile GET never carries game fields.

docs.title: Ideas feed
docs.text:
An idea is a snapshot of one of the caller's plans or recaps with a title and caption. The snapshot is built with the same whitelist and privacy defaults as a share (no dates, no origin, no name, no prices, no private notes, no email): counts, destinations, days and the plan's selected items only.

  • POST /social/ideas {"plan_id": int, "kind": "plan"|"recap", "title": str (<=80), "caption": str (<=500), "locale"?}: needs a handle, a non-private profile and a verified email (403 profile_required|email_unverified). Limit 5 per UTC day (429-style 422 limit_reached), snapshot <= 64 KB. Answers the idea object with status: published, or held when the keyword filter is unsure (visible only to its author and admins until approved); 422 content_rejected when the filter refuses. Idempotent per (author, plan_id, kind): updates it.
  • Idea object: {"id","kind","title","caption","author":{"handle","avatar_url"?},"snapshot":{...},"likes","saves","comments","liked":bool,"saved":bool,"mine":bool,"status","created_at"}.
  • GET /social/feed?scope=for_you|following|new&cursor=&limit= (limit <= 30) -> {"ideas":[...],"next": cursor|null}. Excludes blocked pairs, hidden/removed/held ideas, and ideas of private profiles; followers-visibility authors only for their followers. new is chronological; following is chronological from followed authors; for_you ranks recency + engagement (likes, saves) + taste match (the caller's interests against the idea's tags), computed in SQLite, no AI call.
  • GET /social/ideas/{id}, DELETE /social/ideas/{id} (author), GET /social/profile/{handle}/ideas?cursor=.
  • PUT|DELETE /social/ideas/{id}/like -> 204 (idempotent; no XP).
  • POST /social/ideas/{id}/save -> {"plan_id": int}: remix. Copies the snapshot into the caller's own plans (a new plan named after the idea, source noted) and awards the author XP once per (saver, idea), never for self-saves. DELETE /social/ideas/{id}/save -> 204 (forgets the save mark; the copied plan stays).
  • Comments: GET /social/ideas/{id}/comments?cursor= -> {"comments":[{"id","author":{"handle"},"text","helpful":bool,"mine":bool,"created_at"}],"next"} oldest first; POST /social/ideas/{id}/comments {"text"<=300} (limit 30/day; held comments are shown only to their author and admins); DELETE /social/comments/{id} (comment author or idea author); PUT|DELETE /social/comments/{id}/helpful (idea author only; XP to the commenter once).

Clarifications (T2). Commenting needs the same guards as publishing (non-private profile, verified account, not restricted: 403 profile_required|email_unverified|restricted), and an idea or comment that is held, hidden or removed is reachable only by its author (not removed) and admins. Errors: 404 idea_not_found|comment_not_found|plan_not_found|not_found (report target), 422 title_invalid|text_invalid|snapshot_too_large|content_rejected|limit_reached, 403 idea_unavailable (re-posting a hidden or removed idea). Idea and comment objects carry an additive status. for_you uses an offset cursor, the other scopes an id cursor (treat both as opaque). GET /social/profile/{handle}/ideas returns {"ideas","next"}; an owner sees all their own non-removed ideas there. A saved idea copies destination(s), interests and the item names into a new plan (search_data.remix_of = {idea_id, handle}); saving again returns the existing copy while it exists. A profile report is recorded and listed under reported but never auto-hides; an admin remove on a profile sets it private. POST /admin/social/{target}/{id}/decide answers {"target","id","status"} (target profile takes the handle as id). POST .../restrict answers {"until"}; the reported queue lists published items with unresolved reports (and reported profiles). The inspirer, muse and helpful_voice badges are added to rules.json.

docs.title: Moderation
docs.text:
• POST /social/reports {"target": "idea"|"comment"|"profile", "id": str, "reason": "spam"|"abuse"|"sexual"|"violence"|"misinformation"|"other", "note"?: str (<=200)} -> 204. One report per (reporter, target); 20 per day. Three distinct reporters auto-hide the target (hidden) until an admin decides. Reports of your own content or by unverified users are accepted but do not count toward auto-hide.
  • Keyword filter (committed deny and review lists, plus: any URL or email-like token is held). No AI moderation call (cost ruling; see the plan).
  • Admin (is_admin; bucket admin): GET /admin/social/queue?status=held|reported|hidden&cursor= -> {"items":[{"target","id","status","reason_counts","excerpt","author_handle","created_at"}],"next"}; POST /admin/social/{target}/{id}/decide {"action": "approve"|"remove"} (removing a profile makes it private and also clears its bio and avatar opt-in, so the owner cannot republish the same bio); POST /admin/social/users/{handle}/restrict {"days": 1..365} (no posting, commenting, challenging), DELETE lifts it. 403 restricted for a restricted user's writes. Admin routes answer 404 when SOCIAL_ENABLED is off.

docs.title: Play
docs.text:
• GET /play/state -> {"daily":{"available":bool,"done":bool,"score":int|null,"streak":{"current","longest","freeze_available"}},"packs":[{"id","title_key","questions"}],"challenge":{"id","kind":"destination"|"featured","country"?,"done":bool}|null,"open_h2h": int}.
  • Quiz sessions: POST /play/quiz {"mode": "daily"|"pack", "pack"?: "flags"|"capitals"|"landmarks"|"cuisine", "locale"?} -> {"session_id","mode","pack","questions":[{"index","kind","prompt":{...},"options":[{"id","label"}]}],"expires_at"} (5 questions, no answers). The daily quiz is the same five questions for everyone each UTC day and can be completed once (409 already_done); a started one is resumed. Packs are unlimited but earn XP only up to a daily cap. Questions are served from a committed bank, so a quiz makes no AI call; option order and distractors are deterministic per session.
  • Implementation notes (T3, additive): packs[].questions is the size of the pack's pool. Quiz and answer responses carry extra fields: option code (ISO alpha-2, only on country-labelled options, so clients can localise the name), answers (answers so far), done, resumed, and summary once finished. Option ids are opaque (a-d), shuffled per session. Question prompt.template is one of flag, capital_of, country_of_capital, landmark_country, dish_country. A session idle for 20 minutes after at least one answer is closed as it stands (no XP; the daily stays done) and answering it is 410 session_expired; 422 invalid_pack|invalid_mode|invalid_index|invalid_choice|out_of_order, 404 session_not_found. mode: "challenge" is 422 invalid_mode until the challenge task ships. XP: quiz_perfect is 20 (cap 3/day, daily and packs), streak kind quiz.
  • POST /play/quiz/{session_id}/answer {"index": int, "choice": option id} -> {"correct": bool, "correct_choice": id, "points": int, "elapsed_ms": int, "done": bool, "summary"?: {"score","correct","total","xp"?: game_result, "streak"?}}. Answers are checked, and timed, server-side (served-at to answered-at); the client clock is never trusted. Points: 100 for correct plus up to 50 for speed (linear over 15 s), 0 if wrong. Re-answering returns the first result. A session expires after 20 minutes of the last activity.
  • GET /play/quiz/{session_id} -> session with the answers so far. GET /play/history?limit= -> own last sessions {session_id,mode,pack,score,correct,finished_at}.
  • Head-to-head (asynchronous): POST /play/h2h {"handle", "pack"} -> {"id","session_id","questions":[...]} (creator plays at once; opponent needs a non-private profile and not blocked; 422 limit_reached beyond 5 open or 10 per day). GET /play/h2h -> {"matches":[{"id","opponent":{"handle"},"pack","state":"waiting_you"|"waiting_them"|"done"|"declined"|"expired","you":int|null,"them":int|null,"winner":"you"|"them"|"draw"|null,"expires_at"}]}. POST /play/h2h/{id}/accept -> the opponent's session (same questions), play it with the normal answer route; POST /play/h2h/{id}/decline -> 204. Matches expire after 48 h. The opponent's score is revealed only when both are done.
  • Implementation notes (T4, additive): head-to-head sessions are ordinary quiz sessions of mode: "h2h" (answer them with the normal answer route; POST /play/quiz with mode: "h2h" stays 422 invalid_mode). The create and accept responses are the session view plus id (the match id); the opponent plays the creator's exact questions and option order. List entries also carry session_id (the caller's own session). Matches expire 48 h after creation (410 match_expired on accept); a non-opponent or blocked pair gets 404 match_not_found; accepting twice resumes (resumed: true); declining an accepted or declined match is 409 invalid_state. An unknown, private, blocked, hidden-game or non-existent opponent is 404 profile_not_found; challenging yourself is 422 cannot_challenge_self. The challenger must have a profile with a handle (409 profile_required) and must not be restricted (403 restricted). Limits: 5 open (not declined, not expired, not finished by both) and 10 created per UTC day (422 limit_reached). h2h_complete XP goes to both players when both have finished (cap 3 per day), reported in each session's summary.xp. open_h2h counts matches in waiting_you.
  • Leaderboards: GET /play/leaderboard?scope=global|friends&week=current|previous -> {"week":"2026-W46","rows":[{"rank","handle","score","level"?,"you":bool}],"you":{"rank","score","opted_in"}|null}. Score = the week's quiz and h2h points (Monday 00:00 UTC). Global shows opted-in users only (top 50). Friends = people the caller follows (approved) who allow it, plus the caller. Hidden-game users never appear. Only verified accounts (email-verified or admin-created) appear on a board, and at most 20 finished pack sessions per user per week count toward the weekly score (daily, head-to-head and challenge sessions always count).
  • Weekly challenge ("Know before you go"): GET /play/challenge -> {"id":"2026-W46:JP","kind","country"?,"title_key","done":bool}; start it with POST /play/quiz {"mode":"challenge"}. It is about the country of the caller's next upcoming trip when the bank covers that country, else a featured pack of the week. One XP award per ISO week.
  • Implementation notes (T4, additive): boards count the points of every finished quiz session (daily, packs, head-to-head, challenge) in the ISO week, ties share a rank, zero-point users are not listed. rows are capped at 50; you.rank is null when the caller is not on the board (no points this week, or not opted in / private profile on the global scope) and you is null without a handle. Friends scope lists the caller always, plus followed (state following) users who opted in and are not private. Hidden-game users, private profiles and blocked pairs never appear. level appears only for users with show_level. Challenge: kind: "destination" uses the first country of the soonest trip starting today or later for which the bank holds at least 3 landmarks and dishes (a trip's country comes from its destinations); kind: "featured" rotates the four packs by ISO week. GET /play/challenge and play/state.challenge carry {id, kind, country?, title_key, done} (title_key play.challenge.destination or play.challenge.featured.<pack>). POST /play/quiz with mode: "challenge" resumes a started one or answers 409 already_done once the week's challenge is finished (any country); the questions are the same for everyone with the same challenge id; XP challenge_complete once per ISO week (idempotent), plus quiz_perfect when 5/5.
  • XP: quiz_daily 10, quiz_perfect 20, quiz_pack 5 (cap 3/day), h2h_complete 10 (cap 3/day), challenge_complete 50 (once per week), idea_saved 10 (to the author, cap 5/day), comment_helpful 5. Never for likes, follows, posting or comments. Values live in app/game/rules.json; GET /game/catalog lists the new rules and badges (additive). touch_streak("quiz") keeps the daily-quiz streak (one freeze a week, never punishing).

docs.title: Notifications and sharing (additive)
docs.text:
• Notification kinds: social_idea_saved, social_new_follower (category social), social_idea_liked, social_idea_comment (category social, one per idea per UTC day), quiz_h2h_invite, quiz_h2h_result, quiz_daily (category quiz); GET /notifications/catalog gains the matching h2h_invite, h2h_result, idea_saved, new_follower templates in the 7 languages. Quiz kinds are never sent to hidden-game users. Links: /play/h2h/{id} for the quiz kinds; social_idea_saved and social_new_follower both link to /feed.
  • POST /shares (Sharing API) gains kind: "quiz" (extra field session_id: the caller's finished quiz session; card = pack and score out of 5, never time or answers) and kind: "status" (extra field plan_id: an active trip of the caller; card = "Day N in Place", from server data). Both hide the sharer's name unless show_name.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: Events, all props enums, bools or ints (no handles, no text): see Telemetry.md (social_*, play_*, admin_mod_action).

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text:
Product telemetry answers "which features are used, where do people drop out, what is slow or broken" for all Voyager clients (web today; Android and iOS later). What users are told is in Privacy; this page is the developer contract. The closed schema lives in backend/app/telemetry/registry.py (EVENTS), and a test fails if an event there is missing from this page.

It is separate from POST /api/analytics/events (signed-in only, writes log lines, endpoint unchanged), but the web client sends to that endpoint only while telemetryAllowed(), so one switch covers both.

docs.title: Envelope
docs.text:
POST /api/telemetry, JSON, optionally gzipped (Content-Encoding: gzip), auth optional:

{
  "client": {
    "anon_id": "7f9c2b0e-3c1d-4b8a-9f10-5a2d7e6c4b11",
    "session_id": "1d4a6c52-8e07-4f3b-a2c9-0b6e5d7f8a90",
    "platform": "web",
    "app_version": "1.0.0",
    "locale": "de"
  },
  "events": [
    {"event": "screen_view", "ts": 1767225600000, "screen": "/chat", "props": {"route": "/chat"}}
  ]
}
Field Rule client.anon_id, client.session_id UUIDs. One session per batch. client.platform web, android or ios. client.app_version A token (see Prop types). client.locale A token of at most 16 characters (the web sends <html lang>, e.g. de or zh-CN). events[].event A name from the tables below. Unknown names are dropped. events[].ts Milliseconds since the epoch. A missing value, or one more than 7 days from server time, is replaced by the server time. events[].screen Optional route template (a token). Dropped when it is not one. events[].props Only the props listed for that event, each passing its type check. Anything else is dropped.

A bad client block, a body that is not an object or more than 100 events is 422. Individual bad events and props are dropped silently, so a well-formed batch always answers 204. A body over 64 KB (256 KB once gunzipped) is 413. 404 means telemetry is disabled on the server. The server adds received_at and, for a signed-in caller, user_id; no IP address and no user agent are stored. Details: API Reference.

docs.title: Prop types
docs.text: Type Accepts token (id) A string of 1-64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : / - (no spaces and no @, so free text and e-mail addresses cannot pass) int An integer within ±2^53 (not a boolean) float A finite number within ±2^53 bool true or false enum One of the listed values

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The Web column says whether the web app emits the event today. Events marked "not yet" are accepted by the server so Android, iOS and later web phases can send them without a backend change.

docs.title: Lifecycle and navigation
docs.text: Event Props Web Meaning app_open none yes Collection started (page load, or consent granted later). app_background none yes Page hidden; the queue is flushed. session_start none yes First event after 30 minutes idle. screen_view route (token), referrer_route (token) yes Route changed; referrer_route is the previous route. screen_time route (token), ms (int) yes Time on the previous route, sent when leaving it or hiding the page.

docs.title: Interaction
docs.text:
Auto-captured by one delegated listener (frontend/src/telemetry/autocapture.js); input values and text content are never read.

Event Props Web Meaning ui_tap tid (token), route (token) yes Click on a button, link or other interactive element. ui_toggle tid, route, on (bool) yes Checkbox, radio or switch changed. ui_change tid, route yes Text input, select or textarea changed (never to what). ui_submit tid, route yes Form submitted.

tid is the closest data-tid; otherwise id:<id> when the element has a static-looking id (no digits, no 8+ character hex segment); otherwise auto:<tag>. It is never the visible text.
