docs.title: Settings, consent, performance, errors
docs.text: Event Props Web Meaning theme_change theme (system, light, dark) yes Theme chosen. language_change lang (en, es, de, fr, hi, zh, bn) yes Language chosen. consent choice (granted, denied) grant only The web sends only a grant. A denial is kept on the device and nothing is sent. perf metric (ttfb, fcp, lcp, inp, cls, long_task, cold_start), value (float), route (token) yes, except cold_start Web metrics from the browser timing APIs; lcp, inp, cls and long_task (a count) are sent when the page is hidden. cold_start is for the mobile apps. error kind (js, promise, api), source (token), status (int) js and promise source is a script basename and line (app.js:42) or unknown, never the message. At most 20 per page load. api is not emitted yet.

docs.title: Client rules
docs.text:
These apply to every client; the web implementation is frontend/src/telemetry/.

  • Telemetry never blocks, slows or breaks the UI. Every entry point swallows its own errors and nothing on a user path awaits it.
  • Fetch GET /api/config once at start. A 404, an error or telemetry.enabled: false turns telemetry off for the session, with no retries. This is how a client tolerates an older or self-hosted backend.
  • Events queue in memory and are sent every telemetry.flush_interval_s (15) or at telemetry.max_batch (50) events, clamped to the server limit of 100. The web client sends in idle time.
  • When the page is hidden the rest is sent with fetch(keepalive) plus the bearer token when signed in, otherwise navigator.sendBeacon (which cannot carry headers, so those events are anonymous).
  • The queue is capped at 500 events. It is persisted to localStorage (tp_tq) only when the page is hidden or a send fails, and claimed at the next start; stored events older than 7 days are discarded.
  • Three failures in a row back off exponentially; a 429 honours Retry-After. A 4xx other than 408 and 429 drops that batch (it would fail forever).
  • anon_id is a persistent random UUID (tp_anon). The session ID lives in sessionStorage and rolls over after 30 minutes idle.
  • Routes are templates (/share/:token, /plans/:id, /alerts/:id, /other), never raw URLs, so tokens and ids never leave the browser.
  • Props are filtered client-side with the same token, number and boolean rules, so free text never leaves even if a caller passes it by mistake.
  • Without consent nothing is queued or sent (below).

docs.title: Consent
docs.text: consentRequired() is true for devices in an EU, EEA, UK or Switzerland time zone (every Europe/* zone except Istanbul, Moscow, Minsk and Kiev/Kyiv, plus Reykjavik, Canary, Madeira, Azores and Faroe). Those devices send nothing until the user chooses in the one-time prompt (ConsentPrompt). Elsewhere telemetry is on and can be switched off in Preferences, Privacy (PrivacySwitch). Any visitor, signed in or not, can reopen the prompt from the Privacy choices button in the footer of every page (data-tid="privacy.choices", openPrivacyChoices()); it then marks the choice in force with aria-pressed and has a close button. The choice is stored in localStorage as tp_consent (granted or denied). A denial clears the queue and stops the collectors; a later grant starts them. The wording users see is in Privacy.

docs.title: Storage and retention
docs.text:
What Where Kept Raw events (telemetry_events) $DATA_DIR/telemetry.db, its own SQLite file in WAL mode so ingestion never contends with user data TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS (default 90); not backed up Daily rollups (telemetry_daily, telemetry_daily_totals, telemetry_rollups) airports.db Indefinitely; backed up with the user tables

Ingestion has a global disk guard on top of the per-caller rate limit (RATE_LIMIT_TELEMETRY, 120 batches per 10 minutes). While telemetry.db plus its WAL is over TELEMETRY_MAX_DB_MB (default 1024), or the current UTC day already holds TELEMETRY_MAX_EVENTS_PER_DAY stored events (default 200000), POST /api/telemetry still answers 204 but drops the batch, and logs one warning per hour at most. The file size and the day's count are re-read about once a minute and counted in memory in between, so the check costs nothing per request.

An hourly lifespan task (backend/app/telemetry/maintenance.py) rolls up every finished UTC day, re-rolls the trailing 7 days (late events from offline clients) and prunes raw events past retention. New telemetry.db files are created with auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL and each prune runs PRAGMA incremental_vacuum, so the file shrinks back after a burst (a file created before this keeps its size until a manual VACUUM). telemetry_daily_totals rows with platform = '*' hold exact distinct users and sessions across all events and platforms.

docs.title: Reading it
docs.text: GET /api/admin/telemetry/summary?days=30 (admin) returns daily users, sessions and events, top events, top screens and users_7d, the distinct users over the last 7 UTC days. The web admin page shows it as the Analytics tab, hidden when the endpoint answers 404. Settings: TELEMETRY_ENABLED, TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS, TELEMETRY_MAX_DB_MB, TELEMETRY_MAX_EVENTS_PER_DAY, RATE_LIMIT_TELEMETRY (see Configuration).

docs.title: Adding an event
docs.text:
1. Add it to EVENTS in backend/app/telemetry/registry.py with typed props. Ship the backend first: an event the deployed backend does not know is dropped silently.
  2. Add a row here (the registry test enforces that the name appears on this page).
  3. Add it to the event table in Privacy.
  4. Update the clients.

docs.title: Backend tests
docs.text:
cd backend
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt   # pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, ruff, bandit, pip-audit
python3 -m pytest -q
  • tests/conftest.py points DATA_DIR at a temporary directory (deleted at exit), sets a JWT secret, RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and an empty BACKUP_BUCKET, and seeds the place data once per session.
  • pyproject.toml sets asyncio_mode = "auto". An autouse fixture replaces the Gemini and Anthropic clients in core/llm.py with stubs, so tests never reach a model; tests that need replies fake llm.generate / llm.stream or the client (tests/test_llm.py). scripts/llm_eval.py, which does call the real model, is never run by CI (it refuses when CI is set).
  • tests/test_golden_places_runtime.py runs the 693-case golden set (tests/data/golden_places.csv) against place resolution and autocomplete and forbids web calls. tests/test_build_place_data.py checks the place-data generator. See Place and Airport Data.
  • Coverage, as CI runs it:

bash DATA_DIR=/tmp/test-data ADMIN_PASSWORD=test-admin-pw \ python3 -m pytest --cov=app --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=70

Coverage omits the agent classes, the orchestrator and chat agent, static_results.py, web_tools.py, schemas/travel.py, the seeders, backup.py and database.py.

As of 2026-10-30: 3,794 passed, 1 skipped.

docs.title: Frontend tests
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm test                    # vitest run --passWithNoTests
npm run test:coverage       # with v8 coverage, as CI runs it

Tests are *.test.js(x) files next to the code, run with vitest in jsdom (configured in vite.config.js). On Node 20.18 vitest needs NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-require-module:

NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-require-module npx vitest run

As of 2026-10-30: 38 test files, 532 tests passed.

docs.title: Lint and format
docs.text:
Check Command Backend lint ruff check backend/ Backend format ruff format --check backend/ Frontend lint cd frontend && npx eslint src/ --max-warnings 0

Ruff 0.15.13 is pinned and selects E, W, F, I and UP (ignoring E501 and UP007). The ESLint config (frontend/eslint.config.js) has one substantive rule: lucide icons whose names shadow globals (Map, Image, History, Text, Option, Infinity, Navigation) must be imported under an alias, because a shadowed Map once crashed every multi-city search. There is no lint npm script.

Pre-commit (.pre-commit-config.yaml, install with make install-hooks): ruff lint (--fix) and format on backend/, trailing whitespace, end-of-file, merge-conflict markers, YAML/JSON checks and mixed line endings.

Makefile targets (run from the repo root): install (backend requirements plus npm ci), install-hooks, format, lint (ruff and ESLint), security (bandit, pip-audit, npm audit), test (both suites with coverage), and ci (lint + security + test). Note that make security still ignores PYSEC-2025-185 and PYSEC-2025-183, which CI no longer ignores.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: All in .github/workflows/.

docs.title: ci.yml
docs.text:
Runs on every push to any branch and on pull requests to main.

Job What it does lint-backend ruff check and ruff format --check lint-frontend eslint with --max-warnings 0 security bandit -ll --skip B105,B106,B608; pip-audit (ignoring PYSEC-2023-62); npm audit --audit-level=high test-backend Python 3.12, pytest with coverage ≥ 70% test-frontend Node 20, npm run test:coverage test-deploy-kit pytest deploy/gcp/tests deploy/ci/tests infrastructure/gcp/tests (governor, deployer with fakes, the deploy workflow's scripts, old-prod migration, bootstrap.sh). Its own job so it runs in parallel with test-backend (together they took 4–6 min) host-checks The VM kit's host layer (see below) image-builds Builds (nothing pushed), in parallel with the rest, the images whose inputs the change touches: the app (backend/, .agents/) and Caddy + SPA (frontend/, deploy/gcp/Caddyfile, caddy.Dockerfile), each then Trivy-scanned with the deploy policy (deploy/ci/trivy-scan.sh), and the local-only nginx frontend/Dockerfile (its own files and package*.json; build only, it doesn't ship). It reads the deploy workflow's BuildKit cache. A push with no usable base, or a change to ci.yml, deploy.yml or a deploy/ci script, does all three. Skipped when deploy.yml calls CI (skip-image-builds): its build jobs build and scan the images that ship

docs.title: docs.yml
docs.text:
Runs on push to main and by hand. Installs mkdocs, mkdocstrings[python], mkdocs-material and ghp-import, runs mkdocs build from mkdocs.yml, copies docs_homepage/index.html over site/index.html, and publishes site/ to the gh-pages branch, served at https://rupakc.github.io/travel-planner/. The custom homepage therefore replaces docs/index.md at the site root; the docs pages live under it (for example /Home/, /Architecture/).

To check the docs locally:

pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]"
mkdocs build --strict      # or: mkdocs serve

docs.title: deploy.yml
docs.text:
Runs on every push to main, weekly (Mondays 04:17 UTC, a no-cache refresh of both images) and by hand (workflow_dispatch, input force, default on). One run at a time (runs queue, a tag is never half-moved). The two images are independent, so a Caddy failure never blocks an app fix and vice versa:

ci ─────────────┬──► promote-app    (needs ci + build-app)
build-app ──────┘
ci ─────────────┬──► promote-caddy  (needs ci + build-caddy)
build-caddy ────┘
  • ci calls ci.yml as a reusable workflow (contents: read; plain pushes to main don't run CI twice). Its image-builds job is skipped here.
  • build-app, build-caddy run in parallel with ci (contents: read, packages: write; no id-token, so they can't sign). Each:
  • pins its base images to their current digests (PYTHON_BASE; CADDY_BASE and the SPA builder's NODE_BASE) and computes the image's inputs id with deploy/ci/image-inputs-id.sh: a SHA-256 over the Dockerfile, .dockerignore, every file the Dockerfile's COPYs take from the context (derived from the Dockerfile itself) and the pinned bases;
  • deploy/ci/build-decision.sh reads the label io.voyager.app-inputs / io.voyager.caddy-inputs of the image prod points at. Equal → nothing is built and prod stays (a frontend-only merge doesn't restart the app; a backend-only merge doesn't touch the SPA; a docs-only merge publishes nothing). Missing, unreadable or different → build. A forced run, or a prod image whose io.voyager.fresh-at is missing or over 8 days old → refresh (build with no-cache). An id that can't be computed is empty and also builds: ADD, a JSON or heredoc COPY, a variable in a source, COPY --from/--mount from= naming anything but an earlier stage, a --mount without type= or a bind mount of the context (type in any case), a FROM that is neither an earlier stage, a pinned build arg passed as NAME=ref@sha256:… nor an image pinned by digest, and .dockerignore re-includes other than !**/NAME (those switch all exclusions off instead; !**/NAME re-includes files and directories named NAME);
  • builds and pushes a sha-<commit> tag;
  • scans it by digest with deploy/ci/trivy-scan.sh (Trivy 0.70.0, checksum-pinned): any fixed CRITICAL finding fails (.trivyignore lists accepted ones).
  • promote-app, promote-caddy have a plain needs: [ci, build-<image>], so each is skipped unless both succeeded (no always()). They are the only jobs with id-token: write (plus contents: read, packages: write) and run deploy/ci/promote-image.sh:
  • main's HEAD must be a 40-hex SHA (else fail). If it isn't this commit, stop: nothing is signed, prod doesn't move;
  • a built image is signed with cosign keyless (GitHub OIDC → Sigstore), verified with the identity the VM requires, then prod moves to it and must resolve to exactly that digest;
  • a skipped image is not signed again; prod must still be the digest the build job compared, else the job fails.

So every image signed as deploy.yml@refs/heads/main has passed CI and was main's HEAD when signed. Scheduled and dispatched runs on main sign with the same identity: the certificate carries the workflow file and ref (job_workflow_ref), not the event. Every job is skipped unless github.ref is refs/heads/main.

Building before CI has passed is safe: the image stays unsigned under its sha- tag, the VM refuses unsigned images, and it only ever deploys the digest the prod tag points at. deploy.sh compares each image's io.voyager.build only with its own predecessor (the running app; the live SPA release), so promoting one image while the other keeps an older run number is not a downgrade.

Not in the inputs id: what a RUN step resolves at build time, i.e. pip resolving the version ranges in backend/requirements.txt (npm follows package-lock.json). The weekly refresh picks up those and any new base image: forced builds run with no-cache, and their new digests also end a hold on the VM. It restarts the app once a week (after draining open streams). Each image carries io.voyager.fresh-at (the time of its last refresh, carried forward by cached builds), and build-decision.sh refreshes an image on any run when prod's value is missing or over 8 days old, so a dropped scheduled run (replaced by a queued push) or a schedule GitHub disabled after 60 days of repository inactivity (gh workflow enable deploy.yml / prod-scan.yml re-enables them) doesn't stop refreshes.

Every action in every workflow is pinned to a full commit SHA, with a version comment, because the promote jobs can sign as the identity the VM trusts. Images carry the label io.voyager.build (the workflow run number), and the VM refuses an image from an older run than the one it is running.

docs.title: prod-scan.yml
docs.text:
Daily (05:41 UTC) and by hand: deploy/ci/trivy-scan.sh on ghcr.io/rupakc/travel-planner-app:prod and …-caddy:prod, with the same policy. A finding makes the run fail (a GitHub notification); it never signs or moves anything. Ship the fix by merging it or by running Deploy by hand.

It has no GCP or VM credentials: the VM pulls and verifies by itself (see Deployment on GCP).

The host-checks job runs deploy/gcp/tests/host_checks.sh in debian:trixie (pinned by digest, NET_ADMIN). It checks four things:

  1. Governor rules: the real rules on iptables-nft for every tier, and that a rejected ruleset leaves the old rules intact.
  2. Deployer: deploy/gcp/tests/test_deploy.py drives deploy.sh end to end with fake docker, curl and systemctl (deploy_fakes.py). It runs here as root and again in test-deploy-kit as a normal user; it is skipped off Linux. App scenarios: first deploy, upgrade, manual rollback with a hold, a newer digest ending the hold, automatic rollback, and downgrade refusal (remembered), plus voyager.service started with --no-block. Edge scenarios: an SPA-only swap (no restart; asserts the absence of recreate and reload), a Caddyfile hot reload, an invalid Caddyfile, a reload failure, a failed post-switch check, a symlink or missing asset in the image, pruning to three releases with older assets still reachable, a runtime change (drain, recreate, checks), the drain timeout, a runtime rollback, Caddy downgrades, signature failure, a compose.yaml change drained, GHCR 429 back-off, the cheap no-change run, --rollback-edge (and toggling it back), --rollback-caddy, --window, migration from the old images.env (with and without the new image) and a lost edge directory. The fakes can make docker pull, create, cp, compose up (failing, or exiting 0 while leaving the old container) and caddy adapt fail. The tests then check that infrastructure failures hold nothing and retry, that a failed pull never skips the downgrade check, that a held runtime ships content only, that a broken edge never blocks the app, that emails are rate-limited, that a no-change run makes exactly one docker ps, and that step stops a function at its first failing command.
  3. First boot: first-boot.sh for real with fake curl, docker and systemctl (first_boot_sim.sh), on a first and a later boot: voyager.service ends up active, voyager units are only started with --no-block, and the bundle (built by bootstrap.sh) unpacks without tar warnings.
  4. systemd units: systemd-analyze verify.

CI also runs shellcheck on deploy/gcp/*.sh, deploy/gcp/host/*.sh, deploy/ci/*.sh and infrastructure/gcp/*.sh, ruff on deploy/ and infrastructure/gcp/, and the tests in deploy/gcp/tests (egress governor, the deployer), deploy/ci/tests (build-decision.sh and promote-image.sh against fake docker/git/cosign: skip only on an equal label, sign → verify → move in that order, never sign a skipped or superseded image, fail closed on an unreadable HEAD or digest; image-inputs-id.sh: same inputs give the same id regardless of order and mtime; any change to a source, requirements.txt, .agents/, the Dockerfile, .dockerignore, the base, an executable bit, a new, deleted or renamed file changes it; .dockerignored, gitignored and un-COPYed files don't; unsupported Dockerfiles, foreign --from and context mounts fail; unusual re-includes switch exclusions off; and the real app and Caddy input lists) and infrastructure/gcp/tests (old-prod migration; bootstrap.sh against stub gcloud/curl: dry run calls nothing, beta preflight, billing quota project, clean sorted host bundle).

docs.title: Theming
docs.text: The web app has a light theme (the default) and a designed dark theme. Colours are defined once as design tokens and consumed through Tailwind, so existing classes such as bg-white/80 or text-teal-700 theme themselves.

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
frontend/design/tokens.json is the source of truth:

Key Holds palette Light-mode colours: 22 families (gray, slate, stone, teal, amber, sky, red, emerald, green, violet, rose, cyan, blue, purple, yellow, indigo, pink, orange, lime, fuchsia, primary, accent) with stops 50 to 950, plus white. Values equal Tailwind 3.4's defaults, plus the primary teal (primary-700, teal-700, is the app's primary colour) and the accent coral. dark The same families and stops for html.dark, plus white (the dark page surface). semantic Named roles pointing at a stop: surface, surface-raised, text, text-muted, border, accent.

Edit the JSON, then run cd frontend && npm run tokens. That runs scripts/build-tokens.mjs, which writes src/theme/tokens.css: one CSS variable per colour holding space-separated RGB channels (--c-gray-50: 249 250 251;) under :root (light) and html.dark (dark), plus a print rule that forces the light values. Do not edit tokens.css by hand; a test fails if it differs from the generator output. tailwind.config.js maps each colour to rgb(var(--c-<family>-<stop>) / <alpha-value>), so opacity modifiers keep working. black is deliberately not remapped (overlays).

The semantic colours are also available as utilities: bg-surface, bg-surface-raised, text-text, text-text-muted, border-border, bg-accent.

The token tests (src/theme/tokens.test.js) check that both modes cover the same families and stops with valid hex values and that text/surface pairs meet WCAG contrast. src/theme/darkSurfaces.test.jsx checks that the map and import map render no literal hex colours in dark mode.

docs.title: Switching
docs.text:
darkMode: 'class' in tailwind.config.js: dark styles apply under html.dark. For a component use a token class and it follows the theme; write an explicit dark: variant only where a fixed colour is needed (for example the social sign-in buttons use each provider's published dark variant).

src/theme/ThemeContext.jsx (ThemeProvider, useTheme() returning {theme, resolved, setTheme}):

  • theme is system, light or dark; the default is light. The OS setting is consulted only when system is chosen, and followed live.
  • The choice is stored in localStorage['tp_theme'] (src/theme/themeStorage.js; every access is guarded for private mode).
  • The provider toggles html.dark, sets color-scheme and updates <meta name="theme-color"> (#ffffff light, the dark surface colour in dark).
  • The control is ThemeToggle (NavBar and Preferences, data-tid="nav.theme"), a button that cycles light, dark, system and emits theme_change.

docs.title: No flash
docs.text: frontend/public/theme-init.js is loaded by index.html as a render-blocking classic script before any CSS. It reads tp_theme and sets html.dark, color-scheme and the theme-color meta before first paint. It is an external file because the production CSP is script-src 'self' (no inline scripts). Keep its logic in step with ThemeContext.jsx; src/theme/antiFlash.test.js covers it.

docs.title: Trip Planning Features
docs.text: What a user can do in the app, and where each feature lives in the code. Chat, multi-city routing, personalization and plan sharing have their own pages: Chat Assistant, Multi-City Trips, Personalization and Sharing and Plans.

docs.title: App shell
docs.text:
• Routes (frontend/src/App.jsx): /login, /share/:token (public), /change-password, and the signed-in layout with / (Search and Results), /chat, /nearby (Near me), /alerts, /preferences and /admin (admins only). Any other path redirects to /.
  • Search, Results and Chat stay mounted and are hidden with CSS, so a running search or chat stream survives switching tabs. Logging out clears all search state.
  • A user who must change their password is sent to /change-password first.
  • The header has a notification bell for fare and price alerts (see Fare watch and price alerts and Price watch).
  • The footer credits the place data: "Place data © GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) · Airport data: OurAirports".

docs.title: Search page
docs.text: frontend/src/pages/SearchPage.jsx has four modes.

docs.title: "I know where I'm going"
docs.text:
• Route. From and To use the airport/place typeahead (components/ui/AirportSearch.jsx → GET /api/airports/search). "Add a stop on the way (multi-city)" adds up to 3 intermediate stops, each with optional nights (1–30). The To city is the final destination.
  • Trip. Departure and return dates, budget in USD, nationality (NationalitySearch → GET /api/nationalities/search), residence permits and existing visas, interests.
  • Travellers (TravelerPanel): adults 18–64, seniors 65+, children 5–17, infants 0–4, plus accessibility needs (wheelchair, visual, hearing, cognitive).
  • Discovery style slider (serendipity 0–1): Famous classics, Balanced mix, Hidden gems.
  • Submitting records a recent search and writes the fields back to Preferences. Saved preferences pre-fill the form on load; the budget category maps to USD as low 1000, medium 3000, high 8000.
  • There is no pace control on the form. pace (relaxed / balanced / packed) is set by the "Slow it down" remix or through the API.

docs.title: "Surprise me 🎲"
docs.text: Origin, nationality, dates, optional budget, interests and travellers. POST /api/discover returns 5 destinations. Each card shows city and country, a weather emoji and description, a visa badge (⚠️ when not confirmed by the static table), flight time, a rough cost range and why it matches. "Plan this trip →" fills in the known-destination form.

docs.title: "Compare ⚖️"
docs.text: Seeded once from the known-destination form. Takes 2–3 destinations plus shared trip fields, and makes one POST /api/compare/destination call per destination in parallel, each column with its own loading and error state and a Retry that re-runs only that column. Responses from an earlier run are ignored. components/CompareTable.jsx shows cost estimate, flight, hotel, weather, visa and the Travel Ease grade, marking the best value in each row (stacked cards on phones). "Plan this trip" runs that exact request as a normal full search. Pure helpers are in utils/compare.js. Compare is single-city only (multi-city requests get 422).

docs.title: "From a link ✨"
docs.text:
Plan a trip around a travel blog, a YouTube or TikTok video, a caption, a friend's message or screenshots.

  • Ways in. The fourth mode tab. A hero hint: "Saw a great trip online? Paste the link". A deep link, /?import=<url>: Chat offers it when a message is just a link, or a link plus "plan", and it opens the flow and starts reading. Dropping a screenshot anywhere on the Search page opens the tab with it, under a full-page "Drop it to plan a trip" overlay.
  • Input (components/import/ImportPanel.jsx). One box tells a link from text as you type ("Link — we'll read the page" / "Text — we'll pick out the places"). A drop zone takes up to 4 screenshots, with thumbnails and remove buttons; pasting an image works too, and wrong types, HEIC, unreadable files and files that are still over 5 MB once shrunk are explained. Screenshots are shrunk in the browser before the size check and the upload (long edge ≤ 1568 px, WebP or JPEG at quality 0.85), so a 10 MB retina screenshot is fine. There are three "Try an example" texts. Enter submits a link; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submits text.
  • Progress. Three staged steps: "Reading the page", then "Finding places", then "Putting them on the map". They are announced in an ARIA live region, and the time so far is shown against the typical time. Skeleton rows appear meanwhile. Cancel or Esc stops the request.
  • Errors offer the next step. A blocked source (Instagram and the like), a paywall or an empty page gets "Paste the text" and "Drop a screenshot" buttons. Timeouts get "Try again". The rate-limit message is shown as the server sends it.
  • Review (components/import/ImportPreview.jsx, ImportMap.jsx).
  • "Here's what we found": the trip title and summary, plus a source card (favicon, title, site, author, link).
  • A Leaflet map with numbered pins coloured by kind. They drop in once; reduced motion is respected. Approximate places are hollow pins, fanned out around their town, with an "approximate location" tooltip.
  • The route, with a nights stepper per stop and the option to leave a stop out.
  • Places grouped by stop. Each has a checkbox (with All / None per stop), a kind icon, inline rename, a "Change city" stop picker, a "day trip to …" label, "On the map ★ 4.6" or "Approximate", the source's quote highlighted, and the note.
  • "Couldn't place" places get a town field. "Place it" calls POST /api/import/resolve-place, which drops the place into its stop, or adds the town as a new stop while the route has fewer than 3. A stop picker remains as an alternative.
  • The usual trip fields, prefilled from Preferences: From, leaving date (default a month out; the return date follows the nights), nationality, budget and travellers.
  • Hotels start unticked, and at most 25 places are planned.
  • Planning. "Plan this trip (N places)" runs a normal full search, with the reviewed places as must_include and the source as import_source. Interests from the source are added to the search but not saved to Preferences. Pure helpers are in utils/linkImport.js.
  • Results. The banner counts what the itinerary on screen holds, after the traveller's moves and removals. When the stream ends without an itinerary, the browser's fallback itinerary gives each day its city and places the link places the same way the server does (utils/mustInclude.js). When the itinerary fails, the banner says so and points to Activities instead of spinning. A dismissible banner says "Planned around 11 places from 48 hours in Lisbon — all 11 are in your itinerary", or "10 of 11 … 1 didn't fit: show". Imported activity cards and itinerary rows carry an amber "From your link" chip; tapping it shows the quote and how the place was checked. Places that did not get a slot are listed as "Also from your link" under their day. Trip map pins from the link have an amber ring. The My Plan drawer and the share page show "Inspired by …", and saved plans from a link have a link icon. Print and calendar exports carry the credit and the tags.
  • Analytics. import_started (kind), import_preview_shown (place_count), import_planned, import_failed (code) and import_from_chat.

docs.title: Recent searches
docs.text: A collapsible strip above the known-destination form (components/RecentSearches.jsx). Its open/closed state is remembered per browser. Clicking a card loads the whole search (route, stops, dates, travellers, budget, visas) into the form; "Search again" re-runs it; each card can be deleted. Past dates are moved to start a week from today with the same trip length. The backend keeps the newest 8 per user and merges identical searches, ignoring interest order (/api/recent-searches).

docs.title: Onboarding tour
docs.text: A first-run tooltip tour (components/OnboardingTour.jsx, hooks/useFirstRunTour.js, utils/tour.js). It opens once, 400 ms after load, for users with no recent searches, and only on the Search page in known-destination mode. Six steps: recent searches, route, interests, Preferences, the plan button and My Plan. A step whose element is not on screen is skipped. Each step is a focus-trapped dialog (Esc closes it). Completion is stored in localStorage['tp_tour_done:<username>']; "New here? Take a quick tour" replays it.

docs.title: Results page
docs.text: frontend/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx. Results stream through services/api.js → workers/sseWorker.js. The header shows progress (completed/16) and a status chip per agent (searching, enhancing, done, error) that links to its section. If the stream ends without done, the page reports that the connection was interrupted.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
In display order (AGENT_ORDER):

Section What it shows Flights Outbound and return legs, airline, stops, price and booking link; one group per leg on multi-city trips. Pricing-advisor banner with sparkline, Google Flights price-insights chip, opt-in fare calendar. Filters: max stops, max price, departure and arrival windows (/api/flights/filtered). A Layover button per connection opens a layover mini-plan (POST /api/layover). Weather Forecast Day cards; Open-Meteo data within 16 days, else an LLM estimate; grouped per stay on multi-city trips. Hotels Options across budget tiers. Filters: beds, max price per night, wifi, distance from centre, private washroom (/api/hotels/filtered). Activities Interest-matched activities with price and rating, and weather hints. Filters: interests, max price, availability dates, min rating (/api/activities/filtered). Places to See Landmarks and sights; Google Places data when SERPER_KEY is set. Free Walking Tours Crawled tours (GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, FreeWalkingTour.com, SANDEMANs NewEurope), top picks first per city, each linking to the provider's tour page (components/WalkingToursSection.jsx). What's On Festivals, concerts and markets during the trip; ~ marks a typical-season date. Visa Entry requirement, permitted stay, fee, documents and official link. SIM Cards Local SIMs and global eSIMs. Travel Tips Safety, culture, scams, money. Emergency Card Per-city police, ambulance and fire numbers, embassy, phrases and local laws; printable. Getting Around Local and inter-city transport options. Currency & Forex Exchange rates, where to exchange, card, cash and ATM advice. Itinerary Day-by-day plan with Cards and Timeline views (components/TimelineView.jsx) and a route map (components/TripMap.jsx, Leaflet with OpenStreetMap tiles). See Itinerary. Trip Health Check The stress test: a score ring, issues with suggested fixes, and a re-check of the edited plan. Packing List Weather- and activity-aware checklist; checkbox state is kept in the browser, and items can be added to the plan.

Above the sections:

  • Travel Ease banner (ConfidenceBanner): the Phase 0 grade from the static destination scores.
  • Search panel to edit and re-run the search.
  • Trip Remix (RemixBar, utils/remix.js): five presets — A week later, Half the budget, Make it luxe, Slow it down (relaxed pace), Long weekend. Each re-plans the trip and shows a before/after banner.

On multi-city trips every list is stable-sorted into journey order (utils/orderSectionByCity.js).

docs.title: Verification badges
docs.text: Each section header shows a chip from data.verification (components/VerificationBadge.jsx): Verified, Partly verified, AI-generated, Check details, or a spinning Checking… while hotel, activity and place links are still being checked. Clicking the chip opens a popover with the summary and each check (pass, fail or note, with its source link). Visa and emergency conflicts also show a banner in the section body, and items whose link was matched by name get a "Found online" tag. When the stream ends with a chip still pending, utils/verification.js resolves it. Saved plans drop the live link evidence. Chat does not show badges. The rules are in Agent System.

docs.title: Best-value package
docs.text: Shown once the search has finished (utils/bestValuePackage.js, components/BestValuePackage.jsx). Deterministic rules, no extra agent: a balanced flight per leg, one well-reviewed 3–4 star hotel, cheap or free activities (2 per city, 4 in total), free walking tours (up to 3) and places (2 per city, 4 in total), and a SIM plan covering the trip. Every pick is a real listed item. "Add all to My Plan" merges them in one update without duplicates, and Undo restores the previous selections. Its total uses the drawer's cost arithmetic. It is disabled while a saved plan is open.

docs.title: Budget planner
docs.text: Shown after the best-value package when the search has a budget (utils/budgetPlanner.js, components/BudgetPlanner.jsx). It runs entirely in the browser. The budget is split per person into Flights, Stay and Activities sliders ($10 steps) plus a read-only "Everything else". Defaults: the cheapest fare (summed per leg on multi-city), median nightly rate × nights, and 15% for activities; if those overshoot, activities shrink first, then stay. Under each slider it counts what fits ("6 of 12 hotels fit"). Once the user touches it, over-budget hotel and flight cards are dimmed and tagged, and "Show only what fits" can hide them (selected cards always stay visible). When fewer than 3 hotels fit, Find cheaper hotels runs the hotel filter with the stay share per night; this is the only action that calls the API. Reset restores the defaults; a new search or remix resets everything.

docs.title: Fare calendar and price insights
docs.text:
• Fare calendar (components/FareCalendarStrip.jsx, utils/fareCalendar.js). A "Fare calendar" button in the Flights header, offered only when GET /health reports serpapi_configured, the user is signed in and the trip is single-city. It loads POST /api/flights/fare-calendar: seven cells for departure dates ±3 days with the trip length kept the same, each with the cheapest live fare and its difference from the chosen dates; the cheapest is highlighted. Clicking another date asks for confirmation, then runs a new search with both dates shifted.
  • Price insights. When live fares come with Google's verdict, a chip reads, for example, "Fares are low right now · typical $420–$610" (green, grey or amber for low, typical or high). This is Google's data, not an AI estimate.
  • Pricing advisor. The deferred agent's banner: whether prices look high or low for the route, when to book, and a sparkline.

docs.title: Fare watch and price alerts
docs.text:
A traveller can watch a trip's live fare and be told when it's worth acting on. Offered when GET /health reports fare_watch_available (SerpAPI configured and FARE_WATCH_ENABLED), for signed-in users and single-destination trips departing after today.

  • Watch this fare (components/alerts/WatchFareButton.jsx, WatchDialog.jsx): from the Flights header, the fare calendar ("Watch these dates", with nearby dates pre-ticked), the selected flight in My Plan (Results and Chat), saved-plan cards and the saved-plan viewer. A watched trip reads "Watching · $412" and opens its watch. The dialog shows today's price on Google's typical range and offers "Tell me when the price drops" (default) or "…when it's below $___" (pre-filled with the low end of the typical range), "Include nearby dates (±3 days)", and "Also email me" (hidden without SMTP, disabled with a link to Preferences when the account has no email). Creating a watch takes today's price as the baseline; the first time, the confirmation offers browser alerts (never asked on page load).
  • Checks (backend/app/services/fare_watch.py): a scheduler started with the backend re-checks each active watch every FARE_WATCH_INTERVAL_HOURS (12 h ±10 %) within a daily SerpAPI budget; one check is 1 call (exact dates) or up to 7 (±3 days), cached fares are free. Prices are totals for the trip's travellers. A watch ends when its departure day arrives (watch_expired notice), and three failed checks in a row put it on hold (watch_error notice with Retry).
  • When we tell you (evaluate, one notification per check at most, highest first):
  • Below your target: the price is at or under the target.
  • Price drop (default mode): at least max($15, 5 %) below the reference (see below).
  • Low price: a new lowest for the trip's own dates that Google rates "low" (default mode).
  • Cheaper nearby date (±3 days): a departure at least max($25, 8 %) cheaper than the chosen dates, same trip length (in target mode only when it also beats the target).
  • References and re-arming: the trip's own dates (rules 1–3) and the nearby dates (rule 4) each keep their own reference, so an alert about a nearby date never raises the bar for the trip's own dates. A signal's first alert is measured from the price when watching started; if that price was already under the target, or Google already rated it "low", the confirmation says so ("Already below your target — we'll tell you if it drops further") and the first alert needs a full max($15, 5 %) drop below it. After that, every repeat needs a further drop of max($15, 5 %) below that signal's last alerted price, unless the signal re-armed: in drop mode, once the price climbs back at least max($15, 5 %) above the last alert, the highest price since then becomes the reference (alert at $400, a week at $600, then $450: "dropped to $450 (−$150)"); in target mode, once the price is back above the target by max($15, 5 %), going under the target again alerts. So $1-a-day drifts never alert daily, and a real fall after a rebound is never missed.
  • Never spammy: no alert on the first check (that's the baseline) and never for a rise above where watching started; at most one alert per watch per 24 h (across both signals) unless the price is at least 5 % below the latest alert. Rises are still recorded in the history.
  • Alerts page (pages/AlertsPage.jsx, components/alerts/WatchCard.jsx): a card per watch with the route, dates and travellers, the current price, the change since watching, lowest seen, Google's verdict, a price sparkline with the target as a dashed line, and last/next check. Actions: Re-plan with this fare (runs the normal search with the traveller's preferences; flexible watches also offer the cheaper nearby departure), Book on Google Flights, Check now, Pause/Resume, Edit, and Delete (confirmed inline). Grouped Active / Past trips, with an empty state that points to search. /alerts?watch=ID scrolls to a watch; &replan=1 (from emails) re-plans directly. Signed out, any such link goes through the login page (/login?next=…, same-site paths only) and returns to it after signing in. A watch on hold shows a plain-language reason (never the raw error).
  • Notifications (context/AlertsContext.jsx, components/alerts/NotificationBell.jsx, AlertToast.jsx): the header bell shows the unread count and the latest 10 alerts ("Berlin → Lisbon dropped to $150 (−$70)"), each opening its watch and marking it read, with "Mark all as read". The unread count is polled every 60 s only while the tab is visible (and on focus). A new alert shows as one dismissible toast (a polite live region), or as a native browser notification when the window isn't focused and the traveller allowed it.
  • Email (backend/app/services/alert_email.py, optional): when SMTP_HOST is set, the watch has email on and the account has an address (set on Preferences), fare alerts are also emailed: plain text plus inline-styled HTML with no remote images, old → new price, lowest seen, a text sparkline (▆▄█▁), "See flights" and "Re-plan with this fare" links to APP_BASE_URL, and a link that stops emails for that watch (it opens a confirmation page, so mail scanners that follow links can't turn emails off; mail clients' one-click unsubscribe, RFC 8058, works directly). Expiry and error notices stay in the app. The account email is not verified; changing it is signed-in only and rate-limited.
  • Analytics (track()): watch_created (mode, flex, email), watch_checked_now, watch_live_checked (kind), alert_clicked (kind), watch_replanned, watch_booked.

docs.title: Price watch: hotels, activities and trips
docs.text:
The fare-watch machinery also covers a hotel's price, an activity's price and a whole saved trip's price. Availability is the same (SerpAPI configured, signed-in user). The bell, toasts and optional email are shared, and the Alerts page gains tabs (All / Flights / Hotels / Activities / Trips).

  • Where the buttons are. Watch price on a hotel card (Results and Chat), on the selected hotel in My Plan and in a chat plan; Watch price on an activity card and on picked activities in My Plan; Watch whole trip on saved-plan cards, in the saved-plan viewer and, once the plan is saved, in My Plan. A watched item reads "Watching · $398". The dialog works like the fare dialog ("Tell me when the price drops" or "…below $___", optional email), and the first look is the baseline, never an alert.
  • City names. Watches name the city ("Lisbon"), even when the search stored an airport code ("LIS"): the buttons look the code up in the local airport data, and the server does the same as a safety net. On a multi-city trip an activity is watched in its own leg's city.
  • Hotels (price_sources/hotel.py, hotel_prices.py): the hotel is matched by name and city to a property on Google Hotels (via SerpAPI) for the search's dates and travellers. The price is the total for the stay: all nights and all rooms (one room for up to 4 travellers, then one room per 4 — the same rule for a trip's hotel; the dialog states the basis). A hotel already watched under another name (another card, or a "Not this one?" pick) for the same stay, guests and rooms returns the existing watch. At the active-watch limit, "Not this one?" removes the first watch to make room and puts it back if the new one can't be created. "Not this one?" offers up to 3 other priced properties. Sold out for the dates is "unavailable", not a price.
  • Activities (price_sources/activity.py, activity_prices.py): the price is the "from … per person" figure Google shows for the activity's GetYourGuide or Viator listing, times your travellers. It is read from Google results through SerpAPI; getyourguide.com and viator.com are never fetched or scraped. Only a specific listing is watched, never a category page, and it must carry every place / proper-noun word of the activity, so a generic "small group walking tour" can't match another city's tour. When nothing matches, up to 3 priced listings are suggested. The watch keeps the listing's own currency (a target must be typed in it) and only ever compares like with like; a check that can't find the listing, finds no price or finds another currency is "unavailable". Without a date the watch runs 180 days.
  • Trips (price_sources/trip.py): one total for a saved plan's flight, hotel, activities and other priced parts, with a breakdown (each part marked Live or Estimate, and what its price is). The flight is Google's cheapest fare on your dates for the route, as a fare watch tracks it, not the specific flight you picked. At most 5 activities are priced live; the rest, non-USD listings, multi-city flights, the SIM plan and anything Google can't price are estimates. The hotel is priced like a hotel watch (its property page on Google Hotels, same rooms), from the first look on, so an unchanged trip never shows a hotel drop. An alert says which part moved ("flights −$70, hotel −$42"). The watch works on a frozen copy of the plan, so deleting the plan doesn't stop it.
  • Honesty rules. A price is either observed (a live look, with its source and link) or an estimate (the AI's price from your search). Estimates are labelled, frozen when the watch is created, count towards a trip's total but never move, and never trigger an alert. A watch needs at least one live component: if nothing live matches, it can't be created (no_live_price); the dialog shows the labelled estimate and the suggestions instead.
  • Thresholds. A step per kind sets the drop needed for an alert, for a repeat alert and for re-arming after a rebound: fares and hotels max($15, 5 %), activities max(1 unit of the listing's currency, 5 %), whole trips max($25, 4 %) on the total.
  • Anti-spam (same rules as fares): no alert on the baseline or for a rise; one notification per check; at most one per watch per 24 h unless the price is at least 5 % below the last alert; a repeat needs a further full-step drop unless the price rebounded first. Watching the same subject twice returns the existing watch (already_watching).
  • Checks and limits. One scheduler checks fare and price watches every FARE_WATCH_INTERVAL_HOURS from one daily SerpAPI budget (the price pass runs alongside, so it never delays fare checks, and price checks reserve their worst case so they can't push the budget over; creating a watch holds its worst case too — 2 calls for a hotel or an activity, 10 for a trip — and gives back what it didn't spend), and FARE_WATCH_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER counts every kind together. A watch ends on check-in, the activity date or the departure (watch_expired); three failed, or three "unavailable", looks in a row put it on hold (watch_error, with Retry). Notification kinds: hotel_drop, hotel_target, activity_drop, activity_target, trip_drop, trip_target.
  • Alerts page: a card per kind (components/alerts/cards/) with the current and lowest price, change since watching, sparkline, listing link, Check now, Search the web now, Pause/Resume, Edit and Delete; trip cards show the breakdown. /alerts?kind=hotel&watch=ID opens one watch.

docs.title: Search the web now
docs.text:
Every active watch card (flight, hotel, activity, trip) has Search the web now (components/alerts/LiveCheck.jsx). It asks POST /api/live-check for one live Google Search–grounded answer about that watch (the server builds the question from the stored watch; nothing is typed). The answer opens under the card: the summary exactly as returned, any prices found with the source each one cites, "Searched for" (each query links to Google Search), the Sources list and the disclaimer ("…Not used for your price alerts."). It can be dismissed and is gone when you leave the page.

  • It is separate from Check now: watches, alerts, notifications and price history still come only from the scheduled SerpAPI checks. The live answer never changes the card's price, sparkline or history, and is never stored (component state only, no browser storage).
  • Errors read in plain words: a removed watch (404), a watch whose dates have passed (409 watch_expired, no retry), the rate limit (429, the server's message as-is), the monthly AI limit or disabled billing (503 ai_limit / ai_billing), live search not available on this server (503 grounding_unavailable, e.g. a local Anthropic setup), and no grounded answer (502, with Try again).
  • Google's Search Suggestions widget is not shown; the "Searched for" queries link to Google Search instead.

docs.title: Near me
docs.text:
Near me (/nearby, pages/NearbyPage.jsx, a header tab next to Chat; between 640 and 1024 px the desktop tabs show icons only, with the names as tooltips and accessible names) shows places to see, eat, shop and stay around where you are, from Google Maps grounding (POST /api/nearby with sections: true).

  • The page explains first and asks the browser for your location only when you press Use my location. Coordinates are rounded to about 100 m before they are sent, with the browser's language. While it waits for the browser there is a Cancel button, and after 20 s without an answer (e.g. a dismissed prompt in Firefox or Safari) it stops with the timeout message.
  • Results: the nearest known place ("Lisbon, Portugal", distance; a region or country that repeats the name is left out), then four sections of cards, each with a one-line summary and Open in Google Maps (new tab). A section with nothing shows a short note. Under the cards: "Places from Google Maps" and the Sources list.
  • Location denied, unavailable, timed out or unsupported each get their own explanation, with Try again where it can help. API errors: no known place nearby (404, offering to check again from where you are now rather than a plain retry), the rate limit (429), the AI limit, billing or map results not available here (503), and a failed lookup (502).
  • Results live only in the page's state: nothing goes to browser storage, and they are gone when you leave the page. There is no "use a city instead" fallback yet (the airport typeahead has no coordinates).

docs.title: Live web check and Near me (Google grounding)
docs.text:
Two features use Gemini's grounding tools on Vertex AI through one seam, llm.generate_grounded() (text output, the agent model; links come only from the grounding metadata, never from the model's text). Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-live-check-and-near-me-v2.md. API: Live web check, Near me v2.

  • "Search the web now" (POST /api/live-check, services/live_check.py): a signed-in user asks for a live look at one of their own watches (fare, hotel, activity or trip). The server builds the question from the stored watch and runs one Gemini call grounded with Google Search. The answer comes back with its sources, the searches it ran ("Searched for") and any prices it quoted that a source supports. It is a second opinion, not a measurement: watches, baselines, price history and alerts stay on SerpAPI and never see it.
  • Near me v2 (POST /api/nearby with sections: true, services/nearby_grounded.py): one Gemini call grounded with Google Maps around the user's coordinates, returning places to see, eat, shop and stay. Each item comes from a Maps grounding chunk and carries its Google Maps link; a place the model names without one is dropped. Location privacy: v2 passes the request's lat/lng to Google Maps grounding through Vertex AI (Google's retrieval config) so results are near the user; clients round them to about 100 m first. The backend never stores or logs the coordinates (request logs hold the path only, and the llm_usage line holds counts). The v1 response (activities agent, no sections) is unchanged for installed apps.
  • Clients. The web app has a "Near me" page (above) and a "Search the web now" panel on every active watch card on the Alerts page; the Android app follows the same rules.
  • Provider. Grounding exists only with LLM_PROVIDER resolved to gemini; on anthropic both answer 503 grounding_unavailable (v1 Near me still works). Both use the light_ai rate limit, need sign-in, and count against the Gemini spend cap (503 ai_limit / ai_billing). Google bills each search or Maps query the model issues past a monthly free allowance (5,000 each), so Near me v2 makes one call for all four sections, not four.

Google's terms (Service Terms §20(k) Search, §20(m) Maps) — rules for this code and its clients:

  • Only for the user who asked. Grounded results are shown only to the signed-in user whose request produced them. No background or scheduled grounded calls: the scheduler never uses Search grounding, and the Android "nearby" notification only invites the user to open Near me (its own request runs the call).
  • No storage, no cache, no analysis. Nothing grounded is written to the database, cached (/api/live-check and Near me v2 have no cache, unlike v1), compared with a baseline, fed into alerts or logged with content (the llm_usage line holds counts only). Clients keep results in memory only (web: component state; Android: ViewModel, not Room/DataStore). A Maps place_id may be stored under the terms, but we don't need to.
  • Display. Show sources directly under the content they support, viewable in one interaction; don't edit the grounded text or put ads or other content inside it. Near me shows the "Google Maps" attribution text (unmodified, not translated) and each item's Maps link, opened as is (no interstitial).
  • Search Suggestions. Google's docs ask for the Search Suggestions chip, but the pricing page and Service Terms allow not displaying it at standard pricing under 1 million grounded prompts per day. We rely on that: instead of the chip, clients show the returned queries as a "Searched for" line linking to Google Search. Revisit this if volume ever approaches that limit.

docs.title: Itinerary
docs.text:
components/ItinerarySection.jsx, with helpers in utils/.

  • Drag-and-drop. Activities can be dragged (grip handle) to another day or time of day. The drag uses a custom MIME type so the plan drawer never mistakes it for a plan drop. Each activity also has a Move menu for keyboard and touch users, listing every valid target. Moving onto an occupied slot swaps the two; on multi-city trips moves stay within the same city. Removed activities appear under "Removed" with Restore. The toolbar has Undo (last 20 actions) and Reset, and empty slots show "Free time".
  • Layout overlay. Moves are not written into the itinerary. utils/itineraryLayout.js stores an overlay keyed by each activity's original slot ("<day>-<time_of_day>") and fingerprinted to the itinerary, saved as selections.itinerary_layout. Timeline view, the map, exports, shared plans and the saved-plan viewer all show the arranged itinerary. An overlay whose fingerprint does not match is ignored.
  • Timed schedule. utils/schedule.js estimates start and end times for each activity from its slot (anchors 09:00, 13:30, 18:30), its duration_hours and the travel time from the previous stop (walking up to 1.5 km, else transit, from the slots' coordinates; a 20-minute buffer without them). Times are always derived, never stored, and the UI says they are estimates. A day that starts activities more than 45 minutes late or runs past 23:00 gets a "Tight schedule" note. Activities picked into My Plan keep their scheduled times ("Day 2 · Afternoon · 13:30–16:00").
  • Edits and notes. A slot's activity, location and cost can be edited (selections.itinerary_edits), and notes added (selections.itinerary_notes). Editing is off, with the reason shown, while a saved plan is loaded.
  • Health check. The stress-test agent audits the generated itinerary. After the user rearranges or edits it, Re-check my edited plan sends the arranged itinerary with edits and times, plus current flights, visa and weather (utils/stressTestPayload.js), to POST /api/stress-test. The result replaces the findings on screen; a later change shows "Your plan changed since this check", and errors keep the previous findings.

docs.title: My Plan drawer
docs.text: On both Results (MyPlanDrawer) and Chat (ChatPlanDrawer). Users pick flights (one per leg on multi-city trips), a hotel, activities, places, walking tours, events, a SIM plan, tips, transport options, packing-list items and itinerary slots. The drawer shows a cost breakdown, exports to calendar and print/PDF, and saves, loads and shares plans. Details: Sharing and Plans.

docs.title: Chat, Preferences, Admin and feedback
docs.text:
• Chat: see Chat Assistant.
  • Preferences (pages/PreferencesPage.jsx): Travel Budget, Identity (nationality, current residence, used as the default departure city, and the email for fare alerts, saved on its own via PUT /api/auth/email), Documents (permits, visas), Travel Style (interests, travellers, accessibility), and a Taste Graph card with Reset. Bound two ways to the Search form; see Personalization.
  • Admin (pages/AdminPage.jsx, admins only): a Users tab to create users with a temporary password (at least 8 characters; they must change it on first login), list them, deactivate, reactivate and reset passwords; and a Feedback tab, filterable by page, category and minimum rating.
  • Feedback widget (components/FeedbackWidget.jsx): on every signed-in page. 1–5 stars, a category (bug, feature request, general, praise) and an optional message up to 500 characters, sent to POST /api/feedback.
  • Rate limits: when a limit is hit, the API's 429 message ("Too many requests — please wait N seconds and try again.") is shown as-is (utils/httpError.js). Defaults per 10 minutes: 10 searches, 30 chat messages, 30 compare calls, 10 discover calls, 60 single-agent calls.

docs.title: Trips API
docs.text: Frozen with Phase 2 wave 0. Changes: later changes are additive only (new fields, endpoints or error codes; nothing renamed, removed or re-typed). Every change needs a contract-change note in its PR and an update to this page in the same PR.

docs.title: API contract (frozen at the end of wave 0)
docs.text:
All paths are under /api, with JSON in and out. Every route needs Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and acts only on the caller's own trips: anybody else's trip answers 404 trip_not_found. Errors use the Phase 1 envelope {"detail", "error_code", …}, malformed bodies keep FastAPI's 422 {"detail": [...]}, and timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with Z. Days are YYYY-MM-DD.

today: every GET below and the check-in accept an optional client local date. The server uses it when it is within ±1 day of the server's UTC date, and otherwise uses the UTC date. Clients send the device's local date.

docs.title: Discovery (additive)
docs.text: GET /config gains features.trips: true (the trips API exists), features.journey: bool (JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED) and features.offline_pack: bool (OFFLINE_PACK_ENABLED, default true). When offline_pack is false, clients unregister the service worker and delete every offline cache and pack.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
phase ∈ dreaming | planning | ready | on_the_road | memories. The effective phase, for start s, end e (e = s when missing), override o, today t, prep complete p and READY_WINDOW_DAYS = 14:

  1. o set → o.
  2. s missing → dreaming.
  3. t > e → memories.
  4. s ≤ t ≤ e → on_the_road.
  5. p or (s − t) ≤ 14 days → ready.
  6. otherwise → planning.

day_index = (t − s) + 1 while on the road, else null. days_to_start = s − t when t < s, else null. Golden cases live in backend/tests/fixtures/journey/trip_phase_cases.json, and every client must pass them.

docs.title: Shared objects
docs.text:
Trip:

{"id": 12, "title": "Lisbon in spring", "destination": "Lisbon", "destinations": ["Lisbon", "Porto"],
 "origin": "NYC", "start_date": "2027-04-01", "end_date": "2027-04-08", "nights": 7,
 "phase": "planning", "phase_source": "auto", "days_to_start": 140, "day_index": null,
 "num_travelers": 2, "budget_usd": 3000, "countries": ["PT"],
 "prep": {"done": 3, "total": 9, "percent": 33, "complete": false},
 "has_itinerary": true, "recap_completed_at": null, "created_at": "…Z", "updated_at": "…Z"}
  • title is plans.title, falling back to plans.name.
  • destinations is search_data.destinations, else [destination], else [].
  • phase_source is auto|manual. nights = end − start in days, or null.
  • countries holds ISO alpha-2 codes, resolved locally (no network).
  • prep comes from the prep rules below. For a Dreaming trip it is {"done": 0, "total": 0, "percent": 0, "complete": false}.

GameDelta: exactly as in docs/Accounts-API.md. It is null when the game is disabled.

Place key: <kind>:<slug>. kind ∈ activity|place|food|hotel|event|tour|nearby|other. slug = the name NFKD-normalised, combining marks removed, lower-cased, every run of non-[a-z0-9] replaced by -, trimmed of -, and cut to 60 characters ("" → "x"). The server accepts ^[a-z]+:[a-z0-9-]{1,60}$. The vectors are in backend/tests/fixtures/journey/place_key_cases.json (for example ["activity", "Pastéis de Belém!"] → "activity:pasteis-de-belem").

docs.title: Trips
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips query today? {"trips": [Trip], "pinned_id": 12 \| null, "today": "2026-11-12"}. Sorted by phase (on_the_road, ready, planning, dreaming, memories), then start_date (memories: newest first), then updated_at desc. At most 200 — POST /trips {"title": 1..80, "destination"?: ≤120, "start_date"?, "end_date"?} 201 Trip. Creates a plans row: name = title, search_data = {"destination": d} (or {}), selections = {} 422 trip_dates_invalid, 422 trip_title_invalid GET /trips/{id} query today? Trip 404 trip_not_found PATCH /trips/{id} any subset of {"title", "start_date", "end_date", "phase"}. A null date clears it, and "phase": null clears the override Trip 422 trip_dates_invalid (end < start, span > 365 days, or a year outside 2000–2100), 422 trip_phase_invalid, 422 trip_title_invalid, 404 DELETE /trips/{id} — 204. Deletes the plan and every child row (the same as DELETE /plans/{id}) 404 GET /trips/stats — {"countries": [{"code": "PT", "name": "Portugal", "first_trip_id": 12, "visited_at": "…Z", "source": "checkin"\|"recap"}], "continents": ["EU"], "bucket_goal": 30 \| null, "trips_by_phase": {"dreaming": 1, …}} —

pinned_id is the on-the-road trip with the earliest start, else the trip with the smallest days_to_start, else the memories trip with an end_date in the last 14 days and no recap_completed_at, else null. The POST /plans handler stores start_date/end_date from search_data, so plans saved by any client become dated trips.

docs.title: Prep checklist
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/prep query today? {"items": [PrepItem], "done", "total", "percent", "complete"} 404 PUT /trips/{id}/prep/{item_id} {"done": bool} the same object plus "item": PrepItem, "game": GameDelta \| null 404 prep_item_unknown, 409 prep_item_auto (offline_pack), 409 prep_item_na

PrepItem: {"id", "status": "todo"|"done"|"na", "auto": bool, "due": "YYYY-MM-DD"|null, "overdue": bool, "facts": {…}}. total counts the items that are not na, percent = floor(100 × done / total) (0 when total is 0), and complete = total > 0 and done == total. Items, in order, with due relative to the start (null without a start):

id na when due facts visa the visa row says visa-free start − (visa lead days, or 21) visa_type, max_stay_days, processing_time, official_url, source (ai from the snapshot, else static, else null) passport — start − 30 — bookings — start − 30 flight: bool, hotel: bool (selected in the plan) insurance — start − 14 — documents — start − 7 — stress_test no itinerary start − 7 score: int \| null (the last score, Task 37) sim — start − 3 plan_name \| null money — start − 3 currency \| null (the local currency code) packing — start − 1 items: int emergency_card — start − 1 — checkin no flight selected start − 1 — offline_pack (auto) — start − 1 saved_at \| null

Visa lead days: none for visa-free. Otherwise take the largest number in processing_time: weeks × 7, business days × 1.4 rounded up, days as is. Add 7 days of buffer. When there is no number, use 21. When complete first becomes true, the trip's trip_ready award is made (once per trip).

Stores the merged object with as_of = server time 413 snapshot_too_large (> 262144 bytes as JSON), 422 snapshot_invalid GET /trips/{id}/offline-pack query today? OfflinePack with Cache-Control: no-store. Marks prep offline_pack done (Task 37) 404

  • phrases is null for English-speaking countries.

docs.title: Expenses
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/expenses — {"expenses": [Expense], "totals": {"by_currency": {"EUR": "123.40"}, "usd_estimate": "140.20" \| null, "by_category_usd": {"food": "40.00"}, "unconverted": ["GBP"]}, "rate": {"local": "EUR", "usd_to_local": 0.92, "as_of": "…Z"} \| null} 404 POST /trips/{id}/expenses {"client_id": uuid, "amount": "12.50", "currency": "EUR", "category", "note"?: ≤140, "spent_on": day} 201 Expense, or 200 Expense (the existing row) when client_id was already used on this trip 422 amount_invalid, 422 currency_invalid, 422 category_invalid, 422 note_too_long, 409 expense_limit (2000 per trip) PATCH /trips/{id}/expenses/{eid} a subset of amount, currency, category, note, spent_on Expense the above, 404 expense_not_found DELETE /trips/{id}/expenses/{eid} — 204 404 expense_not_found

Expense: {"id", "client_id", "amount": "12.50", "currency": "EUR", "category", "note", "spent_on", "created_at", "updated_at"}. category ∈ flights|lodging|food|transport|activities|shopping|fees|other. Amounts are decimal strings stored as integer minor units, with the currency's exponent: 0 for JPY KRW VND CLP ISK UGX XAF XOF, 3 for BHD KWD OMR JOD TND, else 2. The rules are 0 < amount ≤ 1,000,000 and no more decimals than the exponent allows. USD estimates use only USD rows and rows in the snapshot's local currency (amount / usd_to_local). Every other currency is listed in unconverted.

docs.title: Journal and places (ratings, visits)
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/journal — {"entries": [Entry]}, sorted by day (nulls last), then created_at 404 POST /trips/{id}/journal {"client_id": uuid, "body": 1..4000, "day"?, "mood"?: "great"\|"good"\|"ok"\|"tough"} 201 Entry, or 200 on a repeated client_id 422 journal_empty, 422 journal_too_long, 422 mood_invalid, 409 journal_limit (500) PATCH /trips/{id}/journal/{eid} a subset of body, day, mood Entry the above, 404 entry_not_found DELETE /trips/{id}/journal/{eid} — 204 404 entry_not_found GET /trips/{id}/places — {"places": [TripPlace]} 404 PUT /trips/{id}/places/{place_key} {"name": 1..120, "kind", "visited"?: bool, "stars"?: 1..5 \| null, "note"?: ≤500, "day"?, "lat"?, "lng"?} (upsert; omitted fields are kept) {"place": TripPlace, "game": GameDelta \| null}. game is set when visited first becomes true 422 place_key_invalid, 422 stars_invalid, 422 note_too_long, 409 places_limit (1000) DELETE /trips/{id}/places/{place_key} — 204 404 place_not_found

Entry: {"id", "client_id", "day", "body", "mood", "created_at", "updated_at"}. TripPlace: {"place_key", "name", "kind", "visited", "stars", "note", "day", "lat", "lng", "visited_at", "updated_at"}.

docs.title: Today
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors POST /trips/{id}/checkin {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD"} 200 {"day", "day_index", "city", "country_code", "new_country": bool, "streak": {"current", "longest", "last_day", "freezes"} \| null, "game": GameDelta \| null}. A second call for the same day returns the same data with an empty delta 409 checkin_out_of_trip (day outside [start, end]), 422 checkin_day_invalid (more than 1 day from the server's UTC date) GET /trips/{id}/checkins — {"days": ["2027-04-01"], "streak": … \| null} 404

The city for day n follows the multi-city allocation of TravelSearchRequest.city_stays (destination_nights honoured), else destination.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/recap query today? Recap 404 POST /trips/{id}/recap/complete query today? {"completed_at", "new_countries": ["PT"], "game": GameDelta \| null}. Idempotent: a repeat returns the first completed_at, new_countries: [] and an empty delta 409 recap_not_ready (today ≤ end date, or no dates)

Recap:

{"trip_id": 12, "title": "…", "start_date": "…", "end_date": "…", "days": 8, "nights": 7, "planned_days": 7,
 "places": [TripPlace], "visited_count": 9, "rated_count": 7, "avg_stars": 4.3,
 "route": [[38.70, -9.14]], "distance_km": 41.2,
 "countries": [{"code": "PT", "name": "Portugal", "new": true}], "continents": ["EU"],
 "spend": {"budget_usd": 3000, "plan_cost_usd": null, "spent_usd": "2140.50", "by_category_usd": {…}, "unconverted": ["GBP"]},
 "journal_count": 5, "checkin_days": 6, "completed_at": null, "can_complete": true}
  • route holds the visited places with coordinates, ordered by day then visited_at (at most 500 points).
  • distance_km is the haversine sum along route, to one decimal, or null with fewer than two points. Clients that have the itinerary may draw the planned route when route is empty.
  • new means the country was added to user_countries by this trip.
  • plan_cost_usd is null on the server (clients compute it with computePlanCost).

docs.title: Stress test (additive)
docs.text: POST /stress-test accepts an optional plan_id. When the caller is signed in and owns the plan, the server stores the returned score as the prep stress_test fact and marks that item done. When the score is higher than the previous one, it awards smart_planner. The response is unchanged.

docs.title: Client notes
docs.text:
Guidance for the web, iOS and Android clients. It adds no API surface.

  • Feature detection. Call GET /config at start-up. Show no trips UI and make no trips call unless features.trips is true. The journey UI (Trips hub, phases, Today, recap) also needs features.journey. When features.offline_pack is false, unregister the service worker (web), delete every offline cache and pack, hide the offline tab and save actions, and never register the service worker again; the server then answers GET /trips/{id}/offline-pack with 404 offline_pack_disabled. A backend without features.trips is the previous backend: behave exactly as before.
  • Phase function. Every client implements the phase rules from "Phases" and must pass the golden cases in backend/tests/fixtures/journey/trip_phase_cases.json. The server value in Trip.phase is authoritative when online. Offline, recompute it from the cached dates and the device's local date.
  • Trip dates. Trip dates are normalised: a stored end before the start is returned as the start, so clients can apply the phase function to the Trip's dates as given.
  • today. Send the device's local date (YYYY-MM-DD) as today= on every GET that accepts it, and use the today echoed by GET /trips for the hub. For check-in, send the local date as day. The server accepts it within +-1 day of its UTC date, so a traveller in Tokyo on the morning of day 1 still gets "Day 1".
  • Offline writes. Create every expense and journal entry with a fresh UUID client_id and queue it in a per-user outbox when offline. Flush the outbox single-flight (one flush at a time, per user). Resending is safe: a repeated client_id answers 200 with the existing row, so exactly one row results. Delete a user's packs and outbox on sign-out.
  • Snapshot. After every plan save or update made while results are on screen, send PUT /trips/{id}/snapshot with the section results as streamed (without verification). It feeds the offline pack and the prep facts.
  • Place keys. Build place_key as <kind>:<slug> with the slug rule in "Shared objects". Test your slug function against backend/tests/fixtures/journey/place_key_cases.json; for example ["activity", "Pastéis de Belém!"] gives activity:pasteis-de-belem. Additive rule (names with non-ASCII letters or digits, such as CJK, Devanagari, Bengali, Arabic, ø, ß): after the slug is built, cut it to 51 characters, trim - (empty becomes x) and append - plus 8 lowercase hex digits, the FNV-1a 32-bit hash (offset 0x811c9dc5, prime 0x01000193) of the UTF-8 bytes of the NFC-normalised name with outer whitespace trimmed. Distinct non-Latin names then get distinct keys, and the key still matches ^[a-z]+:[a-z0-9-]{1,60}$. Pure ASCII names are unchanged. The fixture file carries the vectors. Native clients must adopt this before shipping Trips for non-Latin names.
  • Home screen. Show the Trips hub as the start screen when the signed-in user has at least one trip, otherwise Explore (search). Signed-out users see Explore. Both stay reachable from the tabs.
  • Mobile tabs. Trips (hub and trip detail), Explore (search, chat and Near me), Alerts (fare and price watches), Play (game and bucket list), You (account, preferences, settings).
  • Game ids to translate. Translate each rule id in the "Game" table as game:rules.<id> and each badge as game:badges.<id>.name and game:badges.<id>.desc. The ids: rules traveller_type, plan_saved, trip_ready, smart_planner, trip_checkin, place_visited, country_visited, continent_visited, recap_complete; badges traveller, first_trip, trip_ready, ready_regular, smart_planner, on_the_road, road_warrior, local_explorer, local_legend, countries_3, countries_10, countries_30, continents_3, continents_6, storyteller, memory_keeper. Hide every game element when hide_game is set.

docs.text:
Field-level 422 codes the backend emits beyond the tables above. Clients should show a generic message for any 422 *_invalid code they do not know.

Route Extra code When POST /trips/{id}/expenses, PATCH .../expenses/{eid} 422 spent_on_invalid spent_on is not a YYYY-MM-DD day POST /trips/{id}/expenses, POST /trips/{id}/journal 422 client_id_invalid client_id is missing or not a UUID POST /trips/{id}/journal, PATCH .../journal/{eid} 422 day_invalid day is not a YYYY-MM-DD day PUT /trips/{id}/places/{place_key} 422 name_invalid name is not 1 to 120 characters PUT /trips/{id}/places/{place_key} 422 kind_invalid kind is not one of the place kinds PUT /trips/{id}/places/{place_key} 422 visited_invalid visited is not a boolean

TripPlace.visited_at is a never-cleared first-visit marker: it is set the first time visited becomes true and stays when visited is later set back to false. Clients read visited for the current state and use visited_at only for ordering and "first visited".
