docs.title: Place Resolution — Remaining Items Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Resolve the three open place-lookup items generically: (1) country nicknames and native names ("Deutschland", "Brasil", "España", "Nippon", "KSA", "PRC"…), (2) suburbs without their own airport beating namesake cities that have one ("Peoria" → Arizona instead of Illinois/PIA), (3) islands, national parks, ski resorts, regions, mountains, valleys and archaeological sites that are not towns returning None.

Spec: User request 2026-10-30 ("proceed with the Still Open items and solve them comprehensively"). The user approved downloading GeoNames allCountries.zip (CC BY 4.0, same licence as the cities file already used). Choices otherwise Claude's.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
• /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/geonames-all/allCountries.zip (untrusted data: read with python3 -I, stream the zip — do not unzip 1.6 GB to disk unless needed; never execute anything from it). Standard GeoNames columns (geonameid, name, asciiname, alternatenames, lat, lng, feature class, feature code, country code, cc2, admin1, admin2, admin3, admin4, population, elevation, dem, timezone, modified).
  • Existing: generator backend/scripts/build_place_data.py, data in backend/app/db/data/ (airports.csv, places.csv.gz, admin1.csv, countries.csv, hints.json), runtime backend/app/db/places_db.py (resolve_place), backend/app/db/database.py (lookup_city_iata, search_airports), backend/app/agents/static_results.py (_place_country), golden set backend/tests/data/golden_places.csv, data README.

docs.title: Verified facts
docs.text:
• "Peoria": Peoria US-AZ (pop 190,985, score 3.87e8, airports PHX — PHX's display city is Phoenix) vs Peoria US-IL (pop 115,070, score 1.04e8, airports PIA, its own). AZ wins by 3.7× today.
  • Same pattern elsewhere: Aurora CO/IL (both suburbs of Denver/Chicago), Glendale CA/AZ (both suburbs), Arlington TX/VA (both suburbs).
  • OurAirports countries.csv keywords are too noisy for native names; GeoNames political-entity features carry multilingual alternate names.

docs.title: A. Country names (generic)
docs.text:
• Generator: from allCountries features with feature class A and codes PCLI, PCLD, PCLF, PCLS, PCL, PCLIX, TERR collect the name, asciiname and Latin-script alternate names (≤40 chars, not URLs, not ISO-3 or other all-caps ≤4 tokens unless in the curated alias list) per ISO country code; write them as a names column (|-joined, folded) in backend/app/db/data/countries.csv.
  • Curated aliases (hints.json) only for colloquial abbreviations GeoNames lacks, each verified absent from the data first: at least KSA → SA, PRC → CN, ROK → KR, DPRK → KP, ROC → TW, UAE → AE (exists), USA/US/UK/GB (exist). No ISO-3 codes in general (they collide with IATA codes).
  • Runtime: country names from this column are recognised everywhere a country is today (qualifier "Berlin, Deutschland", no-comma "Munich Deutschland", standalone "Brasil" → the country's gateway airports, _place_country).
  • Collision guard: a country alternate name that is also a tier-0 place name with population ≥ 15k (e.g. a city) does not override the place; measure and report collisions.

docs.title: B. Suburbs without their own airport (generic)
docs.text:
• Generator: mark each place satellite=1 when its first linked airport is not its own (own = the shared own-airport definition: display city equals the place, name contains the place name, or ≤25 km same country) AND that airport is own to a different place with higher score within 60 km. Add the column to places.csv.gz and the places table (versioned reseed handles migration).
  • Runtime dominance: when the top-scoring candidate is a satellite and the best non-satellite candidate (one with its own airport) scores ≥ 1/10 of it, the non-satellite takes its place as the leader; the normal 3× dominance test then runs against the remaining candidates. Otherwise normal rules apply. Expected outcomes (pin as golden rows; calibrate the 1/10 on the probe sets if needed): Peoria → PIA; Glendale → None (both satellites, comparable); Aurora → DEN or None (both satellites); Arlington → DFW group (both satellites, 42×); Springfield → None; Portland → PDX unchanged.

docs.title: C. Non-town features (generic)
docs.text:
• Generator: from allCountries, features with feature codes in a documented allow-list — islands/archipelagos/atolls (ISL, ISLS, ATOL, ISLT excluded), peninsulas (PEN), parks and reserves (PRK, RESN, RESW, RESF), resorts and ski areas (RSRT, ski codes if present), regions/areas/coasts (RGN, AREA, CST), mountains and ranges (MT, MTS, PK, VLC — volcanoes), valleys (VAL), lakes (LK), beaches (BCH), archaeological/historical sites and monuments (ANS, RUIN, HSTS, MNMT), deserts (DSRT), gorges/canyons (GRGE, CNYN) — kept only when notable: alternate-name count ≥ N (calibrate; start at 10; report the count/size trade-off) and an airport within 250 km.
  • New committed file backend/app/db/data/features.csv.gz (≤ 3 MB): geonameid, name, ascii, country_code, admin1, feature_code, notability, lat, lng, airports, alt_names. Airports linked like places but by distance only, same-country first (large/medium within 250 km, ≤3, ranked by (foreign, type, distance)); islands also take airports located on the island when determinable (airport within the island's reach and not farther than the nearest mainland alternative — keep it simple and documented).
  • Loader: new features table + feature_names (tier 0 name/ascii, tier 1 alternates), versioned with the rest.
  • Resolution: after curated hints/exonyms and before giving up, and also as competing candidates: a feature beats town candidates when every town candidate has population < 15k (or none exist) and the feature's notability ≥ calibrated threshold; a town with population ≥ 15k beats a feature of the same name (Banff town vs park both map to YYC — fine either way). Hints still override everything. _place_country uses the feature's country.
  • Autocomplete: features may contribute suggestions (their airports) below town matches, same no-padding rules.

docs.title: D. Measurement (all mandatory, before → after)
docs.text: Run every probe set: 660 (scratchpad/fr), 432 (rr), blind-824 (blind), lc-408 + lc-nc-160 (lc), and the golden set. Constraint: no set gains a WRONG; golden stays green. Report WRONG/NONE per set and per item (A/B/C). Then the controller commissions a fresh blind probe.

docs.title: E. Docs
docs.text: Place-and-Airport-Data.md (sources incl. allCountries, features, satellite rule, country names), data README (regeneration command now takes allCountries), CLAUDE.md one line, Changelog entry.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text: No new deps; stdlib generator; deterministic output; committed data total ≤ 9 MB; no network at runtime or in tests; lookup_city_iata p99 < 3 ms; backend pytest + ruff; frontend untouched unless autocomplete tests need it.

docs.title: Task 1: Generator + data (countries names, satellite flag, features) + loader (+tests)
Task 2: Runtime resolution (A, B, C) + autocomplete + measurement + docs (+tests)
Timed Itinerary (Minute-Level Scheduling) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Every itinerary activity shows an estimated start–end time and the travel time from the previous stop; days that don't fit are flagged; times follow the user's drag-and-drop edits and flow into Timeline, calendar export, print, share and the Health Check re-check.

Spec: Backlog #18. Facts: research-16-18-9.md (#18 section) in the scratchpad. Choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) LLM emits times — rejected: stale as soon as the user moves an activity, and unverifiable; (b) deterministic client-side scheduler applied after arrangeItinerary — chosen: one source of truth that re-runs on every edit; positions/keys (<day>-<time_of_day>) unchanged, so edits/notes/plan picks/.ics UIDs keep working.

Scheduler (pure frontend/src/utils/schedule.js, unit-tested, node env): - scheduleDays(days, edits = {}) -> days' (new objects) adding to each slot start_time "HH:MM", end_time, transit_from_prev: { minutes, mode: 'walk'|'transit', km } | null, and to each day schedule_warnings: string[]. - Bucket anchors: morning 09:00, afternoon 13:30, evening 18:30; slots ordered by existing rank (time_of_day order, odd slots by slotRanks rule — reuse helpers from itineraryLayout.js). - Duration: duration_hours (finite, 0.25–12) else defaults morning 3h / afternoon 3h / evening 2.5h; edits don't change duration. - Transit between consecutive slots: if both have finite lat/lng → km = haversine × 1.3; walk if km ≤ 1.5 (4.5 km/h), else transit (20 km/h + 10 min); minutes rounded up to 5; first slot of a day has no transit. Missing coords → transit_from_prev: null but scheduling assumes a 20-min buffer. - start = max(anchor, prev.end + transit/buffer); end = start + duration. - Warnings: start pushed > 45 min past its anchor → " starts at 14:20 — later than planned"; day ends after 23:00 → "Day N runs past 23:00". Days with no standard slots untouched. - Shared haversine: extract haversineKm from TripMap.jsx into frontend/src/utils/geo.js (TripMap imports it).

Wiring (renderers use scheduleDays(arrangeItinerary(...).days, edits)): - ItinerarySection: row shows "09:00–12:00" under the time-of-day label; between rows a muted transit line ("🚶 12 min walk · 0.9 km" / "🚇 ~25 min by transit" / nothing when unknown); a per-day amber "Tight schedule" chip listing warnings; a one-line note "Times are estimates based on typical durations and distances." - TimelineView: show times in each slot card. - planExport.js (.ics): use start_time/end_time when present (fallback SLOT_HOURS unchanged → existing tests stay green); planItineraryDays returns scheduled days. - planPrint.js, SharePage.jsx, PlanViewModal.jsx: show "09:00–12:00" next to time_of_day. - Stress-test re-check payload (utils/stressTestPayload.js from the polish branch): include start/end/transit; backend stress_test_agent._summarize_itinerary prints HH:MM–HH:MM and transit minutes when present (backend unit test). - Prompts: .agents/itinerary.md and backend/app/agents/itinerary_agent.py — require duration_hours on every slot and lat/lng on every slot that names a specific place (no other changes); backend fallback itinerary unchanged. - ChatPage unchanged. - Docs: Frontend.md, Agent-System.md one line.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text: No new deps. Existing itineraryLayout / planExport / planPrint tests must pass unchanged. Frontend vitest/eslint/build; backend pytest/ruff.

docs.title: Task 2: Renderers (ItinerarySection, TimelineView, planExport, planPrint, SharePage, PlanViewModal) + stress payload/backend summary
Plan a Trip From a Link or Screenshot — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: A traveller pastes a travel blog / article / video link, pastes text (a caption, a friend's message, a list), or drops up to 4 screenshots — and gets a trip: the places are extracted, mapped and shown for review, then a normal full search plans the trip around those places, every one of them visibly scheduled in the itinerary ("From your link"). It must feel magical, fast and trustworthy.

Spec: User request 2026-11-04 — feature #3 "Plan from a link or screenshot", "very thoroughly and comprehensively … ENSURE THESE FEATURES DELIGHT USERS". Design choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Existing building blocks (verified)
docs.text:
• Backend FastAPI; agents call Anthropic directly through BaseAgent (backend/app/agents/base_agent.py, Haiku; Sonnet for chat). beautifulsoup4 and httpx are dependencies. Rate limiting: backend/app/core/rate_limit.py (rate_limit(bucket) dependency, try_consume), settings RATE_LIMIT_*.
  • Place resolution: backend/app/db/places_db.py resolve_place(text), backend/app/db/database.py lookup_city_iata, static_results._place_country; places/features tables carry lat/lng and country.
  • TravelSearchRequest (backend/app/schemas/request.py): origin, destination, destinations (multi-city ≤3 stops), destination_nights, dates, interests, pace, budget, travellers, etc.
  • Orchestrator backend/app/agents/orchestrator.py (phases 0/1/2, SSE); activities agent; itinerary agent backend/app/agents/itinerary_agent.py takes activities (top 12 summarised) and hotels.
  • Frontend: SearchPage.jsx has modes "I know where I'm going" / "Surprise me" / "Compare"; ResultsPage.jsx renders sections incl. ItinerarySection, TripMap (Leaflet), My Plan drawer; saved plans store search_data; share page SharePage.jsx; utils/planExport.js / planPrint.js.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
1. POST /api/import/extract (auth required; new rate-limit bucket import, default 20 per window, setting RATE_LIMIT_IMPORT). Body: { url?: str, text?: str (≤ 20,000 chars), images?: [{ media_type, data_base64 }] (≤ 4, each ≤ 5 MB decoded; png/jpeg/webp/gif; HEIC rejected with a friendly message) } — exactly one kind of source. Response = an ImportPreview (below). Also accepts multipart image upload if simpler for the frontend; document whichever is used.
  2. Safe URL fetching (backend/app/services/link_fetch.py):
  3. http/https only; resolve DNS and reject private, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved, CGNAT and IPv6 equivalents for the initial host and every redirect hop (max 3 redirects, manual redirect handling); connect to the vetted IP (prevent DNS rebinding) while sending the original Host/SNI; timeout 10 s; stop reading at 2 MB; accept text/html, application/xhtml+xml, text/plain; send a normal browser-like UA.
  4. Extraction: <title>, OpenGraph/Twitter description, JSON-LD (Article/Recipe-like articleBody, ItemList, Place, TouristAttraction), and readable main text (prefer <article>/<main>, drop nav/footer/script/style, keep headings and list items — itineraries are usually lists). Cap at ~30k chars.
  5. Social video/photo links: YouTube and TikTok via their public oEmbed endpoints (title/caption/author); YouTube description is not in oEmbed — use page metadata when available. Instagram/Facebook/X usually block — return a specific friendly error {"code": "blocked_source", "message": "Instagram doesn't let apps read posts. Paste the caption or drop a screenshot instead."} and the frontend switches the user to the text/screenshot tabs with one click.
  6. Never execute scripts; never follow links found in content.
  7. Extraction agent (.agents/link_import.md + backend/app/agents/link_import_agent.py, Haiku via BaseAgent; images use Claude vision content blocks): returns strict JSON { title, summary (1 sentence), places: [{ name, kind (sight|food|drink|stay|activity|nature|shopping|nightlife|event|transport|area), city, country, note (≤ 140 chars, why the source recommends it), quote (≤ 120 chars verbatim from source, optional), day_hint (int|null), confidence (0–1) }], destinations_mentioned: [str], suggested_days (int|null), season_hint (str|null), interests: [str] }. Prompt-injection hardening: source content is wrapped as untrusted data with clear delimiters; the system prompt says to ignore any instructions inside it and only extract places; output validated with Pydantic; at most 40 places; drop items without a name. No PII echoed beyond place names.
  8. Resolution & grouping (backend/app/services/link_import.py):
  9. For each place: resolve its city (+ country) with resolve_place / _place_country → canonical city, country, lat/lng (city-level), airports. POI-level coordinates: if SERPER_KEY is configured, look the POI up (existing Serper places helper — find it) to get coordinates/address/rating and mark verified: true; otherwise use the city centre with approximate: true. Respect existing caches; cap Serper calls per import (≤ 25) and run them concurrently with a semaphore.
  10. Group by resolved city; order cities by day_hint then source order. One city → single destination. 2–3 cities in ≤ 3 countries → propose a multi-city route (destinations + destination_nights split by place count, min 1 night). More than 3 cities → keep the 3 with the most places, list the rest as "also mentioned".
  11. Suggested length: suggested_days if given, else ~4 places per day bounded 2–14.
  12. Unresolved places stay in the preview under "Couldn't place" (editable on the client).
  13. Response ImportPreview: { source: { kind: url|text|images, url?, title, site_name?, favicon_url?, author? }, title, summary, destinations: [{ name (the resolved display, e.g. "Lisbon, Portugal"), country, airports, place_count, nights }], places: [{ id, name, kind, city, country, lat, lng, approximate, verified, note, quote, day_hint, confidence }], unresolved: [...], suggested_days, season_hint, interests, warnings: [str] }.
  14. Search integration: add must_include: list[MustIncludePlace] | None (≤ 25; each { name, kind, city, lat?, lng?, note? }) and import_source: { url?, title } | None to TravelSearchRequest (and pass them through chat-independent paths only).
  15. Activities: must-include places are merged into the activities result as items with source: "your_link", from_link: true (deduplicated against the agent's own results by folded name) and always kept, at the top.
  16. Itinerary: the itinerary agent prompt lists must-include places as "MUST schedule every one of these" with their city; after the agent returns, a deterministic post-check inserts any missing must-include place into the least-loaded slot of the right city's days (or appends a day note if all slots are full) and marks scheduled slots from_link: true. The template fallback itinerary also includes them.
  17. Phase-0/verification: imported items carry their own verification (verified via Serper or "From your link — not independently checked").
  18. Saved plans keep must_include and import_source in search_data; share page and print/export show "Inspired by (link)".</li> <li><strong>Chat touch:</strong> if a chat message is just a URL (or contains a URL and "plan"), the assistant replies with a short message and an action that opens the import flow prefilled (<code>/?import=<url-encoded></code>) — no fetching inside chat.</li> </ol> <h3 id="frontend-delight-is-a-requirement-not-polish">Frontend (delight is a requirement, not polish)</h3> <ol> <li><strong>Entry points:</strong> a 4th Search mode tab <strong>"From a link ✨"</strong>; a hero hint on the Search page ("Saw a great trip online? Paste the link"); deep link <code>/?import=<url></code> prefills and auto-starts; drag-and-drop a screenshot anywhere on the Search page opens the import tab with it; paste (Cmd/Ctrl-V) of an image or URL in the import tab works.</li> <li><strong>Import panel:</strong> one smart input that accepts a URL or free text (auto-detects), a screenshot drop zone (thumbnails, remove ×, 4 max, size/type validation messages), and 3 "Try an example" chips (a sample blog URL is risky — use example <em>texts</em>: e.g. "48 hours in Lisbon: Time Out Market, Belém Tower, LX Factory, sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte…").</li> <li><strong>Progress that tells a story:</strong> staged steps with gentle animation — "Reading the page" → "Finding places" → "Putting them on the map" — and a cancel button; skeleton cards. Typical time 5–15 s; show it.</li> <li><strong>Preview ("Here's what we found"):</strong> source card (favicon, title, site, link), the trip title and one-line summary, a Leaflet map with numbered pins coloured by kind (fit bounds; approximate pins drawn hollow with a tooltip "approximate location"), places grouped by city with kind icons (lucide), the source's note/quote in italics, a checkbox per place (all on by default; "Select all / none" per city), inline rename and "Change city" for wrong ones, the "Couldn't place" group with an inline city field to fix, destination chips with nights steppers, and a suggested trip length. Below: the normal trip fields prefilled (origin from preferences, dates = next suitable window: today + 30 days by default, length from the suggestion; interests from the extraction merged with preferences). Primary button: <strong>"Plan this trip (N places)"</strong>. Secondary: "Start over".</li> <li><strong>Results:</strong> a dismissible banner at the top "Planned around 11 places from <em>48 hours in Lisbon</em> — all 11 are in your itinerary" (or "10 of 11 — 1 didn't fit: show"); activity cards and itinerary rows from the link carry a small <strong>"From your link"</strong> chip with the quote on hover/tap; TripMap shows them with a distinct marker; My Plan drawer shows the source. Saved plans list shows a link icon.</li> <li><strong>Errors are friendly and actionable:</strong> blocked source → one-click switch to text/screenshot; no places found → "We couldn't spot any places — try pasting the part of the article with the list"; paywall/404/timeouts → specific messages; rate limit → server detail; image too big / HEIC → explain and suggest PNG/JPEG.</li> <li><strong>Quality bar:</strong> responsive down to 360 px, keyboard accessible (tab order, Enter to submit, Esc to cancel), ARIA live region for progress, reduced-motion respected, consistent with existing Tailwind/lucide style, no layout shift. Analytics events via the existing <code>track()</code> helper (import_started/kind, import_preview_shown/place_count, import_planned, import_failed/code).</li> </ol> <h3 id="docs">Docs</h3> <p>Trip-Planning-Features.md (new section with screenshots-free description), API-Reference.md (endpoint + request fields), Configuration.md (<code>RATE_LIMIT_IMPORT</code>), Architecture.md (flow), CLAUDE.md one line, Changelog entry, README feature bullet.</p> <h2 id="global-constraints">Global Constraints</h2> <p>No new Python/npm dependencies. No network in tests (mock httpx, Anthropic, Serper). SSRF tests are mandatory (private IPs incl. IPv6 and mapped IPv4, redirect to private, non-http schemes, oversized body, wrong content type, DNS rebinding pin). Backend pytest + ruff; frontend vitest + eslint + build. Existing tests stay green.</p> <hr /> <h3 id="task-1-safe-link-fetching-content-extraction-ssrf-tests">Task 1: Safe link fetching + content extraction (+SSRF tests)</h3> <h3 id="task-2-extraction-agent-texturlimages-resolutiongrouping-service-post-apiimportextract-rate-bucket-tests">Task 2: Extraction agent (text/url/images) + resolution/grouping service + <code>POST /api/import/extract</code> + rate bucket (+tests)</h3> <h3 id="task-3-must_include-import_source-through-search-activities-merge-itinerary-prompt-deterministic-post-check-template-fallback-savedshareexport-tests">Task 3: <code>must_include</code> / <code>import_source</code> through search: activities merge, itinerary prompt + deterministic post-check + template fallback, saved/share/export (+tests)</h3> <h3 id="task-4-frontend-import-tab-preview-map-review-edit-progress-errors-deep-link-results-bannerchips-chat-hand-off-tests">Task 4: Frontend import tab, preview (map, review, edit), progress, errors, deep link, results banner/chips, chat hand-off (+tests)</h3> <h3 id="task-5-docs">Task 5: Docs</h3>

docs.title: Fare Watch & Price Alerts — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: A traveller can "watch" the fare for a trip (from the Flights section, the fare calendar, My Plan or a saved plan). The app re-checks live Google Flights prices on a schedule and tells them — in the app (bell + alerts page), optionally by email and by a browser notification — when the price drops, hits their target, or a cheaper nearby date appears, with a one-click way to re-plan or book. It must feel like a helpful friend watching prices, never spammy.

Spec: User request 2026-11-04 — feature #2 "Price alerts on saved trips", "very thoroughly and comprehensively … ENSURE THESE FEATURES DELIGHT USERS". Design choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Existing building blocks (verified)
docs.text:
• Live fares: backend/app/services/serp_flights.py — search(api_key, request, filters) (single-city, cached by _main_key incl. traveller count), search_calendar(api_key, request, window=3) (cheapest outbound-stage fare per date ±3, _calendar_key), price_insights (lowest_price, price_level, typical_price_range, price_history), _cheapest. settings.serpapi_key; /health reports serpapi_configured.
  • Routes: POST /api/flights/fare-calendar (auth, light_ai bucket, 503 without SerpAPI). Rate limiting: backend/app/core/rate_limit.py.
  • App startup: backend/app/main.py lifespan creates tables and starts background tasks (asyncio.create_task(start_periodic_backup(...))). SQLite in $DATA_DIR/airports.db; helpers in backend/app/db/*_db.py; get_connection() is a closing context manager. Backups exclude only regenerable place tables — new tables ARE backed up.
  • Users have an optional email (backend/app/db/users_db.py); no email sending exists.
  • Frontend: Flights section + FareCalendarStrip.jsx + price-insights chip in ResultsPage.jsx; My Plan drawer; saved plans (PlanViewModal.jsx, ChatPage drawer); header/nav in App.jsx; services/api.js; track() analytics.

docs.title: Data model (new tables, created in lifespan)
docs.text:
• fare_watches: id, user_id (FK), plan_id (nullable), origin_code, destination_code (resolved IATA, comma lists allowed), origin_label, destination_label, departure_date, return_date (nullable = one-way), num_travelers, cabin (default economy), flexible_days (0 or 3), alert_mode (any_drop | below_target), target_price (nullable), email_enabled (bool), status (active | paused | expired | error), baseline_price, last_price, lowest_price, lowest_price_date (for flexible), last_notified_price, google_price_level, google_typical_low, google_typical_high, check_count, last_checked_at, next_check_at, lease_until (for safe single-processor scheduling), last_error, created_at, updated_at.
  • fare_watch_history: watch_id, checked_at, price (selected dates), cheapest_price, cheapest_departure_date, cheapest_return_date, price_level. Keep ≤ 120 rows per watch.
  • notifications: id, user_id, kind (fare_drop | fare_target | fare_low_level | fare_cheaper_date | watch_expired | watch_error), title, body, data JSON (watch_id, prices, dates, deep links), created_at, read_at, emailed_at.
  • Limits: FARE_WATCH_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER (default 10).

docs.title: Scheduler (backend/app/services/fare_watch.py)
docs.text:
• Started in lifespan only when serpapi_key is set and FARE_WATCH_ENABLED (default true); loop every FARE_WATCH_TICK_SECONDS (default 300): claim due watches (status='active' AND next_check_at <= now AND (lease_until IS NULL OR lease_until < now)) with an atomic UPDATE setting lease_until (safe if several workers ever run), process with a concurrency semaphore (3), then set next_check_at = now + FARE_WATCH_INTERVAL_HOURS (default 12) ± 10% jitter.
  • Quota guard: FARE_WATCH_DAILY_CALL_BUDGET (default 200 SerpAPI calls/day, persisted counter in meta-like table keyed by UTC date); when exhausted, postpone remaining checks to the next day and log once. One check = 1 SerpAPI call for exact dates (outbound-stage price via the same code path the calendar uses), or the calendar's up-to-7 calls when flexible_days=3 — cached results are reused and cost nothing.
  • Departure date passed (or < today + 1) → status expired + a watch_expired notification (once).
  • Repeated SerpAPI failures (3 in a row) → status error + watch_error notification with a "Retry" action; transient failures just reschedule sooner (1 h).
  • Trigger rules (pure function evaluate(watch, new_check) -> list[Notification], heavily unit-tested):
  • below_target: price ≤ target and the last notification for this watch wasn't already at ≤ this price → fare_target.
  • any_drop: price ≤ last_notified_price or baseline − max($15, 5 %) → fare_drop ("dropped $46").
  • New lowest since watching AND Google price_level == "low" → fare_low_level ("Google says this is a low price for this route").
  • Flexible watches: a nearby date is cheaper than the selected dates by ≥ max($25, 8 %) → fare_cheaper_date.
  • Anti-spam: at most one notification per watch per 24 h unless the price drops a further ≥ 5 % below the last notified price; never notify for increases (but record them); never notify on the first check after creation (that sets the baseline).
  • Prices are per the request's traveller count — label everything "total for N travellers" consistently with the Flights section.

docs.title: Notifications delivery
docs.text:
• In-app: GET /api/notifications?unread_only= (paginated), POST /api/notifications/read (ids or all), GET /api/notifications/unread-count. Header bell with unread badge in App.jsx, dropdown with the latest 10 (icon per kind, relative time, primary action), "Mark all as read", link to the Alerts page. Poll unread count every 60 s while the tab is visible (pause when hidden; refresh on focus).
  • Browser notifications: when the app is open and the user has granted permission, show a native notification for new fare notifications (asked contextually — after creating the first watch, with an explanatory inline prompt, never on page load).
  • Email (optional): SMTP via stdlib smtplib in a thread (asyncio.to_thread) when SMTP_HOST is configured (SMTP_PORT default 587, SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_FROM, SMTP_STARTTLS default true) and the watch has email_enabled and the user has an email. Multipart text + HTML (inline-styled, no remote images): headline, route, dates, old → new price with the delta, lowest seen, a tiny inline-SVG-free text sparkline (e.g. ▁▂▄▂▁), CTA links ("See flights", "Re-plan with this fare") to APP_BASE_URL (new setting, default http://localhost:5174), and an unsubscribe-from-this-watch link (signed token endpoint GET /api/fare-watches/unsubscribe?token= that turns off email for that watch without login). Failures logged, never break checks.
  • Users without an email can add one on the Preferences page (new field, validated) — the create-watch dialog links there.

docs.title: API (auth required; ownership enforced on every route → 404 for others' resources)
docs.text:
• POST /api/fare-watches — from a TravelSearchRequest-like body (origin, destination, dates, travellers) or { plan_id }; resolves codes via the existing request validators (typed cities work); takes an immediate first check (baseline) inline if quota allows (else schedules it), returns the watch with history.
  • GET /api/fare-watches (with latest history + sparkline points), GET /api/fare-watches/{id}, PATCH /api/fare-watches/{id} (status pause/resume, alert_mode, target, email_enabled, flexible_days), DELETE /api/fare-watches/{id}, POST /api/fare-watches/{id}/check ("Check now", rate-limited light_ai, also subject to the daily budget).
  • 503 with a friendly detail when SerpAPI isn't configured; multi-city trips → 422 "Fare watch works for single-destination trips for now".

docs.title: Frontend (delight is a requirement)
docs.text:
1. "Watch this fare" entry points: a bell-plus button in the Flights section header (next to Fare calendar / Filters), on the fare-calendar strip ("Watch these dates"), on a selected flight in My Plan, and on saved-plan cards / PlanViewModal. If already watched → "Watching · $412" state that opens the watch.
  2. Create dialog: shows the current price and Google's typical range bar with today's price marked; options "Tell me about any drop" (default) / "Tell me when it's below $___" (pre-filled with the low end of the typical range, validated), "Include nearby dates (±3 days)" toggle with an explanation, "Also email me" (disabled with a link to add an email if none; hidden if SMTP isn't configured — expose email_alerts_available in /health or a small config endpoint). Success state with a friendly confirmation and (first time only) the browser-notification prompt.
  3. Alerts page (/alerts, nav item with badge): a card per watch — route with city names, dates, travellers, current price (big), change since watching (green/red), lowest seen, Google price level chip, a small SVG sparkline of price history with the target line, last checked ("2 h ago"), next check, status chip (Watching / Paused / Price dropped! / Expired / Problem). Actions: Check now (with spinner, respects rate limit message), Pause/Resume, Edit (target/mode/flex/email), Delete (confirm inline, not a modal dialog), Re-plan with this fare (runs the normal search with the watch's dates or the cheapest nearby dates), Book on Google Flights (existing booking URL format). Group by Active / Past. Empty state that explains the value with an illustration-free friendly design and a CTA to search.
  4. Notification UX: bell dropdown items read naturally ("✈️ Berlin → Lisbon dropped to $142 (−$46) for 1–8 Dec — the lowest we've seen"), clicking opens the Alerts page scrolled to that watch and marks it read; toast for new alerts while the app is open (one at a time, dismissible).
  5. Quality bar: responsive to 360 px, keyboard accessible, ARIA live regions for toasts/badge changes, reduced motion respected, consistent Tailwind/lucide style, no layout shift, no polling while hidden. Analytics via track() (watch_created/mode/flex, watch_checked_now, alert_clicked/kind, watch_replanned, watch_booked).

Price Watch for Hotels, Activities and Whole Trips — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Extend the existing fare watch (PR #23) so travellers can also watch (1) a hotel's price, (2) an activity's price, and (3) the price of an entire saved trip (flights + hotel + activities + other costs), with the same delightful, never-spammy alerts (bell, Alerts page, toasts, browser notifications, optional email).

Spec: User requests 2026-11-04: "similar to the Watch this fare alert for flights create the same alerts for 1. Hotel Prices 2. Prices of the Activities 3. Price of the entire saved trip (all moving parts)"; activity prices: "Rely on AI estimates and also scrape the web to get the latest data (GetYourGuide, Viator)"; "VERY VERY THOROUGHLY AND RIGOUROUSLY … NO REGRESSIONS … MASSIVELY PARALLEL AGENTIC EXECUTION".

docs.title: Verified facts (controller, 2026-11-04)
docs.text:
• Only flight prices are live today (serp_flights, SerpAPI google_flights). Hotel and activity prices are AI estimates from hotels_agent / activities_agent.
  • Hotels — live source works: SerpAPI engine=google_hotels (q="hotels in Lisbon", check_in_date, check_out_date, adults, currency=USD, hl=en, gl=us) returned 20 properties with rate_per_night.extracted_lowest, total_rate.extracted_lowest and a property_token per property (e.g. "Lumen Hotel & The Lisbon Light Show" $100/night, $398 total for 4 nights). A property can be re-checked by property_token (SerpAPI google_hotels property-details mode).
  • Activities: getyourguide.com and viator.com return HTTP 403 to automated clients even for robots.txt — direct scraping would require defeating bot protection and is out of scope (will not be built). Legitimate observed-price source that works: SerpAPI engine=google search (e.g. "Belem Tower tour Lisbon getyourguide"): GetYourGuide organic results carry rich_snippet.top.detected_extensions.price (+ currency, rating, reviews) and extensions: ["Starting from $11.63"]. Viator results in the sample had no price snippet (use when present). backend/app/services/activity_url_resolver.py already queries SerpAPI engine=google — reuse its client/caching patterns.
  • Existing fare watch (merged): backend/app/services/fare_watch.py (pure evaluate, check_watch, scheduler run_due/run_scheduler/start_scheduler, per-signal references + re-arming, cooldown, step()), backend/app/db/fare_watch_db.py (tables fare_watches, fare_watch_history, fare_watch_quota, fare_watch_user_quota; leasing claim_watch, reserve_calls), backend/app/db/notifications_db.py, routes backend/app/api/routes/fare_watches.py + notifications routes, email services/alert_email.py; frontend components/alerts/* (WatchDialog, WatchCard, WatchFareButton, Sparkline, NotificationBell, AlertToast, alertKinds.js), pages/AlertsPage.jsx, context/AlertsContext.jsx, services/api.js.

docs.title: Price sources (honesty rules)
docs.text:
• Observed prices: flights (google_flights), hotels (google_hotels by property_token), activities (Google search snippet price of the matched GetYourGuide/Viator listing). Every observed price carries source (e.g. google_hotels, getyourguide_via_google), observed_at, and a link.
  • Estimated prices: AI estimates from the original search (activities/hotels without a live match, and "other" trip costs such as SIM, local transport). Estimates are frozen at watch creation (not re-asked), always labelled "estimate" in UI/email, and never trigger alerts on their own. A watch whose every component is an estimate cannot be created (friendly message: "We can't find a live price for this yet").
  • Never present an estimate as a live price; never invent drops.

docs.title: Data model (additive; flight tables untouched)
docs.text:
• New table price_watches: id, user_id, kind (hotel | activity | trip), plan_id (nullable), title, subtitle, subject JSON (kind-specific: hotel {name, city, property_token, check_in, check_out, adults, rooms}; activity {name, city, listing_url, listing_title, provider, query, travellers}; trip {plan_id, components: [...]}), currency, alert_mode (any_drop | below_target), target_price, email_enabled, status (active|paused|expired|error), baseline_price, last_price, lowest_price, last_notified_price, last_notified_at, own_peak_price (re-arm), failure_count, last_error, check_count, last_checked_at, next_check_at, lease_until, expires_on (date: check-in / activity date / trip departure), created_at, updated_at.
  • New table price_watch_history: watch_id, checked_at, price, breakdown JSON (trip), observed JSON. ≤ 120 rows/watch.
  • Reuse notifications (new kinds: hotel_drop, hotel_target, activity_drop, activity_target, trip_drop, trip_target, watch_expired, watch_error with data.watch_kind), the SerpAPI daily budget + per-user share (reserve_calls, same quota tables, same FARE_WATCH_* settings — one shared budget), and the scheduler loop (one loop processes due fare watches and due price watches).

docs.title: Rules (shared engine)
docs.text:
• Extract the own-dates signal logic of fare_watch.evaluate (reference = last alerted price or baseline, step() = max($15, 5 %), re-arm on rebound ≥ step with peak reference, target re-arm at target + step, 24 h cooldown cap with further-drop override, never on baseline, never on rises, baseline-already-good rule) into a pure, kind-agnostic module backend/app/services/price_rules.py used by BOTH fare watches and price watches. Fare-watch behaviour must not change: every existing fare-watch test (incl. test_fare_watch_sequences.py) stays green unmodified; add an equivalence test that runs the old sequences through both paths.
  • Trip-specific: alert threshold on the total = max($25, 4 %); the notification explains the change by component ("Your Lisbon trip is $112 cheaper: flights −$70, hotel −$42"). Components that are estimates are held fixed. A trip watch also raises a component-level heads-up only through the total (no separate per-component alerts from a trip watch).

docs.title: Checking
docs.text:
• Hotel check: 1 SerpAPI call (google_hotels property by property_token for the watch's dates/adults) → total stay price (all nights, all rooms) + nightly; property unavailable for the dates → unavailable observation (not a failure; UI "Sold out for your dates"; no alert; counts toward expiry/error only after 3 consecutive).
  • Activity check: 1 SerpAPI google call with the stored query → find the stored listing_url (normalised: scheme/host/path, ignore query) among results → snippet price × travellers (price is "from" per person: label "from $X per person"); listing not found → fall back to same-provider best name match (name_match) only if similarity high; else unavailable (no alert).
  • Trip check: re-price live components (flight via the existing fare path for the plan's selected flight/dates; hotel via property; up to 5 observed activities, rotating if more), estimates fixed; total = Σ; ≤ 8 calls per check, reserved all-or-nothing against the budget; cached results reused free.
  • Cadence 12 h ± jitter (same as fares); expiry the day of expires_on.

docs.title: Creating watches (API, auth, ownership 404s, light_ai rate bucket for create/check-now, 503 without SerpAPI, 409 at the active limit — FARE_WATCH_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER counts fare + price watches together)
docs.text:
• POST /api/price-watches {kind:"hotel", hotel:{name, city, check_in, check_out, adults, rooms?}, alert_mode, target_price?, email_enabled?} → match the AI hotel to a live property via google_hotels (q="<name> <city>", dates, adults; pick by name_match ≥ threshold) → store property_token, take baseline. No confident match → 422 {code:"no_live_price", message:"We couldn't find live prices for this hotel on Google Hotels.", suggestions:[up to 3 live properties with similar names/area and their prices]}; the UI offers to watch a suggestion instead.
  • {kind:"activity", activity:{name, city, date?, travellers}} → search GYG/Viator listing ("<name> <city> getyourguide", then viator) → best name match with a price snippet → baseline; none → 422 no_live_price with the AI estimate shown and up to 3 priced listings found as suggestions.
  • {kind:"trip", plan_id} → build components from the saved plan's selections (selected flight → flight component via existing fare code; selected hotel → hotel match as above; selected activities → activity matches; everything else in the cost breakdown (SIM, transport, tips…) → estimate components); report which components are live vs estimate in the response; baseline total.
  • GET /api/price-watches (with history + breakdown), GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/price-watches/{id}, POST /api/price-watches/{id}/check, POST /api/price-watches/match (is this hotel/activity/plan already watched? no live calls).

docs.title: Frontend (delight bar)
docs.text:
• Watch buttons: hotel cards (Results + Chat), activity cards (Results + Chat), My Plan selected hotel/activities, and "Watch whole trip" on saved-plan cards, PlanViewModal and the My Plan drawer (when the plan is saved). Watched state "Watching · $398".
  • Create dialog (shared shell with the fare dialog, kind-specific body): hotel shows the matched Google Hotels property name (so the user sees what is tracked), nightly + total, dates; activity shows the matched listing (provider logo-free text, title, rating, "from $X per person", link); trip shows the breakdown table (component, price, Live/Estimate badge) and the total. Modes: any drop / below target. Email toggle. "Not this one?" for hotel/activity → pick a suggestion.
  • Alerts page: tabs/filter chips All · Flights · Hotels · Activities · Trips (counts), a card per kind via a kind→card registry (components/alerts/cards/), trip card with stacked breakdown bar (flights/stay/activities/other), Live/Estimate badges, sparkline of the total, "what changed" line; actions as for fares (Check now, Pause, Edit, Delete, Re-plan, Book/Open listing).
  • Notifications/toasts/emails per kind with natural copy ("🏨 Lumen Hotel dropped to $352 for 10–14 Dec (−$46)", "🎟️ Belém walking tour is now from $9.90 (−$1.73)", "🧳 Your Lisbon trip is $112 cheaper: flights −$70, hotel −$42").
  • Quality: responsive 360 px, keyboard, ARIA live, reduced motion, no layout shift, polling only while visible (existing).

docs.text:
• Phase 1 (parallel, separate worktrees):
  • P1-core (pw/core): price_rules.py extraction (+ equivalence tests), price_watches + history tables, generic check pipeline with a PriceSource protocol async def check(watch: dict, api_key: str) -> PriceObservation and a kind→source registry, scheduler extension, API skeleton (/api/price-watches CRUD/check/match with kind dispatch to registered sources), notification kinds, frontend: Alerts page tabs + kind→card registry + generic dialog shell + api.js functions. Ships with a fake test source for tests only.

  • P1-activity-src (pw/activity-src): backend/app/services/activity_prices.py — find_listings(name, city, api_key) -> list[ActivityListing] (GYG then Viator queries), match_listing(name, listings), price_listing(listing, api_key) -> ActivityPrice|None (re-search, URL-normalised match, snippet price parse incl. "Starting from $X", currencies), fixtures recorded live (≤ 6 calls).
  • Phase 2 (parallel, after Phase 1 merges into feat/price-watch-all): P2-hotel (hotel source registration + hotel UI), P2-activity (activity source + UI), P2-trip (trip aggregator + trip UI + Watch whole trip).

docs.title: Phase 0 — Foundations (theme + dark mode, i18n, telemetry, parity matrix) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Give the web app the three foundations every later phase builds on: a token-driven theme with a user-selectable dark mode, full UI translation into 7 languages, and a zero-cost telemetry pipeline (backend + web SDK). Also write the cross-client feature-parity matrix.

Architecture: Every Tailwind colour family the app uses is remapped to CSS variables that flip under html.dark, so the ~17k lines of existing JSX get dark mode without class rewrites; hand tuning follows. i18n is i18next + react-i18next with one JSON file per namespace per language, so the extraction tasks run in parallel without touching each other's files. English is bundled; other languages load lazily. Telemetry is a new anonymous-capable POST /api/telemetry that validates every event against a closed registry (no free text can get in) and appends to a separate telemetry.db. A small web SDK batches events in the background with delegated auto-capture.

Tech Stack: FastAPI + SQLite (backend); React 18, Tailwind 3.4, Vite 6, vitest, i18next ^27 + react-i18next ^18 (frontend; peer react >= 18, checked on npm 2026-11-10 — pin a release at least 2 weeks old).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-voyager-reimagined-design.md (§8 Telemetry, §9 Look, feel, language, §10 parity, §2 constraints).

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Two-way compatibility: the new SPA must work against the previous backend (/api/config or /api/telemetry 404 → telemetry silently off, no retries). The new backend must keep serving the previous SPA (POST /api/analytics/events unchanged).
  • Telemetry never blocks or slows the UI: no await on the critical path, every SDK entry point wrapped in try/catch, work deferred with requestIdleCallback (falling back to setTimeout(…, 1)).
  • Telemetry never carries free text the user typed, precise location, email/name, or other users' content. The server enforces this with a closed per-event prop schema.
  • Telemetry is disclosed and can be switched off (Settings → Privacy). Users whose device timezone is EU/EEA/UK/CH get a one-time consent choice and are opted out until they choose.
  • Raw telemetry is kept 90 days in $DATA_DIR/telemetry.db and is not backed up. Daily aggregates live in the main DB table telemetry_daily and are backed up with the user tables.
  • Languages and codes: en English, es Spanish, de Deutsch, fr French, hi Hindi, zh Chinese (Simplified), bn Bengali. en is the fallback.
  • [call, deviates from spec §9]: the canonical catalogue lives at frontend/src/i18n/locales/<lang>/<ns>.json, not a root i18n/. The SPA image build copies only frontend/, and the deploy inputs hash/path filters key on it. Plurals use i18next JSON v4 suffixes (_one, _other, …), which map 1:1 to Android <plurals> and iOS String Catalog plural variations. Update the spec text in Task 12.
  • Light is the default theme; options are system / light / dark, stored in localStorage key tp_theme; the language lives in tp_lang.
  • Never translate: brand "Voyager", airport/IATA codes, currency codes, place names coming from data, AI/static content strings from the backend (server strings stay English in Phase 0, except AI output per Task 11).
  • Python 3.12, ruff clean; npx eslint src/ --max-warnings 0; mkdocs build --strict; every existing test keeps passing.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Storage/network hostile browsers (Safari private mode with localStorage throwing, ad-blockers blocking /api/telemetry, offline): the app works, there's no console spam and no retry storm. → Test in Task 5.
  2. Old backend (no /api/config, /api/telemetry → 404): the SDK disables itself for the session after the first 404. → Test in Task 5.
  3. PII sneaking in (an id prop carrying "jane@x.com" or "hello world", unknown props, oversized batches): it gets dropped server-side and the request still returns 204. → Test in Task 2.
  4. Dark mode leaking into print/PDF export and Leaflet maps: print is always light, and map tiles are dimmed rather than inverted in a way that breaks markers. → Test in Task 6.
  5. Missing translation keys and long strings: a key missing in de shows English, never the raw key, and every locale has every en key with matching {{placeholders}}. → Test in Task 7 (catalogue parity test).

docs.title: Task 1: Telemetry storage
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/db/telemetry_db.py - Modify: backend/app/main.py (lifespan: create tables; start the maintenance loop from Task 3) - Modify: backend/app/db/vm_backup.py and backend/app/db/backup.py (add telemetry_daily wherever the user-table list is defined) - Test: backend/tests/test_telemetry_db.py

Interfaces: - Produces: - telemetry_db_path() -> Path → Path(settings.data_dir) / "telemetry.db" - create_telemetry_tables() -> None. In telemetry.db: telemetry_events(id INTEGER PK, ts INTEGER ms, received_at INTEGER ms, event TEXT, session_id TEXT, anon_id TEXT, user_id TEXT NULL, platform TEXT, app_version TEXT, locale TEXT, screen TEXT NULL, props TEXT json) with indexes (ts), (event, ts). In the main DB (get_connection): telemetry_daily(day TEXT, event TEXT, platform TEXT, events INTEGER, users INTEGER, sessions INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(day,event,platform)) and telemetry_rollups(day TEXT PRIMARY KEY, done_at TEXT). - insert_events(rows: list[dict]) -> int (one transaction, executemany, returns the count) - rollup_day(day: str) -> int (YYYY-MM-DD UTC; idempotent: replaces that day's rows, records telemetry_rollups; users = distinct coalesce(user_id, anon_id)) - prune(before_ms: int) -> int

  • [ ] Step 1: Write failing tests test_insert_and_rollup (insert 3 events, 2 anon ids, 1 user, 2 sessions on one day → rollup_day gives events=3, users=2, sessions=2; running it twice gives the same rows), test_prune_removes_only_older, test_telemetry_db_is_separate_file (after insert, the main DB has no telemetry_events table).
  • [ ] Step 2: Run cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_telemetry_db.py → FAIL (module missing).
  • [ ] Step 3: Implement with its own connection helper mirroring database.get_connection (WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout=5000).
  • [ ] Step 4: Run the test file → PASS; run the full backend suite → PASS.
  • [ ] Step 5: Commit feat(telemetry): separate telemetry store with daily rollups

docs.title: Task 2: Event registry + validation
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/telemetry/__init__.py, backend/app/telemetry/registry.py - Test: backend/tests/test_telemetry_registry.py

Interfaces: - Produces: - PROP_TYPES = {"id", "int", "float", "bool"} | {"enum:<a|b|c>"}. id matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,64}$ (no spaces or @, so no sentences and no emails). - EVENTS: dict[str, dict[str, str]] (event → prop → type). It ships with at least the families from spec §8: app_open, app_background, session_start, screen_view{route:id, referrer_route:id}, screen_time{route:id, ms:int}, ui_tap{tid:id, route:id}, ui_toggle{tid:id, route:id, on:bool}, ui_submit{tid:id, route:id}, search_submit{mode:enum:<search|chat|compare|link|discover>, travelers:int, nights:int, multi_city:bool}, search_first_section{ms:int}, search_complete{ms:int, sections:int, errors:int}, search_abandon{ms:int, sections:int}, section_expand{section:id}, plan_select{section:id}, link_out{section:id, domain:id}, share{target:id, object:id}, alert_event{action:id, kind:id}, onboarding_step{step:int, action:enum:<view|next|skip|done>}, theme_change{theme:enum:<system|light|dark>}, language_change{lang:enum:<en|es|de|fr|hi|zh|bn>}, consent{choice:enum:<granted|denied>}, feature_used{feature:id, page:id} (bridge from the old track()), perf{metric:enum:<ttfb|fcp|lcp|inp|cls|long_task|cold_start>, value:float, route:id}, error{kind:enum:<js|promise|api>, source:id, status:int}. - clean_event(raw: dict) -> dict | None: unknown event → None. Unknown props or props failing their type are dropped, not the whole event. Strings longer than 64 are dropped. ts must be within ±7 days of server time, else replaced by the server time. - clean_client(raw: dict) -> dict | None: anon_id (UUID), session_id (UUID), platform enum web|android|ios, app_version id, locale id ≤ 16; invalid → None.

  • [ ] Step 1: Write failing tests: clean_event({"event":"ui_tap","props":{"tid":"jane@x.com","route":"/results"}})["props"] == {"route":"/results"}; "hello world" dropped the same way; clean_event({"event":"nope"}) is None; an enum outside its set is dropped; test_every_event_documented (every EVENTS key appears in docs/Telemetry.md; that doc is written in Task 12, so mark this test xfail(strict=True) until then and flip it in Task 12).
  • [ ] Step 2: Run → FAIL.
  • [ ] Step 3: Implement (a pure module: no I/O).
  • [ ] Step 4: Run → PASS.
  • [ ] Step 5: Commit feat(telemetry): closed event registry and validation

docs.title: Task 3: Telemetry + config API, maintenance loop, admin summary
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/api/routes/telemetry.py, backend/app/api/routes/client_config.py - Modify: backend/app/main.py (routers; lifespan task), backend/app/core/config.py, backend/app/core/rate_limit.py (bucket telemetry), backend/app/api/routes/admin.py - Test: backend/tests/test_telemetry_api.py, backend/tests/test_client_config.py

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 1 insert_events, rollup_day, prune; Task 2 clean_event, clean_client. - Produces: - Settings: telemetry_enabled: bool = True, telemetry_retention_days: int = 90, rate_limit_telemetry: int = 600, public_base_url: str = "". - POST /api/telemetry. Body {"client": {...}, "events": [{"event","ts","screen","props"}]}, max 100 events, raw body ≤ 64 KB (else 413), accepts Content-Encoding: gzip (decompressed ≤ 256 KB). Auth is optional (get_optional_user, so user_id is the user's id when signed in). Always 204 when well-formed, even if every event was dropped; 422 only for a malformed envelope; 404 when telemetry_enabled is false. Inserts via asyncio.to_thread. Not behind require_ai_access. - GET /api/config → {"public_base_url": str, "telemetry": {"enabled": bool, "flush_interval_s": 15, "max_batch": 50}, "features": {"telemetry": true}}. Public, no rate limit, Cache-Control: max-age=300. public_base_url defaults to the request's own base URL when the setting is empty. - Lifespan task telemetry_maintenance(): every hour, roll up every day since the last rollup, up to yesterday (UTC); prune < now - retention. Errors are logged, never raised. - GET /api/admin/telemetry/summary?days=30 (admin) → {"days": [{"day","users","sessions","events"}], "top_events": [{"event","events"}], "top_screens": [{"route","views"}]} from telemetry_daily, plus today's live numbers from raw events.

  • [ ] Step 1: Write failing tests: anonymous POST → 204 and a row stored with user_id NULL; signed-in → user_id set; a PII prop is not stored; 101 events → 422; gzip body accepted; telemetry_enabled=False → 404; /api/config shape; the admin summary needs admin (403 for a user) and returns the rolled-up counts; POST /api/analytics/events behaves exactly as before (the existing test_analytics.py still passes untouched).
  • [ ] Step 2: Run → FAIL.
  • [ ] Step 3: Implement. Add the telemetry bucket to the _bucket_limit mapping.
  • [ ] Step 4: Run backend suite + ruff check backend/ → PASS.

docs.title: Task 4: Theme tokens + dark mode mechanism
docs.text:
Files: - Create: frontend/design/tokens.json, frontend/scripts/build-tokens.mjs, frontend/src/theme/tokens.css (generated, committed), frontend/src/theme/ThemeContext.jsx, frontend/src/theme/themeStorage.js - Modify: frontend/tailwind.config.js, frontend/src/index.css, frontend/index.html, frontend/src/main.jsx, frontend/package.json (script tokens) - Test: frontend/src/theme/tokens.test.js, frontend/src/theme/ThemeContext.test.jsx

Interfaces: - Produces: - tokens.json: { "palette": { "<family>": { "50": "#…", …, "950": "#…" } }, "dark": { "<family>": {…} }, "semantic": { "surface", "surface-raised", "text", "text-muted", "border", "accent": … } }. The families are exactly those the code uses: gray slate stone teal amber sky red emerald green violet rose cyan blue purple yellow indigo pink orange lime fuchsia, plus primary (the current teal ramp), a new accent coral ramp, and white. Light values = Tailwind 3.4 defaults (so light mode looks identical to today). Dark values: neutral ramps reversed (50↔950, 100↔900, …) and nudged to a blue-grey night palette; colour ramps reversed with saturation reduced ~15 % for the light end; white → #111827-ish raised surface. black is not remapped (it's used for overlays). - build-tokens.mjs writes tokens.css: :root { --c-gray-50: 249 250 251; … } and html.dark { … } as space-separated RGB channels. - Tailwind: darkMode: 'class'; every family above becomes { 50: 'rgb(var(--c-gray-50) / <alpha-value>)', … }. - ThemeProvider, useTheme() -> { theme: 'system'|'light'|'dark', resolved: 'light'|'dark', setTheme(t) }. It toggles html.dark, sets color-scheme, and updates <meta name="theme-color"> (light #ffffff, dark the dark surface). system follows matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') live. Storage helpers swallow localStorage errors. - An inline script in index.html, before the CSS, applies dark from tp_theme/the system setting to prevent a flash.

docs.title: Task 5: Web telemetry SDK
docs.text:
Files: - Create: frontend/src/telemetry/client.js, frontend/src/telemetry/autocapture.js, frontend/src/telemetry/consent.js, frontend/src/telemetry/perf.js, frontend/src/telemetry/routes.js - Modify: frontend/src/utils/analytics.js (track() also emits feature_used), frontend/src/main.jsx (initTelemetry() after render, in idle time), frontend/src/App.jsx (screen views on location change) - Test: frontend/src/telemetry/client.test.js, consent.test.js, autocapture.test.js

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 3 GET /api/config, POST /api/telemetry (shapes above). - Produces: - initTelemetry({ appVersion }) -> void (fetches /api/config once. A 404 or enabled:false → off for the session; consent denied → off). - emit(event: string, props?: object) -> void (never throws; no-op when off). - setUserPresent(bool) (no ids are stored client-side; the server derives user_id from the bearer token, which the client attaches when present). - Queue rules: flush every flush_interval_s or at max_batch; on visibilitychange→hidden use navigator.sendBeacon with a Blob (application/json), since sendBeacon can't send auth headers. Beacon flushes are therefore anonymous, so pending events are flushed with fetch(…, {keepalive:true}) + auth first when signed in, with the beacon as fallback. The queue persists to localStorage key tp_tq (cap 500, oldest dropped). After 3 consecutive network failures, exponential backoff up to 5 min. 404 → disable. - anon_id in localStorage tp_anon (UUID via crypto.randomUUID, with a fallback); session_id rotates after 30 min idle. - consent.js: consentRequired(tz = Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone) -> bool (true for Europe/* except Europe/Istanbul, Europe/Moscow, Europe/Minsk, Europe/Kiev/Europe/Kyiv; plus Atlantic/Reykjavik, Atlantic/Canary, Atlantic/Madeira, Atlantic/Azores, Atlantic/Faroe); getConsent() -> 'granted'|'denied'|null; setConsent(choice) (emits consent); telemetryAllowed() -> bool (= choice granted, or no choice and not required). - autocapture.js: one delegated listener each for click, change, submit on document (capture phase, passive). Element id = closest [data-tid] value; else closest [id] as id:<id>; else auto:<tagName lowercase>. Never reads input values or text content. Route = routeTemplate(location.pathname) from routes.js (/share/:token, /plans/:id, … so tokens/ids never get sent). - perf.js: TTFB/FCP from navigation + paint timing; LCP, INP (approximated from event entries' max duration), CLS and long-task count from PerformanceObserver where supported; error events from window.error / unhandledrejection with source = script file basename + line, never the message.

docs.title: Voyager iOS app (spec Phase 7) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: A native SwiftUI iPhone + iPad app in rupakc/travel-planner-ios with parity to today's web app and the Android app (sign-in, onboarding, search in all modes, streamed results, My Plan, chat, alerts, near me, share viewer, settings, admin). Built, linted and tested only on GitHub Actions macOS runners. Phase 1 account features plug in later through seams that exist from day one.

Architecture: An XcodeGen-generated app target (project.yml, no hand-edited .xcodeproj) over one local Swift package, Packages/VoyagerKit, with one target per core layer and per feature module. Every target, test target and its dependency edges are declared in Package.swift by Task 1, so later tasks only add files inside their own target directories and can run concurrently. Colours, strings and the telemetry registry are vendored from the travel-planner repo at one pinned commit (upstream.lock) and turned into an asset catalog, String Catalogs and a parity fixture by Python generators, so the web stays the single source. Networking is URLSession + async/await. SSE is read with URLSession.bytes and parsed off the main actor. State is Observation (@Observable) and tokens live in the Keychain. Every screen reads an injected AppEnvironment whose dependencies are protocols, with fakes for tests and previews.

Tech Stack: Swift 6 (language mode 6, strict concurrency), SwiftUI, Observation, iOS 17.0 deployment target, Xcode 26.0.1 on macos-15 runners, XcodeGen 2.43.0, SwiftLint 0.59.1, swift-snapshot-testing 1.18.3 (test-only, the only third-party package), Swift Testing for unit tests, XCUITest for UI smoke, MapKit, AuthenticationServices, UserNotifications, BackgroundTasks. Python 3.12 (stdlib only) for generators and the stub backend.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-voyager-reimagined-design.md (§10 iOS, §4 accounts, §7 notifications, §8 telemetry, §9 design and i18n, §2 store rules). Contracts: docs/API-Reference.md, docs/Telemetry.md, docs/Internationalization.md, docs/Theming.md, docs/Feature-Parity.md, frontend/design/tokens.json, frontend/src/i18n/locales/. Parity reference: ~/travel-planner-android (README, its spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-android-app-design.md, docs/reference/api-contract.md, docs/reference/web-ui-inventory.md, docs/Networking-and-SSE.md, docs/Onboarding-and-Traveller-Types.md).

Owner decision (2026-11-11): Phase 7 starts now, in parallel with Phase 1. Everything that needs Phase 1's API (sign-up, verification, reset, OAuth, Sign in with Apple, refresh tokens, account deletion) is in Wave 6. Wave 6 starts only after the Phase 1 API contract is merged in travel-planner.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Repo rupakc/travel-planner-ios, public, MIT. Git identity rupakc (noreply). The controller creates the repo. Tasks work on branches and the controller merges.
  • iOS 17.0 deployment target, iPhone and iPad (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1,2), all iPad orientations, multitasking (Split View, Slide Over, Stage Manager) supported.
  • Swift 6 language mode with complete strict concurrency in every target, and zero warnings. The app target sets SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS = YES. Package targets cannot use unsafe flags, so scripts/ci/test-unit.sh fails when the build log has a warning: from a file under Packages/VoyagerKit/Sources or App.
  • No Xcode locally. Every build, test and lint runs on GitHub Actions macos-15. Python tooling also runs locally (python3 -m pytest -q tools/tests). No .xcodeproj/.xcworkspace is committed (.gitignore has *.xcodeproj, *.xcworkspace except the package's implicit one).
  • Pins: every action is pinned by commit SHA, using the SHAs the main repo already uses (checkout 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 v4.4.0, upload-artifact ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 v4.6.2, download-artifact d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 v4.3.0, setup-python a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 v5.6.0, cache 0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 v4.3.0, setup-node 49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 v4.4.0). Tools pinned in tools.lock (version + SHA-256 of the downloaded archive). A new pin must be a release at least 14 days old on the day it is added.
  • Third-party code: only swift-snapshot-testing (test targets only). No Firebase, no Alamofire, no analytics SDK (spec §10: direct APNs, no Firebase on iOS).
  • Two-way compatibility (CLAUDE.md, spec §2): the app feature-detects every endpoint newer than today's API. GET /api/config, GET /api/auth/providers, /api/telemetry and POST /api/devices with platform: "ios" may answer 404/422. Each one degrades silently to "off" for the session, with no retry storm and no error UI.
  • Theme: light is the default. Options system / light / dark, stored in UserDefaults key tp_theme (same key name as the web). Colours come only from generated tokens (SwiftLint custom rule no_raw_color bans Color(red:, Color(#colorLiteral, UIColor(red: outside Sources/DesignSystem/Generated/).
  • Languages en, es, de, fr, hi, zh (bundle zh-Hans), bn, with en as fallback. The language picker lists native names in web order: English, Español, Deutsch, Français, हिन्दी, 中文（简体）, বাংলা. Stored in UserDefaults tp_lang. Brand names (Voyager, Apple, Google, Facebook, GitHub), IATA codes, currency codes, place names and backend data are never translated. User-facing text in feature targets only goes through L10n (SwiftLint custom rule no_literal_text bans Text(" with a literal outside #Preview and test targets).
  • AI calls send locale (base language code) exactly like the web's localeField(): on /api/search, /chat, /discover, /compare/destination, /stress-test, every single-agent and /filtered route.
  • Telemetry follows docs/Telemetry.md exactly, with platform: "ios". It uses only events and props in the vendored registry. It never blocks: no await on a user path, and every entry point is non-throwing and synchronous for the caller. No free text, location, email or name ever goes into props.
  • Honesty rules carry over unchanged: estimates are labelled, verification chips are shown as the backend sends them, static-first data stays when the AI fails, and "Book" always means "open the provider page" (SFSafariViewController). No in-app payments.
  • Performance budget (spec §10): cold start < 400 ms to first frame on iPhone XS; 60/120 fps scrolling; LazyVStack/List with stable ids; remote images downsampled with ImageIO; no JSON decoding or SSE parsing on the main actor; nothing but first-frame work before the first frame.
  • Accessibility: Dynamic Type up to AX5 without truncating primary actions, VoiceOver labels on every icon-only control, 44 pt targets, Reduce Motion respected, AA contrast in both themes (tokens are already contrast-tested on web).
  • App Store rules that shape the design (spec §2): in-app account deletion (5.1.1(v)) and Sign in with Apple next to other social logins (4.8) ship in Wave 6 before any App Store submission. UGC report/block/filter (1.2) comes with Phase 5 social, not this plan.
  • Bundle id io.github.rupakc.travelplanner (same as Android), display name "Voyager", URL scheme voyager. Base URL from the build setting VOYAGER_BASE_URL (Debug http://127.0.0.1:8001, Release $(VOYAGER_PROD_BASE_URL), which CI fills from the repo variable VOYAGER_PROD_BASE_URL and which is empty until the owner sets it). The trusted-host list is VOYAGER_TRUSTED_HOSTS (space-separated), the one setting that also feeds associated domains (spec §2a).

docs.title: Verification convention (used by every task)
docs.text:
• CI(<filter>) means: push the task branch, then gh workflow run ios-ci.yml --ref <branch> -f only_testing=<filter> && gh run watch --exit-status. only_testing takes xcodebuild -only-testing: values (DomainTests, DomainTests/ItineraryLayoutTests). An empty value runs everything. Pass = the run is green, and the "Test summary" step lists the named suites with 0 failures. The failing-test step and the passing step are each one CI round-trip.
  • CI(full) = a push without the input: all jobs (tools, lint, unit × iPhone/iPad, ui-smoke × iPhone/iPad, sim-build).
  • PY(<path>) = python3 -m pytest -q <path> locally (and in the tools CI job).
  • Snapshot tests are recorded on CI: gh workflow run ios-ci.yml --ref <branch> -f only_testing=<suite> -f record_snapshots=true, then gh run download <id> -n snapshots -D Packages/VoyagerKit/Tests and commit the PNGs. After that, re-run without recording and expect it green. Review each recorded PNG (Read tool) before committing it.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. The app goes to the background mid-stream (lock the phone during a 60 s search, or a Slide Over resize while the itinerary streams): on return the search resumes by retrying once and replaying into the sections already shown. You get no duplicated sections and no lost static data, and search_abandon is not sent for a stream that finished. → ResultsModelTests.test_interruptedStreamRetriesOnceAndKeepsSections + test_modelSurvivesViewRebuild in Task 24.
  2. An older or partial backend (/api/config 404, /api/auth/providers 404, /api/telemetry 404, POST /api/devices 422 for ios, /api/notifications 404): the app works, every social button shows the "coming soon" note, telemetry turns itself off for the session after one request, and nothing loops. → tests in Tasks 5, 6, 7, 33.
  3. Stale and expired sessions (the 24 h JWT expires while backgrounded; a late 401 arrives for the previous token after a fresh login; a reinstall leaves a Keychain item behind): only a 401 for the current token signs the user out, with the "session expired" message. A reinstall starts signed out. → AuthStateTests in Task 7 and APIClientTests.test_staleUnauthorizedIgnored in Task 5.
  4. Long strings and other scripts (German and French labels, Hindi/Bengali/Chinese glyphs, AX5 Dynamic Type, an iPhone SE width, iPad Split View at 1/3 width): nothing clips a primary action, and a missing translation shows English, never the raw key. → generator test test_missing_key_falls_back_to_english (Task 3), SharedUISnapshotTests (Task 13), the audit snapshots in Task 40.
  5. Telemetry leaking user content (a tid built from a plan name, a route with a share token, a burst of 1 000 taps, the disk full): ids failing the token rule are dropped on the device, routes are templates, the queue is capped at 500, and a write failure never surfaces. → TelemetryPropsTests, TelemetryQueueTests in Task 6.

docs.title: Repository layout and module graph
docs.text:
travel-planner-ios/
  project.yml                 XcodeGen: target Voyager (app), VoyagerUITests; schemes Voyager, VoyagerUI
  Config/                     Base.xcconfig, Debug.xcconfig, Release.xcconfig (bundle id, base URL, trusted hosts)
  App/                        VoyagerApp.swift, AppDelegate.swift, Voyager.entitlements, PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy,
                              Resources/Assets.xcassets (AppIcon placeholder, LaunchBackground), InfoPlist.xcstrings (generated)
  Packages/VoyagerKit/        Package.swift (all targets below), Sources/<Target>/, Tests/<Target>Tests/
  UITests/                    XCUITest smoke tests
  Upstream/                   vendored from travel-planner @ upstream.lock: locales/<lang>/<ns>.json, tokens.json,
                              telemetry_registry.json (exported), SOURCE (sha + date)
  i18n/pending/en/<ns>.json   English-only keys not yet in the web catalogue (must be empty before release, Task 41)
  tools/                      gen_tokens.py, gen_catalog.py, export_registry.py, stub_backend/, tests/
  scripts/ci/                 bootstrap.sh, select-xcode.sh, generate.sh, sim-destination.sh, lint.sh,

  scripts/upstream/sync.sh    re-vendor Upstream/ at a SHA;  scripts/fonts/fetch.sh  (Inter, Sora with checksums)
  upstream.lock, tools.lock, .swiftlint.yml, .github/workflows/ios-ci.yml
  docs/                       Architecture, Modules, Networking-and-SSE, Localization, Theming, Telemetry, Testing,
