docs.title: Phase 1 — Accounts + game engine Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Let strangers sign up (native username/email/password with a 30-minute confirmation link, or Apple, Google, Facebook or GitHub), recover a password, stay signed in on mobile, manage an account area (avatar, name, settings, connected sign-in methods, export, delete), and use AI only once verified and within a daily quota. Add the XP/badge/streak engine with its first two hooks, onboarding complete and email verified.

Architecture: The plan is additive. The users table gains columns, and twelve new tables hold tokens, identities, sessions, invites, settings, quotas and the game. One wave-0 task freezes the whole schema, and another freezes every seam in shared files: settings, router stubs registered in main.py, the error envelope, URL building, game hooks and the quota dependency. After that, each later task owns its own files. OAuth is a server-side authorization-code flow. Provider state lives in SQLite, and a browser-binding cookie or a client PKCE verifier protects the one-time handoff code, so tokens never travel in a URL. Each provider is a small adapter behind one protocol. Game values (points, caps, badges, levels) are a JSON config file, not code.

Tech Stack: FastAPI + SQLite, PyJWT (HS256 sessions; RS256/ES256 provider tokens through cryptography), httpx (provider calls; httpx.MockTransport in tests), Pillow (avatars), stdlib smtplib through services/alert_email.send_message; React 18 + react-router 6, i18next (existing), vitest.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-voyager-reimagined-design.md (§2 constraints, §2a owner decisions, §4 Accounts and identity, §5a gamification, §8 telemetry, §11 Phase 1). Style model: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-phase0-foundations.md.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Two-way compatibility (CLAUDE.md). The new backend keeps serving the previous SPA and the Android app in the field. POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/change-password, PUT /api/auth/email and GET /api/auth/providers keep their current request fields and response keys; changes are additive. The new SPA works against the previous backend: a 404 from any new endpoint, or a /api/config without the auth block, hides that feature without an error (no "Create account", no Account sections, no game chip).
  • Contract freeze. The "API contract" section below is frozen at the end of wave 0 because the iOS and Android apps build against it. Changing it after that needs a contract-change note in the PR and an update to docs/Accounts-API.md in the same PR.
  • Identity key. users.username stays the immutable internal key. No existing table is migrated. New tables key on users.id.
  • Existing tokens keep working. A JWT without tv counts as token_version 0. Admin-created users keep is_first_login semantics and count as verified for AI (signup_method = 'admin').
  • Every absolute URL (email links, OAuth redirect_uri, avatar URLs, mobile redirects) comes from core/urls.public_base_url() = PUBLIC_BASE_URL, else APP_BASE_URL, with the trailing / stripped. Moving to a custom domain is a config change.
  • Providers are config-gated. A provider counts as configured only when all its credentials are non-empty. Unconfigured providers still show their button on every client, and tapping one shows the existing "coming soon" note. Setting the credentials and restarting the app container is all it takes: no code change and no client update.
  • PKCE S256 + state on Google, GitHub and Facebook. Apple documents no PKCE, so Apple uses state + nonce (checked in its id_token). Mobile clients must also send their own S256 challenge, which binds the handoff code to the app.
  • Auto-link only to an account whose email we have verified (users.email_verified = 1), and only from a provider identity whose email is verified and trusted. Google, Apple and GitHub (primary verified email) are trusted. Facebook is untrusted unless FACEBOOK_EMAIL_TRUSTED=true. A pending (unverified) native account is never linked.
  • Secrets never in logs or URLs. Verify/reset tokens, handoff codes, refresh tokens, provider codes and secrets are never logged and never put in an API URL. The one exception is the dev link log (see Task 8), which runs only when SMTP is unset and EMAIL_LOG_LINKS=true or the base URL host is localhost/127.0.0.1. The SPA removes ?token= / ?code= from the address bar with history.replaceState before its first request.
  • Stored secrets are hashes. Every random token is ≥ 256 bits from secrets.token_urlsafe(32), and only its SHA-256 hex is stored. Apple's refresh token, which account deletion needs in order to revoke, is stored Fernet-encrypted with a key HKDF-derived from JWT_SECRET_KEY (info b"voyager-identity-secret").
  • Passwords. Server minimum is 10 characters, at most 128, not in the committed top-10k list (case-insensitive), and not equal to the username or the email's local part. The rule applies to sign-up, reset, change-password and admin-set passwords (admin temporary passwords included).
  • Unverified accounts cannot run AI; the daily quota sits on top of the 10-minute windows. Both are enforced in the _limited(...) router dependencies and in ChatAgent._full_plan_refusal. Admins are exempt from the quota, not from the windows.
  • Game guardrails (§5a). Awards are computed server-side only from server-observed events, never from client claims or telemetry. Every award is idempotent (a unique idem_key) and capped per rule per day. There are no points for volume, and the game never gates a core feature. hide_game hides every game element on every client, while XP still accrues.
  • Free tiers only. No new service: SMTP (existing settings), SQLite and local disk for avatars.
  • i18n. Every new user-visible string is in all 7 languages (en es de fr hi zh bn). Each frontend task creates its own new namespace and edits no existing namespace JSON. The backend email strings live in backend/app/i18n/emails/<lang>.json, with their own parity test. Brand "Voyager", provider names and codes are never translated.
  • Telemetry. Phase 1 events are added once to the closed registry (Task 4). Props are enums, ints and ids only: never an email, username or display name.
  • Python 3.12, ruff check backend/ clean; cd frontend && npx eslint src/ --max-warnings 0; mkdocs build --strict; cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q and cd frontend && npm test keep passing. Every interactive element gets a data-tid.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Email link prefetch and double clicks. Mail scanners (Outlook Safe Links, Gmail) GET every link, and people click twice. Opening /verify?token=… must never consume the token (only the SPA's POST does). A second POST on a used token answers 409 token_used, and the page shows "already confirmed, sign in" rather than an error. Tests in Task 27 (test_verify_twice_is_token_used) and Task 16 (renders already-confirmed on token_used).
  2. Concurrent refreshes from a mobile app. Two requests refresh at the same moment with the same refresh token. The loser gets 401 refresh_stale inside the 30 s grace window, and the family is not revoked. Reuse after the grace window revokes the family. Tests in Task 7 (test_refresh_reuse_within_grace_keeps_family, test_refresh_reuse_after_grace_revokes_family).
  3. Pre-account-takeover through linking. An attacker signs up natively with the victim's email and leaves it pending; later the victim uses Google with the same email. The pending row must be deleted, never linked. A Facebook (untrusted) email never auto-links. An admin-created account with an unverified matching email gets email_in_use_unverified, not a link. Tests in Task 32 (test_pending_native_account_is_replaced_not_linked, test_untrusted_email_never_links, test_unverified_existing_email_is_refused).
  4. Mixed versions. The old SPA on the new backend: login works, a pending account's 403 detail is shown as text, and the additive fields are ignored. The new SPA on the old backend: /api/auth/signup, /api/account, /api/game/me and /api/config.auth all 404 or are missing, and the UI hides those features with no console errors. Tests in Task 7 (test_login_response_keeps_legacy_keys) and Task 5 (old backend hides signup and account sections).
  5. Username and email collisions. Jane vs jane, a username held by a pending account whose link expired, two sign-ups racing for one name, and two redemptions racing for an invite's last use. Comparisons are case-insensitive, an expired pending holder is released, the insert runs inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and invite consumption is a conditional UPDATE. Tests in Task 2 (test_username_taken_is_case_insensitive, test_expired_pending_releases_username), Task 9 (test_last_use_cannot_be_redeemed_twice) and Task 27 (test_signup_race_one_wins).

docs.title: API contract (frozen at the end of wave 0)
docs.text: All paths are under /api. JSON in and out. Unless noted, auth means Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Error envelope for every new error: {"detail": "<English sentence>", "error_code": "<code>"}, plus extra keys where listed. Clients render text from error_code (web: the errors namespace) and fall back to detail. Malformed bodies keep FastAPI's default 422 {"detail": [...]}. Every 429 carries Retry-After (seconds).
  • client is optional on every endpoint that issues a session: "web" (default), "ios" or "android". Mobile clients receive a refresh_token. Optional device_name is a string of at most 64 characters.
  • locale is optional: one of en es de fr hi zh bn. It selects the email language and is stored as users.locale.
  • Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with Z. Days are YYYY-MM-DD (UTC unless stated).

docs.title: Shared objects
docs.text:
User, returned by login, /auth/me, sessions and /account. Every legacy key is kept:

{"id": "6f1c…uuid", "username": "jane_doe", "display_name": "Jane", "email": "jane@example.com",
 "email_verified": true, "is_admin": false, "requires_password_change": false,
 "account_verified": true, "has_password": true, "signup_method": "password",
 "avatar_url": "https://<base>/api/avatars/6f1c….webp?v=3"}

display_name falls back to username. avatar_url is null when there is no avatar (clients draw initials). account_verified is signup_method == "admin" or verified_at is not null. signup_method is one of admin|password|oauth.

Session:

{"access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 86400,
 "refresh_token": "rt_…", "user": User}

refresh_token is present only for client ios/android. expires_in is 86400 for web and 3600 for mobile. The JWT claims are sub (username), uid, tv, is_admin, is_first_login, iat, exp.

GameDelta. It is empty when nothing was awarded, and it is always present where listed:

{"xp": 150, "awards": [{"rule": "email_verified", "points": 50}],
 "badges": [{"id": "verified", "earned_at": "2026-11-11T10:00:00Z"}],
 "level_up": {"from": 1, "to": 2}}

When nothing was awarded: {"xp": <total>, "awards": [], "badges": [], "level_up": null}. When the game is disabled: null.

Settings. Every key is always present, and PATCH accepts any subset; unknown keys return 422:

{"language": null, "theme": "system", "currency": "USD", "units": "metric", "timezone": null,
 "hide_game": false, "hide_community": false, "profile_visibility": "public", "telemetry_opt_out": false}

language is one of the 7 codes or null. theme is system|light|dark. currency matches ^[A-Z]{3}$. units is metric|imperial. timezone is an IANA name that zoneinfo accepts, or null. profile_visibility is public|followers|private.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Request 200 response Errors GET /config (additive) — — existing keys plus "auth": {"signup_mode": "open"\|"invite", "signup_available": bool, "password_reset_available": bool, "min_password_length": 10, "verify_ttl_s": 1800}, and features.accounts: true, features.game: bool — GET /auth/providers (filled in) — — {"providers": [{"id": "apple"\|"google"\|"facebook"\|"github", "configured": bool, "start_url": "/api/auth/oauth/<id>/start" \| null, "id_token": bool}]}, always in the order apple, google, facebook, github —

signup_available = email delivery available (SMTP set, or dev link logging on). password_reset_available uses the same rule. id_token is true when native ID-token sign-in is configured (Apple and Google only).

docs.title: Native accounts
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Request Success Errors POST /auth/signup — {"username", "email", "password", "display_name"?, "invite_code"?, "locale"?, "client"?} 202 {"status": "verification_sent", "email": "<as given, lower-cased>", "expires_in": 1800}. The same response when the email already belongs to an active account: that owner gets an "already registered" email instead, and nothing is created 409 username_taken, 422 username_invalid, 422 username_reserved, 422 email_invalid, 422 password_too_short, 422 password_too_long, 422 password_common, 422 password_matches_identity, 422 display_name_invalid, 403 invite_required, 403 invite_invalid, 503 email_unavailable, 429 rate_limited POST /auth/verify-email/resend — {"email", "locale"?} 202 {"status": "verification_sent"}, always (no enumeration) 429 rate_limited, 503 email_unavailable POST /auth/verify-email — {"token", "client"?, "device_name"?} 200 {"status": "verified", "session": Session \| null, "game": GameDelta}. session is set when the token activated a pending account and null when it confirmed an email on an already active account 400 token_invalid, 410 token_expired, 409 token_used, 409 email_changed (the account's email is no longer the one the token was issued for) POST /auth/password-reset/request — {"email", "locale"?} 202 {"status": "reset_sent"}, always 429 rate_limited, 503 email_unavailable POST /auth/password-reset/confirm — {"token", "new_password", "client"?, "device_name"?} 200 {"status": "password_reset", "session": Session}. It bumps token_version and revokes every refresh token. A pending account becomes active and verified (the email is proven) 400 token_invalid, 410 token_expired, 409 token_used, the password errors above POST /account/email/verify yes {"locale"?} 202 {"status": "verification_sent", "email": "…", "expires_in": 1800} 409 already_verified, 422 no_email, 503 email_unavailable, 429 rate_limited

Username rule: lower-cased, then ^[a-z0-9_]{3,20}$, not in RESERVED_USERNAMES (Task 2), and unique case-insensitively against every existing username. Email: the existing _EMAIL_RE, lower-cased, ≤ 254. display_name: NFC, stripped, 1–50 characters, no control characters. Tokens expire 30 minutes after issue and are single use. Issuing a new token of the same purpose invalidates the previous ones. Emails go to <base>/verify?token=… and <base>/reset-password?token=….

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Request Success Errors POST /auth/login (additive) — {"username", "password", "client"?, "device_name"?}. username may also be the account's email 200 Session, with the legacy keys kept: user.username, user.is_admin, user.requires_password_change, user.email 401 (unchanged text) for bad credentials, 403 {"error_code": "account_pending", "email_hint": "j•••@example.com"} only when the password was right, 429 POST /auth/refresh — {"refresh_token"} 200 {"access_token", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "rt_…"}, rotated 401 refresh_stale (an already-rotated token reused ≤ 30 s after rotation; the family is kept), 401 refresh_invalid (unknown, expired, revoked, user inactive, or reused after the grace window, which revokes the family), 429 POST /auth/logout optional {"refresh_token"?} 204, and revokes that refresh token's family — POST /auth/logout-all yes — 204; bumps token_version and revokes every refresh token — POST /auth/change-password (additive) yes {"current_password", "new_password", "client"?}. current_password may be "" when has_password is false 200 {"access_token", "token_type", "expires_in"}, plus refresh_token for mobile. Bumps token_version, revokes every refresh token, and the new token keeps this session alive 400 "Current password is incorrect" (unchanged), the password errors above as 400 with error_code GET /auth/me (additive) yes — User 401 session_revoked when tv is stale PUT /auth/email (additive) yes unchanged {"email", "email_verified": false, "verification_sent": bool}. A changed email starts unverified, and a link is sent when email is available unchanged

Any authenticated route answers 401 {"error_code": "session_revoked"} when the JWT's tv ≠ users.token_version.

docs.title: OAuth
docs.text:
<p> is one of apple, google, facebook, github.

Method, path Auth Request Success Errors GET /auth/oauth/<p>/start — (browser navigation) query client=web\|ios\|android, return_to=/path (web; same-origin path, default /), challenge=<b64url S256> (required for ios/android), redirect_uri=<allow-listed> (ios/android; default <base>/auth/callback), link=<ticket> (optional) 302 to the provider. Sets the cookie tp_oauth=<binding> (HttpOnly, Path /api/auth/oauth, Max-Age 600, SameSite=None; Secure on https, else Lax) Unknown <p>: 404. Not configured, bad return_to, missing challenge or bad redirect_uri: 302 to <final>?error=<code> GET/POST /auth/oauth/<p>/callback — (provider redirect; Apple uses POST form_post) the provider's code, state, error, Apple's user 302 to <final>?code=<handoff> 302 to <final>?error=<code> POST /auth/oauth/exchange — (web also sends the tp_oauth cookie) {"code", "verifier"?, "device_name"?} (the client type is the one given at start) one of the three results below 400 code_invalid (unknown, expired, used, or the cookie/verifier doesn't match) POST /auth/oauth/complete — {"signup_token", "username", "display_name"?, "invite_code"?, "client"?, "device_name"?, "locale"?} 201 {"status": "signed_in", "session": Session, "game": GameDelta} 400 signup_token_invalid, 409 username_taken, 422 username_invalid, 422 username_reserved, 403 invite_required, 403 invite_invalid POST /auth/oauth/link-ticket yes {"provider", "client"?} 200 {"start_url": "/api/auth/oauth/<p>/start?link=<ticket>&client=web"} (the ticket lasts 5 min and is single use) 404 provider_unknown, 409 provider_unavailable POST /auth/oauth/<p>/id-token (apple, google) — {"id_token", "nonce"?, "authorization_code"? (apple), "display_name"?, "client": "ios"\|"android", "device_name"?} the same results as exchange 404 when native is not configured for <p>, 400 id_token_invalid DELETE /account/identities/<p> yes — 204 404 identity_not_found, 409 last_sign_in_method

<final> is <base>/auth/callback for web, or the client's redirect_uri for mobile. redirect_uri must exactly match one entry of OAUTH_MOBILE_REDIRECTS (default ["voyager://auth/callback", "<base>/auth/callback"]). Callback error codes: cancelled, state_invalid, provider_error, provider_unavailable, email_in_use_unverified, identity_in_use, account_inactive, bad_request. The handoff code lasts 120 s and is single use. Web exchange needs the tp_oauth cookie whose hash was stored at start. Mobile exchange needs verifier, with b64url(sha256(verifier)) == challenge.

Exchange / id-token results:

{"status": "signed_in", "session": Session, "game": GameDelta, "return_to": "/"}
{"status": "needs_username", "signup_token": "…", "suggested_username": "jane", "display_name": "Jane Doe",
 "email": "jane@example.com", "invite_required": false, "return_to": "/"}
{"status": "linked", "provider": "github", "return_to": "/account"}

signup_token lasts 30 min. email is null when the provider gave none.

docs.title: Account
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Request Success Errors GET /account yes — {"user": User, "identities": [{"provider", "email", "linked_at"}], "settings": Settings, "onboarding": Onboarding} — PATCH /account yes {"display_name"} {"user": User} 422 display_name_invalid GET /account/settings yes — Settings — PATCH /account/settings yes a subset of Settings Settings 422 (FastAPI default) PUT /account/onboarding yes {"step": 0..5, "done": bool, "skipped"?: bool, "traveller_type"?: "^[a-z_]{1,32}$"} {"onboarding": Onboarding, "game": GameDelta} 422 PUT /account/avatar yes multipart/form-data, field file (jpeg/png/webp/gif), ≤ 2 MB 200 {"avatar_url": "…"} 413 avatar_too_large, 415 avatar_type, 422 avatar_unreadable DELETE /account/avatar yes — 200 {"avatar_url": null} — GET /avatars/<user_id>.webp — — image/webp, Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable 404 GET /account/export yes — 200 application/json with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="voyager-export-<username>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.json": {"format": "voyager-export", "version": 1, "exported_at", "account", "identities", "settings", "onboarding", "preferences", "plans", "recent_searches", "taste", "feedback", "fare_watches", "price_watches", "notifications", "devices", "game"} 429 DELETE /account yes {"password"} when has_password, else {"confirm_username"} 204. Deletes everything the export lists, the avatar file and the user's telemetry rows, and revokes Apple tokens 403 password_incorrect, 400 confirmation_mismatch, 409 last_admin GET /account/quota yes — {"day": "2026-11-11", "resets_at": "2026-11-12T00:00:00Z", "buckets": {"search": {"used": 3, "limit": 20}, "chat": …, "compare": …, "discover": …, "light_ai": …, "import": …}}. limit is null when unlimited (admin, or quotas off) —

Onboarding: {"step": 0, "done": false, "skipped": false, "traveller_type": null, "completed_at": null}. Once done is true it stays true, and starter XP is awarded once, when done && !skipped.

docs.title: AI gate (on every _limited(...) route and chat full plans)
docs.text:
• 403 {"detail": "Confirm your email to use the AI planner.", "error_code": "email_unverified"} for a signed-in user whose account_verified is false.
  • 429 {"detail": "You've used today's AI allowance for <label>. It resets at midnight UTC.", "error_code": "ai_daily_quota", "bucket": "search", "resets_at": "…"} with Retry-After = seconds to the next UTC midnight. Chat refuses in-stream with that text, the same way it handles the search bucket today.

docs.title: Game
docs.text:
Method, path Auth Success Errors GET /game/me yes {"xp": 150, "level": 2, "level_min_xp": 100, "next_level_xp": 250, "badges": [{"id", "progress", "target", "earned_at"}], "streaks": {"daily": {"current", "longest", "last_day", "freezes"}}, "recent": [{"rule", "points", "created_at"}], "hidden": false} (recent is the last 10) 404 when GAME_ENABLED=false GET /game/catalog — {"version": 1, "rules": [{"id", "points", "daily_cap", "once"}], "badges": [{"id", "rule", "target", "tier": "bronze"\|"silver"\|"gold", "icon": "<lucide name>"}], "levels": [{"level": 1, "min_xp": 0}, …]} with Cache-Control: max-age=300 404 when disabled

Clients translate badge and rule names by id: game:badges.<id>.name / .desc, game:rules.<id>.

docs.title: Admin (additive)
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors POST /admin/invites {"max_uses": 1..1000 = 1, "expires_in_days": 1..365 = 14, "note"?: "≤ 80 chars"} 201 {"id", "code": "VOY-XXXX-XXXX", "code_prefix": "VOY-XXXX", "max_uses", "uses": 0, "expires_at", "note"} (the code is shown only here) 422 GET /admin/invites — [{"id", "code_prefix", "max_uses", "uses", "expires_at", "revoked_at", "note", "created_at"}] — DELETE /admin/invites/<id> — 204 (revokes it) 404

GET /admin/users rows also gain signup_method, account_status, email_verified, display_name (no tokens and no hashes).

docs.title: Shared-file hotspots and how conflicts are avoided
docs.text: Hotspot Rule backend/app/main.py (router list, lifespan, middleware) Only Task 1 edits it. It registers every Phase 1 router (stub modules), the body-size limit for avatars, the table creation and the maintenance loop. Later tasks fill their own router module. backend/app/core/config.py Only Task 1, which adds every Phase 1 setting (list in Task 1). backend/app/db/users_db.py Only Task 2. It provides every user-row helper later tasks need. backend/app/api/routes/auth.py, backend/app/api/routes/admin.py Only Task 7 (admin invites live in the new admin_invites.py). backend/app/core/rate_limit.py, backend/app/agents/chat_agent.py, backend/tests/conftest.py Only Task 14. backend/app/api/routes/client_config.py Only Task 27. backend/app/telemetry/registry.py + docs/Telemetry.md Only Task 4, which adds every Phase 1 event up front. Game award call sites Task 1 freezes backend/app/game/hooks.py as no-op stubs. Task 10 fills the bodies. Tasks 12 and 27 call the hooks. frontend/src/services/api.js Not edited in Phase 1. Task 5 creates services/authApi.js, accountApi.js, gameApi.js and apiError.js with every call in the contract. UI tasks only import them. frontend/src/App.jsx, context/AuthContext.jsx, components/ui/NavBar.jsx, telemetry/routes.js Only Task 5. It adds every route, stub page and stub component. Each later task overwrites only its own stub file. Locale JSON One new namespace per task (named in each task). No Phase 1 task edits an existing namespace. Task 5 owns errors (every error_code). frontend/src/pages/AdminPage.jsx Only Task 26. frontend/src/components/auth/SocialSignInButtons.jsx Only Task 18. frontend/src/pages/LoginPage.jsx Only Task 15. Docs (CLAUDE.md, docs/Configuration.md, API-Reference.md, Deployment-GCP.md, Privacy.md, Feature-Parity.md) Only Task 36. Task 6 creates docs/Accounts-API.md and is the only Phase 1 edit to mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Task 1: Backend seams (settings, error envelope, URLs, router stubs, hooks, quota seam)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/core/errors.py, backend/app/core/urls.py, backend/app/services/account_maintenance.py (async account_maintenance(), the hourly loop below), backend/app/core/session_payload.py, backend/app/core/ai_quota.py (stub), backend/app/game/__init__.py, backend/app/game/hooks.py (stubs), backend/app/api/routes/{signup,sessions,oauth,account,avatars,account_data,game,quota,admin_invites}.py (each router = APIRouter()) - Modify: backend/app/core/config.py, backend/app/main.py - Test: backend/tests/test_phase1_seams.py

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 2 create_account_tables(), purge_expired(now) -> dict[str, int] (wired in the final step, after Task 2 merges). - Produces: - class ApiError(Exception): __init__(self, status: int, code: str, detail: str, *, headers: dict | None = None, **extra). The handler in main.py returns {"detail", "error_code", **extra}. - public_base_url() -> str; public_url(path: str) -> str (path starts with /). - user_payload(user: dict) -> dict: the User object in the contract. avatar_url is public_url(f"/api/avatars/{id}.webp?v={avatar_rev}") only when avatar_source is set and $DATA_DIR/avatars/<id>.webp exists. has_password is password_hash != "!". - game.hooks.on_email_verified(user_id: str) -> dict | None and on_onboarding_complete(user_id: str) -> dict | None. The stubs return None. - ai_quota.daily_quota(bucket: str) -> Callable, a FastAPI dependency. The stub does nothing. _limited(bucket) becomes [Depends(require_ai_access), Depends(rate_limit(bucket)), Depends(daily_quota(bucket))]. - Settings (with these defaults): signup_mode: Literal["open","invite"] = "open", email_log_links: bool = False, account_token_ttl_minutes: int = 30, pending_purge_days: int = 7, refresh_token_days: int = 60, refresh_family_max_days: int = 365, mobile_access_token_minutes: int = 60, google_client_id/google_client_secret: str = "", google_native_client_ids: list[str] = [], github_client_id/github_client_secret: str = "", facebook_app_id/facebook_app_secret: str = "", facebook_graph_version: str = "v24.0", facebook_email_trusted: bool = False, apple_services_id/apple_team_id/apple_key_id/apple_private_key: str = "", apple_native_client_ids: list[str] = [], oauth_mobile_redirects: list[str] = ["voyager://auth/callback"] (<base>/auth/callback is always allowed as well), ai_daily_quota_enabled: bool = True, ai_daily_quota_search: int = 20, …_chat: int = 100, …_compare: int = 40, …_discover: int = 20, …_light_ai: int = 200, …_import: int = 20 (0 = unlimited), game_enabled: bool = True, game_rules_path: str = "", rate_limit_auth_email: int = 10, rate_limit_email_address: int = 3, rate_limit_signup: int = 5, rate_limit_oauth: int = 30, rate_limit_refresh: int = 60, rate_limit_account: int = 30. - main.py: includes the nine new routers with prefix="/api". Adds BodySizeLimit(prefix="/api/account/avatar", max_bytes=2*1024*1024 + 64*1024, message="That image is too big — use one under 2 MB."). In the lifespan, after create_users_table(), calls create_account_tables() and starts account_maintenance() (every 3600 s, await asyncio.to_thread(purge_expired, now), logging errors and never raising, cancelled on shutdown like telemetry_task).

  • [ ] Step 1: Write failing tests: test_api_error_envelope (a route raising ApiError(409, "username_taken", "x", bucket="s") → {"detail": "x", "error_code": "username_taken", "bucket": "s"}); test_public_url_prefers_public_base_url (PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://a.example/ → public_url("/verify") == "https://a.example/verify"; empty → falls back to APP_BASE_URL); test_user_payload_shape (keys equal the contract User set; display_name falls back to the username; avatar_url is None when the file is missing; password_hash "!" → has_password False); test_stub_routers_importable (each of the nine modules exposes an APIRouter named router, and GET /api/account answers 404 or 405 rather than failing at import); test_limited_includes_quota_dependency.
  • [ ] Step 2: Run cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_phase1_seams.py → FAIL.
  • [ ] Step 3: Implement, except the lifespan wiring.
  • [ ] Step 4: Rebase on Task 2 and add the lifespan wiring. Run the whole backend suite and ruff check backend/ → PASS.

docs.title: Task 2: Schema + user-row helpers
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/db/accounts_schema.py, backend/app/db/reserved_usernames.py - Modify: backend/app/db/users_db.py - Test: backend/tests/test_accounts_schema.py, backend/tests/test_users_db_phase1.py

Interfaces: - Produces: - create_account_tables() -> None. It is idempotent. It adds users columns with ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN when missing: email_verified INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, account_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' (active|pending), signup_method TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'admin', verified_at TEXT, token_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, display_name TEXT, avatar_source TEXT (upload|provider), avatar_rev INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, locale TEXT, last_login_at TEXT, invite_id INTEGER. It also creates indexes on lower(username) and lower(email) (non-unique; existing data may predate the rule) and these tables: - account_tokens(id INTEGER PK, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, purpose TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(purpose IN ('verify_email','reset_password')), token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, email TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, expires_at TEXT NOT NULL, used_at TEXT), with an index on (user_id, purpose) - refresh_tokens(id TEXT PK, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, family_id TEXT NOT NULL, token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, client TEXT NOT NULL, device_name TEXT, token_version INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, last_used_at TEXT, expires_at TEXT NOT NULL, family_expires_at TEXT NOT NULL, rotated_at TEXT, revoked_at TEXT), with indexes on user_id and family_id - user_identities(id INTEGER PK, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, provider TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, email_verified INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, display_name TEXT, picture_url TEXT, secret_enc TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, last_used_at TEXT, UNIQUE(provider, subject)), with an index on user_id - oauth_tickets(hash TEXT PK, kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('state','handoff','signup','link')), provider TEXT, user_id TEXT, data TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', binding_hash TEXT, client_challenge TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, expires_at TEXT NOT NULL, used_at TEXT) - invite_codes(id INTEGER PK, code_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, code_prefix TEXT NOT NULL, note TEXT, max_uses INTEGER NOT NULL, uses INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_by TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, expires_at TEXT NOT NULL, revoked_at TEXT) - user_settings(user_id TEXT PK, data TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL) - user_onboarding(user_id TEXT PK, step INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, skipped INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, traveller_type TEXT, completed_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL) - ai_usage_daily(day TEXT, user_key TEXT, bucket TEXT, used INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, PRIMARY KEY(day, user_key, bucket)) - xp_ledger(id INTEGER PK, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, rule TEXT NOT NULL, points INTEGER NOT NULL, idem_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, meta TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL), with indexes on (user_id, created_at) and (user_id, rule, created_at) - user_badges(user_id TEXT, badge_id TEXT, progress INTEGER NOT NULL, target INTEGER NOT NULL, earned_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(user_id, badge_id)) - user_streaks(user_id TEXT, kind TEXT, current INTEGER NOT NULL, longest INTEGER NOT NULL, last_day TEXT, freezes INTEGER NOT NULL, freeze_week TEXT, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(user_id, kind)) - purge_expired(now: datetime) -> dict[str, int]. It deletes pending users older than pending_purge_days (and their account_tokens), account_tokens 1 day past expiry, oauth_tickets past expiry, refresh tokens 7 days past expiry or revocation, and ai_usage_daily older than 8 days. It returns counts per table. - In users_db.py: - create_user(..., signup_method="admin", account_status="active", email_verified=False, display_name=None, locale=None, password_hash=None). It lower-cases the email, and password_hash="!" marks an account with no password. - get_user_by_login(identifier: str) -> dict | None (an exact username, else a case-insensitive username, else a lower-cased email) - get_user_by_email(email) -> dict | None - username_available(name: str, now: datetime) -> bool: case-insensitive. A pending holder whose newest token has expired doesn't count, and is deleted. - create_pending_user(username, email, password, display_name, locale, invite_id) -> dict: inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Interfaces: - Produces: - @dataclass(frozen=True) ProviderProfile(subject: str, email: str | None, email_verified: bool, email_trusted: bool, display_name: str | None, picture_url: str | None). - class OAuthError(Exception) with a .code (a contract callback error code). - class OAuthProvider(Protocol): id: str, uses_pkce: bool, callback_methods: tuple[str, ...], configured() -> bool, native_configured() -> bool, authorize_url(*, redirect_uri, state, nonce, code_challenge) -> str, async exchange(*, code, redirect_uri, code_verifier, nonce, form: dict) -> tuple[ProviderProfile, str | None] (the second item is a secret to store, Apple's refresh token), async verify_id_token(id_token, *, nonce: str | None) -> ProviderProfile (native; the default raises OAuthError("bad_request")), async revoke(secret: str) -> None (the default does nothing). - registry.PROVIDER_ORDER = ("apple", "google", "facebook", "github"); get_provider(id) -> OAuthProvider | None (it imports services.oauth.<id> lazily and reads PROVIDER; an ImportError → None, so providers merge independently); override(id, provider) for tests. - pkce_verifier() -> str (43–128 characters), pkce_challenge(verifier) -> str (b64url SHA-256, no padding). - http_client() -> httpx.AsyncClient (timeout 10 s, User-Agent: Voyager/1); set_transport(transport | None) for tests. - jwks.verify_jwt(token, *, jwks_url, issuers: set[str], audiences: set[str], nonce: str | None = None, nonce_is_hash: bool = False) -> dict. Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 2 set_avatar; Task 1 public_url. - Produces: - avatar_path(user_id) -> Path ($DATA_DIR/avatars/<id>.webp). - process_upload(data: bytes, content_type: str) -> bytes. It raises ApiError 413/415/422. Accepted types are image/jpeg|png|webp|gif, sniffed with Pillow (the declared type alone isn't trusted). Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 40_000_000 and the bomb warning becomes an error. It applies ImageOps.exif_transpose, uses the first frame, converts to RGB(A), centre-crops square, resizes to 256 with LANCZOS, and saves WebP at quality 82 with no metadata. - save_avatar(user_id, webp: bytes, source: str) -> str (an atomic write via a temp file and os.replace; returns avatar_url); remove_avatar(user_id). - async import_provider_photo(user_id: str, url: str) -> bool, a best effort. The host must be one of lh3.googleusercontent.com, avatars.githubusercontent.com, platform-lookaside.fbsbx.com or graph.facebook.com over https; the response is capped at 2 MB with a 5 s timeout and no redirects off-list. On success it stores the photo with source "provider"; on any failure it returns False. - Routes PUT/DELETE /account/avatar (bucket account) and GET /avatars/{user_id}.webp (FileResponse with the immutable cache header; a non-UUID id → 404). - [ ] Step 1: Write failing tests: a 1000×600 JPEG → a 256×256 WebP with no EXIF; a PNG with an alpha channel keeps transparency; text/plain bytes labelled image/png → 415; 2.1 MB → 413; a decompression bomb (a 10k×10k PNG header) → 422; the GET serves the bytes with the cache header; import_provider_photo refuses https://evil.example/x.png and an http:// URL. - [ ] Step 2: Run → FAIL. docs.title: Tasks 28–31: Provider adapters (one file each, parallel)
docs.text:
Each task creates backend/app/services/oauth/<id>.py exposing PROVIDER: OAuthProvider, and backend/tests/test_oauth_<id>.py. Every test runs against FakeIdP / MockTransport only. Each test file covers: configured() false when any credential is empty; authorize_url has exactly the listed parameters; exchange builds the right token request (asserted from the transport) and maps the profile; provider error responses → OAuthError("provider_error"). Commit feat(oauth): <Name> provider.

Task Provider Configured when Authorize Token / profile Profile mapping 28 google google_client_id + google_client_secret https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth; response_type=code, scope=openid email profile, state, nonce, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256, prompt=select_account POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token (form, with code_verifier); verify the id_token with JWKS https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs, iss {https://accounts.google.com, accounts.google.com}, aud google_client_id, nonce sub; email; email_verified (bool or "true"); trusted = verified; name; picture. Native: verify_id_token with aud ∈ google_native_client_ids; native_configured() when the list is non-empty 29 github github_client_id + github_client_secret https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize; scope=read:user user:email, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256, allow_signup=true POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token with Accept: application/json and code_verifier; GET https://api.github.com/user and /user/emails with Accept: application/vnd.github+json, X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28 subject str(id); email = the primary && verified one, else the first verified one, else None; verified/trusted accordingly; name or login; avatar_url. A test covers "only an unverified email → email None" 30 facebook facebook_app_id + facebook_app_secret https://www.facebook.com/{facebook_graph_version}/dialog/oauth; scope=public_profile,email, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256, response_type=code GET https://graph.facebook.com/{ver}/oauth/access_token (client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code, code_verifier); GET /{ver}/me?fields=id,name,email,picture.width(256).height(256) with appsecret_proof = hex(HMAC-SHA256(app_secret, access_token)) id; email; email_verified = email is not None; email_trusted = settings.facebook_email_trusted; name; picture.data.url (only when is_silhouette is false). A test covers "trusted false by default" 31 apple apple_services_id + apple_team_id + apple_key_id + apple_private_key https://appleid.apple.com/auth/authorize; response_type=code, response_mode=form_post, scope=name email, state, nonce (no PKCE: uses_pkce False); callback_methods ("POST",) POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/token; client_secret = an ES256 JWT {iss: team_id, iat, exp: iat+300, aud: "https://appleid.apple.com", sub: client_id} with header kid. The private key accepts a PEM with real or \n-escaped newlines. Verify the id_token with JWKS https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys, iss https://appleid.apple.com, aud = client_id, nonce sub; email; email_verified ("true"/true); trusted = verified; the name comes from the first-time user form field JSON (name.firstName + lastName), else None; no picture. Return the refresh_token as the secret. revoke(secret) POSTs https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke (token, token_type_hint=refresh_token). Native: aud ∈ apple_native_client_ids; nonce_is_hash=True (claim = hex SHA-256 of the raw nonce); an authorization_code is exchanged with client_id = the token's aud for a refresh token. Tests: the client-secret JWT verifies with the public key; the escaped-newline PEM works

docs.title: Task 32: OAuth flow routes
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/db/oauth_db.py, backend/app/services/oauth/flow.py - Modify: backend/app/api/routes/oauth.py (it also serves GET /auth/providers, which no backend route serves today; auth.py stays Task 7's) - Test: backend/tests/test_oauth_flow.py

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 11 registry, pkce_*, secrets_box, OAuthError; Task 7 issue_session; Task 9 check_invite/consume_invite; Task 13 import_provider_photo; Task 8 send_account_email (verify mail for untrusted-email accounts); Task 2 helpers; Task 1 hooks. - Produces: - oauth_db.put_ticket(kind, *, ttl_s, provider=None, user_id=None, data=None, binding=None, client_challenge=None) -> str (plaintext); take_ticket(kind, token, now) -> dict | None (atomic UPDATE … SET used_at where unused and unexpired; None otherwise). - flow.resolve_identity(profile: ProviderProfile, provider: str, *, link_user_id: str | None, secret: str | None) -> Result, where Result is one of SignedIn(user), NeedsUsername(pending_data), Linked(user) or Refused(code). Rules, in order: 1. A known (provider, subject) → its user. An inactive user → account_inactive. Update last_used_at, the identity email and the secret. 2. link_user_id set → attach (a subject owned by another user → identity_in_use). 3. email_verified and email_trusted and an active user with that email and email_verified=1 → attach and sign in. 4. A pending user with that email → delete it (and its tokens), then continue. 5. An active user with that email and email_verified=0 → email_in_use_unverified. 6. Otherwise → NeedsUsername. - On complete: create the user with signup_method 'oauth' and password_hash '!'. When the email is verified and trusted → email_verified=1, verified_at=now and hooks.on_email_verified. When the email is untrusted → email_verified=0 and a verify email is sent. The identity row is inserted, import_provider_photo runs as a background task, and invite mode needs a valid invite_code (consumed). - The suggested username is the email local part or name, folded to [a-z0-9_], trimmed to 20 and padded to ≥ 3, with _2, _3, … until available. - The routes per the contract. Buckets: oauth on all of them, except /auth/providers, which has none. The first /auth/providers call logs oauth.configured providers=[…] redirect_uris=[…] once (the <base>/api/auth/oauth/<p>/callback URIs the owner registers in each console). - [ ] Step 1: Write failing tests with a fake provider through registry.override: test_web_round_trip (start → 302 with a state → callback → 302 /auth/callback?code= → exchange with the cookie → signed_in or needs_username → complete → session); test_exchange_without_cookie_fails (400 code_invalid); test_mobile_requires_challenge_and_verifier (no challenge → redirect error=bad_request; a wrong verifier → 400); test_mobile_redirect_allowlist; test_state_single_use_and_10_min_expiry; test_pending_native_account_is_replaced_not_linked; test_untrusted_email_never_links; test_unverified_existing_email_is_refused; test_link_ticket_attaches_identity; test_identity_in_use; test_unconfigured_provider_redirects_with_provider_unavailable (never a 5xx); test_apple_form_post_callback (POST callback with a user JSON name); test_return_to_rejects_offsite (//evil.com and https://evil.com → /); test_providers_listing_order_and_flags; invite mode → needs_username.invite_required true, and complete without a code → 403. - [ ] Step 2: Run → FAIL. Step 3: Implement. Step 4: Run the backend suite → PASS. - [ ] Step 5: Commit feat(oauth): authorization-code flow with PKCE, linking and handoff codes

Forgot → reset → the old tab gets session_revoked. OAuth is covered by Task 35, since no real credentials exist yet; in the browser, check that every provider shows "coming soon".
