docs.title: Execution waves
docs.text:
Each wave starts when the previous one is merged to main. Inside a wave, every task runs in its own worktree in parallel, because the tasks own disjoint files.

Wave Tasks (parallel) Count Gate 0 — seams 1 backend seams · 2 schema + users_db · 3 password policy · 4 telemetry events · 5 frontend seams · 6 contract doc 6 Task 1's last step rebases on Task 2. When wave 0 merges, the contract is frozen and the iOS/Android teams start 1 — modules backend: 7 sessions · 8 emails · 9 invites · 10 game engine · 11 OAuth core · 12 account API · 13 avatars · 14 AI gate + quotas; frontend: 15 sign-up · 16 verify · 17 recovery · 18 OAuth pages · 19 profile · 20 settings · 21 security · 22 data · 23 quota UX · 24 game UI · 25 onboarding hook · 26 admin invites 20 Frontend tasks need only Task 5 and the contract (API mocked); backend tasks need only Tasks 1–3 2 — flows 27 sign-up/verify/reset API · 28 Google · 29 GitHub · 30 Facebook · 31 Apple · 32 OAuth flow · 33 export + delete · 34 deploy config 8 27 needs 7, 8, 9, 10; 28–31 need 11; 32 needs 7, 9, 11, 13; 33 needs 11, 13 3 — integrate 35 provider E2E · 36 docs · 37 translation review (one agent per language) · 38 browser E2E + three review passes 4 (+6 reviewers) 35 needs 28–32

Merge cadence: one PR per wave (as in Phase 0), or a PR per task when CI time allows. Each PR is green and deployable on its own: every wave leaves the features hidden or harmless until the next lands. Wave 1 UI against the wave-0 backend sees 404s and hides itself, and wave-1 backend routes exist with no UI pointing at them.

docs.title: Deferred (later phases)
docs.text: Seasonal challenges, leaderboards and more badges come in Phase 5. Streak hooks (daily quiz, trip check-ins) come in Phases 2 and 5. Notification categories and quiet hours in Settings come in Phase 6. The traveller-type badge comes with Phase 2's shared onboarding. AASA/assetlinks for universal links come in Phases 7 and 8. A refresh-token device list ("signed-in devices") can come later.

docs.title: Phase 1 follow-ups (accounts + game engine)
docs.text: Deferred items from the Phase 1 run (plan 2026-11-11-phase1-accounts-game.md). Each was reviewed and judged safe to ship without the fix. Grouped by area, most important first.

docs.title: Owner actions (before turning features on)
docs.text:
• Sign-up is off until you opt in. Native sign-up needs SIGNUP_ENABLED=true plus email delivery (SMTP). OAuth sign-up turns on per provider once its credentials are set. See docs/Deployment-GCP.md → "Sign-in providers and email".
  • Credentials to provide: Google, GitHub, Facebook and Apple OAuth (client IDs/secrets; Apple Services ID, team ID, key ID, private key), SMTP host/user/password/sender. Register <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/api/auth/oauth/<provider>/callback in each console. Run infrastructure/gcp/bootstrap.sh before adopting the new SECRET_MANAGER_SECRETS list.
  • Existing users and password reset. Reset mail goes only to a verified address (or a pending sign-up). Admin-created users with an unverified email must confirm it once ("Send link") before self-service reset works. Consider an in-app prompt to confirm the address.
  • Mobile apps: confirm the Android and iOS /config parsers ignore unknown keys (auth, features.accounts, features.game) and render user.email: null.

docs.title: Security hardening
docs.text:
• Rule-3 auto-link: a victim who clicks an unsolicited verify link gives an attacker's untrusted-identity account a verified email; their later trusted Google sign-in would auto-link into it. Refuse auto-link into an account with no trusted identity.
  • Native ID-token sign-in accepts a missing nonce (Apple, Google). Make it required once the mobile apps ship (Phases 7/8).
  • Apple native sign-in without authorization_code stores no revocable secret; consider requiring the code (App Store review expects revoke on delete).
  • JWKS: an unknown kid refetch can be spammed (no negative cache); network failures map to provider_error, not provider_unavailable; nonce=None skips the nonce check.
  • Invite mode: an existing-email sign-up leaves the invite unconsumed, so an invite holder can probe whether an address is registered.
  • Legacy JWTs without uid resolve by username until they expire (≤ 24 h after the sessions deploy).
  • Avatar provider import trusts the declared Content-Type; multipart is parsed before the auth check.

docs.title: Correctness and robustness
docs.text:
• New rate-limit buckets (account, oauth, refresh) answer the legacy 429 {"detail"} without error_code: "rate_limited".
  • An OAuth account with no provider email (or an untrusted one while SMTP is off) stays email_unverified for AI with no way out.
  • Non-atomic sequences: change-password + bump + revoke; put_onboarding read-modify-write; unlink_identity count + delete (two concurrent unlinks can leave a password-less account with no sign-in).
  • id-token route: profile.display_name and _signed_in sit outside the error guard (500 possible); in complete, a DB lock timeout shows as 400 signup_token_invalid; a 409 email_changed consumes the link.
  • Account deletion: a LastAdminError after a client disconnect logs "Task exception was never retrieved".
  • Avatar decodes queue in the shared default executor (6 threads); use a dedicated one.
  • vm_backup re-uploads the user tables almost every 5 minutes (ai_usage_daily, last_login_at change constantly); exclude volatile tables.
  • Daily AI quota also applies per IP to anonymous callers (dev only; production requires sign-in); document or drop.
  • One tp_oauth cookie per browser: two concurrent starts collide (code_invalid).
  • Game rules are cached per process (an edit at the same path needs a restart).

docs.title: Web app
docs.text:
• /config failure is cached as empty for the page load, hiding account editing, settings sync and the game until reload; retry once.
  • AuthContext: the mount-time /auth/me has no staleness guard; the spinner can stick if another tab stores a token while it is in flight.
  • Router-state notices replay on reload and the "signed out" notice is never cleared; a dead-token link error loses its toast.
  • Only the last held game award is kept within the 15 s replay window.
  • tp_oauth_method is never cleared; ChooseUsername display-name maxLength is 60 (contract 1–50); has_password defaults differ between Security and Data sections.
  • ProfileSection reads email_verified from AuthContext, which PUT /auth/email doesn't update until reload.
  • Settings: card narrower than the others; the time-zone select shows the device zone while the stored value is null; edits debounce 1 s (an immediate export shows the old value); pending debounced edits are lost on sign-out; a shared device can push user A's language/theme up to user B.
  • AccountPage can't tell loading from unavailable; a 500/offline leaves only Profile with no retry.
  • Account menu lacks arrow-key navigation; edit controls pop in after load.
  • Tests to add: settings language device-up-sync and consent mirroring; quota limit-reached and non-404 cases; delete 409/400 errors; resend 429 retryAfter; onboarding step clamp > 5.

docs.title: Code health
docs.text:
• Private helpers used across modules: users_db._hash/_delete_user_rows/_holder_blocks, invites_db._hash, account._display_name, alert_email._POLICY/_sender/_mail_domain, feedback_db._row_to_dict. Promote to public helpers (e.g. a core/accounts_helpers module).
  • PASSWORD_DETAIL lives in routes/auth.py; auth.py lazily imports signup.address_allowed. Move both next to core/passwords / a shared email module.
  • Email _LOCALES is hand-maintained and not checked against the SPA's language list.
  • Telemetry game_award.rule, badge_earned.badge, auth_result.code are free-form ids (could be enums).
  • docs/API-Reference.md endpoint table doesn't list the account endpoints (it links Accounts-API.md).
  • Agent error sections show raw SDK text when no model key is configured (predates Phase 1).

docs.title: Phase 2 follow-ups
docs.text: Deferred items from the Phase 2 (journey) execution: reviewer minors, the final whole-branch review's Minor list, and the E2E findings. None blocks the journey being on. Grouped by area; pick up opportunistically.

docs.title: Owner / external actions
docs.text:
• Native-speaker review of the hi, bn and zh UI text and of the 34-language phrase list (owner ruling 4). The model-reviewed text shipped.
  • Real-device check of the service worker and IndexedDB on Safari/iOS (only Chromium was exercised in the E2E). Confetti and the recap countries reveal were not observed in the E2E; look at them once.
  • Mobile teams (Android phase 8, iOS phase 7): the client placeKey rule changed (non-ASCII names get a -<8 hex> FNV-1a suffix; see docs/Trips-API.md Client notes and the shared fixture); GET /trips/{id}/offline-pack may answer 404 offline_pack_disabled; place visited_at is a never-cleared first-visit marker, use visited; extra field-level 422 codes are listed in Trips-API.md.
  • docs_homepage/index.html still says "Travel Planner".

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
• No per-user trip cap on POST /trips (final review M3). Rows can each hold a 256 KB snapshot.
  • Stress-test progress (M5): use resolve_today, do not award smart_planner on the first ever score, make previous-score read/write atomic.
  • Recap complete (M6) and check-in: the claim commits before add_countries/award; a crash between loses them with no retry.
  • Check-in accepts a day of UTC +/-1 so "tomorrow" feeds the streak (M11); countries/recap are self-claimed via editable dates.
  • /trips/stats and list_trips run prep_summary per plan (N+1); pick_pinned counts manual-phase trips; POST /trips returns a generic 422 for a bad title instead of trip_title_invalid; a plan rename via PUT clears the trip title (undocumented).
  • request.json() is read before the 256 KB check in the snapshot/offline routes (Caddy bounds it at 32 MB) (M1). GET offline-pack writes (prep tick, award); documented only here (M13).
  • Expenses: concurrent patch edge cases; \d accepts Unicode digits; JSON-number amounts get a generic 422; usd/category rounding differs by a cent.
  • _currency is null without a rate; snapshot body read fully before the size check; a null snapshot value passes validation.
  • Check-in: an award hook failure after insert is never retried; GET /checkins always returns streak: null.
  • Phrases: Simplified Chinese only (Taiwan wants Traditional); country-map judgement calls BE/SK/BA/ME/RS/MO; is/tl/pt thank-you wording.
  • Test hygiene: several tests have no RED record; stub-era seam tests; trip tables' idempotency test does not assert columns; add_countries does not validate country codes.

docs.title: Web: offline, auth, i18n
docs.text:
• Overlapping SW precache runs can leave no served shell; the 2 MB sw-assets cap silently drops files (add a build guard that the entry chunk is listed); a lazy chunk first needed offline after a deploy fails (M10).
  • Outbox treats 409 as sent, so offline writes that hit journal_limit/expense_limit/places_limit vanish silently (M8). A 5xx from /auth/me signs the user out (M9). Device residue after a non-revoked 401 (packs, outbox, tp_exp_pending:*, tp_quiz_*, tp_tour_done:* stay) (M7). Web Locks two-tab test missing.
  • sizeKb uses string length; telemetry unsupported / open kb 0 semantics; PhaseMenu focus return; offline manual phase lost (pack has no phase).
  • i18n: lazy-namespace gate loads even when it renders nothing; skeleton lacks an accessible name; PREFETCH_PATHS is broader than /account,/admin; the lazy list is written three times; branding test greps English only; fr/de buttons over 1.6x English length for "Enregistrer", "Überspringen", tab "Vorbereitung".

docs.title: Web: journey UI
docs.text:
• Trips hub: ring goal 0, multi-city "Day N" city, no focus trap/Escape mid-save, d.trips without ?., failed refetch flips hasTrips true to false, useHasTrips does not refresh after the first trip is saved mid-session, config-loading flash of Search at /.
  • Prep: concurrent toggle rollback restores a whole snapshot; 409 does not reload; stale data on trip.id change; global .confetti selector; overdue amber on na rows.
  • Today: directions query is name-only (no city); click emits next_up not directions; "Next up" still shows a slot already marked Visited; missing dates show a dash.
  • Expenses: category chips lack arrow keys; generic saveFailed for all server errors; a synced row can linger; formError/failed/savingRef/busy leak across a trip switch; the queue test passes without the fix.
  • Journal: queued entry without created_at sorts first in its day; double-failure stale rollback.
  • Recap: invented departure_date today+45 for Discover; RecapMap dark border; over-budget is colour-only; repeat-completion test hits the mock; no trip-change guard on finish/share.
  • Near me "I'm here": telemetry fires before save succeeds; a name over 120 chars fails with a generic error; visited set not reset on trip change; no offline/failure tests; uses the rounded user location as lat/lng (ruling R35); hidden for Maps-grounded items (R41) so visits cannot be marked on v2 results.
  • Results/Chat integration: savedTripId clear untested; the stricter searchMatchesPlan skips the snapshot for legacy plans without origin; chat notifies trips changed before the snapshot PUT lands.
  • Onboarding/coach/play: opening /onboarding directly does not mark it seen; seen flag not per user; passport saved on Skip; home airport is device-only and unread (wire into Explore origin prefill); JourneyCoach does an extra GET /account; /game/me fetched twice; stats failure hides sections silently; goal save bypasses the settings context.
  • Explore/tabs: scrollIntoView may scroll the page; no active-tab-scroll test; prefill effect runs with the flag off; duplicate tour anchors; skeleton copy on /play,/you.
  • Theme: gray-400 on dark gray-100 chips is 4.26:1 (below AA); gray-400 and gray-500 collapse in dark; BestValuePackage pairs bg-teal-700 with border-teal-600; the E2E covered only part of the light/dark x 375/1280 grid in English.
  • Completeness: nights default 1 makes 1 day = 100%; no layout-moved-slot test.

docs.title: Process notes
docs.text: • Before the journey flipped on for everyone, E2E walked all 8 journey steps; mixed-version checks of the old SPA against the new backend were done by API calls, not in the old SPA's UI.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Journey redesign (web) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Turn the web app from "a search that produces a plan" into a companion for the whole trip. It gets a Trips hub with every saved plan as a trip in its phase (Dreaming → Planning → Ready → On the road → Memories), a phase-aware trip screen (prep checklist, Today, offline pack, expenses, journal and ratings, recap), the journey tabs (Trips / Explore / Alerts / Play / You), the shared 5-step onboarding, and the Phase 2 gamified touches of spec §5a. Every existing saved plan becomes a trip with no data loss.

Architecture: A trip is a saved plan. plans gains nullable title, phase (a manual override), start_date, end_date and recap_completed_at, and seven new tables hang off it (trip_expenses, trip_journal, trip_ratings, trip_prep, trip_snapshots, trip_checkins, user_countries). One wave-0 task freezes the schema and another freezes every backend seam: settings, router stubs, the ownership helper, game hooks and the prep/money/phrases stubs. A third freezes every frontend seam: the API module, the journey flag, routes, nav, stubs and the shared journey namespace. The Trips API is published in docs/Trips-API.md at the end of wave 0 for the iOS and Android apps. The phase is computed server-side from the dates by one pure function, mirrored in JS and pinned by shared golden cases. The offline pack is a small hand-written service worker plus IndexedDB, so it needs no new dependency and no CSP or Caddy change. The new UI stays hidden behind features.journey until the last task switches it on.

Tech Stack: FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib sqlite3, JSON1), pydantic v2; React 18 + react-router 6, i18next, Leaflet (existing), IndexedDB and Service Worker APIs (no new npm or pip dependency), vitest, pytest.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-voyager-reimagined-design.md: §3 journey tabs and phases, §3a trip data model, §5a gamification, §9 onboarding, §11 Phase 2 row. Style model: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-11-phase1-accounts-game.md. Folded-in follow-ups: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-11-phase0-followups.md and 2026-11-11-phase1-followups.md (Tasks 29–34).

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Two-way compatibility (CLAUDE.md). The new backend keeps serving the previous SPA and the Android app in the field. GET/POST /api/plans, GET/PUT/DELETE /api/plans/{id}, the share routes and GET /api/share/{token} keep every request field and response key. New plan columns appear as extra keys, which old clients ignore. The new SPA works against the previous backend: when /api/config has no features.trips, the journey UI, the service worker and every trips call stay off, and the app is exactly today's.
  • Ship-alone merges. The journey UI renders only when features.journey is true (JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED, default false until Task 42). It can also be turned on for one browser with localStorage.tp_journey = "1", but only when features.trips is true. While the flag is off, /, /chat, /nearby, /alerts, /preferences, /account and /admin render as today.
  • Contract freeze. The "API contract" section below is frozen when wave 0 merges. Changing it later needs a contract-change note in the PR and an update to docs/Trips-API.md in the same PR.
  • Additive schema only. ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN and CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, nothing renamed or dropped. The date backfill of existing plans runs exactly once (marker meta.trips_backfill_v1).
  • Existing plans migrate. Every row in plans is a trip. Its dates are its columns, else search_data.departure_date/return_date. DELETE /api/plans/{id} (old SPA) also deletes the trip's child rows.
  • Honesty rules stay. Rates and prices in the pack, expenses and recap are labelled with their date and source ("rate from 12 Nov, approximate"). An estimate never awards points. The static-first data stays: the pack uses static emergency numbers when no AI snapshot exists, labelled source: "static".
  • Game guardrails (§5a). Awards come only from server-observed events (plan saved, prep complete, check-in, place visited, recap completed, traveller type set, stress-test score improved), never from telemetry or client claims. Each award has an idempotency key and a daily cap. There are no points for volume, hide_game hides every game element, and the game never gates a feature. Point values live in backend/app/game/rules.json.
  • i18n. Every new user-visible string is in all 7 languages (en es de fr hi zh bn). Each frontend task owns one namespace, named in the task. The only edits to existing namespaces are the ones named in a task: errors (Task 4), game (Task 15), onboarding (Task 26, which adds keys and never renames any, because the mobile apps read them), and chat.title (Task 31). Use informal es/de and vous in fr. Never translate "Voyager". Dates, numbers and currency go through i18n/format.js.
  • Telemetry. Phase 2 events are added once to the closed registry (Task 3). Props are enums, ints and bools only: never an amount, a journal text, a place name or a trip title.
  • Offline storage is per user. IndexedDB records are keyed "<user_id>:<trip_id>". Sign-out (and session_revoked) deletes that user's packs and outbox. The service worker never caches /api/*.
  • CSP and deploy. Production CSP stays script-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:. The service worker is /sw.js from frontend/public/, served by the existing no-cache SPA handle. No Caddyfile change, so a deploy never recreates Caddy.
  • Accessibility. Every interactive element gets a data-tid. Animations (confetti, passport stamp, reveal) are CSS-only, and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns them off. Tap targets are at least 44 px on phones.
  • New primary buttons use bg-teal-700 hover:bg-teal-800 text-white (5.47:1). Task 38 sweeps the old bg-teal-600 buttons.
  • Python 3.12, ruff check backend/ clean; cd frontend && npx eslint src/ --max-warnings 0; mkdocs build --strict; cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q, cd frontend && npm test and python3 -m pytest -q deploy/gcp/tests keep passing.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Opening the app offline. In airplane mode, a reload of /trips/12/offline must show the saved pack, not the login page. Today AuthContext drops the token on any /auth/me failure, a network error included. Expected: a network error keeps the token and the cached user and marks the app offline. A real 401 still signs out. The service worker serves the cached shell. Tests in Task 21 (keeps the session when /auth/me fails offline, navigation falls back to the cached shell).
  2. Day boundaries across time zones. A traveller in Tokyo opens Today at 07:00 on day 1 while UTC is still the day before. They expect "Day 1", a working check-in and the trip in On the road. The client sends its local date (today=), and the server accepts it within ±1 day of the UTC date. Tests in Task 6 (golden case tokyo_morning_day1) and Task 14 (test_checkin_accepts_client_day_ahead_of_utc).
  3. Mixed versions and legacy plans. The old SPA on the new backend must list, load, update and delete plans as before, including a Dreaming trip created by the new SPA (minimal search_data, empty selections). The new SPA on the old backend shows no journey UI and registers no service worker. Tests in Task 7 (test_get_plans_keeps_legacy_keys, test_dreaming_trip_loads_in_old_drawer_shape, test_delete_plan_cascades) and Task 4 (old backend keeps the classic shell).
  4. Offline writes sent twice. An expense or journal entry added offline is retried after reconnecting, possibly from two tabs. Exactly one row must result. Every write carries a client_id with UNIQUE(plan_id, client_id), and a repeat answers 200 with the existing row. The outbox flush is single-flight. Tests in Task 9 (test_same_client_id_twice_one_row), Task 10 (journal equivalent) and Task 21 (concurrent flushes send each item once).
  5. Odd dates and partial data. Odd inputs must degrade to a sensible state with no crash: a plan with no dates, a return_date before departure_date, a multi-city plan with destination_nights, an itinerary whose slots lack coordinates, selections missing keys, or a trip of more than 365 days. Expected states: Dreaming, a single-day trip, the right city for each day, a recap with a null distance, and 422 trip_dates_invalid on edits. Tests in Task 6 (golden cases), Task 13 (test_no_coordinates_distance_null) and Task 20 (renders without itinerary).

docs.title: API contract (frozen at the end of wave 0)
docs.text:
All paths are under /api, with JSON in and out. Every route needs Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and acts only on the caller's own trips: anybody else's trip answers 404 trip_not_found. Errors use the Phase 1 envelope {"detail", "error_code", …}, malformed bodies keep FastAPI's 422 {"detail": [...]}, and timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with Z. Days are YYYY-MM-DD.

today: every GET below and the check-in accept an optional client local date. The server uses it when it is within ±1 day of the server's UTC date, and otherwise uses the UTC date. Clients send the device's local date.

docs.title: Discovery (additive)
docs.text: GET /config gains features.trips: true (the trips API exists), features.journey: bool (JOURNEY_UI_ENABLED) and features.offline_pack: bool (OFFLINE_PACK_ENABLED, default true). When offline_pack is false, clients unregister the service worker and delete every offline cache and pack.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
phase ∈ dreaming | planning | ready | on_the_road | memories. The effective phase, for start s, end e (e = s when missing), override o, today t, prep complete p and READY_WINDOW_DAYS = 14:

  1. o set → o.
  2. s missing → dreaming.
  3. t > e → memories.
  4. s ≤ t ≤ e → on_the_road.
  5. p or (s − t) ≤ 14 days → ready.
  6. otherwise → planning.

day_index = (t − s) + 1 while on the road, else null. days_to_start = s − t when t < s, else null. Golden cases live in backend/tests/fixtures/journey/trip_phase_cases.json, and every client must pass them.

docs.title: Shared objects
docs.text:
Trip:

{"id": 12, "title": "Lisbon in spring", "destination": "Lisbon", "destinations": ["Lisbon", "Porto"],
 "origin": "NYC", "start_date": "2027-04-01", "end_date": "2027-04-08", "nights": 7,
 "phase": "planning", "phase_source": "auto", "days_to_start": 140, "day_index": null,
 "num_travelers": 2, "budget_usd": 3000, "countries": ["PT"],
 "prep": {"done": 3, "total": 9, "percent": 33, "complete": false},
 "has_itinerary": true, "recap_completed_at": null, "created_at": "…Z", "updated_at": "…Z"}
  • title is plans.title, falling back to plans.name.
  • destinations is search_data.destinations, else [destination], else [].
  • phase_source is auto|manual. nights = end − start in days, or null.
  • countries holds ISO alpha-2 codes, resolved locally (no network).
  • prep comes from the prep rules below. For a Dreaming trip it is {"done": 0, "total": 0, "percent": 0, "complete": false}.

GameDelta: exactly as in docs/Accounts-API.md. It is null when the game is disabled.

Place key: <kind>:<slug>. kind ∈ activity|place|food|hotel|event|tour|nearby|other. slug = the name NFKD-normalised, combining marks removed, lower-cased, every run of non-[a-z0-9] replaced by -, trimmed of -, and cut to 60 characters ("" → "x"). The server accepts ^[a-z]+:[a-z0-9-]{1,60}$. The vectors are in backend/tests/fixtures/journey/place_key_cases.json (for example ["activity", "Pastéis de Belém!"] → "activity:pasteis-de-belem").

docs.title: Trips
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips query today? {"trips": [Trip], "pinned_id": 12 \| null, "today": "2026-11-12"}. Sorted by phase (on_the_road, ready, planning, dreaming, memories), then start_date (memories: newest first), then updated_at desc. At most 200 — POST /trips {"title": 1..80, "destination"?: ≤120, "start_date"?, "end_date"?} 201 Trip. Creates a plans row: name = title, search_data = {"destination": d} (or {}), selections = {} 422 trip_dates_invalid, 422 trip_title_invalid GET /trips/{id} query today? Trip 404 trip_not_found PATCH /trips/{id} any subset of {"title", "start_date", "end_date", "phase"}. A null date clears it, and "phase": null clears the override Trip 422 trip_dates_invalid (end < start, span > 365 days, or a year outside 2000–2100), 422 trip_phase_invalid, 422 trip_title_invalid, 404 DELETE /trips/{id} — 204. Deletes the plan and every child row (the same as DELETE /plans/{id}) 404 GET /trips/stats — {"countries": [{"code": "PT", "name": "Portugal", "first_trip_id": 12, "visited_at": "…Z", "source": "checkin"\|"recap"}], "continents": ["EU"], "bucket_goal": 30 \| null, "trips_by_phase": {"dreaming": 1, …}} —

pinned_id is the on-the-road trip with the earliest start, else the trip with the smallest days_to_start, else the memories trip with an end_date in the last 14 days and no recap_completed_at, else null. The POST /plans handler stores start_date/end_date from search_data, so plans saved by any client become dated trips.

docs.title: Prep checklist
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/prep query today? {"items": [PrepItem], "done", "total", "percent", "complete"} 404 PUT /trips/{id}/prep/{item_id} {"done": bool} the same object plus "item": PrepItem, "game": GameDelta \| null 404 prep_item_unknown, 409 prep_item_auto (offline_pack), 409 prep_item_na

PrepItem: {"id", "status": "todo"|"done"|"na", "auto": bool, "due": "YYYY-MM-DD"|null, "overdue": bool, "facts": {…}}. total counts the items that are not na, percent = floor(100 × done / total) (0 when total is 0), and complete = total > 0 and done == total. Items, in order, with due relative to the start (null without a start):

id na when due facts visa the visa row says visa-free start − (visa lead days, or 21) visa_type, max_stay_days, processing_time, official_url, source (ai from the snapshot, else static, else null) passport — start − 30 — bookings — start − 30 flight: bool, hotel: bool (selected in the plan) insurance — start − 14 — documents — start − 7 — stress_test no itinerary start − 7 score: int \| null (the last score, Task 37) sim — start − 3 plan_name \| null money — start − 3 currency \| null (the local currency code) packing — start − 1 items: int emergency_card — start − 1 — checkin no flight selected start − 1 — offline_pack (auto) — start − 1 saved_at \| null

Visa lead days: none for visa-free. Otherwise take the largest number in processing_time: weeks × 7, business days × 1.4 rounded up, days as is. Add 7 days of buffer. When there is no number, use 21. When complete first becomes true, the trip's trip_ready award is made (once per trip).

docs.title: Snapshot and offline pack
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors PUT /trips/{id}/snapshot {"emergency_card"?, "forex"?, "visa"?, "packing_list"?, "weather"?}: each an object or null; other keys ignored 204. Stores the merged object with as_of = server time 413 snapshot_too_large (> 262144 bytes as JSON), 422 snapshot_invalid GET /trips/{id}/offline-pack query today? OfflinePack with Cache-Control: no-store. Marks prep offline_pack done (Task 37) 404

Clients send the snapshot after every plan save or update made while the results are on screen. Values are the section results as streamed, without verification.

OfflinePack:

{"version": 1, "trip_id": 12, "generated_at": "…Z", "title": "…", "start_date": "…", "end_date": "…",
 "destinations": [{"city": "Lisbon", "country_code": "PT", "country_name": "Portugal"}],
 "emergency": {"source": "ai"|"static"|null, "as_of": "…Z"|null,
   "cities": [{"city": "Lisbon", "emergency_numbers": {…}, "embassy": {…}|null, "hospitals": [], "local_phrases": []}]},
 "phrases": {"language": "pt", "language_name": "Português", "items": [{"id": "help", "text": "Socorro!", "romanized": null}]} | null,
 "address_card": {"hotel_name": "…", "area": "…"|null, "city": "Lisbon",
   "take_me_to": {"text": "…", "romanized": null}|null} | null,
 "currency": {"local": "EUR", "home": "USD", "rate": 0.92, "as_of": "…Z", "source": "snapshot"} | {"local": "EUR", "home": "USD", "rate": null, "as_of": null, "source": null} | null,
 "selections": {"itinerary", "itinerary_layout", "itinerary_edits", "itinerary_notes", "itinerary_slots", "hotel", "flight", "sim", "packing_list"},
 "checkins": ["2027-04-01"]}
  • rate is local units per 1 home unit.
  • home is USD unless the snapshot's forex has a rate from the traveller's home currency.
  • phrase ids: help, call_police, need_doctor, take_me_to, thank_you, how_much, where_toilet, dont_understand.
  • phrases is null for English-speaking countries.

docs.title: Expenses
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/expenses — {"expenses": [Expense], "totals": {"by_currency": {"EUR": "123.40"}, "usd_estimate": "140.20" \| null, "by_category_usd": {"food": "40.00"}, "unconverted": ["GBP"]}, "rate": {"local": "EUR", "usd_to_local": 0.92, "as_of": "…Z"} \| null} 404 POST /trips/{id}/expenses {"client_id": uuid, "amount": "12.50", "currency": "EUR", "category", "note"?: ≤140, "spent_on": day} 201 Expense, or 200 Expense (the existing row) when client_id was already used on this trip 422 amount_invalid, 422 currency_invalid, 422 category_invalid, 422 note_too_long, 409 expense_limit (2000 per trip) PATCH /trips/{id}/expenses/{eid} a subset of amount, currency, category, note, spent_on Expense the above, 404 expense_not_found DELETE /trips/{id}/expenses/{eid} — 204 404 expense_not_found

Expense: {"id", "client_id", "amount": "12.50", "currency": "EUR", "category", "note", "spent_on", "created_at", "updated_at"}. category ∈ flights|lodging|food|transport|activities|shopping|fees|other. Amounts are decimal strings stored as integer minor units, with the currency's exponent: 0 for JPY KRW VND CLP ISK UGX XAF XOF, 3 for BHD KWD OMR JOD TND, else 2. The rules are 0 < amount ≤ 1,000,000 and no more decimals than the exponent allows. USD estimates use only USD rows and rows in the snapshot's local currency (amount / usd_to_local). Every other currency is listed in unconverted.

docs.title: Journal and places (ratings, visits)
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/journal — {"entries": [Entry]}, sorted by day (nulls last), then created_at 404 POST /trips/{id}/journal {"client_id": uuid, "body": 1..4000, "day"?, "mood"?: "great"\|"good"\|"ok"\|"tough"} 201 Entry, or 200 on a repeated client_id 422 journal_empty, 422 journal_too_long, 422 mood_invalid, 409 journal_limit (500) PATCH /trips/{id}/journal/{eid} a subset of body, day, mood Entry the above, 404 entry_not_found DELETE /trips/{id}/journal/{eid} — 204 404 entry_not_found GET /trips/{id}/places — {"places": [TripPlace]} 404 PUT /trips/{id}/places/{place_key} {"name": 1..120, "kind", "visited"?: bool, "stars"?: 1..5 \| null, "note"?: ≤500, "day"?, "lat"?, "lng"?} (upsert; omitted fields are kept) {"place": TripPlace, "game": GameDelta \| null}. game is set when visited first becomes true 422 place_key_invalid, 422 stars_invalid, 422 note_too_long, 409 places_limit (1000) DELETE /trips/{id}/places/{place_key} — 204 404 place_not_found

Entry: {"id", "client_id", "day", "body", "mood", "created_at", "updated_at"}. TripPlace: {"place_key", "name", "kind", "visited", "stars", "note", "day", "lat", "lng", "visited_at", "updated_at"}.

docs.title: Today
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors POST /trips/{id}/checkin {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD"} 200 {"day", "day_index", "city", "country_code", "new_country": bool, "streak": {"current", "longest", "last_day", "freezes"} \| null, "game": GameDelta \| null}. A second call for the same day returns the same data with an empty delta 409 checkin_out_of_trip (day outside [start, end]), 422 checkin_day_invalid (more than 1 day from the server's UTC date) GET /trips/{id}/checkins — {"days": ["2027-04-01"], "streak": … \| null} 404

The city for day n follows the multi-city allocation of TravelSearchRequest.city_stays (destination_nights honoured), else destination.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /trips/{id}/recap query today? Recap 404 POST /trips/{id}/recap/complete query today? {"completed_at", "new_countries": ["PT"], "game": GameDelta \| null}. Idempotent: a repeat returns the first completed_at, new_countries: [] and an empty delta 409 recap_not_ready (today ≤ end date, or no dates)

Recap:

{"trip_id": 12, "title": "…", "start_date": "…", "end_date": "…", "days": 8, "nights": 7, "planned_days": 7,
 "places": [TripPlace], "visited_count": 9, "rated_count": 7, "avg_stars": 4.3,
 "route": [[38.70, -9.14]], "distance_km": 41.2,
 "countries": [{"code": "PT", "name": "Portugal", "new": true}], "continents": ["EU"],
 "spend": {"budget_usd": 3000, "plan_cost_usd": null, "spent_usd": "2140.50", "by_category_usd": {…}, "unconverted": ["GBP"]},
 "journal_count": 5, "checkin_days": 6, "completed_at": null, "can_complete": true}
  • route holds the visited places with coordinates, ordered by day then visited_at (at most 500 points).
  • distance_km is the haversine sum along route, to one decimal, or null with fewer than two points. Clients that have the itinerary may draw the planned route when route is empty.
  • new means the country was added to user_countries by this trip.
  • plan_cost_usd is null on the server (clients compute it with computePlanCost).

docs.title: Game (additive rules and badges)
docs.text:
These are new rule ids in GET /game/catalog. Clients translate them as game:rules.<id> and game:badges.<id>.name|desc.

rule points daily cap idempotency key traveller_type 25 1 once per user plan_saved 10 3 plan_saved:<plan_id> trip_ready 50 2 trip_ready:<plan_id> smart_planner 15 3 smart_planner:<plan_id>:<score> trip_checkin 10 1 trip_checkin:<plan_id>:<day> place_visited 5 10 place_visited:<plan_id>:<place_key> country_visited 25 5 country_visited:<user_id>:<code> continent_visited 50 3 continent_visited:<user_id>:<continent> recap_complete 100 2 recap_complete:<plan_id>

Badges (id (rule, target, tier, icon)): - traveller (traveller_type, 1, bronze, compass) - first_trip (plan_saved, 1, bronze, map) - trip_ready (trip_ready, 1, bronze, circle-check) and ready_regular (trip_ready, 5, silver, badge-check) - smart_planner (smart_planner, 3, bronze, brain) - on_the_road (trip_checkin, 3, bronze, calendar-check) and road_warrior (trip_checkin, 14, silver, calendar-range) - local_explorer (place_visited, 10, bronze, map-pin) and local_legend (place_visited, 50, silver, map-pinned) - countries_3 (country_visited, 3, bronze, stamp), countries_10 (country_visited, 10, silver, globe) and countries_30 (country_visited, 30, gold, earth) - continents_3 (continent_visited, 3, silver, earth) and continents_6 (continent_visited, 6, gold, globe-2) - storyteller (recap_complete, 1, bronze, book-open) and memory_keeper (recap_complete, 5, silver, library)

New streak kind trip_checkin (freeze_per_week: 1). Settings gains bucket_list_goal: int 1..250 | null (default null). PUT /account/onboarding with traveller_type awards traveller_type once.

docs.title: Stress test (additive)
docs.text: POST /stress-test accepts an optional plan_id. When the caller is signed in and owns the plan, the server stores the returned score as the prep stress_test fact and marks that item done. When the score is higher than the previous one, it awards smart_planner. The response is unchanged.

docs.title: Shared-file hotspots and how conflicts are avoided

docs.title: Task 2: Schema, one-time migration and shared row helpers
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/db/trips_schema.py, backend/app/db/trip_children.py, backend/app/db/user_countries_db.py, backend/app/db/trip_snapshot_db.py - Test: backend/tests/test_trips_schema.py

Interfaces: - Produces: - create_trip_tables() -> None. It is idempotent. - It adds the plans columns that are missing: title TEXT, phase TEXT, start_date TEXT, end_date TEXT and recap_completed_at TEXT. - It creates these tables: - trip_expenses(id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL, client_id TEXT NOT NULL, amount_minor INTEGER NOT NULL, currency TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, note TEXT, spent_on TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(plan_id, client_id)) - trip_journal(id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL, client_id TEXT NOT NULL, day TEXT, body TEXT NOT NULL, mood TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(plan_id, client_id)) - trip_ratings(plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL, place_key TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, visited INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, stars INTEGER, note TEXT, day TEXT, lat REAL, lng REAL, visited_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(plan_id, place_key)) - trip_prep(plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL, item_id TEXT NOT NULL, done_at TEXT, meta TEXT, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(plan_id, item_id)) - trip_snapshots(plan_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, data TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL) - trip_checkins(plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL, day TEXT NOT NULL, city TEXT, country_code TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(plan_id, day)) - user_countries(user_id TEXT NOT NULL, country_code TEXT NOT NULL, first_plan_id INTEGER, source TEXT NOT NULL, visited_at TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(user_id, country_code)) - It adds an index on plan_id for trip_expenses and trip_journal. - Backfill: when meta has no trips_backfill_v1, it sets start_date/end_date from json_extract(search_data, '$.departure_date' | '$.return_date'), but only where the column is NULL, json_valid(search_data), and the value matches YYYY-MM-DD. It then writes the marker. All of this runs in one transaction. - TRIP_CHILD_TABLES: tuple[str, ...] (the six plan_id tables) and delete_trip_children(conn, plan_id: int) -> None. - add_countries(user_id: str, codes: list[str], plan_id: int, source: Literal["checkin","recap"]) -> list[str], which returns the newly added codes (INSERT OR IGNORE); list_countries(user_id: str) -> list[dict]. - get_snapshot(plan_id: int) -> dict | None (with as_of); put_snapshot(plan_id: int, data: dict) -> str, which merges into the stored object, so a key sent as null clears it, and returns as_of.

Interfaces: - Produces: - Python: - trip_dates(plan: dict) -> tuple[date | None, date | None]: the columns, else search_data. An end before the start becomes the start. - effective_phase(start, end, override, today, prep_complete, ready_window_days=14) -> str - days_to_start(start, today) -> int | None, day_index(start, end, today) -> int | None - resolve_today(client_today: str | None, now: datetime | None = None) -> date - trip_geo: - trip_cities(search_data: dict) -> list[str] - city_for_day(search_data: dict, start: date, end: date | None, day_index: int) -> str | None (uses allocate_city_days; past the last stay → the last city) - country_of(place: str) -> str | None (resolve_place, lru_cache(2048)) - trip_countries(search_data: dict) -> list[str] (ordered and unique) - continent_of(code: str) -> str | None - JS: effectivePhase({start, end, override, today, prepComplete, readyWindowDays = 14}) -> string, dayIndex(start, end, today) -> number | null, daysToStart(start, today) -> number | null, localToday(now = new Date()) -> 'YYYY-MM-DD' (local calendar date). - The fixture is a list of {"name", "start", "end", "override", "today", "prep_complete", "phase", "day_index", "days_to_start"} with at least 20 cases. Required names: no_dates_dreaming, end_before_start_single_day, day_before_start_ready_window, fifteen_days_out_planning, prep_complete_far_out_ready, first_day_on_the_road, last_day_on_the_road, day_after_end_memories, override_wins, tokyo_morning_day1 (client today one day ahead of UTC), no_end_date.

docs.title: Task 21: Offline infrastructure (namespace offline)
docs.text:
Decision: a hand-written service worker plus IndexedDB, with no Workbox and no new dependency. - /sw.js is same-origin, so script-src 'self' and worker-src 'self' already allow it. - The existing Caddy SPA handle serves it with Cache-Control: no-cache. - The worker caches only the app shell and the hashed /assets/*. Pack data lives in IndexedDB. - Navigations go network-first, so a deploy shows up whenever the user is online. - It is registered only when the user saves a pack (never at app start), and features.offline_pack: false unregisters it everywhere.

Files: - Create: frontend/public/sw.js, frontend/vite/swAssets.js, frontend/src/offline/{registerSW,packStore,outbox,idb}.js, frontend/src/offline/useOfflinePack.js, frontend/src/offline/useOnline.js, frontend/src/i18n/locales/<lang>/offline.json, deploy/gcp/tests/test_caddyfile_spa.py - Modify: frontend/vite.config.js (adds swAssetsPlugin({version: appVersion})), frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx, frontend/src/components/offline/OfflineBanner.jsx - Test: frontend/src/offline/sw.test.js (loads public/sw.js into a node:vm context with fake self, caches and fetch), frontend/src/offline/{packStore,outbox,registerSW}.test.js (fake-indexeddb is not added; idb.js falls back to an in-memory map that the tests use), frontend/vite/swAssets.test.js, frontend/src/context/AuthContext.offline.test.jsx

Interfaces: - Produces: - swAssetsPlugin({version}) -> VitePlugin. It emits sw-assets.json = {"version", "shell": ["/", "/index.html", "/theme-init.js", "/favicon.svg", "/manifest.webmanifest"], "assets": ["/assets/…"]}. The list holds every emitted .js/.css chunk and every locale chunk, with no .map files and no file over 2 MB. - sw.js: - On the precache message, it fetches /sw-assets.json (no-store), caches every URL into voyager-shell-<version>, deletes the other voyager-shell-* caches and replies {ok, bytes}. - Navigation requests: network first; on failure, the cached /index.html. - /assets/*: cache first, then network. - Everything else, /api/* included, is not intercepted. - The purge message deletes every voyager-* cache. - registerSW.js: ensureServiceWorker() -> Promise<ServiceWorkerRegistration | null> (null when unsupported, not a secure context, or import.meta.env.DEV), precacheShell() -> Promise<{ok: boolean, kb: number}> and disableOffline() -> Promise<void> (purge plus unregister). - packStore.js: savePack(userId, pack), getPack(userId, tripId), listPacks(userId), deletePack(userId, tripId), clearUser(userId), storageMode() -> 'idb' | 'memory'. - outbox.js: - enqueue(userId, {method, path, body, key}) (a repeated key replaces the entry); - flush(token, userId, fetchImpl = fetch) -> Promise<{sent, failed, dropped}>: single-flight; 2xx and 409 are sent; other 4xx except 408/429 are dropped; 5xx and network errors are kept; - pending(userId) -> Promise<number>; - startAutoFlush(getToken, getUserId) -> stop (on online and every 60 s while items are queued). It emits outbox_flush. - useOnline() -> boolean; useOfflinePack(userId, tripId) -> {pack, savedAt, loading}. - AuthContext: - When /auth/me rejects (a network error), it keeps the token, restores the user from tp_user_cache ({id, username, display_name, is_admin}, written on every successful load) and exposes offline: true. It revalidates on online. HTTP 401/403 behave as today. - logout() and session_revoked call clearUser(user.id) and outbox clearing for that user, and remove tp_user_cache. - When /config says features.offline_pack === false, it calls disableOffline() once. - OfflineBanner: "You're offline. Saved trips still work." Plus "{{count}} changes waiting to sync" from pending. - test_caddyfile_spa.py: the CSP contains script-src 'self' and worker-src 'self' blob:; /sw.js does not match the @asset immutable matcher; the SPA handle sets Cache-Control "no-cache".

  • [ ] Step 1: Write failing tests:
  • navigation falls back to the cached shell; /api/trips is not intercepted; /assets/a.js is served from the cache; precache deletes the old version caches;
  • the plugin lists the chunks and skips maps;
  • keeps the session when /auth/me fails offline; a 401 still signs out; logout clears that user's packs and outbox but not another user's;
  • concurrent flushes send each item once; a 5xx is kept, a 400 is dropped, a 409 counts as sent;
  • offline_pack false → disableOffline is called;
  • the Caddyfile test.
  • [ ] Step 2: Run cd frontend && npm test -- src/offline vite src/context and python3 -m pytest -q deploy/gcp/tests/test_caddyfile_spa.py → FAIL.
  • [ ] Step 3: Implement; translate. Step 4: Run both, plus npm run build (dist/sw.js and dist/sw-assets.json exist) → PASS.
  • [ ] Step 5: Commit feat(offline): service worker shell, IndexedDB packs, outbox and offline-safe session

docs.title: Execution waves
docs.text:
Each wave starts when the previous one has merged to main. Inside a wave every task runs in its own worktree in parallel, because the tasks own disjoint files (see the hotspot table).

Wave Tasks (parallel) Count Gate 0 — seams and contract 1 backend seams · 2 schema + migration · 3 telemetry · 4 frontend seams · 5 contract doc · 6 phase/geo helpers + golden cases 6 Task 1's last step rebases on Task 2. When wave 0 merges, the contract is frozen and the iOS/Android teams start against docs/Trips-API.md 1 — modules backend: 7 trips core · 8 prep · 9 expenses · 10 journal + places · 11 offline pack · 12 phrases · 13 recap · 14 check-in · 15 game rules + hooks; frontend: 16 hub · 17 trip screen · 18 completeness · 19 prep UI · 20 Today · 21 offline infra · 22 pack UI · 23 expenses UI · 24 journal UI · 25 recap UI · 26 onboarding · 27 coach marks · 28 Play/You · 29 Explore + tabs; follow-ups: 30 dark contrast · 31 naming · 32 feedback pill · 33 lazy English 27 Backend tasks need only wave 0, through the stubs. Tasks 11 and 13 import Task 9/10 helpers inside functions, so their merge order doesn't matter. Frontend tasks need only Task 4, with the API mocked. Tasks 17, 20, 22, 23 and 24 import Task 21's offline modules: merge 21 first inside the wave, or guard the imports per the task 2 — integration 34 Results · 35 Chat · 36 Near me · 37 backend joins 4 34 needs 18; 35 needs 34's tripSnapshot.js (start it once 34's util is pushed, or merge 34 first); 37 needs 8 and 11 3 — finish 38 teal sweep → then 39 docs ∥ 40 translation review (one agent per language) → 41 E2E + reviews → 42 switch on 5 (+6 reviewers) 38 runs alone first (it touches 25 files). 42 merges only after 41 is green

Merge cadence: a PR per task, or one per wave. Each PR is green and deployable on its own. The wave 1 backend routes have no UI pointing at them, the UI is invisible until features.journey is on, and the service worker registers only when a user saves a pack, which they can't do until the journey UI is visible. Task 42 is a one-line config change that the owner can revert in app.env.

docs.title: Owner-question rulings (main controller, 2026-11-12)
docs.text:
The owner delegated these decisions. They bind the tasks.

  1. Onboarding for existing users: existing users see the new onboarding once. It can be skipped, and a skip counts as seen.
  2. Home route: / shows the Trips hub to a signed-in user who has at least one trip. Everyone else, including signed-out visitors, keeps the Search page. Both remain reachable from the tabs.
  3. Rollout: the final task switches the journey on for everyone. The product is already in a limited test with selected users.
  4. Native review: a native-speaker review of the hi, bn and zh UI text and of the phrase list goes on the follow-ups list for the owner. Ship the model-reviewed text.
  5. Hotel address: show the hotel name plus a "take me to" phrase in the local language. A local-script address is deferred until the data exists.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Price alerts 2.0 Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make price alerts a delight. Each watch gets a price story: an interactive chart, the lowest price seen, a typical range, a target slider and a plain-language verdict. A real drop becomes a drop moment: an animated card, a "you're saving $X" counter and XP. A savings tally with milestones and a shareable "I saved $X" card sums all watches. Watching gets smarter: one-tap watch on every card, suggestions when a plan is saved, an opt-in weekly digest, quiet hours, per-category caps and grouped pushes. Every honesty rule stays.

Architecture: Everything is additive to the existing fare-watch and price-watch services. One flag-gated seam in each _notify passes new notifications through services/alert_pipeline.py, which enriches data with drop facts, records savings, awards Deal-hunter XP and hands push and email to a delivery layer (quiet hours, caps, grouping, outbox loop). New read models (story, savings, suggestions) are pure functions over the stored rows and history, so they need no SerpAPI call and work in production, where there is no key. One-tap watches are created pending (no live look). The scheduler makes their first look, in priority order (nearest departure, closest to target), with adaptive intervals. New routes live under /api/alerts/*. They are frozen in docs/Alerts-API.md at the end of wave 0 for the iOS and Android apps. The UI stays hidden behind features.price_alerts_v2 until the last task.

Tech Stack: FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib sqlite3), pydantic v2, zoneinfo; React 18, i18next, inline SVG charts, Canvas 2D for the share card, the Web Share API (no new npm or pip dependency), vitest, pytest.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-voyager-reimagined-design.md: §6 price alerts, §5a "Price alerts" row (Deal hunter, $50/$200/$1,000 milestones, target-hit celebration, estimates never award), §2a budget (250 SerpAPI searches a month, prioritised watches, adaptive intervals, "checked N days ago"; one-tap watch and suggestions never fire a live search), §8 telemetry, §11 Phase 3 row. Style model: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-12-phase2-journey.md and docs/Trips-API.md. 2026-11-12-phase2-followups.md has no Phase 3-tagged item; its line "Price-alert gamified touches: Phase 3" (Phase 2 Deferred) is Task 5.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Two-way compatibility (CLAUDE.md). Every existing route keeps its request fields, response keys and semantics: /api/fare-watches*, /api/price-watches*, /api/notifications* and the unsubscribe pages. New watch keys (pending_first_check) and new notification data keys (drop, game, digest) are extra keys that old clients ignore. A pending watch has last_price: null, which the old SPA already renders as "Getting price…". The new SPA works against the previous backend: with no features.alerts_api in /config it renders today's Alerts page and no v2 control.
  • Ship-alone merges. The backend v2 behaviour (pipeline, delivery, digest loop, adaptive scheduling) runs only when PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED=true (settings.price_alerts_v2_enabled, default false until Task 22). With the flag off, _notify, email, push and next_check behave byte-for-byte as today. The /api/alerts/* read routes always exist. The web UI renders when features.price_alerts_v2 is true, or for one browser with localStorage.tp_alerts2 = "1" when features.alerts_api === 2.
  • No SerpAPI in production. features.live_prices = bool(settings.serpapi_key). Without a key: the story, savings, digest and suggestions work from stored data. Every price shows "checked N days ago". One-tap watch and the suggestions sheet are hidden. POST /alerts/quick-watch answers 503 live_prices_off. Nothing in the v2 code path may call SerpAPI except the scheduler's existing check functions. Tests, dev and E2E use the fake SerpAPI (Task 3), never the real key.
  • Honesty rules stay. Estimates are labelled and frozen, and they never alert, never count toward savings and never award XP. A "saving" is always the drop between two observed prices, worded "caught a drop of $X", never "you saved" without "if you book now". Currencies are never converted: the USD tally counts only USD watches, and other currencies are listed separately.
  • Anti-spam. The existing evaluate() rules are unchanged: one alert per check, separate own-dates and nearby-dates references, a repeat needs a further step unless a rebound re-armed it, never on the baseline, and the 24 h cooldown. Quiet hours, per-category daily caps and grouping apply only to push and email. The in-app notification row is always written.
  • Additive schema only. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN, nothing renamed or dropped. The new tables join the GCS user-table backup set.
  • Game guardrails (§5a). Awards come only from server-observed alerts with observed prices. Each award has an idempotency key and a daily cap, and point values live in game/rules.json. hide_game hides every Deal-hunter element, and the game never gates a feature.
  • i18n. Every new user-visible string is in all 7 languages (en es de fr hi zh bn). Each frontend task owns one namespace, named in its heading. The only edits to existing namespaces: game (Task 5) and alerts (Task 17, which adds keys and renames none). Use informal es/de and vous in fr, and never translate "Voyager". Amounts, dates and "N days ago" go through i18n/format.js. Advice and verdicts travel as codes plus params, never as English text, and clients translate them. Push, email and digest text stays English, as today, until Phase 6 adds server-side localisation.
  • Telemetry. The Phase 3 events go into the closed registry once (Task 1). Props are enums, ints and bools only, never an amount, a price, a title or a place.
  • Motion and accessibility. Animations (the drop card's count-up, the falling-price motif, confetti on a target hit, chart transitions) are CSS-only or requestAnimationFrame, and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce shows the final state at once. The chart is keyboard-scrubbable (←/→ between points, with an aria-live readout). Every interactive element has a data-tid, tap targets are ≥ 44 px, and primary buttons are bg-teal-700 hover:bg-teal-800 text-white.
  • Python 3.12, ruff check backend/ clean, cd frontend && npx eslint src/ --max-warnings 0, mkdocs build --strict. cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q and cd frontend && npm test keep passing.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. No key, stale data. In production, with no SERPAPI_KEY, a watch last checked 9 days ago must show its story, the "checked 9 days ago" label and the advice checks_paused, never "great price now". No one-tap button and no suggestions sheet appear, and the digest loop doesn't crash. Tests: Task 4 test_story_without_key_says_paused, Task 7 test_quick_watch_503_without_key, Task 10 test_digest_skipped_when_no_looks_this_week, Task 14 hidden when live_prices is false.
  2. Estimates and currencies leak into savings. A trip watch with frozen estimate parts, a hotel watch that holds only an estimate, and a EUR activity drop. docs.title: API contract (frozen at the end of wave 0; published as docs/Alerts-API.md)
docs.text: All paths are under /api, with JSON in and out. Every route needs Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and acts only on the caller's watches: another user's watch answers 404 watch_not_found. Errors use the Phase 1 envelope {"detail", "error_code"}, and timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with Z. kind ∈ flight | hotel | activity | trip. flight means a fare_watches row, and the other kinds are price_watches rows.

docs.title: Discovery (additive)
docs.text: GET /config gains features.alerts_api: 2 (the routes below exist), features.price_alerts_v2: bool (PRICE_ALERTS_V2_ENABLED) and features.live_prices: bool (a SerpAPI key is configured).

docs.title: Shared objects
docs.text:
Money: {"amount": 412.0, "currency": "USD"}.

PriceStory:

{"kind": "flight", "watch_id": 7, "currency": "USD", "mode": "below_target", "target": 380.0,
 "points": [{"at": "…Z", "price": 455.0}], "baseline": 455.0,
 "latest": {"at": "…Z", "price": 412.0}, "lowest": {"at": "…Z", "price": 398.0},
 "typical": {"low": 390.0, "high": 520.0, "source": "google"},
 "verdict": "good", "advice": {"code": "near_target", "params": {"gap": 32.0}},
 "checked_at": "…Z", "checked_days_ago": 0, "next_check_at": "…Z", "pending_first_check": false,
 "estimate": null, "caught": 57.0, "live_prices": true}
  • points: observed prices only, oldest first, at most 90 (the newest).
  • typical: for flights, Google's google_typical_low/high (source: "google"). For other kinds, when there are ≥ 6 points, the nearest-rank p25/p75 of the points (source: "history"). Otherwise null.
  • verdict, for the latest price p and typical [lo, hi]: p < lo → great; p ≤ lo + 0.25 (hi − lo) → good; p ≤ hi → typical; else high. It is null without typical or latest, and null when checked_days_ago > 3 and live_prices is false.
  • estimate: {"price", "source"} for a frozen estimate (labelled "estimate"), else null.
  • caught: the watch's saving as defined under Savings, or null.
  • advice.code: the first rule that matches, in this order:
  • pending — there is no look yet.
  • checks_paused {days} — live_prices is false and checked_days_ago > 3.
  • below_target {by} — latest ≤ target.
  • near_target {gap} — latest − target ≤ the kind's step (price_rules).
  • at_lowest — latest == lowest and ≥ 3 points.
  • below_typical, within_typical or above_typical — the verdict is great/good, typical or high.
  • steady {days} — the last 5 points are within 1 % of each other.
  • few_checks {n} — otherwise.

Golden cases: backend/tests/fixtures/alerts/story_cases.json, shared by every client.

Savings:

{"total_usd": 245.0, "by_currency": {"EUR": 12.0}, "drops_caught": 4, "targets_hit": 1,
 "watches_active": 6, "best": {"kind": "hotel", "watch_id": 3, "title": "…", "caught": 120.0, "currency": "USD"},
 "milestones": [50, 200, 1000], "next_milestone": 1000, "progress_pct": 24, "since": "…Z"}

A watch's caught amount = max(0, baseline − the lowest alerted observed price), taken from alert_savings rows. Watches are summed: USD watches into total_usd, other currencies into by_currency. Nothing is ever converted. progress_pct = floor(100 × total_usd / next_milestone), and next_milestone is null once $1,000 is passed. Deleted watches still count, and since is the first row's time. Golden cases: savings_cases.json.

AlertPrefs:

{"digest_weekly": false, "digest_day": 1, "instant": "all",
 "quiet_hours": {"enabled": true, "start": "22:00", "end": "07:00"},
 "daily_cap": {"flight": 3, "hotel": 3, "activity": 3, "trip": 3}, "group_window_min": 15,
 "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata"}
  • digest_day is an ISO weekday (1 = Monday).
  • instant is all or targets_only. With targets_only, only target hits push or email, and everything else waits for the digest.
  • Caps run from 1 to 10 and group_window_min from 0 to 120.
  • timezone is read-only here, a mirror of the account setting. Without it, quiet hours are not applied (the response says so with "quiet_hours_active": false).

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Method, path Request Success Errors GET /alerts/summary — Savings — GET /alerts/watches/{kind}/{id}/story — PriceStory 404 watch_not_found, 422 kind_invalid POST /alerts/watches/{kind}/{id}/advice — {"tip": "…", "source": "ai", "generated_at": "…Z", "cached": bool}. Uses the pricing-advisor agent with the stored history (no SerpAPI) and is cached 24 h per watch. light_ai bucket and the AI gate apply 422 advice_unsupported (not flight), 503 ai_limit, 404 POST /alerts/quick-watch {"kind", "title": 1..120, "subtitle"?: ≤160, "spec": {…}, "plan_id"?: int, "surface": "results"\|"chat"\|"trip"\|"suggest"}. A flight spec holds the POST /fare-watches trip fields. The other kinds hold their POST /price-watches spec 201 {"kind", "watch": Watch, "existing": false}. The watch is pending: alert_mode: any_drop, email off, no live look, first check queued. A match of an existing active watch answers 200 with "existing": true 503 live_prices_off, 409 watch_limit (the shared active limit, with the existing message), 422 spec_invalid GET /alerts/suggestions?plan_id= — {"suggestions": [{"kind", "title", "subtitle", "spec", "reason": "selected_in_plan"\|"trip_total"\|"departure_soon", "already_watching": bool}], "live_prices": bool}, at most 5, built locally 404 trip_not_found GET /alerts/preferences — AlertPrefs — PUT /alerts/preferences any subset of the writable AlertPrefs keys AlertPrefs 422 alert_prefs_invalid GET /alerts/digest/unsubscribe?token= / POST — HTML page (the same pattern as the watch unsubscribe pages); sets digest_weekly=false —

Watch objects (additive). Every watch from /fare-watches* and /price-watches* gains pending_first_check: bool.

Notifications (additive). - A drop notification's data gains drop: {"from", "to", "amount", "pct", "currency", "target_hit": bool, "observed": true} and game: GameDelta | null. - The new kind price_digest has the usual title/body plus data.digest: {"week": "2026-W46", "watches": [{"kind", "watch_id", "title", "latest", "change_7d", "lowest", "checked_at"}], "savings": Savings}. - A grouped push carries data.group_count (a string).

GameDelta is exactly as in docs/Accounts-API.md.

docs.title: Delivery rules (push and email only)
docs.text:
For each new notification, in order: 1. expired and error notes are delivered as today. 2. instant = targets_only and not target_hit → no push or email. 3. The category's sent count today (the user's local day) ≥ daily_cap[kind] → no push or email. 4. Local time in quiet hours ([start, end), wrapping midnight; start = end means disabled; skipped without a timezone) → due at the next local end. 5. Otherwise due now. If a push for this user went out less than group_window_min ago, the item is held until that window ends and is sent then as one push covering every item held for that user ("3 prices dropped").

Email keeps the per-watch email_enabled opt-in and follows rules 1–4, never grouping.

docs.title: Execution waves
docs.text:
Each wave starts when the previous one has merged to main. Inside a wave, at most 3 tasks run in parallel worktrees, and they own disjoint files (see the hotspot table).

Wave Tasks (parallel) Gate 0 — seams and contract 1 backend seams · 2 frontend seams · 3 contract + golden cases + fake SerpAPI When it merges, docs/Alerts-API.md is frozen and the mobile teams start 1 — backend core 4 story · 5 moments + savings + game · 6 delivery + prefs Task 5's after_insert calls Task 6's dispatch through the stub, so the merge order doesn't matter 2 — backend watching 7 quick watch · 9 suggestions · 10 digest 9's round-trip test needs 7: merge 7 first, or skip that test until 7 lands 3 — scheduling + first UI 8 adaptive checks · 11 price story UI · 12 drop moment 8 alone touches run_due and next_check 4 — watching UI 13 savings + share · 14 one-tap · 15 suggestions sheet — 5 — composition 16 prefs UI · 17 hub · 18 integration 17 needs 11, 13 and 16's components (16 merges first, or 17 uses the stub) 6 — docs 19 docs ∥ 20 translation review — 7 — finish 21 E2E + reviews → 22 switch on 22 merges only after 21 is green

Every PR is green and deployable alone. The backend v2 behaviour is off by default, the read routes have no UI until the flag, and frontend controls render only with features.price_alerts_v2 (or the override).

docs.text:
• Localised push and email text, and the global 3/day notification cap across categories: Phase 6 (§7).
  • OG share pages and the 1080×1920 story-format share card: Phase 4. Phase 3 shares a client-rendered square PNG and text.
  • Friend leaderboards for Deal hunter: Phase 5.
  • APNs delivery of drop pushes: Phase 6/7. Android FCM already receives them, with the new data keys.
  • Converting non-USD savings into one total (this needs a rate source with an honest date label).

docs.title: Owner questions
docs.text:
1. SerpAPI in production. Without a key, prod shows only the stored history: there is no one-tap watch, no suggestions and no new drops, so the drop moment and savings stay dormant. Will you add a key (the Free Plan is 250/month, already exhausted for November, or a paid plan) so the feature can actually delight in production?
  2. Wording. Is the "caught a drop of $X" framing acceptable instead of "you saved $X"? We can't know whether the user booked. The share card says "I caught $245 in price drops with Voyager".
  3. Digest defaults. Opt-in, Mondays 09:00 local, email + in-app. Should the digest also push (it is currently in-app only, to avoid noise)?

docs.title: Owner-question rulings (main controller, 2026-11-12)
docs.text:
1. SerpAPI key in production: this stays the owner's call. Ship everything config-gated, with the "live checks paused" state shown when no key is set. Nothing may fail or invent prices without a key.
  2. Savings wording: use "caught a drop of $X". "You saved" is never used, because we can't know whether the user booked.
  3. Digest channels: the digest goes out in-app and by email. Its push is off by default, with a user toggle in alert preferences.

docs.title: Phase 3 follow-ups (from the Task 21 browser run)
docs.text:
Severity: minor unless noted. None blocks the release.

  • Drawer "Watch price" button (My Plan card) still shows the un-watched eye-off state for a hotel that is already watched via one-tap; the results card shows "Watching". Make the drawer card read the same watch state.
  • Alerts header: after Deal hunter is earned, the track still says "Next badge: Deal hunter, 1 of 1". Show the all-done line when the badge is earned.
  • Drop moment shows "+15 XP" (the deal_drop award) while the notification's game.xp is 25 (award plus badge). Decide which number the card should show; today the card omits the badge bonus.
  • SavingsShareCard picks light/dark from prefers-color-scheme, not the app theme toggle, so the PNG can mismatch the page.
  • A hotel watch whose property cannot be found shows both "Getting today's price" and "Sold out for your dates" (pending_first_check true while the check says unavailable). Prefer the unavailable state only.
  • Price story chart: keyboard scrubbing supports the arrow keys only; Home/End do nothing. Add them (jump to first/latest check).
  • /api/config is served with max-age=300, so after a server restart without SERPAPI_KEY the SPA keeps live_prices: true for up to 5 minutes (by design; noted for the runbook).
  • The first automatic drop card after a load was once skipped while tp_drop_seen already held the id (not reproduced; later loads showed the card every time). Watch for it.

docs.title: From the final review and task reviews
docs.text:
Severity in brackets.

  • [low] Several drops for one user dispatched in the same scheduler pass, before the first kicked flush has claimed anything, can each go out as a separate push seconds apart (alert_delivery grouping relies on sent_at).
  • [low] push._locks is keyed by event loop and each flush pass runs in a new loop, so entries accumulate (about 24 a day, cleared by the weekly reboot). Use a WeakKeyDictionary.
  • [low] alert_outbox and alert_digests are never pruned; the 180-day notification prune leaves their rows (saving-title lookups then fall back to an empty title).
  • [low] alert_digest.build_digest labels the week from the UTC now while the claim uses the local ISO week (cosmetic, zones far east of UTC).
  • [low] POST /api/alerts/quick-watch is not gated on price_alerts_v2_enabled.
  • [note for owner] With v2 on, re-check cadence is daily; legacy was every 12 h. Decide whether that is the intended trade for the SerpAPI budget.
  • [low] A grouped push's data.kind is the last row's kind, so the Android channel and priority follow it (T6).
  • [low] A crash after claiming an outbox row loses it, and a send failure after the digest claim loses that week's digest (claim-before-send, no retry).
  • [low] alerts_db uses datetime.utcnow() (deprecated); price_watch kind default is hotel (T1).
  • [low] _is_legacy does one query per outbox item (T6); N+1 saving-title lookup (T5).
  • [low] Advice cache is not keyed by locale; now() is not injectable in alert_story (T4).
  • [low] Quick-watch: _pending_spec is in serialize, _pending_expiry accepts a past date, the first look is not de-duplicated, and tests use a fake source with kind hotel (T7).
  • [low] alert_schedule._starved swallows a TypeError silently; a duplicate assert in a restored test (T8).
  • [low] Digest: missing tests noted in T10 review.
  • [low] Savings share card: round the total, focus trap/restore in the dialog, canvas text wrap, hard-coded tick values (T13).
  • [low] Price story: the slider thumb hit area is under the 44 px tap target (T11); Prefs: quiet-hours notice wording and focus styles (T16).
  • [low] The es Deal-hunter badge name needs a native check (T5); redundant SHELL_NS listing (T2).
  • [low] fare_cheaper_date no longer counts as a caught drop (fixed in #161); no follow-up needed.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Sharing Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use - [ ] checkboxes.

Goal: Any plan, trip recap or savings tally becomes a share card (link size 1200x630, story size 1080x1920) plus a public page whose Open Graph/Twitter tags make previews right on X, Facebook, WhatsApp, LinkedIn and chat apps. The sharer picks what is revealed. Links can be listed and revoked.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-voyager-reimagined-design.md §5 "Sharing", §5a (Memories, Price alerts rows), §8 telemetry, §2a PUBLIC_BASE_URL.

docs.title: Owner-question rulings (main controller, 2026-11-12)
docs.text:
1. Privacy defaults. A new share reveals only: trip title, destination(s), number of days and the plan's selections. Hidden unless the sharer ticks them: exact dates (dates: hidden default, month, exact), origin (show_origin), traveller display name (show_name). Email, nationality, visas, permits and accessibility are never exposed. OG tags and OG images show at most the month and year, even when dates=exact.
  2. Legacy links keep working. The old POST /plans/{id}/share (no body) and its tokens behave as today, because the previous SPA and the apps rely on them. New shares come from POST /api/shares, which always applies the options. GET /api/share/{token} answers for both kinds of token.
  3. Crawler pages. Caddy serves the SPA, so crawlers (User-Agent match on a fixed list) asking for /share/<token> are proxied to the app's GET /api/share/{token}/page, a small server-rendered HTML page with OG/Twitter tags, noindex, and a link into the SPA. People get the SPA as before. If the app answers 4xx/5xx or is an older build, Caddy falls back to the SPA index.html. No inline script anywhere (CSP).
  4. One renderer for cards. The server draws the PNG (Pillow, no new dependency) at GET /api/share/{token}/card.png?size=link|story, so web, iOS and Android show identical cards and OG images use it. Rendered PNGs sit in a small in-process TTL cache.
  5. Kinds in this phase: plan (covers itinerary), recap, savings. Deferred: quiz score (no quiz until Phase 5) and status (ephemeral "Day 3 in Lisbon" stays a native text share). Both are in the follow-ups.
  6. No XP for sharing. Raw volume earns nothing (§5a guardrail). The Memories (recap) and Price-alerts (savings card) touches already exist, so the sharing "gamified touch" is the card itself. Sharing never gates a feature and hide_game is untouched.
  7. Search engines. Every public share page and image sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex and <meta name="robots" content="noindex">.
  8. Rollout. Flag SHARING_V2_ENABLED (default false, switched to true in the last task if safe). Off: /api/shares*, /page, card.png answer 404 and features.sharing is 0; the SPA keeps the old share button.
  9. Revocation. Revoke deletes the row (or clears the legacy token); the public routes then 404 at once. Cached PNGs are keyed by token and the cache is cleared for that token on revoke; Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 is the only residual exposure and is documented.
  10. Views are not counted (no tracking of anonymous visitors). Telemetry share_view fires from the SPA only, with the kind.

docs.title: Global constraints
docs.text:
• Two-way compatibility (CLAUDE.md): no existing route changes shape; every new field is additive; the new SPA feature-detects features.sharing >= 1 from GET /api/config and otherwise keeps the old share flow. Schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS only; the new table joins the GCS user-table backup set (follow how Phase 3 added alerts_* tables).
  • Public output exposes nothing private: all text is HTML-escaped; no email; names only with show_name; never raw search_data, only the whitelist. Add tests that feed hostile names (<script>, quotes) and assert escaping.
  • Rate limits (new buckets, settings RATE_LIMIT_SHARE_PUBLIC 120 and RATE_LIMIT_SHARE_MANAGE 30 per 10 min): public routes by client IP, /api/shares* by user. Document in docs/Configuration.md. Tests run with limits off, so add one test that enables them.
  • i18n: all new strings in 7 languages in one new namespace share (server-rendered page text and card text are English plus the sharer's locale, see Task 2). catalog.test.js passes. Informal es/de, vous in fr.
  • Telemetry: new events in telemetry/registry.py and docs/Telemetry.md (registry test): share_open (kind), share_create (kind, dates), share_action (kind, target: native, copy, download, x, facebook, whatsapp, linkedin), share_revoke (kind), share_view (kind). Props are enums only. Every control carries data-tid.
  • Theme tokens, no hard-coded colours (cards drawn on the server use a fixed brand palette from frontend/design/tokens.json values copied once into the renderer, with a test that they match the token file).
  • Python 3.12, ruff check backend/, cd frontend && npx eslint src/ --max-warnings 0, mkdocs build --strict, backend and frontend suites green.

docs.title: API contract (docs/Sharing-API.md, additive-only after Task 9)
docs.text:
All under /api, JSON, errors {"detail","error_code"}. GET /config gains features.sharing: 0|1.

  • POST /shares (auth, share_manage): {"kind":"plan"|"recap"|"savings","plan_id":int?,"options":{"dates":"hidden|month|exact","show_origin":bool,"show_name":bool},"locale":"en"?}. plan_id required for plan and recap (404 plan_not_found if not the caller's). Idempotent per (user, kind, plan_id): returns the existing share and updates its options. Answers {"token","kind","url","card_url":{"link","story"},"options","created_at"}. 404 sharing_disabled when the flag is off. 422 invalid_kind.
  • GET /shares (auth): {"shares":[{token,kind,title,url,options,created_at}]}, newest first, max 100.
  • DELETE /shares/{token} (auth): 204, 404 share_not_found if not the caller's.
  • GET /share/{token} (public, share_public): existing shape for plan tokens (name, created_at, updated_at, search_data, selections) plus, for new shares, kind, options, owner_name (only with show_name), and for recap/savings a card object (headline, stats[], destination?, period?). 404 for unknown or revoked.
  • GET /share/{token}/page (public): HTML with OG/Twitter tags (og:title, og:description, og:image = absolute card.png?size=link, og:url, twitter:card=summary_large_image), noindex, <a href=/share/token>.
  • GET /share/{token}/card.png?size=link|story (public): PNG, Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, X-Robots-Tag: noindex.

Card content: brand line, headline (7 days in Lisbon, My trip to Japan: recap, Caught drops worth $X), up to three stat chips (counts only: activities, hotels, places; recap: places visited, countries; savings: drops caught), month and year only when dates is not hidden, the sharer's display name only with show_name. Plan card never includes origin unless show_origin.

docs.text: Phase 5 (Social + Play) shipped on 2026-11-12 with SOCIAL_ENABLED and PLAY_ENABLED on by default after the opus final review. Nothing here blocks that; each item is a candidate for a later PR.

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
• Optional AI moderation classifier behind services/moderation.py::classify (spend-cap aware).
  • Translated entity names for the quiz bank; etiquette and "where is this" packs (need curated content and image rights).
  • Push reminders for the daily quiz; comment threads; mobile apps (Android, iOS) adopting docs/Social-API.md.
