docs.title: Addendum: everything auto-deploys within minutes (2026-11-06)
docs.text: Addendum to the lean GCP design (2026-11-06-gcp-lean-deploy-design.md, §6 "Deploys"). It replaces the decision that Caddy changes wait for a weekly night window. Requirement: the backend, the SPA and Caddy all go live automatically within about 5 minutes of the deploy workflow finishing, with no regression in security.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The SPA was baked into the Caddy image, so every frontend change produced a new Caddy digest. Recreating Caddy cuts every open connection, including SSE searches and chats that run for minutes, so the deployer staged new Caddy digests until Sunday 04:00 Berlin.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Content is not the runtime. The Caddy image still carries /srv (the SPA) and /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, but the VM serves neither from the container. deploy.sh copies them out of each verified image with docker create + docker cp (never started, --network none) into /var/lib/voyager/edge/releases/<full sha256 hex>/.
  2. Checks: only regular files and directories (no symlinks, devices or FIFOs); index.html present and every /assets/… it references present; at most 200 MB.
  3. Normalised: root-owned, 0644/0755, plus SOURCE, BUILD and .complete.
  4. Directory name: the full digest. It can't collide, and only a validated 64-hex string becomes a path.
  5. Atomic switch. Relative symlinks current, prev1 and prev2 are replaced with ln -s to a temp name and then mv -T (rename). Caddy bind-mounts the whole directory read-only at /edge, never a single file (a file bind mount pins the inode and never sees a rename), and runs --config /edge/current/Caddyfile.
  6. Old assets stay servable: try_files across the last three releases. The other option was a shared, age-pruned assets pool. Try_files was chosen because it needs no second store and no pruning-by-age rule, and it can't serve an asset no kept release contains. The @asset file matcher tries /current/srv{path}, /prev1/srv{path} and /prev2/srv{path} under root /edge. Hits are immutable for a year. Misses are an uncached 404 (before this change, a 404 also carried the one-year header). Three releases are kept and the rest deleted. An edge rollback swaps current and prev1, so the release left behind stays an asset fallback.
  7. Caddyfile hot reload. When the release's Caddyfile differs from current's:
  8. it is adapted with caddy adapt --validate in a throwaway container (--network none --read-only, uid 10002, no capabilities, 128 MB, with the real SITE_HOST/ACME_EMAIL from site.env). This is never a second Caddy inside the 96 MB Caddy container.
  9. The image used is the running runtime image (same Caddy, by label) for content updates, and the new image for runtime changes.
  10. The JSON is posted to /load on the admin API (127.0.0.1:2019, inside the container) with busybox wget. Caddy applies /load atomically and gracefully: listeners are reused and open connections finish on the old config. A refusal leaves the old config; the symlinks go back, the digest is held and an email goes out.
  11. After a switch, deploy.sh checks through Caddy (container IP, --resolve, -k) that / is byte-identical to the new index.html and its entry asset loads. A wrong answer rolls back; no answer at all (Caddy down) is left to the converge step.
  12. Runtime changes recreate, automatically. Image label io.voyager.caddy-runtime = SHA-256 over the base image pinned by digest (the workflow resolves caddy:2.10-alpine and passes the pinned ref as the CADDY_BASE build arg, so the build uses exactly what is hashed) and the final stage of caddy.Dockerfile without comments and without the two content COPY lines (deploy/gcp/caddy-runtime-id.sh).
  13. A different (or missing) label means: validate with the new image, drain, switch, recreate, then check health (admin API plus / and an asset).
  14. On failure it goes back to the previous runtime and release, holds the digest and sends an email.
  15. CADDY_IMAGE (what compose runs) changes only here. CADDY_CONTENT_IMAGE tracks the content.
  16. Drain. New app endpoint GET /internal/streams → {"active_streams": n}, counted in core/sse.guarded_stream.
  17. It isn't under /api or /health, so Caddy never routes it, and a request carrying any forwarding header gets a 404. It exposes a single number.
  18. deploy.sh polls it on the compose network (172.30.0.10:8001) every 3 s for up to 90 s, then recreates anyway. If the count can't be read (an old app), it recreates at once.
  19. The converge step uses the same drain when compose would recreate Caddy for a changed compose.yaml (compose config hash vs the container's com.docker.compose.config-hash label).
  20. Security kept.
  21. Every digest, content-only included, is cosign-verified against the deploy.yml@refs/heads/main identity before it is pulled.
  22. Downgrades are refused (io.voyager.build, compared with the live release's BUILD) and remembered in refused-digests, so they aren't re-verified every minute.
  23. Holds (failed-digests) apply to Caddy digests as to the app.
  24. No new ports; the admin API stays on loopback inside the container; extracted files are never executed; Caddy stays non-root with no capabilities.
  25. Faster, cheap polling. The timer runs every 60 s (RandomizedDelaySec=5s, AccuracySec=1s).
  26. One anonymous GHCR token covers both repositories and is cached for 4 min (re-fetched on a 401). A run with nothing new is two HEADs: no pull, no cosign.
  27. A 429 backs off (Retry-After, else 60 s × 2ⁿ, capped at 30 min, in /run/voyager-deploy/backoff). A failed signature check is retried after 10 min. "Held" and "refused" notes are logged once, not every minute.
  28. Smaller pulls. caddy.Dockerfile puts the runtime RUN layer before the content COPYs, so those layers are cached and identical across releases. A frontend change downloads only the SPA layer. Content-only images are removed once their files are extracted; the runtime and previous runtime images are kept for rollback.
  29. The window. --window is accepted and ignored. voyager-window.timer stays, repurposed: Sunday 04:00 Berlin, reboot only if /run/reboot-required (unchanged behaviour for reboots).
  30. Migration safety.
    • The image's own /edge/current points at its baked /srv and Caddyfile, so a new image still serves its SPA under the old compose.yaml (for instance if the old deployer's Sunday window applies it before --update-host).
    • first-boot.sh unpacks the kit under the deploy lock (no mixed old/new files) and then runs deploy.sh.
    • Before any network call, deploy.sh rebuilds a missing current from the pinned image. An old images.env has no CADDY_CONTENT_IMAGE and an unlabelled runtime, so the first new image takes the runtime path: one drained recreate, which also applies the new compose definition. Certificates stay in caddy_data.

docs.title: Timing (measured on 2026-11-06 runs, estimated on the VM)
docs.text: Step Time Deploy workflow (CI ≈ 4.5 min → publish ≈ 1.5 min) ≈ 6 min VM notices prod moved ≤ 65 s SPA/Caddyfile: verify + SPA layer pull + extract + switch ≈ 30–60 s App: pull + health (Docker health interval 30 s) ≈ 1–4 min Merge → live ≈ 7–9 min (1–3 min after the workflow)

docs.title: Proposals (not done; they would save minutes but touch CI gates)
docs.text:
The first two were done on 2026-11-07 (branch perf/faster-deploy): per-image build jobs run in parallel with CI and Trivy-scan the shipped images by digest; per-image promote jobs sign them and move prod after CI; unchanged images (io.voyager.app-inputs / io.voyager.caddy-inputs) are not rebuilt. See Testing and CI.

  • build-and-scan builds and Trivy-scans the legacy nginx frontend/ image, which isn't deployed, and waits for every test job. Scanning the Caddy image that ships instead (and the app image publish builds, by digest) would be more useful and could run in publish after the push and before moving prod, saving about 1 min.
  • The app image gets a new digest on every merge (revision label), so the app restarts, cutting its SSE streams, even on frontend-only merges. A content label for the app (like the Caddy runtime id) would skip those restarts. The same drain could also run before app recreates.
  • start_interval: 5s on the app's healthcheck (Docker ≥ 25) would shorten the health wait from about 30 s to about 5 s. Left out: changing the app service would restart the app during the migration.

docs.title: Review fixes (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
• Errexit that works. Bash ignores set -e in functions called from if/||/&&. Every deploy step now runs through step FN: in plain context, in a subshell with set -e, with its status in a variable, and images.env is read back afterwards. Every pull, docker create/cp, compose up and write is also checked explicitly.
  • Fail closed. An unreadable or non-numeric build label (on the new image, or the live one's, falling back from the release's BUILD to the runtime image's label) refuses instead of skipping the downgrade check. After compose up, the container's image ID must equal the intended digest's before health counts.
  • Holds vs retries.
  • Holds: content/validation failures and an admin-API refusal (by digest), an unhealthy app (by digest), and an unhealthy Caddy runtime (by runtime id, held-runtimes; also written by --rollback-caddy).
  • Retried after 5 min, nothing held: infrastructure failures, and an SPA that Caddy doesn't serve after the switch.
  • An image with a held runtime ships its content on the current runtime when its Caddyfile validates there; nothing is ever recreated onto a held runtime.
  • Containment. A broken edge directory never blocks app deploys or app/Caddy rollbacks. Emails and repeated infrastructure errors go out at most once an hour per kind. The live content image is kept until it is replaced, at the cost of one SPA layer of disk, so a lost edge directory is rebuilt offline.
  • Cheap no-change run. Converge runs only when the hash of compose.yaml/site.env/app.env/images.env changed or one docker ps shows a service not running.
  • Minors.
  • .staging is 0700.
  • window.sh no longer prunes images; deploy.sh removes old app and Caddy images by digest, keeping current and previous. A failed runtime image is removed.
  • Caddy health: running image ID, admin API, readable /edge/current/srv/index.html and plain-HTTP redirect; HTTPS only warns.
  • --rollback-edge is a toggle (it releases the hold of the release it returns to).
  • caddy.Dockerfile notes that the runtime id hashes lines, not the contents of COPYed host files.

docs.title: Re-review fixes (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
• HTTPS is part of Caddy health. A wrong HTTPS answer is always unhealthy. No HTTPS answer is tolerated only when HTTPS gave no answer before the change too (https_baseline, probed before the recreate) or on a first deploy. This applies to runtime deploys, converge recreates and --rollback-caddy. The previous runtime image is removed only after the new one passes.
  • No flip-flopping. An SPA that Caddy serves wrongly after a successful switch/reload is held (email once). A runtime or app compose up that fails, or leaves the old container, twice in a row for the same digest is held.
  • Minors. While the app step only waits to retry, the edge step still runs. Refused images (downgrade, no build label) are removed. An unknown live build falls back to the label of the image the live release came from, else the deploy retries; it never uses another image's label.

docs.title: Voyager on GCP for < $30/month — deployment design (v5, final for review)
docs.text: Grounding: measured runtime profile (scratchpad/gcp-plan/runtime-profile.md), official prices fetched 2026-11-06 (scratchpad/gcp-plan/pricing-facts.md), four rounds of adversarial review (critique-cost-r1.md, critique-reliability-r1.md, Rounds 1–4). Round 4: cost APPROVE, reliability APPROVE with conditions — the conditions are folded in below (§2.2, §2.3, §12). §11/§12 list every finding and its fix.

docs.title: 0. The idea in one paragraph
docs.text:
Run the existing app container on Google's always-free e2-micro VM with SQLite on its persistent disk. Everything the app does today — durable writes, the in-process price-watch scheduler, push delivery, 80-second AI streams — keeps working with small changes, and the bill is flat ≈ $4/month. The usual ways a small deployment blows its budget (autoscaling compute, load balancers, NAT, image scanning, log volume, egress floods) are each designed out or capped on the box itself, so the guarantee doesn't depend on billing data that can lag a day.

(v1–v2 used Cloud Run scale-to-zero at ≈ $0.50/month. Reviews showed SQLite on vanishing, overlapping, CPU-throttled instances needs fencing, commit-before-reply uploads, client retries and a brake — the riskiest code in the app to save ≈ $3.50. It stays documented as Option B in §9.)

docs.title: 1. What the app needs (measured)
docs.text: Need Measured On an e2-micro (shared 2 vCPU, bursts; 1 GB RAM) CPU A search: 0.7–2.0 CPU-s over ~80 s 3–10 concurrent searches sustained; spikes fit the burst Memory 117–145 MB idle, 209 MB peak; DB 45 MB ≈ 600–750 MB peak with OS + Docker + Caddy; container memory limits + zram (no swapfile on the slow disk) State SQLite; user data ≈ 1 MB, place data ≈ 45 MB On the persistent disk — the disk is the source of truth Long requests Search ~80 s, worst > 300 s No platform timeout; Caddy streams SSE Background Watch tick (300 s), backup loop Run in-process, always-on CPU

docs.title: 2. Architecture (Option A — recommended)
docs.text:
Browser / Android ──HTTPS (IPv4 only)──► e2-micro VM, us-east1, Standard network tier
                                         Debian 13 · unattended-upgrades (+ one weekly night reboot window, Berlin time)
                                         Docker Engine + compose plugin, systemd-managed
                                          ├─ caddy  : TLS for your domain, SPA files, /api + /health → app,
                                          │           SSE flushing, persistent /data volume (certs)
                                          ├─ app    : FastAPI + SQLite (WAL) on the persistent disk
                                          └─ host   : egress governor (nftables + per-minute counter),
                                                      image-pull deployer (systemd timer), log rotation
        ├── backup: changed user tables → GCS (us-east1, free tier) via tmpfs export
        ├── PD snapshot schedule: daily, keep 7, storage location us-east1
        └── FCM push via the VM service account (ADC)
GitHub Actions (free): test → build → push to GHCR (public, free) → move the `prod` tag
VM pulls `prod` by digest (no inbound deploy access, no CI root on the box)
Secrets: Secret Manager → fetched at container start into memory (tmpfs), never on the disk
Monitoring: free uptime check + email alert; budget $10 with email alerts

docs.title: 2.1 Durability on a VM (fixes the Cloud Run-era backup code)
docs.text:
• New BACKUP_MODE=vm: the local disk is authoritative. Restore from GCS only if the DB file is missing (fresh disk), after deleting stray -wal/-shm. No startup merge, ever (merging would revive deleted watches, devices, plans and taste resets).
  • Backup exports only user tables into tmpfs, uploads only when the export's hash changed, every 5 min, plus once at clean shutdown (--timeout-graceful-shutdown 5, compose stop_grace_period: 20s).
  • Mount guard: restore runs only if the data directory is the mounted persistent disk (never on an empty, unmounted path that could later overwrite GCS).
  • Backup status (last success time) is reported in /health; a free uptime-check content match alerts if backups stop.
  • SQLite WAL + synchronous=NORMAL on PD is crash-safe; nightly PD snapshots are crash-consistent copies of the whole disk. Worst case after losing the disk itself: ≤ 5 min of user changes.
  • Restore drill before go-live: (a) fresh disk ← GCS; (b) new VM ← PD snapshot.

docs.title: 2.2 The cost guarantee, on the box
docs.text:
• Egress governor (tiered, so no single abuser can take the site down for a month): Standard-tier egress is free up to 200 GiB/month per billing account, then $0.085/GiB; the VM can send 1 Gbps. A systemd timer adds up per-minute TX deltas (reboot-safe, atomically persisted; after a disk restore it takes the larger of its total and Monitoring's sent_bytes_count). The month resets at 00:00 America/Los_Angeles (Google's billing month). Rules live in Docker's DOCKER-USER chain (an INPUT rule would not stop DNAT'd traffic to Caddy) and are re-applied after Docker starts; closure is verified by a curl from outside during rollout. | Month-to-date egress | Action | |---|---| | always | per-source-IP bandwidth meter (nftables) + tc shaper ≈ 50 Mbit/s; top talkers logged | | 150 GiB | email warning (SMTP on 587, or a custom metric → free alert); shape to 20 Mbit/s | | 200 GiB (free allowance used) | shape to 10 Mbit/s; email | | 400 GiB (≈ $17 overage) | close 80/443 until the month resets or you reopen; email | Worst-case GCP bill ≈ $4 + $17 ≈ $21 < $30, and a single abusive IP is throttled long before.
  • IPv4 only: a VM's external IPv6 is Premium tier (outside the 200 GiB). IPv6-only phones still reach IPv4 via carrier NAT64.
  • No Cloud Logging volume: logs stay on the VM (Docker json-file, 10 MB × 5 per container); no logging agent → no ingestion bill; errors are visible via docker logs over IAP.
  • Fixed compute: one VM; a flood makes the app slower, never pricier. App limits still apply: AI routes require sign-in in production, login rate limit, real-client-IP rate limits.

docs.title: 2.3 Deploys
docs.text:
• CI runs tests, builds ghcr.io/rupakc/travel-planner-{app,caddy}, and moves the prod tag only on a manual "promote" (not every merge).
  • Images are signed in CI (cosign keyless / build provenance); only the manual promote job, behind a protected GitHub environment, can move the prod tag.
  • On the VM a timer resolves prod to a digest every 5 min, verifies the signature, writes the digest into the compose env file and pulls by digest (new layers land before anything stops), then up -d, polls /health, and rolls back to the previous digest automatically if it fails. Caddy holds requests briefly (lb_try_duration 30s) during app restarts; Caddy itself changes rarely and only in the night window.
  • Schema changes stay additive (all existing migrations are), so a rollback never meets an incompatible DB.

docs.title: 3. Monthly cost (official prices, us-east1)
docs.text:
Item Cost e2-micro VM $0.00 (Always Free) 30 GB pd-standard (boot + data, total ≤ 30 GB) $0.00 (Always Free) Static external IPv4 (in use) $3.65 ($0.005/h) Egress, Standard tier $0.00 (≤ 200 GiB, enforced on the box) PD snapshots (regional us-east1, ~2–5 GB incremental) ≈ $0.10–0.30 GCS backup bucket $0.00 (5 GB free in us-east1; soft delete off) Secret Manager, uptime check, alerting, IAP, OS Login $0.00 GHCR, GitHub Actions $0.00 Total GCP ≈ $3.75–3.95 / month (≈ $4.50–4.70 incl. 19 % VAT) Optional: faster pd-balanced 10 GB boot disk if the disk benchmark is poor + ≈ $1.00 Your own domain (outside GCP, e.g. .de/.com) ≈ $0.80–1.20 / month

Worst case under any traffic: ≈ $21 (the governor's 400 GiB hard stop); normal ≈ $4. Not GCP: Anthropic (set a monthly limit in the Anthropic console) and SerpAPI (free plan, daily budget 8 calls).

docs.title: 4. Guardrails
docs.text:
1. Fixed compute + on-box egress governor + no log ingestion → the GCP bill cannot run away.
  2. Budget $10 before tax (≈ $11.90 with VAT), email alerts at 50/90/100 % actual + forecast.
  3. Uptime check (free) → email if the site is down 10 min (incl. a governor closing the ports).
  4. No LB, NAT, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, Artifact Registry, scanning, versioned objects, soft delete, or IPv6 egress.

docs.title: 5. Code & config changes
docs.text:
1. Backup vm mode (§2.1): disk-authoritative, restore-if-missing, no merge, user-table export in tmpfs, change counter, 5-min cadence; Cloud Run mode unchanged.
  2. Secrets at start: small entrypoint fetches named secrets from Secret Manager with the VM's identity into process env; refuse to start with an empty JWT_SECRET_KEY.
  3. Proxy/IP: uvicorn --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=<compose network range>; app port never published; login rate-limit bucket; ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_AI=false in prod.
  4. FCM via ADC (VM service account, cloud-platform scope + IAM roles), key file as fallback; Android google-services.json from the new Firebase project; Android prod URL = your domain.
  5. Slim image (drop unused claude-agent-sdk, python-dotenv); stable layer order.
  6. SSE hygiene: 15 s keepalives in search Phase 1 and chat; cancel agent tasks when the client disconnects.
  7. deploy/gcp/: compose.yaml (memory limits measured under load — start app 550 MB, caddy 96 MB; log rotation; health checks; restart policies), Caddyfile, Caddy image with the built SPA, host scripts (tiered egress governor, signed-digest deployer, zram), cloud-init for first boot.
  8. infrastructure/gcp/bootstrap.sh (idempotent gcloud), .github/workflows/deploy.yml (test → build → GHCR; promote job), docs/Deployment-GCP.md runbook; remove the old Cloud Run Terraform/workflow so nobody applies it by mistake.

docs.title: 6. Infrastructure
docs.text:
• New project under rupak97.4@gmail.com; APIs: compute, iap, oslogin, secretmanager, monitoring, storage, fcm, billingbudgets (no Cloud Run, AR, scanning).
  • VM: e2-micro, us-east1, Debian 13, 30 GB pd-standard, static IPv4 on Standard tier, no IPv6, Shielded VM, OS Login, cloud-platform scope with a dedicated vm-runtime service account (bucket objectUser on the backup bucket only, secretAccessor on its secrets, FCM send).
  • Firewall: 80/443 from anywhere; 22 only from IAP (35.235.240.0/20). No inbound deploy path.
  • Snapshot schedule: daily, keep 7, storage location us-east1.
  • Bucket (us-east1): uniform access, public access prevention, soft delete off, versioning with a newer-versions cap, lifecycle 30 days.
  • DNS: A record for your domain → the static IP (at your registrar; no Cloud DNS bill).

docs.title: 7. Rollout (with checks)
docs.text:
1. Confirm the billing account has nothing else using the free tiers.
  2. bootstrap.sh with you (you paste secret values; I never see them).
  3. Disk benchmark (fio on pd-standard); switch the boot disk to 10 GB pd-balanced (+$1) only if image pulls/backups are visibly slow.
  4. Data: fresh start, or migrate old-prod users/plans (strip the 886 MB export to user tables offline, verify row counts per table, place on the disk before first start).
  5. Promote the first image; smoke-test web, Android prod build, a search (SSE), a watch tick, a push, both restore drills, a reboot, a deploy during an active search, and the governor (lower its threshold temporarily, confirm ports close and the alert arrives, restore).
  6. Watch billing for 48 h; hand over the runbook.

docs.title: 8. Decisions for you
docs.text:
1. Option A (VM, ≈ $4 flat, simplest, recommended) or Option B (Cloud Run, ≈ $0.50, complex).
  2. Region: us-east1 (free VM; ~100–130 ms from Germany, invisible on 80-second AI streams). An EU VM would cost ≈ $10/month more.
  3. Domain: buy one (≈ $10/year; recommended before the Android release bakes the URL in) — or start on a free sslip.io name and switch later.
  4. Data: fresh start or migrate old-prod users/plans.
  5. Billing: new project under rupak97.4@gmail.com; confirm nothing else bills on that account.

docs.title: 9. Option B — Cloud Run scale-to-zero (≈ $0.30–0.60/month), not recommended now
docs.text: Viable if traffic becomes spiky/global. Needs: commit-before-reply user-table uploads through one paced uploader (GCS ≤ 1 write/s per object), generation fencing that re-imports instead of going read-only, client retry/idempotency on web + Android, alerts delivered only after durable commits, an HTTP tick with in-app OIDC checks, a multi-metric brake that reopens automatically, no image scanning, log exclusions, a Cloud Run spend cap.

docs.title: 10. Other options rejected
docs.text: Option Monthly Why not e2-micro in europe-west1 (paid) ≈ $10.4 Pays to save ~100 ms on 80-second AI streams Cloud Run min-instances=1 ≈ $10–14 Idle compute for a 2 %-CPU app Cloud Run instances (Preview) ≈ $6 Preview, no SLA, no persistent disk Firebase Hosting + Cloud Run ≈ Option B 60 s rewrite timeout breaks 80 s searches Cloud SQL / Firestore ≥ $7–10 / rewrite For 1 MB of data IPv6-only VM ≈ $0.2 Many networks still lack IPv6; IPv6 egress is Premium tier anyway Load balancer for a domain ≈ $18+ Caddy does TLS for free

docs.title: 11. Review findings → fixes (rounds 1–3)
docs.text: Round Finding Fix 1–2 Cloud Run: stale overwrites, fail-open restore, after-response uploads, OOM w/o SIGTERM, fencing outages, no client retries, 1 write/s GCS limit, brake as an off-switch Design moved to a VM; Cloud Run kept as Option B with the full fix list 1 Image scanning $0.26/image No Artifact Registry; GHCR 1 Budgets/spend caps lag and don't cap On-box governor + fixed compute; budget only as a backstop 3 Egress past 200 GiB uncapped (1 Gbps) Egress governor closes ports at 190 GiB + tc shaper + alert 3 Logging either uncapped or absent Local rotated logs, no ingestion agent 3 IPv6 egress is Premium tier IPv4 only 3 Snapshots not free, multi-region default Regional us-east1, keep 7; ≈ $0.10–0.30 3 Backup code restores over the disk at every start; merge revives deletions BACKUP_MODE=vm: disk authoritative, restore-if-missing, no merge 3 pd-standard 30 GB is slow (3.6 MiB/s); 45 MB per-minute backup copies User-table export in tmpfs, 5-min cadence, change counter; fio benchmark; optional pd-balanced 3 COS has no compose and doesn't auto-patch by default Debian 12 + unattended-upgrades + weekly reboot window 3 Let's Encrypt duplicates/shared limits; sslip.io dependency Persistent Caddy /data; own domain recommended 3 Memory ~600–750 MB peak on 1 GB Container memory limits + swapfile 3 IAP SSH push deploy = CI gets root; missing OS Login API Pull-based deploy by digest; manual promote 3 Narrow VM scopes break ADC; secrets must not hit the disk cloud-platform + IAM; secrets fetched into memory 3 Deploy restarts kill streams; every merge deploys Pull-before-stop, Caddy request holding, manual promote 3 GCS soft delete billed; 60 s loop = 43k ops/month Soft delete off; change counter; 5-min cadence 1–3 VAT, per-account free tiers, Anthropic is the real cost $10 budget incl. VAT; billing-account check; Anthropic limit

docs.title: 12. Round 4 conditions → folded in
docs.text: Finding Fix Firewall INPUT rule wouldn't stop Docker-published ports Governor rules in DOCKER-USER, re-applied after Docker starts; tested from outside One client could close the site for the month Tiered governor (shape at 150/200 GiB, close at 400 GiB ≈ $17), per-IP meter, top-talker log Counter resets on reboot; month boundary Persisted deltas; reset at 00:00 America/Los_Angeles; Monitoring cross-check after restore No outbound port 25 for warnings SMTP 587, or custom metric → free alert compose pull re-reads the tag; image provenance Pin by verified digest; cosign/provenance; protected promote job; auto-rollback on failed health Unmounted data dir could trigger a stale restore Mount guard data_version misses same-connection writes Hash of the export Swapfile on pd-standard thrashes and bloats snapshots zram Debian 12 past regular security support Debian 13 Backup failures invisible Backup status in /health + uptime content match Budgets are pre-tax $10 pre-tax (≈ $11.90 incl. VAT) 450 MB app limit ≈ 4 searches Limit measured under load during rollout (start 550 MB)

docs.title: 13. Decisions (user, 2026-11-06)
docs.text:
1. Option A — always-free e2-micro VM.
  2. Region us-east1.
  3. Free domain now (sslip.io hostname from the static IP); own domain later (one Caddyfile line + Android PROD_BASE_URL update).
  4. Migrate old-prod users with their own data (plans, preferences, taste signals, recent searches, feedback) from ~/gcp-decommission-export-20260830; price watches/notifications did not exist then.
  5. New project under rupak97.4@gmail.com.
  6. Auto-deploy: a merge to main deploys automatically once every CI job passes (supersedes the manual promote in §2.3). The signed-digest pull, health check and automatic rollback stay.
  7. LLM provider: Anthropic → Gemini on Vertex AI ("Agent Platform"), authenticated with the VM's service account (ADC, no API key):
  8. specialist agents (all 13 + packing, pricing advisor, itinerary, stress test, chat routing/extraction, chat itinerary) → Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite ($0.30 / $2.50 per 1M input/output, official price page 2026-11-06), thinking kept low;
  9. chat conversational replies → Gemini 3.8 Flash ($0.75 / $3.75 until 2026-12-31, then $1.50 / $7.50).
  10. Estimated ≈ $0.11 per full search vs ≈ $0.23 on Claude Haiku 4.5 (to be measured on real searches before switching).

  11. AI spend hard cap $20/month (VAT applies: personal account) via a spend-cap budget on Agent Platform (Gemini); with ≈ $4–5 hosting the whole GCP bill stays < $30. When the cap trips, AI features pause until the next month; the app shows a friendly "AI limit reached for this month" message.

  12. Governor re-tuned for the $25 AI cap: with $25 reserved for Gemini, hosting may not exceed ≈ $5, so the governor's hard stop moves from 400 GiB to 200 GiB (zero overage). To keep one abuser from closing the site, each source IP gets a daily byte quota (≈ 3 GiB/day) and ≈ 4 Mbit/s — a single IP would need > 60 days to reach 200 GiB; the 150 GiB warning email still fires first. Hosting worst case ≈ $4.0 pre-tax.

Budget summary after decisions: hosting ≤ ≈ $4.0 + Gemini ≤ $25 (hard cap) → ≤ ≈ $29 pre-tax, worst case; ≈ $5–15 in a normal month (≈ 50–100 searches). Google budgets and caps are pre-tax: if 19 % VAT applies to your account, the gross worst case is ≈ $34.5 — set the Gemini cap to $20 to stay under $30 gross.

Final cap (user, 2026-11-06): VAT is added → Gemini spend cap $20/month. Worst case ≈ $4 + $20 = $24 pre-tax ≈ $28.6 incl. 19 % VAT. Governor stays at 200 GiB (zero overage).

docs.title: Live "Search the web now" + Near Me v2 — design & API contract
docs.text: Status: decided (user, 2026-11-06). Verified against Google's Service Terms §20(k)/(m) and Vertex grounding docs, 2026-11-06 (Service Terms §20(k) Grounding with Google Search, §20(m) Grounding with Google Maps; Agent Platform pricing).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Watches and alerts stay on SerpAPI. Google's §20(k) forbids background (non-user-prompted) grounded checks, storing grounded results to build a database, and analysing them. So Gemini web search is never used by the scheduler, never stored, never compared with baselines, never feeds alerts, notifications or price history.
  2. New: "Search the web now" — a user-initiated Gemini call with Google Search grounding for one watch (fare, hotel, activity, trip). The answer is returned to the requesting user only, displayed once with its sources, and not persisted anywhere (no DB, no cache, no logs of content). Clients keep it in memory only (Android: ViewModel state, not Room/DataStore; web: component state).
  3. Near Me v2 uses Gemini with Grounding with Google Maps around the user's coordinates and returns four sections: places to see, places to eat, places to shop, places to stay — each item with an "Open in Google Maps" link. Results go only to the requesting user; no server-side cache (Maps terms allow storing grounded results only for display evaluation ≤ 90 days or chat history); clients keep them in memory only. place_id may be stored (allowed) but we don't need to.
  4. Background "nearby" notifications must not call Maps grounding. The Android worker only posts an invitation ("See what's near you") that opens Near Me, where the user's own request runs.
  5. Both features use the existing per-user light_ai rate limit, require sign-in, and count against the Gemini spend cap (₹1,800). Free allowances: 5,000 Search-grounding queries + 5,000 Maps queries per month (shared across Gemini models), then $14 / 1,000 queries.

  6. Attribution/display: show sources directly under the content they support ("Sources" list with titles + links); Near Me shows "Google Maps" attribution text per Google's guidelines and each item's Maps link. Do not modify grounded text or intersperse ads/other content inside it. Search Suggestions: we display the returned search queries as a "Searched for" line linking to Google Search (permitted to skip the Search Suggestions widget under the pricing page's volume condition; record that in docs).

  7. Provider ruling: grounding exists only on the gemini provider. With LLM_PROVIDER resolved to anthropic (local dev), /api/live-check and /api/nearby with sections: true answer 503 {"detail":{"code":"grounding_unavailable","message":"Live web and map results need the Gemini provider."}}; v1 nearby is unaffected. One shared seam: core/llm.py gains generate_grounded(...) (text output, returns text + grounding chunks + web search queries + usage) used by both features; tests stub it. JSON mode is not combined with grounding (uncertain on Vertex) — parse structured bits from the text and take links only from grounding metadata.

docs.title: POST /api/live-check (auth required, light_ai bucket)
docs.text:
Request:

{"kind": "flight" | "hotel" | "activity" | "trip", "watch_id": 123}
  • kind=flight uses /api/fare-watches/{id} ownership; other kinds /api/price-watches/{id}; 404 if the watch isn't the caller's. The server builds the prompt from the stored watch spec (route + dates
  • travellers / hotel + dates + guests / activity + city + date / trip parts). No free-text prompt from the client.

Response 200:

{
  "kind": "hotel",
  "watch_id": 123,
  "checked_at": "2026-11-06T18:00:00Z",
  "summary": "Plain-text answer from Gemini (grounded), unmodified.",
  "quotes": [
    {"label": "Booking.com, 3 nights", "amount": 412.0, "currency": "EUR", "source_index": 0}
  ],
  "sources": [{"title": "…", "uri": "https://…"}],
  "searched_for": ["memmo alfama lisbon price 1-4 dec 2026"],
  "disclaimer": "From a live web search just now. Prices change quickly — check the provider before booking. Not used for your price alerts."
}
  • quotes may be empty; each quote must cite a source by index; amounts are copied from the grounded answer (never invented); unparseable → omitted.
  • Errors: 404 {"detail":"Watch not found"}; 429 rate limit (string detail); 503 {"detail": {"code":"ai_limit"|"ai_billing", "message": "…"}} (same friendly copy as other AI routes); 502 {"detail":{"code":"live_check_failed","message":"…"}} when the model returns no grounded answer.
  • Never written to the DB, never logged with content (usage log line only: tokens, search query count, latency).

docs.title: POST /api/nearby v2 (auth required, light_ai)
docs.text:
Request (backward compatible):

{"lat": 38.72, "lng": -9.14, "limit": 8, "sections": true, "language": "en"}
  • sections absent/false → v1 behaviour unchanged ({place, items} from the activities agent), so already-installed apps keep working.
  • sections: true → v2:
{
  "place": {"name": "Lisbon", "region": null, "country": "Portugal", "country_code": "PT",
            "lat": 38.72, "lng": -9.14, "distance_km": 0.4},
  "sections": [
    {"id": "see",  "title": "Places to see",  "items": [ITEM, …]},
    {"id": "eat",  "title": "Places to eat",  "items": [ITEM, …]},
    {"id": "shop", "title": "Places to shop", "items": [ITEM, …]},
    {"id": "stay", "title": "Places to stay", "items": [ITEM, …]}
  ],
  "attribution": "Google Maps",
  "sources": [{"title": "…", "uri": "https://maps.google.com/…"}]
}

ITEM:

{"name": "Time Out Market", "summary": "One-line why, from the grounded answer",
 "maps_uri": "https://maps.google.com/?cid=…", "place_id": "ChIJ…", "category": "eat"}
  • Each item must come from a Maps grounding chunk (uri/title/placeId); items without a Maps link are dropped (no invented places). limit per section (1..10, default 6). Sections may be empty (UI shows a friendly empty state). place still resolved from the local places DB (unchanged).
  • Errors: v1's 404 no_place / 502 agent_error codes unchanged; plus 503 ai_limit/ai_billing.
  • No server cache for v2.

docs.title: Clients
docs.text:
• Web: new top-level "Near me" page (/nearby) — browser geolocation with a clear permission explainer and a manual "use a city instead" fallback (typed place → coordinates via /api/airports/search or the places DB if available; else skip), four sections with cards, "Open in Google Maps" links (new tab, rel=noopener), Google Maps attribution, loading/empty/error states, a11y as the rest of the app. Alerts page: "Search the web now" on every watch card (fare, hotel, activity, trip) showing the result panel (summary, quotes with source links, Searched for, disclaimer), never cached in storage.
  • Android: Near me screen uses v2 (sections: true) with four sections, Maps intent links (geo/Maps URI), attribution; results kept in ViewModel memory only (remove any Room/DataStore cache of nearby results; keep only the coarse location cell). Nearby notification worker posts only an invitation (no API call). Alerts: "Search the web now" on watch cards, same panel; memory only.

docs.title: Voyager reimagined — whole-journey redesign, iOS app, accounts, social, telemetry (program design)
docs.text: Status: design for the program. Each phase below gets its own implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/) and ships as its own PRs. Owner's brief: 2026-11-10 (20 points, summarised in §1). Decisions marked [call] are mine (the owner delegated them); everything else is from the brief.

docs.title: 1. Intent
docs.text:
Turn Voyager from "a search that produces a plan" into a companion for the whole trip: before (dream, plan, book-watch, prepare), during (today, nearby, money, safety) and after (recap, memories, share, where next). It has the same experience on web, Android and a new native iOS app. The brief puts user experience first: fast, engaging, interactive, light and pleasant by default with dark mode, in seven languages.

Success looks like this: a traveller signs up in under a minute with the method they like. They plan a trip and get a price-drop moment that makes them smile. They use the app every day of the trip, come back afterwards to relive and share it, and keep returning between trips for quizzes, ideas and alerts.

docs.title: Goals (from the brief)
docs.text:
1. Journey-centred redesign of web + Android; native iOS (iPhone + iPad) in its own repo with its own CI.
  2. Sign-in: Google, Facebook (Meta), GitHub, and native username/email/password. Native sign-up sends a confirmation email valid 30 minutes; the link activates the account and lands in the app. Forgotten-password reset.
  3. Account area: avatar + name, settings and preferences, feature toggles and customisation.
  4. Share plans, itineraries and status to Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook and others.
  5. Immersive, localised, push-based recommendations (mobile first).
  6. Price alerts that delight and engage.
  7. Gamification + social: share travel ideas, interact, quizzes, points.
  8. Thorough telemetry for every interaction on all three clients, with zero UX cost.
  9. Identical onboarding on all three clients.
  10. Languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Hindi, Chinese (Simplified), Bengali.
  11. Light theme by default; user-toggled dark mode.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Booking or payments inside the app (we link out; no PCI scope).
  • Photo hosting (the e2-micro has a 30 GB disk). Photos stay on the device; recaps render on the device.
  • Real-time chat between users (DMs). Social means public ideas, comments, follows, likes and quizzes.

docs.title: Anti-goals (shipping these counts as failure even if it "works")
docs.text:
• Anything that slows first paint, typing, scrolling or streaming. Telemetry, social and gamification are all off the critical path.
  • Dark patterns: forced sharing, fake urgency, fake price drops, points for spam.
  • Breaking the existing honesty rules (observed versus estimated prices, verification badges, static-first data).
  • Breaking the deploy contract: backend changes are additive; old SPA ↔ new app and new SPA ↔ old app both work.

docs.title: 2. Constraints
docs.text:
• Infra: one always-free e2-micro (1 GB RAM, shared vCPU), SQLite, Caddy, AI behind a GCP spend cap. New features must fit, so there is no new database server, queue or paid service unless the owner adds one.
  • Two-way compatibility (CLAUDE.md): new endpoints are feature-detected by clients. Nothing gets removed or renamed without a deprecation step. Mobile apps in the field lag even further, so the same rule applies to them.
  • Self-registration opens the AI to strangers. The spend cap stays. [call] Add per-user daily AI quotas on top of the 10-minute windows. Unverified accounts cannot run AI.
  • Store rules that shape the design (verified requirements, not preferences):
  • App Store 4.8: an app offering third-party social login must also offer an equivalent privacy-focused login. [call] Add Sign in with Apple on iOS, and on web/Android too so one account works everywhere.
  • App Store 5.1.1(v) and Google Play: an app with in-app sign-up must offer in-app account deletion.
  • App Store 1.2 / Play UGC policy: user-generated content needs report, block, filtering and a moderation queue. These are part of the social phase, not an add-on.
  • Privacy labels (App Store) and Data safety (Play) must declare the telemetry we collect.
  • Instagram login for personal accounts is not available. Meta retired the Instagram Basic Display API on 2024-12-04, and Instagram Login now serves only business/creator accounts. [call] "Continue with Facebook" covers Meta. Instagram stays a sharing target.
  • Telemetry and the law. The brief says users should not be aware of telemetry. [call] Telemetry is invisible in the experience (no lag, no nagging, batched in the background). It is not undisclosed: it appears in the privacy policy and store labels, can be switched off in Settings → Privacy, and EU/UK users get a one-time consent choice as ePrivacy/GDPR require. Collecting it secretly would expose the owner to GDPR fines and app-store removal. No cross-app tracking, so there is no App Tracking Transparency prompt.
  • Things only the owner can provide. Every feature that depends on them is config-gated and hidden until configured, the same pattern as SERPAPI_KEY: Google OAuth client, GitHub OAuth app, Meta app (Facebook Login + Instagram Stories sharing), Apple Developer Program (Sign in with Apple, APNs, TestFlight/App Store), an SMTP sender, optionally a TikTok developer app (Share Kit), and Xcode installed locally (optional; CI builds on macOS runners).

docs.title: 2a. Owner decisions (2026-11-10)
docs.text:
• Domain: build on the current sslip.io host for now (a limited product–market-fit run with selected users). Make a later move to a custom domain a config change:
  • One setting, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, drives every absolute URL: OAuth redirect URIs, verify/reset links, share pages, OG tags, emails and the Caddy site host.
  • GET /api/config reports the canonical base URL. The mobile apps read it at startup and use it for API calls once it's served from a host they already trust.
  • Universal links / app links are declared for a list of hosts in one build setting per app, so adding the new domain is one line plus a store update. Old sslip.io links keep redirecting.
  • A runbook section in docs/Deployment-GCP.md lists the switch steps (DNS, SITE_HOST, provider consoles, AASA/assetlinks).
  • Known limitation until then: Google OAuth may refuse an sslip.io redirect URI. If it does, Google sign-in stays hidden until the domain exists; GitHub, Facebook and native sign-in are unaffected.
  • Budget: stay on free tiers. Price alerts must fit SerpAPI's 250 searches/month: watches are prioritised (nearest departure, closest to target), re-check intervals adapt, and every price shows an honest "checked N days ago" label. One-tap watch and suggestions never fire a live search by themselves. AI gets strict per-user daily quotas, and moderation uses the cheapest model only on posts that the keyword filter can't decide.
  • Sign-up mode [call]: SIGNUP_MODE=open|invite (default open, per the brief). For a PMF cohort the owner can switch to invite codes without a deploy of new code.

docs.title: 3. The journey (information architecture, same on all clients)
docs.text:
Bottom tabs on mobile, top nav on web; on iPad and wide web, a sidebar:

Tab Purpose Trips (home) Every trip as a card in its phase: Dreaming → Planning → Ready → On the road → Memories. The current or next trip is pinned at the top with a phase-aware "what now" panel. Explore Search / chat / compare / from-a-link / surprise-me (existing modes, one entry point), plus the community ideas feed. Alerts Price watches with a live price story (see §6). Play Daily quiz, challenges, badges, level, leaderboard, scratch map of countries. You Avatar, name, profile, settings, preferences, privacy.

A trip's phase follows its dates (the user can override it). Each phase changes the trip screen:

  • Before: plan (existing results + My Plan), a countdown, a prep checklist built from existing data (visa lead time, packing list, SIM, forex, emergency card, documents, insurance reminder), price watches, a pre-trip stress test, and share the plan.
  • During: a Today view (today's slots with derived times, next-up card, walking directions out to maps apps), Near me (existing /nearby), an offline pack (emergency card, phrases, address card in the local script, currency converter with the last-known rate), an expense log, and status sharing ("Day 3 in Lisbon").
  • After: an auto-generated recap (route map, days, places, distance, countries, spend versus budget), place ratings, journal notes, a recap card to share, a scratch-map update + badges, and "where next" (existing discovery, seeded from the trip and the Taste Graph).

docs.title: 3a. Data model for trips [call]
docs.text: A trip is a saved plan with new nullable columns phase, start_date, end_date, title. A Dreaming trip has no dates. New child tables hold trip_expenses, trip_journal and trip_ratings, keyed by plan id. The old SPA reads plans exactly as today and ignores the new columns.

docs.title: 4. Accounts and identity
docs.text:
• Native sign-up: username, email, password (zxcvbn-style strength meter on the client; server minimum 10 characters, checked against a top-10k common-password list). The account is created pending. A verify email goes out with a single-use, random 256-bit token (only its SHA-256 stored), expiring 30 minutes after issue. The link opens /verify?token=…; on web that activates, signs in and redirects into the app. Mobile uses universal links / app links for the same URL, so the link opens the app. Resending invalidates the previous token, rate-limited. Pending accounts that are never verified are purged after 7 days [call].
  • Password reset: request by email. The response is identical whether or not the account exists (no enumeration). Same token rules, 30 minutes [call]. A successful reset revokes the user's other sessions.
  • Sessions [call]: keep the HS256 JWT but add a per-user token_version claim so sessions can be revoked, plus a refresh token for mobile so users aren't signed out every 24 h. Existing tokens keep working (a missing claim is treated as version 0).
  • OAuth (Google, GitHub, Facebook, Apple) [call]: a server-side authorization-code flow with PKCE + state. Web uses a redirect; mobile uses ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs with a callback to the app's universal link. Email-verified provider identities link to an existing account with the same verified email; anything else creates a new account. One user can have several identities (new user_identities table). GET /api/auth/providers lists every provider with configured: true|false. Owner, 2026-11-10: the sign-in buttons (Google, Facebook, GitHub, Apple) are always visible. Tapping one that isn't configured yet shows a friendly inline note ("Google sign-in is coming soon, use email for now"), never an error page. A provider starts working as soon as its credentials are set, with no client update.
  • Account area: avatar (provider photo, an uploaded image resized to 256 px WebP and stored on disk under 2 MB, or generated initials), display name, handle; language, theme (system/light/dark), currency, units, home-tab sections and feature toggles (e.g. hide Play, hide community), notification categories + quiet hours, privacy (profile visibility, telemetry opt-out), connected sign-in methods, change password, export my data (JSON), delete account.
  • Admin-created users keep working. is_first_login keeps its meaning. The AI gate (verified email required for AI) counts admin-created accounts as verified (signup_method = admin), so existing users are not locked out.
  • Identity key [call]: username stays the immutable internal key, so plans, preferences, recent searches, taste, feedback and devices need no migration. OAuth sign-ups pick a username once, with a suggestion prefilled. The public display name can change; the username can't.
  • Account linking [call]: a provider identity links automatically only to an account whose email we have verified (new email_verified column). Admin-created emails start unverified and are verified by a link from the account page. Facebook's email is untrusted by default (FACEBOOK_EMAIL_TRUSTED=false): it never auto-links. Otherwise linking happens only from the account page while signed in. This prevents account takeover by email.

docs.title: 5. Social, sharing and gamification
docs.text:
• Profiles: public handle, avatar, home country, countries visited (scratch map), level, badges, and published ideas. Visibility: public / followers / private.
  • Ideas feed: publish a plan or a recap as an idea (a snapshot copy; private notes and prices are optional). Like, save to my trips ("remix", which exists as utils/remix), comment, follow. Ranking is chronological plus engagement plus taste match, computed in SQLite.
  • Safety: report (with reasons), block, keyword filter, and a cheap Flash-Lite moderation classification of new posts/comments before they go public (a borderline post is held for the admin queue). Per-user posting limits. Admin moderation tab.
  • Quizzes: a daily 5-question quiz plus topic packs (flags, capitals, cuisine, landmarks, etiquette, "where is this?"). The question bank is generated offline by script, auto-checked by a second model pass and committed as data in seven languages, so a quiz costs no live AI calls. Questions and answers are validated server-side, timing is scored, and there are streaks.
  • Points (XP) ledger, append-only with idempotency keys: quiz answers, daily streaks, a completed trip recap, published ideas that others save, verified email, and a price watch that catches a drop. Points are never awarded for raw volume of posts/likes, so spam earns nothing. Levels, ~30 badges, weekly friends + global leaderboards.
  • Sharing: every plan, itinerary, recap, status, quiz score and price-drop win can become a share card (1080×1920 story and 1200×630 link sizes) with a link to a public page. That page is server-rendered with Open Graph/Twitter tags, so previews look right on X/Facebook/WhatsApp/LinkedIn.
  • Mobile: the native share sheet. On iOS, Instagram Stories through its documented URL scheme (needs the Meta App ID); TikTok through Share Kit when configured, otherwise the share sheet.
  • Web: the Web Share API with files where supported; otherwise X/Facebook/WhatsApp/LinkedIn intents, copy link and download image.

docs.title: 5a. Gamification across the whole journey (owner, 2026-11-10)
docs.text:
Gamification isn't only the Play tab: every phase of a trip and every main feature earns and shows progress. One engine powers it, built in Phase 1 next to accounts, so each later phase only adds hooks: - Engine: an append-only XP ledger (idempotency key per award), a rules table (event → points, daily cap per rule), badges with progress (3/5 countries in Asia), levels, streaks with a weekly "streak freeze", and seasonal challenges. Awards are computed server-side from events the server already sees (plan saved, watch created, quiz answered), never from client claims, so they can't be faked through telemetry. - Where it shows (same on all clients):

Moment Gamified touch Onboarding The traveller-type result is the first badge; finishing setup gives starter XP and unlocks the scratch map. Dreaming Saving ideas from the feed and remixing them; a "bucket list" goal ("visit 30 countries") with a progress ring. Planning A plan completeness meter (flights, stay, days filled, visa checked, packing); stress-test fixes earn "Smart planner" progress. Ready The prep checklist is a quest: each ticked item fills a "Trip ready" bar, and at 100 % a badge appears with a confetti moment (reduced motion respected). Price alerts A "Deal hunter" track: XP for each real drop caught, a savings milestones badge ($50/$200/$1,000 saved), and a target-hit celebration. Estimates never award points. On the road Daily check-in streak during the trip, "local explorer" for places visited from Near me, a passport-stamp animation on arriving in a new country. Memories Finishing the recap gives XP plus a scratch-map reveal of new countries and region badges (continents, UNESCO sites seen, cuisines tried from ratings). Social XP when others save/remix your idea (not for likes), helpful-comment badges chosen by the idea's author, friend leaderboards. Play The daily quiz, topic packs, a head-to-head quiz with friends (asynchronous) and weekly challenges tied to destinations in the user's upcoming trips ("Know before you go: Japan").
  • Guardrails: no points for raw volume (posts, likes, searches); daily caps per rule; streaks are never punishing (a freeze, no loss messaging); every game element can be hidden in Settings ("Hide Play & points"); points never gate core features.
  • Telemetry measures whether each touch helps (retention, plan completion, alert engagement), so point values can be tuned. Values are config, not code.

docs.title: 6. Price alerts that delight
docs.text: Keep every honesty rule. Add: - A price story per watch: sparkline/history, the lowest seen, "typical" range, a target price slider, and a plain-language advisor line (existing pricing-advisor). Estimates stay labelled and frozen. - A drop moment: a push/email with the amount and percentage saved; in the app, an animated drop card and a "you're saving $X" counter (reduced motion respected). - A savings tally across all watches, a shareable "I saved $X" card, and XP for drops. - Smarter watching: one-tap "watch this" on any flight/hotel/activity/trip card. Smart suggestions on what to watch when a plan is saved. A weekly digest (opt-in) instead of noise. - Anti-spam: the existing evaluate() rules plus quiet hours, a per-category daily cap and grouped notifications.

docs.title: 7. Immersive notifications
docs.text:
• Server-sent (FCM for Android as today; direct APNs for iOS: a new sender next to services/push.py, and /api/devices additively accepts platform: "ios"): price drops, trip countdown (T-30 visa check, T-7 packing, T-1 check-in + weather), a morning brief on each trip day, a weather change for today's outdoor slots, the daily quiz, and social events (follows, likes, comments, saves). Delivery respects categories, quiet hours in the device's timezone, and a global cap (3/day, price drops exempt). Text is localised server-side from the same string catalogue.
  • Location-aware recommendations [call], computed on the device: the app uses significant-location-change / geofences (opt-in, explained when asked). On arrival somewhere new during a trip, the app calls /nearby and shows a local notification ("You're near Belém — Pastéis de Belém is 4 min away"). The server never stores a location history, which keeps the privacy labels and the 1 GB box simple.

docs.title: 8. Telemetry
docs.text:
• One event schema for all three clients (docs/Telemetry.md, versioned): {event, ts, session_id, anon_id, user_id?, platform, app_version, locale, screen, props}. Event families: lifecycle (app open/background, session), navigation (screen view + time on screen), interaction (tap/toggle/submit, with a stable element id instead of text), search/chat funnel (submit, first section, all sections, abandon), section engagement (expand, select into plan, link-out), share, alert, social, quiz, onboarding steps, performance (TTFB, time to first section, cold start, frame drops), and errors (crashes, API failures).
  • Never collected: free text the user typed, precise location, email/name in props, other users' content.
  • Zero-cost delivery: buffered in memory and flushed every 10–20 s or 50 events, on backgrounding, and through sendBeacon / BGTaskScheduler / WorkManager. Persisted offline (IndexedDB / file) with a cap. Sent gzipped. The client never awaits it. On the server, POST /api/telemetry is a fast append into a separate SQLite file (telemetry.db, WAL) so it never contends with user data, plus a nightly rollup into daily aggregates, raw events kept 90 days [call]. It is a new pipeline: the existing POST /api/analytics/events (signed-in only, writes log lines) stays as it is. The new endpoint accepts anonymous events, and props is a closed per-event schema (enums, numbers, ids), so free text cannot get in. Raw events are not backed up to GCS; daily aggregates are [call].
  • Consent gate [call]: clients show the one-time choice when the device region or timezone is EU/EEA/UK/CH. The VM has no geo-IP and adding one isn't worth it. Everyone has the Settings switch.
  • Admin analytics tab: daily actives, funnels, retention cohorts, feature usage, alerts, quiz, performance.

docs.title: 9. Look, feel, language
docs.text:
• Design system [call]: one token set (colour, type, spacing, radius, elevation, motion) defined once in the main repo as JSON and generated into Tailwind CSS variables, Android Material 3 theme values and iOS asset catalog/colour sets. Android already ships a designed light + dark theme, so the token set starts from Android's palette and is reconciled in the design phase. Android is restyled only where the new design deliberately changes it. Light is the default: warm off-white, an ocean-teal primary, a sunset-coral accent. The dark theme is designed rather than inverted. Motion is short and purposeful, and prefers-reduced-motion is respected. Final visual direction is set in the design phase with mockups before building.
  • i18n [call]: the web catalogue is frontend/src/i18n/locales/<lang>/<namespace>.json (i18next, JSON v4 plural suffixes such as _one/_other). Generators emit Android strings.xml and iOS .xcstrings from it, and CI fails on missing keys (on web, the catalogue parity test). Dates/numbers/currency are formatted per locale. Noto Sans Devanagari/Bengali/SC fallbacks are loaded only when needed. AI outputs come back in the user's language (a language instruction in agent prompts). Static tables keep English content, with UI chrome translated. Translations are machine-drafted, then reviewed by a second model for meaning; native speaker review of hi/bn/zh is recommended before marketing in those languages.
  • Onboarding (identical on all clients): it replaces Android's current onboarding but keeps its traveller-type result as part of step 2 [call]. 5 steps sharing the same keys, order and copy: welcome → how you travel (interests/pace) → home airport + passport (for visa) → notifications (contextual ask) → first trip or explore. It is skippable and resumable, and its progress is telemetered. The existing OnboardingTour becomes the in-app coach marks after onboarding.

docs.title: 10. iOS app
docs.text:
• Repo rupakc/travel-planner-ios (public, MIT, like Android). SwiftUI, Swift 6, iOS 17+ [call]. iOS 17 runs on iPhone XS/XR (2018) and newer, and on iPads from the 6th generation. Going lower would mean giving up Observation and modern SwiftUI for a very small share of devices.
  • Architecture: feature modules as Swift packages; Observation; async/await. Server-sent events read with URLSession.bytes, parsed off the main actor. Swift Codable models mirror the API. MapKit for maps. Keychain for tokens. No heavy third-party dependencies (Firebase Messaging only if FCM→APNs is chosen over direct APNs [call: direct APNs from the backend with an Apple auth key; no Firebase on iOS]).
  • iPad: NavigationSplitView, multi-column results, keyboard shortcuts, pointer support.
  • Performance budget: cold start < 400 ms to first frame on an iPhone XS; 60/120 fps scrolling; lazy stacks; image downsampling; no main-thread JSON.
  • CI: GitHub Actions macos-15. On every PR: build, SwiftLint, unit tests, snapshot tests and a UI-test smoke run on iPhone + iPad simulators. On main: an archive, uploaded to TestFlight once signing secrets exist.
  • Parity: a written parity matrix (web ↔ Android ↔ iOS) lives in the main repo's docs and gates "done".

docs.title: 11. Phases (order and why)
docs.text:
# Phase Ships Depends on 0 Foundations Design tokens + light/dark on web, i18n framework + the 7 catalogues for existing web UI, telemetry pipeline (backend + web SDK), parity matrix — 1 Accounts + game engine Sign-up/verify/reset, OAuth (config-gated; the owner sends provider credentials after the build), sessions, account area, delete/export, daily AI quotas, the XP/badge/streak engine and its first hooks (onboarding, email verified) 0 2 Journey redesign (web) Trips hub, phases, prep checklist, Today, offline pack, expenses, recap, shared onboarding 0, 1 3 Price alerts 2.0 Price story, drop moment, savings, one-tap watch, digest 2 4 Sharing Share cards, public OG pages, share flows 2 5 Social + Play Profiles, ideas feed, moderation, quizzes, head-to-head, leaderboards, challenges 1, 4 6 Notifications Server categories/quiet hours/caps, trip-phase pushes, APNs 1, 2 7 iOS app Full parity, starting once Phase 1's API is stable; tracks web phases from then on 1 8 Android parity All new features + tokens + i18n + onboarding + telemetry each phase

Each phase from 2 onwards includes its gamified touches from §5a; they belong to its "done", not to Phase 5. Phases 7 and 8 run in parallel with 2–6 once the API for a phase is merged. Each phase follows the same loop: plan → parallel implementation agents in worktrees → tests → three independent review passes → fix → PR → merge (green CI deploys).

docs.title: 12. Left to the builder
docs.text: Exact component structure, endpoint shapes (within §4–§8 and the compatibility rule), the copy (first in English, then translated), badge list and point values (tuned with telemetry later), and the visual details inside the token system.
